author: Mekunekud
subject: Re: [Shaman] Healing Stream Totems Usefulness
content_md:
In Vanilla, it did scale with healing. 65% over the duration/2.16% per tick. If you went for maximum healing power, at least by BWL levels, you can reach nearly 1000 healing power and your 650 extra healing over 30 ticks means its nearly 40 healing a tick every 2 seconds for 5 people for 80 mana for no real upkeep. Its one of the most efficient spells in the game.
Ofc it COULD scale better and shamans aren't lacking for AoE healing in the first place but the only "better" healing spell in the game in terms of mana value is Judgement of Light.
It's just all dependent on group setup and fight. Would I use it in an extremely intensive fight where I'd be spamming Chain Heals constantly? Not really. Would I drop it on a fight like Huhuran where there's a slowly increasing DoT where a melee group gets progressively harder to heal? Yes. I would because it'd be roughly 500 Hp/5 for absolutely no effort.
OFC its bugged on Turtle WoW, like alot of private servers but when working as intended, on the right fights, it helps healing shamans immensely.

The Guardian Totems talent increased damage reduction for Stoneskin/Windwall does not show up on the buff panel for your character. It shows the unmodified amount.

 1 Put 2 talent points in Guardian Totems.

The buffpanel should show the correct values of the respective buffs. It is very difficult to assess whether or not the talent does anything in general because of the fluctuating damage numbers.

author: Aniki22
subject: Предложение по изменению шаманов
content_md:
My English is bad, so I will use a translator, I hope you can understand me.

Let's start with a few clarifications to understand who shamans are.
 1. This is a class that personally does not have any possible abilities other than interacting with the spirits of the ancestors and the elements.
 2. Spirits are sentient beings that need to be contacted, and some spirits compete with each other, such as fire and water.
 3.Although Blizzard hasn't made it official, each element works better in different situations, for example, the healer shaman uses the water element while the earth element is better suited for defensive abilities.

What is my proposal? is to showcase each shaman specialization as a synergy between the shaman and a separate element.

 1. Create a separate talent tree for a tank shaman using the power of the earth.

A) The current talents from the enhancement specialization, such as increased dodge chance and armor gain from equipped equipment, will look great there.
b) Add an ability similar to earthquakes from later versions so that the shaman can maintain the threat level on a group of enemies.
c) Earth shock should only be a tank shaman ability and replace taunt.
d) Rockbiter weapon will also be available only to the tank shaman to increase the outgoing threat from him.
I think various talents and passive abilities that will increase his survivability will not be difficult to come up with, for example "mountain stability" - something between the ability of dwarfs and tremor totem (reducing damage taken and immune to all types of debuffs for a short time)
And probably last but not least, this is an attempt to leave the place of the shaman in the raid and the group as support, this is to strengthen all the totems of the earth in the specialization of the shaman of the tank.

 2. With a shaman-healer, in my opinion, nothing special needs to be done; it responds well to the requirements of the water element.

 3. My favorite enhancement specialization deserves to be more distinctive than it is. To begin with, I would like to clarify that the enhancement shaman uses the element of air and thanks to it increases his speed, and he also uses more powerful abilities to deal either strong damage or to control the enemy.
A) Replace Earth shock with Wind Shear from a later version with the ability to interrupt spells and also deal damage.
b) Lightning is more related to the elements of air than to any others, therefore the enhancement shaman should use them, and in order for this to be possible, I would suggest introducing the mechanics as in the future additions "Maelstrom Weapon" for accumulating charges and reaching 5 charges cast lightning or Chain Lightning on an enemy instantly and at no mana cost.
c) Strengthen the lightning shield so that it does not have charges, but simply hangs on the shaman for the allotted time and deals damage not only in response to an enemy attack, but every few seconds.
d) Increase the general mobility of the shaman enhancement.

 4. Probably the most difficult specialization to implement, since I see an elemental shaman who uses mainly the fire element.
a) Add Lava Burst and implement interaction between Lava Burst and Flame Shock.
b) Replace all abilities that use lightning with fire ones (yes, I understand the amount of work).
c) Add a passive ability to the shaman to increase spell damage for himself and his group (alternative to enhancement shaman for casters only)
d) Increase the damage of all fire totems and possibly add new ones or change old ones.

Well, such a small change to replace the appearance of the wolf for the Trolls and Tauren with the lizard / tiger and Deer.

I hope someone liked my ideas, I look forward to your comments.

author: Fishi
subject: Suggestions
content_md:
Hello fellow Shaman enjoyers!
There is a lot of discussion and speculation about changes for shamans, and as someone who has been playing enhancement since forever, I'd like to advocate for my most beloved spec here.
These are just my personal opinions, and although I am not a person of math and mechanics, I still firmly believe 3 simple fixes would make shaman soar a little higher in raids and dungeons already!
 1.) Please allow shaman and paladin buffs stack.
We are playing on a crossfaction server, which I adore, but a soft mutual exclusivity barring my two favourite classes apart from each other breaks my heart, and to an extent, my gameplay. I do not believe that allowing totems and blessings to mix would make much of an impact negatively - it would further allow sustainabilty regarding mana towards classes that need it the most, and the most overu- i mean, popular dps specs are already broken to hell and back, an extra teaspoon of crack wouldn't stir up much water in their direction. If anything, it could be a change that would welcome both dps / tankadins and ele / enh into raids.
 2.) Stormstrike debuff stack removal
It would be such a lovely thing to give to boomkins, assassination rogues and eleshams, among others, a lovely flat nature dmg increase! It already takes a debuff slot, so why not make it beneficial to the entire raid? Nature damage is already wet noodle tier, this way at least it could make a sizable impact, potentially, which brings me to my next point -
 3.) Curse of the Elements to include nature damage
Quite self explanatory, and would help us a lot, especially spellhancement / ele / boomie friends.
I do not think that these changes are in any way overly excessive, they could add a lot not only to enhancement or shamans, but to raids and other classes as well, without directly empowering shamans, therefore making a bit less of an impact in PvP, in which I believe shamans already are quite fine at.
Please share your opinions, and if you agree with any of these points, make some noise!
Thank you very much for reading. Have a wonderful time, fellow turtles!

author: Mekunekud
subject: Re: Suggestions
content_md:
My personal suggestions are
 1.) Buff the shit out of Mana Spring Totem. It's currently garbage and due to cross faction, it should at least equalise Blessing of Wisdom like it did in WOTLK.
 2.) Make Stormstrike a stacking debuff with a duration for Arcane/Nature. 5% per stack with a 20 second duration. This buffs Arcane mages, balance druids, other shamans and dagger rogues as well as people who have nature based damage ontop of that.
 3.) Make Earth Shock only do the threat multiplier when Rockbiter is applied. It's silly otherwise because it means Stormstrike is nothing but an extra swing to Enhancement Shamans and the entire point is to buff Nature damage, which most of which comes from shamans in the first place. This isn't game breaking and allows shamans a slight improvement.
 4. Make the +15% Lightning Shield talent into a +15% any elemental Shield talent. The talent to cast it on another target can remain as LS but for a tanking shaman at 60, you will likely be using Earth/Water Shield over Lightning Shield and that means the talent is boring and avoidable. 15% healing or mana restored wouldn't break the balance since they aren't overly strong anyway.
 5.) Totems to have 30 yards baseline other than fire totems.
Also, reworking of Shaman T1 and T2 so there's no spirit and a more focused statline. T1 should be healing and T2 should be caster focused.

author: Fishi
subject: Re: Suggestions
content_md:
Tier sets definitely need to a rework.
I would also suggest making Ancestral Knowledge into something useful - instead of a +5% max mana, I'd rather have a +X% mp/5 that works during casting. That would make the talent feel less like a waste / nearly useless gateway to Flurry, and would boost leveling immensely.
Every spec would benefit from it, and I think it fits with the theme of shamans way more.
Some folks have suggested making the various weapon enhancements into 'stances', for example rockbiter for tanking, windfury for melee dps, flametongue for ele, and frost for healing. While personally I don't really agree with that direction, it can definitely have a positive impact on simplifying some of the playstyle issues shaman has, especially tanking, which several shaman players seem to be very fond of.

author: Gladeshadow
subject: Help! Shamans and racial spells/abilities
content_md:
Hi! Making a shaman is something I'd like to do soon, and Turtle WoW has made it even ore interesting. Racials may not matter to some, but for me they add much more flavor to the game and are a lot of fun. So I'm looking for feedback and thoughts from other shamans or potential shamans about what works and what could potentially work well. Both the racial abilities **and** the racial spells can create some fun combinations or ways to play. Here are some pros for each race as I recall.

Orc:
 **Racial spell:** Feral Spirit | 21% Base Mana Cost | 5 Minute Cooldown |
Summons two Spirit Wolves under the command of the Shaman for 20 seconds.
 **Racial abilities:**
Axe Specialization - Skill with Axes and Two-Handed Axes increased by 5.
Blood Fury - Increases base melee attack power by 25% for 15 sec and reduces healing effects on you by 50% for 25 sec.
Command - Damage dealt by Hunter and Warlock pets increased by 5%.
Hardiness - Chance to resist Stun effects increased by an additional 25%.
Orcs seem like a solid choice. Good at burst damage in general. Not a huge synergy between skills and racials that I've noticed.

Troll:
 **Racial spell:** Hex | 21% Base Mana Cost | 5 Minute Cooldown |
Transforms the enemy into a frog that cannot cast, and does 66% less damage for up to 4 seconds. Only works on Beasts, Humanoids and Critters.
 **Racial abilities:**
Beast Slaying: Damage dealt versus Beasts increased by 5%.
Berserking: Increases your casting and attack speed by 10% to 30%. At full health the speed increase is 10% with a greater effect up to 30% if you are badly hurt when you activate Berserking. Lasts 10 sec.
Bow Specialization: Skill with Bow Weapons increased by 5.
Regeneration: Health regeneration rate increased by 10%. 10% of total Health regeneration may continue during combat.
Throwing Specialization: Skill with Throwing Weapons increased by 5.
Trolls seem like a nice choice due to hex and berserking. Hex in particular looks like an excellent means of controlling a target, allowing the user some time more time to kill, escape, or do whatever else is needed.

Tauren:
 **Racial spell:**:
Tauren: Spirit Link | 21% Base Mana Cost |10 Minute Cooldown |
Link the spirits of an ally and their 3 closest allies within 15 yards together. When linked targets take damage, 10% is distributed among the other linked allies. Lasts 20 seconds.
 **Racial abilities:**
Cultivation: Herbalism skill increased by 15.
Endurance: Total Health increased by 5%.
Nature Resistance: Nature Resistance increased by 10.
War Stomp: Stuns up to 5 enemies within 8 yds for 2 sec.
And exclusive to Turtle WoW: Plainsrunning!
Spirit Link looks like a mixed bag that could help or harm the party. Would love to hear feedback about it. War stomp is excellent, allowing a specced fire nova totem to trigger without the possibility of foes killing it beforehand. It also allows time for a lesser healing wave or more time to turn into a spirit wolf to escape if needed. And it's simply a stun, which shamans lack, and additional interrupt. Plainsrunning is another nice ability to help the user and possibly confound opponents.

At this point, I'm mostly torn between trolls and tauren. No disrespect to orcs! I'd like to hear from those about why they are good as well. But mostly to hear about all the choices, which all look excellent.

author: Mekunekud
subject: Searing Totem buff.
content_md:
Can the devs look into giving Searing Totem a buff? It's such an anemic totem at high level, even outside stacking spell power, that it becomes functionally useless.
Even into WOTLK, noone uses Searing Totem even tho on a single target boss, where the duration should be the deciding factor, it's so inferior to Magma Totem that you may as well not bother.
I suggest either halving the cast time, so its a single target version of Magma Totem with a longer duration at better mana efficiency and thus it delivers the same impact every second rather than every 2 seconds, or increase the scaling of Searing Totem so that it becomes a viable totem to drop for Elemental Shamans/T2.5 shamans and thus buffs their DPS since at the moment, It's functionally worthless in every possible situation.
For example, a top end searing totem is worth all of 25 DPS on a single target, even if hit capped. while Magma Totem is worth 37 DPS on single target. That seems ridiculous that a single target totem, even talented with 15% damage, be outdone by a pure basic AoE totem.

author: Mekunekud
subject: Re: Searing Totem buff.
content_md:
I mean shamans need buffs across the entire board but from a Vanilla perspective, it's not really going to happen through gear. There's a big reason that in WOTLK, a fairly large amount of Enhancement talents were spell power/AP from Int and so forth and without those, shamans can't really compete without dual wield WF on some basic level.
If they were to nerf the WF buff so it was just 2 extra attacks without AP and allow shamans to dual wield, it might make Enhancement more viable as DPS. We'd still not be on par with warriors and rogues but then at least the white damage value would go up and mana dependency go down.
The only other real buff would be to allow totems to provide their weapon buffs to shamans regardless of their current weapon buff, so Shamans would get WF totem and WF weapon buff, obviously non-self proccing for some degree of balance, so Shamans operate like paladins with seals and so Shamans can either use a totem or use an oil without losing one of their primary core abilities.

author: Rafale
subject: How to fix Bloodlust ?
content_md:
Bloodlust is badly designed right now :

 - It costs too much mana for enh shamans which lack it
 - You always need to give it to MT to secure threat at beginning of fight
 - You can be a resto shaman and use it, which is absurd when we look at the talents in that tree

Solution :

Bloodlust (**no mana cost**, 3 min cd)
Increases melee, ranged, and spell casting speed by 20% for a party member within 20 yards. Lasts 20 sec.
 **This ability can only be used after scoring a melee critical strike. Each time you gain a melee critical strike, the cooldown of Bloodlust is reduced by 5 sec.**

Benefits :
 - Only real enhancement shamans will be able to use bloodlust. No resto shamans will have to get it.
 - Reactive gameplay and blocks the "give to MT at pull".
 - Real scaling for enhancements which will have to build their gear on crit (synergy with Flurry, elemental focus, elemental devastation)

author: Mekunekud
subject: Re: How to fix Bloodlust ?
content_md:
Make it 10%. Make it buff both the shaman and their target. Means you aren't missing out on the buff by donating it to someone like the tank.
further changes I'd like to see.
Make the LS buff talent in the early tree into a general elemental shield buff.
Make the "cast on someone else" talent, which while interesting is a bit of a drain on enhancement outside pre-pull/drink, into a "melee critical hits recharge shield charges by 1".
Add in a talent later on that links to both that procs the shield effect on crit at the same time with a short internal cooldown on LS to prevent triple crit WF getting an extra 700 damage from procs.
This allows melee DPS shamans a way to regenerate mana via water shield and melee crits.
It also allows tank shamans a bit of survivability via a high base crit (due to agi) through Earth Shield.
It also plays into crit stacking, which shamans benefit from alot as melee due to Flurry and WF, without breaking the class in terms of overall DPS due to the high costs of shaman abilities in general.
Would also like to see Stormstrike changed a bit. Its fine now in terms of mana cost but the debuff should be changed so it gives a flat 10% shock damage buff so shamans can use it to amp up frost shock in DPS roles and still use it as a tank. Currently it's nothing but an extra melee swing, which is fine, and I'm not even sure it can be used in raids without pushing buffs off, which doesn't help Shamans already anemic dps.

What blizzard has occasionally done in the past was putting "fuck u" talents as requirements for other talents. For instance you needed parry for dual wield in TBC - parry also reduiced your aggro output. This means you couldn't dual wield tank if you wanted to as shaman in 2.0 - 2.3.

One drastic change they could make is neuter it to a selfcast. But to me at  least enhancement has always been more about enabling your team than yourself.

author: Klouther
subject: Side buff to Totem's
content_md:
Recently I started levelling a shaman after casually playing a pally for quite a few months and the first thing that I found problematic was the Totem System.

Totem's ought to be the counterpart for paladin Blessing's yet they are quite inferior to them: you need to do a few questchains *to get all the basic totems and the reagent to use them*, their uptime cost is far higher and depends on positioning, resistance totem's use slots for WFT, STR, AGI or healing totems making them less desirable to use and the base range of the totem's is pretty limiting on itself.

So here's my proposal; change the totems(the item's you need to carry around to cast Totem's) to grant self buffs.

Earth Totem-> Increase armor and resistance contribution from your gear by 5%.
Fire Totem-> Your auto attacks, Lightning Bolt and Chain Lightning deal 10% of your stamina as extra fire damage.
Water Totem-> You receive 5% of your spirit as hp+5 & mp+5.
Air Totem-> Increases your hit and spell hit by 2%.

These are just suggestion from someone with only leveling experience as a clasisc shaman so far so feel free to point out better alternatives or ones with a better "classic feeling". This post is mainly to highlight a possible path to buff the base strenght of shamans without the need of a patch.

The pros-> my proposed change would be an item database change which is quicker to do from a dev standpoint and easier to tune(or scrap), players will get something useful of the totem's taking bag space instead of it being a reagent you need to drop Totem's and therefore provide utility for yourself or group, it would make completing the totem questchain feel more rewarding instead of "now you can use half your skillset", possible addition of PR elements.

The cons-> if implemented, it would add another layer to balancing the class, it might upsept PvP balance, the buffs might appear too weak/strong and players will probably whine about it and ask to buff/nerf it and take away dev's time, other classes might feel entiltled to ask for something similar

author: Gladeshadow
subject: Troll and Tauren Shaman Racials
content_md:
Hi all!

Orcs have a great shaman racial that works to boost their damage - thus working very well with their Blood Fury racial ability. The troll and tauren racials, on the other hand, are rather lackluster and could use some reworking or even complete overhauls.

Starting with the trolls, their hex does this: *Transforms the enemy into a frog that cannot cast, and does 60% less damage for up to 5 seconds*.
What's frustrating about this is that the enemy can attack and still maintains control of their movement. Against casters it's ok, but against melee it's basically a (strong) attack debuff on a high cool down. Really not great. I suggest replacing it with the version of hex we see troll npcs use in the game. Specifically this one: <https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=24053/hex> which does this: *Transforms an enemy into a frog, rendering it unable to attack or cast spells for 5 sec.* The loss of control is very iconic when hexed, as I'm sure we've all experienced. It's not an overly powerful ability since it's basically a stun  where the opponent randomly moves instead of standing still. You could compare it to paladins' hammer of justice, which lasts longer and has a shorter cooldown. Hex would be much more in flavor with this change and allow for more versatile use, such as fight control or providing opportunity for an escape, such as hexing and then using ghost wolf.

The tauren shaman racial does this: *Link the spirits of an ally and their 3 closest allies within 15 yards together. When linked targets take damage, 15% is distributed among the other linked allies. Lasts 20 seconds.*  Talking with others, this seems to be the least popular shaman racial. The cooldown of 10 minutes does it no favors since that effectively prevents using it often. But going into the ability, it's an overall mixed bag. Sure, it makes your tank tankier, but at the cost of everyone else's hit points. This could work moderately well with chain heal, but it's easy enough to imagine scenarios where spirit link hurts the team. Like when a boss does aoe damage or hits someone other than the tank, the linked health may cause enough damage to players to kill them. Probably a rare scenario, but not one I'd even want the possibility of, so why risk using spirit link in the first place when things are otherwise fine?
Overall, this is a very in flavor ability but both the orc and troll racials are always good to use, unlike this ability. At the least, perhaps this could buff armor or completely reduce damage by a small amount when used, like the retail Spirit Link Totem does: *reduces damage taken by all party and raid members within 10 yards by 10%*. Then it would at least provide a buff to every affected party at the time.

These changes would give a larger reason to pick a specific shaman race depending on goals. Right now, orc is the only race with a nice ability. I think these proposed changes could create some equality among the racial spells - used differently, but each good and flavorful.

For the first, that sounds like a good change. I'd really see it less as a stun with movement, and more as a different sort of Polymorph.

For the second, though...I wonder if the problem isn't more in people using it wrong. "It makes your tank tankier." ...well, why would you ever want to use it on the tank? The tank's job is to *stop* other people from taking damage, not to be the last man standing. I'd prefer to cast that on a melee DPS or on a healer, as an insurance policy in the event that the tank loses aggro, or an attack does area damage. Use it to put damage the tank couldn't stop back *on* the tank, not to take damage off of them.

author: Kairion
subject: Lightning Shock - Fixing Enhancer Part 1/x
content_md:
It is not particularly controversial to say that enhancement shaman is one of the weaker class specs that a group can bring to a raid. At the same time enhancement is one of the best classes in the entire game for burst damage.

In order to make him more attractive to raids, his personal dps should be helped out a bit, while not increasing his burst potential even more.

In PvP players can reach hitcap fairly quickly. Even with just skilling Nature's guidance shaman has a 98% chance to land his shocks in PvP. This is in contrast to PvE where even with Nature’s Guidance shocks still have a 14% chance to miss their targets. It follows that improving spell hit chance for shaman improves his PvE performance while keeping PvP largely unchanged.

There are many different ways to achieve this, but the most elegant in my opinion would be giving shaman a new shock which he was supposed to have during wows development cycle but was rolled into Earthshock in Patch 0.9. Its name was Lightning shock and its referenced here (<https://wowwiki-archive.fandom.com/wiki/Patch_0.9>) . The spell itself remains in the game with the name Shock (<https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=2608/shock>). Many mobs still use it and ist a shock that deals nature damage without extra effect.

Now Lightning Shock would have to be tweaked a little bit. As all different flavors of shocks do provide an extra effect next to their damage. The extra effect for Lightning Shock should be it is guaranteed to hit.
It being guaranteed to hit would be a 100% turtle addition and not the original intent of blizzard

Giving this spell with equal damage & scaling to Earthshock allows enhancers to slot it into their rotation instead of Earthshock. This overall increases his damage done with spells by about 14-17% without generating bonus threat and with no negative impact on PvP.

Now it has to be said, this alone does not make the enhancement shaman viable, but it would be a small step on the road similar to how holy strike is quite a noticeable but not omnipotent improvement to Retri and Protection paladin

Lorewise it also fits well, as Earth, Fire & Water all have their shocks, but the wind element does only have totems but no shock. Lightning Shock neatly closes this gap.

Huge thanks to Daggerfallvanillaenhancedenjoyer on the Turtlewow discord for helping me brainstorm and come up with this idea and providing the sources for the removed Lightning Shock to begin with

author: Original3
subject: Re: Lightning Shock - Fixing Enhancer Part 1/x
content_md:
Big +1

Only thing, I would make differently is the spell hit thingy.
As someone, who is actively raiding as Shaman tank, I can say how unpleasant is that 14% - 17% chance to miss with Earth Shocks. On boss pulls it makes a big polarization of combat. You either get a lot of threat at the begining, that you can sustain with downranking ES and hitting with Rocbiter weapon, or you get resist/miss and it makes you fail your main task as tank.
(by the way, shaman tank has better threat opening potantial than warrior, since we don't have to build up rage)

Shaman Tanks solve this problem with Nat Pagles Broken Reel. But that trinket still has CD and it forces you to lose trinket slot, that could be used for mitigation oriented trinket.

What can solve this? Talents or Gear.

There are two solutions I have:

 1. Rework talent Thunderhead (very useless talent)

Row 3 - Reduces the chance, that your opponent resists your Shock spells by 10%

 2. Rework Weapon Mastery to Combat Mastery

Row 6 - Increases the damage of your melee weapons by 2%/4%/6%/8%/10%. In addition, reduces the chance, that your opponent resists your Shocks spells by 2%/4%/6%/8%/10%.

author: Kairion
subject: Re: Lightning Shock - Fixing Enhancer Part 1/x
content_md:
Melee hittable on Shocks has massive implications that i don't think are helpful for the game.

You trade  a higher misschance for being parryable / Dodgeable
How should it interact with stuff light Nightfall & Winter chill. These effects specifically improve spells agains the target.
Elemental devastation turns from bad to 100% useless
It does not fit with classic theme one bit
Physical "elemental attacks" can pierce spellshields
Can it Proc spellbased procs, what about melee based procs?
Does weaponskill make an impact here? because if it does you made Orc even more decisively be the best race than it already is
etc.

Also all interrupts produce a lot of threat. Earthshock is significant here in the sense that it does noticeable damage. Its much more interesting if the class with a kick every 6 seconds has to consider if they really want to kick the boss and risk drawing aggro or rather let the cast trough. Just dumbing down earthshock and hard tying aggro to earthshock makes dedicated tanks better, but funnily enough makes emergency "taunt" with earthshock worse. So these things are all tradeoffs. While the new shock just solves DPS shamans problems without creating any for people who do different things.

author: Fishi
subject: Re: Lightning Shock - Fixing Enhancer Part 1/x
content_md:
Well, I'd like to scream into the void in here as well;
I feel like shaman is incredibly stunted. We have crazy good tools on paper, but the numbers just fall short, as if we're feared for being too strong on our own, or offering too much power to our allies.
The result is us hitting like wet noodle and offering raw sticks of spaghetti for support.
Please give totems some form of scaling. Totems pale in comparison to anything a paladin can offer at endgame content.
Please give shamans ap from agility AND strength. We already hit lighter than my grandpa's farts, (apart from that one time in combat when wf kicks in, which in itself is also an issue) we have sooo little of both on endgame gear, i don't think this can break the game in any way; the meat of our damage is white hits, so please let's make those white hits count.
Speaking of which, please add threat reduction to AT LEAST windfury, but to the two dps specs as a whole would be hella sweet.
Please consider a proactive way for us to maintain mana.
Please fix weapon imbues, give them some form of scaling as well; ap AND spell power as well, for you can only really stack one, or at least make str/agi + spell power gear available for shamans
Please do something to the tier sets. Them being only good for healing (and mildly okay for ele) hurts a little in the heart.
Please fix Ancestral Knowledge. That talent is crazy useless. (I usually suggest a mp/5=[your level]/2, but please feel free to get creative)
Please fix resto. Even just switching the totem reduction talent to go down to the first row so that we can reach the hit talent with meaningful choices would help a lot to spend the rest of our points more meaningfully.
Please consider adding another melee filler ability available to enh shamans in stead of stormstrike and please make stormstrike baseline, enha needs another melee hitter (a slam-like ability has been brought up in a few spots lately and i am enamored with the idea), ele could use it very well, and as there is no functioning nature damage debuff available to worthy of taking a debuff slot;
Please fix stormsrike debuff. 12 secs of 20% increased nature damage RAIDWIDE would make nature oriented classes feel a lot more validated, and shaman would feel a lot more valid choice to bring to raids.
This is all, from the top of my head, and the bottom of my heart.
Thank you for reading.

author: Darkgestalt
subject: Re: Enhance needs help PVe / PvP
content_md:
When it comes to Kairions suggestions, I dont think adding another button to press is really the right solution here. Shamans already are quite the piano-fighters as it is. Now that they added a racial spell and bloodlust to the mix, I feel focussing on tweaking the class within the established toolkit is the best option.

Reducing the innate threat of Earthshock is vital, both for dps shamans and tanks. As Downfall made clear, dps shamans of any variety are unable to use Nature shock damage without needlessly maxing threat which is just stupid. And for tanks, as soon as an enemy is resistant, or worse immune, to nature damage they lose 50% of their threat generators! For a shamtank all shock-types should be able to generate additional threat.

For pvp, it is my personal opinion that not all specs for all classes need to be equally competitive. Obviously there needs to be a good pvp option, but its not like the warrior class has full protection spec be a pvp build. Nor do you expect a subtlety Rogue to outdamage Combat in a raid. Same with Enhance, it allows the shaman to dps in raids and solo, and tank in instances. I feel thats fine for now.

I suggest we follow Trymv1s idea and make Stormstrike a self-buff, getting it away from the debuff limit on bosses. Making Lighting Bolt instant would be insane burst damage with regular hit, WFproc, Stormstrike AND lightning bolt. Thats a bit silly.
Instead, just have it give its bonus on all spell damage (any elemental type) and removing the max 2 limitation.

Then change the wording on Rockbiter and Earth shock to this:
Rockbiter rank 1
Imbue the Shaman's weapon, increasing melee attack power by 50 and allowing melee attacks and elemantal shocks to cause additional threat when using that weapon.  Lasts for 5 minutes.

Earth shock rank 1
Instantly shocks the target with concussive force, causing 19 to 22 Nature damage.  It also interrupts spellcasting and prevents any spell in that school from being cast for 2 sec.

author: Srgtsyphilis
subject: Re: Enhance needs help PVe / PvP
content_md:
I'm no theory carter, and don't have much experience in raiding and end game.
Although, I read several topics on the subject and from what I gather, the issues with Enhancer are twofold :
 1) Mana issues and mana management
 2) DPS and threat generation are dependent on spell hit, which isn't given neither by talents nor gear

Many suggestions have already been made.
I'd like to try and give additionnal imput here.

There are talents that comme directly from xpacs that could adresse the mana issues if implemented :
 - Shamanistic Focus : After landing a melee critical strike, you enter a Focused state.  The Focused state reduces the mana cost of your next Shock spell by 60%.
 - We could imagine an Improved Elemental Shields (from WOTLK) which buffs all shields and which would give access to a Static Shock (again from WOTLK) like 1 point talent in place of Thunderhead which would increase the number of orbs and would give a chance to apply the effect on melee hits. It would solve the issue of Lightning Shield when not being hit, improve its mana efficiency and give a chance to proc Water Shield and regain mana
There are some other existing talents that would do the job, but we don't want to bloat the tree too much and these are the ideas that I like most.

Like other people suggested, regarding spell hit chances, it could ne included in Elemental Devastation as a two way talent : spell crit would give melee crit, melee crit would give like 5% spell hit.
Then we could add some other 5% elsewhere in the tree, in place of Ancestral Knowledge for exemple or combined with Weapon Mastery.
Like that, the spell miss chances would be reduced to 4-7% which seems to be acceptable.

When it comes to the tanking part, the ideas posted above are still valuable. Although, to give it a bit more of a flavor, I thought of a talent which would require 3 points in Spirit Shield, in the same line as Stormstrike
Placeholder name : when equipped with a shield, Shock spells all generate bonus threat and Earth Shock now taunts the enemy.
It'd ne deep enough si that it feels like a commitment and it would give Tank-Sham the opportunity to use the other Shocks aswell, so more of the toolkit available.

Other than that, I'd love some tweaks, obviously, but these wouldn't be make or break things.
 - Insta Ghost Wolf with 2 points in the talent
 - Stormstrike being a personnal buff, maybe affecting all Magic damage
 - Giving some more usefulness to Imbued Weapons other than WF and RB, for tanking, like spell damage on Flametongue, or giving a special effect to Stormstrike depending on the imbue.

Tell Me what you guys think and thanks to the many posters who seek to improve our beloved spec

author: Mzgnkh
subject: Elemental Devastation change suggestion
content_md: One change I'd like to see is Elemental Devastation in the elemental tree giving a stacking casting speed buff to the entire group rather than a melee crit buff to the shaman. Right now, elemental shaman doesn't really bring anything unique compared to both enhancement (bloodlust) and resto (mana tide), which doesn't sit well with me since shamans are a support class. AFAIK no other class buffs casting speed, so it would be a unique perk of the elemental spec. The talent would have to be moved to tier 5 or 6 to make it out of reach of the other specs and the percentage it gives would likely have to be adjusted to make sure it's not over- or underperforming, but it would be great if elemental shamans could become a viable caster group buffer like they were in TBC without outright copying the TBC hit/crit fire totem.

author: Darkgestalt
subject: Mastering the Elements quest bug
content_md:
The questline to Da Voodoo quest, the sunken temple classquest, has 2 paths you can follow. You can either get Elemental Mastery from Beram Skychaser or Sagorne Creststrider OR you can directly go to Bath'rah the Windwatcher who gives Mastering the Elements.

Both Elemental Mastery (8410) and Mastering the Elements (8411) require you to hand in elemental air, fire, wind and water. Afterwards, you get the Spirit Totem quest (8412) and merrily continue on.

However, Mastering the Elements does NOT make you eligible for Spirit Totem. You can complete the quest, Bathy-boy takes your 4 elemental items, you get some XP (citation needed) and he even shows you the quest description for Spirit Totem. But if you press Accept, you hear a error sound and a message that 'you are not eligible for that quest'.

Has anyone else ran into this problem? For now I recommend all shamans to strictly go to Beram or Sagorne to get Elemental Mastery instead and avoid going to Bath'rah directly!

author: Thegr8equalizer
subject: Totem Twisting - Fixing Enhancer part 4/x
content_md:
Totem twisting is a vital part of enhancement gameplay and a very fun game mechanic.
The current situation makes it very mana intensive to totem twist while mostly gimping enhancement dps without providing much of anything else for themselves to compensate. The idea is to allow enhancement shamans to totem twist and rip the benefits of iit.

Taking into consideration the shortcomings of enha dps itemisation and the lack of mana sustain this is the talent I have come with.

Totemic Current - 5 Row - Requires 20 points in Enha tree - 3 talent points: "Whenever you have an air totem, an earth totem, a fire totem, and a water totem active at the same time, you gain a 10 sec buff that  gives you 40/80/120 spell power and 3%/6%/9% spell crit and hit.You also regen 10%/20%/30% of your base mana in 10 sec (this has a 20 sec ICD),the buff will be reapply upon summoning another 4th totem and will instantly cancel upon casting non-instant spells"

Promote totem twist gameplay, while providing mana sustain mechanic to support the heavy mana usage of totems and giving a good buff to promote spellhance gameplay without creating issue if ele/resto try to cheese it because of the non-instant spell rule.

The values are placeholder and could be change :)

Tell me what you all think about it! If you like it, if you think it's useless or need some tweaks!

source: [Vanilla Dev Explains Shaman](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iH7xKE0W7Pc&t=15m56s)

Totem twisting was never a design feature and the original creators tried their best to not make it a thing. They only tolerated it because shamans were not popular picks for raids (outside of healing) and so they allowed it to "get him in the door".

As such, on a server that wants to keep classic design philosophy paramount, I don't think actively encouraging it is the way to go. Now, since shamans are still not first picks for dps it can be left as is for now. I'm with Kairion on this one if there ever will be a fix for shaman totems.

For anyone else interested, that interview also has some amazing insight on enhancement in general.

author: Stinkyjames
subject: Re: Totem Twisting - Fixing Enhancer part 4/x
content_md:
Here is something I was thinking about yesterday to keep from adding buttons to enhancement without doing a major overhaul.

Idea 1
Execute: So either an increased critchance for WF or an increased procchance for WF on targets below 20%
WIffing: When an auto attack outside of WF aura doesnt crit you get a 5% extra chance to proc wf, stacking up to 15% and consumed on next wf

Idea 2
So I was thinking about making enhancement more elemental, making WF baseline instead of a weapon buff, and have the frost/flame/rock weapon enchants interact with how this wf reacts.
Frostbrand: Two extra attacks as frost that reduces the target movement speed
Flametongue: Two extra attacks as fire that increase searing totem damage taken
Rockbiter: Windfury as is, two extra attacks with bonus attackpower

Idea 3
Elemental shields consumed reduce effectiveness by 25% (3 charges 100% - 2 charges 75% - 1 charge 50%) and charges can be generated by getting critical hits with melee and spell. But the final charge does not deplete until the duration of the buff is over.

I dont think enhancement really needs a boost in damage, but more a boost in damage output through mana consumption and or regeneration Reducing enhancement shock cost and totem cost by a baseline %.

I have no idea how to handle the spellhit issues, perhaps mirror enhancement melee hit to spellhit, but there are smarter folks out there with better ideas.

author: Original3
subject: Earth Shield and Wind Shear
content_md:
Here are suggestions for 2 spells I would add to make Shaman tank more vaible and still not Overpowered, please give me feedback and help adress it to Developers, so the suggestion may come true!

 **EARTH SHIELD**
 *Requires level 60*

 *250 mana*
 *30 sec cooldown*

The caster is surrounded with an earthen shield, increasing Defense skill by 20% and causing attacks to heal the Shaman for 20% of the total damage done. This effect can only occur once every few seconds. 3 charges. Lasts 10 min. Only one elemental shield can be active on the Shaman at any one time."

Idea of this spell is to give Shaman tanks crush immunity.
Don't forget, that we cannot use plate gear and our stamina pool is very limited, since we don't have powerful tier sets with big loads of stamina, like warriors do. This makes us very squishy and some bosses are just a no-no for shaman tanks, cause their crit could delete us from the world.
What this spell does is, that you lower the Defense cap from items from 140 to 67. I find this very fair, cause we don't have access to non-tier plate items with defense, such as Helm of Domination or Pauldrons of the Unrelenting.
I also think the ability isn't super OP, but you can make some CD,mana cost or duration changes to balance it a bit.
It also makes Shaman tank gearing more flavourful, 'cause now it's just stacking armor, health and dodge.

 **WIND SHEAR**
Requires level 60

 *150 mana*
 *8 sec cooldown*

Hits target with the power of wind increasing time between their attacks by 5%. Stacking up 3 times. Causes additional threat.

I am shaman tanking on Turtle WoW for a longer time already and I see our threat generation as very solid one. At least with similar geared dps.
The problem appeared, when I was supposed to hold threat against naxxramas geared players and it was very challenging.
Warriors deal with this problem very easily, they can just dual wield instead of equiping a shield and therefore increase their threat generation by a lot.
Druids can equip Manual Crowd Pummeler, which icreases their TPS by 30%-ish.

Having another threat generating ability on shamans is therefore a big Quality of Life. Also, the attack speed reduction makes us more tanky.

These two changes can make Shaman a competetive raid tank, who is still not overpowered, is uniqe in its own way and still cannot kick off warriors or druids of their throne.

Same reason Paladin tanks are great for the extra blessing, judgement and aura.

author: Original3
subject: Re: Earth Shield and Wind Shear
content_md:
When it comes to Earth Shield Defense bonus, we forget about one important thing - scaling with gear.

Warriors scale good with gear because their tier sets are very strong.
Druids scale good with gear because of bear form armor rating.
Paladins scale good with gear because of good Spell power coefficients.

Also, keep in mind that first boss you need crit immunity to is Chromaggus. By the time your guild reaches him, you might already have 67 defense rating.

Look at this pieces you can obtain without entering a raid:
Helm of the Great Chief (6), Evil Eye Pendant (7), Redoubt Cloak (7), Enchant Bracer - Deflection (3), Draconian Deflector (10), Naglering (5), Force of Will (7).

With this gear and Earth Shield active you can get 414 defense rating.
With better gear (like MC and BWL) you can achieve 440 without any issue.

Another thing I want to mention is the lore part of the elements, and how shamans use them.
Fire/Lightning - magical damage to hurt your enemies
Wind - imbuing the weapon with wind to hit enemy multiple times
Water - healing wounds of your enemies
Earth - protection of yourself and your allies

Last thing I want to mention is, how vanilla makes every spec uniqe in some ways.

Warriors are good in general, best threat generation, best defensive abilities.
Druids have the biggest Health pool and Polymorph immunity.
Paladins are by far the best AoE tanks.

The way I want to see shaman tank is, to be more defensive than threat tank.
We don't need to get taunt or insane threat generating.
I want shaman tank to be best option for bosses that hit hard and/or do high magical damage.

author: Haroone
subject: Enhancement Suggestions
content_md:
Hello, I have a thread for potential changes. These ideas are my own as well as interpretations of other ideas shared already. I like to think things out in hopes it can inspire devs to address some issues enhancement faces, even if it isn't a 1-for-1. For context, I'm a supporter of shaman tanking, but dpsed for raiding. I will also not be suggesting overall system changes like adjusting mob stats, although that has been talked about quite a bit.

 1. Stormstrike being a buff instead of de-buff and increasing initial damage for any shocks. This would allow DPS to use Flame and Frost Shock with Stormstrike without worrying about additional threat generation.

 2. Get rid of Thunderhead. I don't believe other class tanks need additional assistance with aoe threat with the current spells and talents of other classes already and would realistically only be used at the start of pulls unless, a shaman really wants to waste mana throughout a fight continually casting it. I feel class utility can be capitalized in other areas of their kit. It also doesn't address any issues Resto or Elemental had prior to the change.

 3. Add a talent to the second-last row of Enhancement Talents to add spell hit % equal to physical hit %. I feel there should still be value in spell hit gear, but would help shocks and lightning spells land to make up for needing to prioritizing physical hit and itemization not being much of an option with both. This would also give variety at the end of the tree and could be a choice tanks can leverage for the Earth Shock being the closest to Taunt that they have.

 4. Replace the Windwall and Grounding totem bonuses in the "Guardian Totems" talent with a temporary bonus to Stoneskin Totem for the casting Shaman to add additional resistance for Shaman tanking without adding an extra button and move the talent lower in the tree to prevent Resto and Elemental from getting unintended resistances.

 5. Add 1 mp5 per talent point to the Ancestral Knowledge talent as the 5% Mana alone, does not do enough to address Shaman Mana issues. This would at least help, but would not fully resolve the issue. It's also high enough in the tree that it is accessible without much investment for other specs.

 6. Flametongue Weapon Totem doesn't see much use due to WF being so prominent and the overall better option. Change Flametongue Totem to add bonus spell power instead of current fire damage. This would add a benefit for Elemental and Resto Shaman to be in caster groups.

 7. Itemization needs some tweaks so Shaman don't need every stat under the sun. I can't think of ways to update this without overhauling how Shaman gain effects from stats (mana from Intellect, attack power from Agility) or creating very specific items that would have useless stats like Intellect or spell power if a Warrior or Hunter used it. Maybe converting a portion of Agility into block instead of strength? Trying to keep from major system changes and focus on current talents and spells.

 8. Adding an ability that works similar to judgement, but use the weapon enchantment to augment the next auto-attack like Heroic Strike.
Rockbiter - aoe radius like cleave to hit multiple targets for 75% physical damage, but threat-boosted.
Flametongue - increased damage scaling with spellpower like Flametongue Weapon on the next auto-attack, but the entire damage is fire damage instead of physical with additional fire damage.
Frostbrand - similar to Flametongue, but less damage scaling, uses Frost magic, and is a guaranteed Frostbrand slow proc.
content_html:
Hello, I have a thread for potential changes. These ideas are my own as well as interpretations of other ideas shared already. I like to think things out in hopes it can inspire devs to address some issues enhancement faces, even if it isn't a 1-for-1. For context, I'm a supporter of shaman tanking, but dpsed for raiding. I will also not be suggesting overall system changes like adjusting mob stats, although that has been talked about quite a bit.

1. Stormstrike being a buff instead of de-buff and increasing initial damage for any shocks. This would allow DPS to use Flame and Frost Shock with Stormstrike without worrying about additional threat generation.

2. Get rid of Thunderhead. I don't believe other class tanks need additional assistance with aoe threat with the current spells and talents of other classes already and would realistically only be used at the start of pulls unless, a shaman really wants to waste mana throughout a fight continually casting it. I feel class utility can be capitalized in other areas of their kit. It also doesn't address any issues Resto or Elemental had prior to the change.

3. Add a talent to the second-last row of Enhancement Talents to add spell hit % equal to physical hit %. I feel there should still be value in spell hit gear, but would help shocks and lightning spells land to make up for needing to prioritizing physical hit and itemization not being much of an option with both. This would also give variety at the end of the tree and could be a choice tanks can leverage for the Earth Shock being the closest to Taunt that they have.

4. Replace the Windwall and Grounding totem bonuses in the "Guardian Totems" talent with a temporary bonus to Stoneskin Totem for the casting Shaman to add additional resistance for Shaman tanking without adding an extra button and move the talent lower in the tree to prevent Resto and Elemental from getting unintended resistances.

5. Add 1 mp5 per talent point to the Ancestral Knowledge talent as the 5% Mana alone, does not do enough to address Shaman Mana issues. This would at least help, but would not fully resolve the issue. It's also high enough in the tree that it is accessible without much investment for other specs.

6. Flametongue Weapon Totem doesn't see much use due to WF being so prominent and the overall better option. Change Flametongue Totem to add bonus spell power instead of current fire damage. This would add a benefit for Elemental and Resto Shaman to be in caster groups.

7. Itemization needs some tweaks so Shaman don't need every stat under the sun. I can't think of ways to update this without overhauling how Shaman gain effects from stats (mana from Intellect, attack power from Agility) or creating very specific items that would have useless stats like Intellect or spell power if a Warrior or Hunter used it. Maybe converting a portion of Agility into block instead of strength? Trying to keep from major system changes and focus on current talents and spells.

8. Adding an ability that works similar to judgement, but use the weapon enchantment to augment the next auto-attack like Heroic Strike.
Rockbiter - aoe radius like cleave to hit multiple targets for 75% physical damage, but threat-boosted.
Flametongue - increased damage scaling with spellpower like Flametongue Weapon on the next auto-attack, but the entire damage is fire damage instead of physical with additional fire damage.
Frostbrand - similar to Flametongue, but less damage scaling, uses Frost magic, and is a guaranteed Frostbrand slow proc.

content_md:
> **Haroone wrote: Mon Mar 20, 2023 6:40 pm**
> The 5mp5 added to Intellect is due to the high Mana costs shaman have for their spells in general and it's the first tier of the tree to make it more accessible without large investment. I don't think it ruins balance and would have much impact.

 5mp5 isn't very much at all no, either at 60 or at 14. My point is though that if you take Blessing of Wisdom as an example, it gradually builds up to 33mp5 at 60. 5mp5 is just a pitiful amount. But since it's a static feature of a talent, you can't have 33mp5 at level 14 because it is just a must have talent. I don't think it can be balanced well.

Regarding Resto and Ele taking a %int talent, Eles give up the Tidal Mastery crit chance in the resto tree, and the chance to get Nature's Swiftness if they chose to go for the %int, which is a perfectly fine tradeoff if they so choose. It doesn't really matter if Restos take the int since their damage isn't an issue.

At the end of the day, Shamans are multiple attribute dependant. You can't get around that fact. Lightning and Shocks are a big part of the Shaman PvE gameplay that just get resisted because Shamans cant get that much spell hit, let alone Enhance afford to get that much spell hit. Most other caster specs have a +10% hit talent so they only then need to worry about a further 6~7%. It's asking too much of a Shaman to gear for physical dps, spell dps and mana for longevity, all without the aid that other casters get from their talents. I don't believe there are any talents that convert regular hit into spell hit, nor say str into int, so I'd rather stick to what other classes have in their trees for the most part rather than creating a new type.

Trading the Concussion talent for a 10% spell hit is a 5% PvP damage nerf for a ~5% PvE dps increase that helps both Ele and Enh actually use their kit. Having Nature's Guidance on top of that might be a bit too good for Ele PvE, but they still have massive mana problems to contend with vs regular casters so it seems like less of an issue than Enh dreading wasting mana on Shocks.

Dual wield is clearly massively altering Shamans identity. It is a clear departure from Classic and alignment with TBC. That would imho be a massive fail flavorwise. But there are more practical reasons why shaman shouldn't get dualwield

 1. Dualwield itself doesn't solve a DPS problem. Shaman as a class is already needing too many stats to be useful. Requiring a massive increase to Hitchance from gear on top of everything. And if you add support talents for dualwield, you might as well just add equivalent talents for twohander playstile instead.

 2. Anyone who's ever been raiding knows that one handed weapons are much more contested in the lootpool as is. Turning one of the few classes who uses two handers to one handers just makes one handed weapons even more contested while leaving twohanders even less desirable

 3. Stormstrike and Rockbiter in their classic iteration would have to be changed to their TBC version to work with dual wield. The former only hitting with one weapon gets much worse when dualwielding and the latter gives you flat attackpower, applying to both weapons.

 4. Even if all these issues are addressed by copying TBC you are still just an autoattackbot with no mana and no spellhit. So while it helps with the DPS, the gameplay will be as scuffed as ever. Minus the fun of occasionally blowing someone up with WF crits

2. Anyone who's ever been raiding knows that one handed weapons are much more contested in the lootpool as is. Turning one of the few classes who uses two handers to one handers just makes one handed weapons even more contested while leaving twohanders even less desirable

3. Stormstrike and Rockbiter in their classic iteration would have to be changed to their TBC version to work with dual wield. The former only hitting with one weapon gets much worse when dualwielding and the latter gives you flat attackpower, applying to both weapons.

4. Even if all these issues are addressed by copying TBC you are still just an autoattackbot with no mana and no spellhit. So while it helps with the DPS, the gameplay will be as scuffed as ever. Minus the fun of occasionally blowing someone up with WF crits

author: Beefchalupa3
subject: Suggestions on buffing Elemental PvE without making it too strong in PvP
content_md:
So, elemental is clearly great in pvp already, but it's lackluster in pve for a few reasons, primarily for two reasons:
1. mana inefficiency
2. lack of nature resistance reduction
For mana inefficiency, I think it's pretty straightforward. But you could fix it through talents or just a straight mana cost reduction. I think the clearcasting talent reducing the next 2 casts by 40% is strange, it could easily be 50% or 60% instead.

Now, the second point is interesting because we now know from Blizzard classic that endgames bosses actually had just 23 nature resistance. Turtle's values simply being overtuned and not blizz-like are a massive nerf to elemental shaman. That being said, the common suggestion of adding nature resistance reduction to curse of elements would be a great alternative.

Instead of adding more utility to Warlocks though, here are my suggestions of potential new talents and other changes to the elemental tree:

Rolling Thunder (0/3): Your Lightning and Chain Lightning reduce your target's Nature Resistance by 5/10/15 for 15 seconds. Stacks up to 5 times. (This could also just be 1 point at 15 resistance reduction, since it's so late in the tree).

Similar to a Priest's Shadow Weaving talent, this will apply a stacking debuff to the target. I think this stacking buff is the best way to go about this change, because this will increase PvE effectiveness while not affecting PvP much, where it's all about burst and a slow stacking debuff like this will never really be useful. More importantly, this will give exactly 75 nature resistance reduction, the same amount as curse of elements gives.

(alternatively, this could provide a personal BUFF to the player that increases their own spell penetration for 15 seconds, to make sure it doesn't affect anyone else, or have a situation where just 1 shaman is forced to take this talent for the rest of the raid).

In order to fit this talent into the tree, I propose this: Move Lightning Mastery up 1 or 2 spots on the tree. It never made much sense getting cast time reduction so late anyways. Then, slot in Rolling Thunder where Lightning Mastery used to be, and make Lightning Mastery a prerequisite. Finally, we should condense some talents similar to what was done to druid talents like natural weapons and some feral talents, where they got 5 pointers reduced into 3 pointers.

Recommendations on condensing and streamlining the talent tree:

Reverberation:  Getting only 0.2 second off cd per point just feels bad, even though it's quite a decent talent. It kind of feels bad to put points in, I think this could be condensed into 3 points at 0.33 seconds each.

Call of Thunder: I actually think this talent should have its location swapped with Lightning Mastery regardless of any other changes. It makes more sense to get cast time reduction earlier in the leveling process like all other spellcasters do, and then get crit chance later. Because this maxes out at 6% crit, which is weird for 5 points, this could also be condensed into 3 points at 2% each. This way we have space for adding points into Rolling Thunder. You could also throw in another 6% mana reduction here.

Call of Flame and Improved Fire Totems: I think it would make sense to combine these into one talent, since they are both about fire totems. The fire element in general also seems lackluster, maybe you should add a part of this talent, or baseline, that gives flametongue weapon some useful bonus like 2% spell hit.

I'm not necessarily recommending ALL these changes be made, but I think adding in the nature debuff Rolling Thunder talent, along with 1 or 2 other talent point shrinks would put elemental into a much better place.

Finally, I think all of shamans final talents in every tree are pretty lackluster. Other classes get build-defining, exciting skills and we just get utility stuff. Give us totem of wrath or something, or some kind of cool ability that has to do with the elements.

I think a fire elemental totem would be a very cool addition as the final elemental talent. This would be both flavorful, very lore appropriate, and not affect pvp much because the totem can just be killed instantly by other players. And we need a cool CD to use that isn't just a free crit every couple minutes.

Anyways, just wanted to get the discussion started. I might also make a post about revamping the resto tree, since that tree is so bad that resto shamans will go enhance just to get bloodlust lol.

author: Ninjerk
subject: Re: Suggestions on buffing Elemental PvE without making it too strong in PvP
content_md:
I remember having the idea at some point (either while playing Light's Hope or maybe retail classic TBC) that since Shaman seem to often rely on probability that it would be interesting to have a mechanic that interacted with their various elemental shields. I'm not sure how they would all work, but having an Elemental talent that would increase the number of stacks of water shield downlinked to a talent that would consume a globe and restore the usual amount of mana on spells landed (perhaps only on LB and/or CL).

If the probability and/or amount of mana restored were adjusted appropriately, it could provide some relief in terms of mana efficiency between crits and force the shaman to occasionally change up their rotation to reapply water shield.

Comparing Elemental to other caster specs, much could be done simply and elegantly by provided a flat %-based reduction to enemy resistance a la Elemental Precision or that early Shadow talent for priests.

Other changes could include rebalancing Elemental Fury to be a 5-point talent like Frost mages get and having that 21-point slot be something else (e.g., the water shield talent or move Elemental Mastery up and invent a new 31-point talent).

I agree that getting cast time reduction so late is odd, but I'm guessing it's that deep to make Enhancement and Resto hybrid specs more difficult to turn into dps-lite type things. I think it's possible to meet somewhere in the middle.

Reverberation seems more like something Enhancement would naturally benefit from relatively early in their tree.

I think those are most of my random thoughts from over the years (about Elemental, anyways).

The only reason I can think of, it's to support the raid, but if this was the idea, is it worth it?

Enh already has mana problems on it's own, adding two new abilities on it's rotation isn't going to help either. author: Whoopie
subject: How to fix Shaman's PvE and not break PvP
content_md:
There are some issues with Shamans in PvE, most of which comes down to either sustain damage or mana issues in prolonged fights. Here are some stuff that might help the class feel better and not make them stronger in PvP.

 **1. Water Shield**
 *Water shield is a great addition, but it's mostly for some solo PvE or situational PvP. There is no real use for it in raid settings nor in most PvP situations, where you can kill your target from afar and refill after.*

How to fix it?
Make Water Shield cost 0 mana to not break MP5 rule and add passive mana regen to the shield **OR** make it that you expend one Water Globe from the ability whenever you score a critical hit with Damaging spell, Melee hit or Healing spell, this can only proc every few seconds. In addition, reduce all damage caused by 10% while Water Shield is active. As we all know, damage is not one of Shaman's problem. Mana is. This can balance both worlds without the need to cast downranked spells.

 **2. Earth Shield**
 *Another great addition that needs a Thunderhead-like treatment. Again, there is no use in raids and works only in situational PvP.*

How to fix it?
Create a new Talent in Resto talent tree (Row 6) leading from talent Healing Way (which can be made into 2-point talent anyway) that makes Earth Shield castable on allies with increased Globes (6 or 9 globes). Only one Earth Shield can be active at one time. This will help Shaman healers without making Ele any stronger in PvP and give them some sort of buff on the main tank.

 **3. Bloodlust**
 *This talent is a support ability that you kind of don't want to use on others but somehow have to. It's an ability that makes you feel bad every time you use it. That being said, it has no use in PvP and 10% melee attack speed for a melee build for 20 seconds is useless anyway.*

How to fix it?
Make Bloodlust always proc on Shaman too whenever he uses it on an ally AND make the Shaman receive 10% less damage from all sources while under Bloodlust effect. This fills Shaman's need of "oh sht" button while tanking and can help their easily kitable squishiness in PvP without making them unkillable or too oppresive.

That's all for now.

author: Kairion
subject: Re: mana issues really killing gameplay, solutions?
content_md:
Enhancement can be quite a manahungry spec.

There are a few reasons for this.
 1. Enhancer shamans usually wanna wear gear with strength & Agility, not Intelligence & Spirit. As a result their manapool is comparatively small.
 2. The way mana regeneration works is extremely unkind to shamans. After casting a spell you don't regenerate any mana for 5 seconds (Outside of some classes that have specific talents for that (shaman has none of them)). So if you use shocks on CD you are almost perfectly negating all your manaregeneration.
 3. Shocks are incredibly expensive spells due to both high damage and secondary effects.
 4. You went for Stormstrike first, The elemental tree can reduce the manacost a bit, but you don't have access to it yet and the effect is quite small.

You can remedy the problem in a few ways:
 1. Cast a few spells in rapid succession and then don't cast for a while. This allows your manaregeneration to kick back in. Refrain from using casts to finish someone off as it shuts off your manaregen.
 2. Make heavy use of Stength of the Earth & manaspring totem - they are incredibly good spells if you are near them for the full duration - place them in the area you wanna farm and kite the mobs within range.
 3. Get some gear with spirit - while generally seen as a weak move, while lvling spirit is actually useful, particularly when combined with trick #1
 4. You can eat and drink at the same time. Meaning you need less mana to heal if you also carry food with you.

But at the end of the day Enhancement Shaman is the class/spec with by far the most manastruggles in the entire game

author: Kairion
subject: Re: Stormstrike is a yellow hit and yet does not proc Elemental Devastation
content_md:
Yellow doesnt automatically mean spell.

Stormstrike is a melee based ability, not a spell. As a rule of thumb, if  you can cast it while silenced, its not a spell.

Other abilities in that category are
Heroic strike
Sinister strike
Aimed shot

This is why stormstrike doesnt proc elemental devastation.

Now, I'm not sure if this applies to *Turtle WoW* specifically as there have been a **lot** of modifications done to the software.  For all I know, becoming Neutral with Thunder Bluff, for example, actually *might* let a Human do quests for Thunder Bluff NPCs.  This would **not** apply to other sub-factions, however, such as Orgrimmar, the "Horde Forces" sub-faction some NPCs use, and of course, the PvP sub-factions.  So, this same Human might wander into Thunder Bluff and get destroyed by, say, a Defiler's Den NPC, if they headed to that bluff.

author: Azuredrak0
subject: Re: Shaman Tanks definitely needs some love, and not just because of it...
content_md:
I've been doing Shaman tanking for a while, and yes there are some gaping issues with shaman tanking.  Whether intentional or unintentional, they both prevent Shamen from being main tanks and also add uniqueness and challenge to class tanking.   If I were to summarize the issues in order of importance, it would be the following:

 1. No real taunt
 - not much to be said here.  Earth Shock is great, but it's not a taunt.  Engineering may provide a momentary AOE taunt with Dummies, but it's not a solution.  Shaman "taunting" totem is pretty useless in raid setting.  I think Paladins struggle in this area too.
 2. Poor/challenging gearing options
 - proper gearing is a nightmare.  It's impossible to get good +defense stacking, leaving shamen open to crits.  This leaves  options for stacking as much +Sta and +Dodge/Parry as possible to be able to absorb crits/crushing and avoid regular hits.  At the same time, Mail doesn't provide as much armor as Plate.  To make matters even more interesting, sometimes the best gearing option for the slot is meant for Druid tanks, which means it's leather with even less armor.  Not complaining, but experienced tanks and healers can agree this this setup is challenging to heal.
 3. Poor/challenging AOE threat management
 - totems have their own threat, and they dont' pass it to the shamen.  Best option on AOE pull is Chain Lightning and Engienering Sapper charge, also grenades.  There isn't much in the toolbox outside of reactive damage items/enchants/trinkets.

Some of the best suggestions I've seen that should not require super heavy implementation.
Empower shocks ability - next shock provides an additional effect.  For Earth Shock the effect would be a taunt.  Alternatively, we can always just get a new rank of ES (in a book version) that does same damage but has a taunt component.
Change Guardian Totems talent - add additional effect to Guardian Totems talent to maybe reduce crit chance of enemies to the effected party members.  This would be highly desirable for tanks of all kind that are not Def capped.
Threat from totems transfer to shamen - this would effectively solve for AOE threat generation.

author: Sunflowerdeath1
subject: Re: Shaman Tanks definitely needs some love, and not just because of it...
content_md:
I have tanked as shaman in 60lvl 5 mans and with all changes made to shamans it feels very viable.

Most important change is water shield - it finally gives enough mana and saves from drinking after every pull. And I don't have situations that requires taunt badly. Actually I like more having eartshock, cause it can build threat from distance and interrupts spells. AoE-pulls in 5-man dungeons are probably designed for not very experienced players, so you can do without aoe-aggroing spells, but it definitely would make life much easier.

The hardest part is finding gear for a shaman tank. Having talent for 30% armor from shields helps a lot, considering that mail has less armor than plate. If you compare gear sets for warrior and for shaman, in pre-raid BIS shaman can have around 5.2k hp unbuffed with 6.5k armour, and warrior has same hp, but up to 7.5k armor and slightly higher mitigation. So in first raids such as MC or ZG they can be somewhat comparable. But if you compare end-game BIS its not even close - its possible to get on warrior 7 to 7.5k hp and 10k armor unbuffed, while max for shaman is 6.5k hp and 8k armor and much less mitigation vs crits from bosses. This is main problem that I wish to be adressed by devs.

author: Imonobor
subject: Re: Shaman Tanks definitely needs some love, and not just because of it...
content_md:
Shamans were originally intended to wear plate and to tank with it.
So here's a suggestion that will not sit well with everyone, but I think it will fix a couple of things, especially the gearing options:

Put at the end of the enhancement tree a new talent (or talents) that will reduce all damage done by the shaman by 25%, buff all threat by 35% (to compensate lost damage), make fire totems transfer their threat to the shaman, turns frost shock into a mini-taunt (3-4 sec of forced attacks on shaman) and lets them wear plate. Numbers are ofcourse subject to balancing, but the idea is to make the talent extremely undesirable for DPS shamans, especially in PVP, because having them suddenly wear plate in BGs might break balance a fair bit.

This solves gearing, taunt and AoE threat. Mana might still be an issue, but there is plenty of pala tank gear choices that have int and MP5 on them, so that could help a bit.

Now let me know in how many unforeseen ways this will break the game :D

Water shield - mid fight when going OOM
Earth shield - active cooldown when larger damage spike is coming

 4) shaman was supposed to be the offensive archetype of the hybrid while paladin was supposed to be the defensive archetype, that is why shaman has a caster dps spec while paladin has a tank spec instead.

Please stop spreading nonsense online.

author: Terras
subject: Re: Shaman Tanks definitely needs some love, and not just because of it...
content_md:
I love that some people are looking at this and bouncing around ideas that could make the class more fun. I see the whole thing behind not wanting shamans to be able to tank raids but better than anyone else, but I bet it would still be a benefit overall to at least have them as a decent option. Assuming you're not a part of the "No shaman tanks" camp. I would love to see some sort of mechanic for Shaman Tanks that improves their defenses and aggro as the fight progresses. Let me see if I can present a decent set of ideas below that have functional mechanics and fit the theme of communing with the elements below.

#1. Give lighting shield (LS) a debuff based stacking effect. Let's say that each time a mob takes damage from LS they gain a stack of Static Charge (SC). Now let's have SC give something like the following effect: "For each stack of SC the effected unit has the aggro of lighting-based spells against it increased by X%. For each stack of SC there is an X% chance to restore 1 charge of LS to the target if LS is active. Effect may stack up to X number of times." This would give a chance to have a slow build aggro that is usable with a range of shaman abilities.

#2. Give Earth shield (ES) a buff based stacking effect. For this one we will go with the effect Stubborn Earth (SE). SE would be triggered as normal per ES but have the following effect instead: "For each stack of SE the shaman's armor is increased by X% and their spell resistance is increase by X. For each stack of SE, the shaman regenerates X% of max HP over X seconds. Effect may stack up to X number of times."

#3. Give Water Shield (WS) a buff based stacking effect. First, I would remove the charge effect from WS and make it more like an aura while keeping it exclusive against LS and ES. Next, I would give it the effect Ebb and Flow (EF) which would be as follows: "While WS is active the shaman gains 1 stack of EF every X seconds up to X number of times. For each stack of EF, the shaman receives X mana every X seconds. Each time the shaman casts a spell they lose all stacks of EF."

#4. Give the shaman a skill/talent at around lvl 50 that makes them immune to crit/crushing blows from mobs while they have a shield equipped in their off hand and any of their shield spells active.

TL:DR
I would love the shaman to have abilities that tied into the concept of communing with elements while they fight. The longer they commune with an element the better the effects and to get the greatest benefit they have to learn to balance communing with the different options effectively like the warrior class has traditionally done with the stance dance.

That's what I've got. I don't claim to be a shaman expert and I hope that I've added to the conversation with taking from anyone else.

content_md:
I've been thinking about Bloodlust as a channeled AoE buff for the party, BUT allowing the Shaman to still be able to move and use melee attacks. Any spells cast would break the channeling. This would firstly dissuade Restos from taking it, but secondly also allow the Shaman themselves to benefit.

The numbers would have to be toned down but I think it would lead to some interesting gameplay as you'd have to think about the timing more, so as not to lose duration on the channel from stray hits.

I don't believe there is anything like this in vanilla, but it isn't too far away from the new Decisive Strike implementation, and is a bit more involved support gameplay wise than simply throwing a buff on someone. Most of all though it just sounds interesting and fun to me.

Thoughts?

author: Kairion
subject: Re: Reworking Lightning Shield
content_md:
Thunderhead is conceptually a great talent, it allows you to deal a bunch of damage while generating threat for someone else. Shaman despite not being a great DPS has threat problems, so it fits the bill of allowing him to do more damage without ripping threat and buffs your tanks abilities in a group.

That being said, lightning shield is prohibitively expensive to cast. Its high spellscaling means you can get some use out of spaming lower ranks on a paladin tank, but with a Warrior or Druid tank who doesn't typically have spelldamage statted, it is just horrible.

Lightning shield is a conditional spell. The person with lightning shield needs to be hit for it to proc, and only one proc can occur every 2 seconds. It can't crit either. So i would strongly suggest heavily reducing the manacost of the spell either baseline or with the improved lightning shield talent (which currently is horrible as is)

Another option to consider would be letting Elemental focus apply on LS. Its an elemental spell, but for some reason it is not considered offensive and therefore doesn't get the cost reduction. Damage comparison between earthshock and LS truely make LS look horrible when considering Elemental Focus & Conviction lowering earthshocks manacost to 225 mana for 517 - 546 dmg (2.36 dmg per mana) while the conditional shield with no additional effects and 4 talent points exclusively buffing itself dealing 683 dmg for 296 mana (2.3 dmg per mana).
