author: Akos1896
subject: Shaman change ideas - long
content_md:
Hey guys!

Note from later: the 3 builds I was talking about were ele, enh and resto. Did not cover resto going deep into enh for additional bloodlust.

I wanna share with you how I'd change the shaman builds to make them more viable without giving them the paladin treatment. I might be wrong, this is a personal take.

My problem with the builds is the following:
 * Ele is mostly a PVP build which suffers in PVE. Very mana dependent and easy to oom. Usually outshadowed by mages.
 * Enhance is mostly sought by guilds having a strong melee core who really wanna bloodlust at bosses. Suffers both in PVE and in PVP. Has no real crowd control or escape mechanism and this hits really hard considering they don't have plate armor.
 * Resto is mostly fine, chain heal is OP. Resto shaman is in raids (mostly) to chain heal and set up wf totems for melee.

I think the main problem lies in how the shaman class is designed. The class is 60% utility and 40% anything else. They can be healers, melee and rdps but they should not be as good in these roles as classes with less utility because their added value would make them too OP in comparison. For example an enhance shaman should never be as good as a rogue as a melee dps because the shaman provides many additional tools for the group which the rogues do not.
If both of them had the same dps prowess, enhancement shaman would be an objectively better class because of versatility.
In my opinion the core of the problem is that shamans have to be made viable without making them equal in power level to classes which have much less utility.
Of course mages are vendors, they decurse, crowd control and port, warlocks give hs, ss, summon, aoe, fear, banish but a shaman gameplay mostly revolves around these utilities even if you play as a melee.
Poison cleansing, disease cleansing, redirecting spells, kiting, damage reduction, team buff, slow mana refill, purging and healing even if you are on paper a melee guy.
Shaman utility is based on versatility and they are expected to support the team if any of the situations arise for which they have a tool. Shamans have a tool for most situations.
This is another point I'd slightly change, making some talents considerably stronger or weaker in performing certain utility stuff. This can help shamans focus more on their actual on paper role like dps or healer and
this could make the need towards different shaman builds more prevalent among guilds. Now if a guild is at least somewhat serious it's go resto or go home unless they really love bloodlust.
I wanna offer some changes which would in my opinion make all 3 main build desirable while they would all be filling different niches.

What I'd change

Enhancement
I'd start the buffs with a nerf. In my opinion base wf totem should be much weaker while improved wf should be as strong as it is today. This would mean that guilds would actually want enhancement shamans if they want
real wf buffs.
In turn I'd give enhancement shamans an efficient crowd control ability (you can't expect the mail gear guy to rely on frost shock, earthbind totem and prayers when it's time to run against a bunch of enemies). This would add survavibility.
A mass fear, a mass stun, a sleep effect or just making the shaman much faster for 10 sec to run away (even indoors), I don't know. The point is to give them an oh shít button because their gear is not strong enough to warrior they way out of a really bad pull. Ancestral guardian talent is useful but not enough.
I'd take away ancestral knowledge from their talent tree and put it to ele (later explaining, why).
I'd put elemental devastation in enhancement talent tree but slightly reworked because enhancement has much less probability to spell crit. Might link the melee crit increase to having less than a certain percentage of your life.
I'd also add a stun chance for improved lightning shield procs to further improve enhancement shamans a bit (maybe 10% stun chance per proc, stun lasts to 2 sec). This would also make thunderhead better since enhancement shamans could give stune chance to tanks.
These changes would free up 2 additional talent points in the enhancement tree where the crowd control ability could be inserted.
I'd integrate nature guidance's 3x1% melee hit into thundering strikes talent (I'd remove guidance from the resto tree). Since this talents has 5 levels, I'd add 0,6% plus hit chance per level.

This wh nerf would ensure that enhancement shamans are sought after in guilds. Passive +melee crit at low health would add a bit of power to them while the crowd control spell would give much desired survivability to them.
In my opinion an enhancement shaman would still perform worse than a rogue as a dps but his added utilities would balance things out and would make enh a valid pick. Specially since real wf would only come from them, no more
resto shaman wf spamming. The idea that we take one build and expect it to bring everything good a shaman can (except bloodlust or even with bloodlust in case of enh+resto hybrid which in reality almost only has healing roles) has narrowed down things too much leading to resto or nothing ways of thinking by guilds.

Elemental
Elemental is in an interesting spot. They are very good at PVP but at PVE there are problems. Mana problems. Randomly stopping dps and starting to chain heal to make people survive then having to explain why dps was so low.
The main problem here I think is the tidal mastery talent. You are kinda forced to go 21 talents deep in resto to be a good ele. This is not a problem now because a lot of elemental talents are kinda irrelevant (like elemental devastation
from earlier). But if you wanna make the ele talent tree more interesting you have to make tidal mastery go up in the resto talent tree making it easier to obtain. Let it switch places with healing focus freeing up a bunch of ele talent points then make the tree a bit more interesting! Elemental devastation was already taken out and ancestral knowledge was brought in. Delete earth's grasp (spread it's bonuses alongside the enhancement tree for slight enh buff) and we are at balance for now.
Instead of improved fire totems give ele shamans either two spell penetration talents or two talents for passive mana regen. At the same time I'd include shocks in the storm reach talent so that ele can use most of its offensive arsenal without any awkward repositioning.
I'd change flametongue totem, too.
Melee enhance is an enhancement shaman's job and improved wf will always be the number one choice for that. Flametongue totem currently lives in a world which has no place for it.
I've read it somewhere and agree that it should be changed to a spell damage totem. To remain consistent, flamestrike weapon could add a stackable spell damage buff for your next spell after each melee hit (would help
enhancement shamans with their shocks). With a limit of course, let's say max stack is 5. Flamestrike totem could be improved via call of flame talent. All shamans could add a bit of party-wide spell damage but only ele flamtongue totem would actually make a real difference (don't make the added spell damage too big but make it considerable).
This would help ele a lot. No need for all those resto talents (healing should be rarely their job anyway, only in emergencies). In exchange more mana, added mana regen or spell penetration and guilds would look for ele shamans to buff their casting party. What wf is for the enhancement melee group, the same could be flametongue (almost) to a caster group.
I'd also integrate nature guidance's  3x1% spell hit to call of thunder (guidance would be removed from resto tree). Since this talent has 5 levels, I'd add 0,6% plus hit chance per level.
I think ele shamans should not outperform mages. If they stay slightly below them, balance is reached because they add more extra utility to the group.

Resto
I promised to explain why I'd put ancestral knowledge to ele and not resto. My way of thinking is the following: resto is usually needed for chain heals and wf besides the usual utility. Without wf they need some kind of rebalancing which is even more important because resto is currently the only well-balanced shaman build in my opinion. If we take away wf, we have to give something. My take is health and mana regen. A potent mana regen totem would make up for the lack of ancestral knowledge at resto tree.
I'd change for resto the following: make restorative totems give a much higher buff for mana and life totem. Everyone could use the base ones like now but improved mana totem would have much higher restorative abilities.
I'd also buff mana tide. Make it 3 minute cd and slightly higher mana output.
There's also a nerf I'd add here which could help resto being more distinguished from non-resto builds. I'd change healing wave and chain heal base casting time to 3,5 sec instead of 3 sec. In exchange improved healing wave talent would reduce 1 sec instead of 0,5 sec if all talents are spent there. I'd put the talent a bit deeper into the tree but not much deeper. I want to make a build talent sacrifices to get this talent but if it is put too deeply, resto shaman leveling is seriously harmed. I think resto should be able to learn improved healing wave 5/5 until early level 20s. This way we'd define the different shaman builds' utility a bit better. Builds not visiting the resto tree deep enough could mostly operate with lesser healing waves in an emergency situation because chain heals would be too slow. DPS shamans without resto talents would be less expected to become near perfect healers in a sec but they could still help in (ineffectively) if it is really needed.
I'd remove nature's guidance from the resto tree and would increase the base cooldown of cure disease and cure poison from 1,5s to 3s. Then I'd a 3 part talent to the resto tree, each one decreasing cure desease and cure poison cooldown by one second, making it an instant cast if the talent is fully learned. This can further differentiate the resto build from the others and would make resto better in one specific utility. In a raid if a party doesn't have a shaman for cleaning totem, enh and ele can still help in the poison or disease clearing but this would be suboptimal in case of a mass poisoning or mass disease. This would change resto shamans from the wf+chain heal guys into a chain heal guy with good mana+health regen totems who is a specialist in raidwide poison and disease removal.
As said before, I'd also integrate nature guidance's 3x1% melee hit into thundering strikes talent and 3x1% spell hit to call of thunder. Since these talents have 5 levels, I'd add 0,6% plus hit chance per level.

With these changes each build would be (in my opinion) viable without being overpowered and each build would be seeked by guilds for different reasons.

Other things I'd consider to change:
 * Give stoneclaw totem a bit more HP.
 * Give (not improved) healing stream a bit better healing abilities. Highest version of it would become a meme among rank 20 players as it stands.
 * Slightly buff windwall totem because noone is using it.
 * Make searing totems cast fire 1,5x faster and possibly make their damage a bit lower. They are there partially for damage dealing but mostly to ping casters. If you ping them quicker, spellcasting would take even more time.
 * I am unsure how to nerf base wf but an idea: wf totem still grants the extra attack with the same success rate but instead of giving extra attack power to it, the extra attack would damage 1/2 as much as the melee character's normal hit.
__________

The differences I think this would make:
Elemental
Less emphasis on healing or mass poison/disease clearance. Buffing casters including itself instead of wf spam. Larger mana pool, shocks are easier to use. More focus on doing actual dps work, would do additional things like being a healer less often because of the nerfs. More oriented into the caster dps direction. Welcome by guilds wanting to buff caster parties. Less oom. Can't really support a melee party anymore and would make a bad healer by himself.

Restoration
Minimal emphasis on wf, mostly seeked by healer/caster groups. Clear role in disease and poison cleansing, providing extra mana making its caster group oom later, including himself. Life regen totem would almost feel like a renew almost giving the resto shaman a heal over time ability, too.

Enhancement
More survivability, added crit chance at lower health and a new form of utility with thunderhead. Less emphasis on healing (emergency only). Clear choice for guilds wanting a wf totem.

They can be healers, melee and rdps but they should not be as good in these roles as classes with less utility because their added value would make them too OP in comparison. For example an enhance shaman should never be as good as a rogue as a melee dps because the shaman provides many additional tools for the group which the rogues do not.

Of course mages are vendors, they decurse, crowd control and port, warlocks give hs, ss, summon, aoe, fear, banish but a shaman gameplay mostly revolves around these utilities even if you play as a melee.
Poison cleansing, disease cleansing, redirecting spells, kiting, damage reduction, team buff, slow mana refill, purging and healing even if you are on paper a melee guy.
Shaman utility is based on versatility and they are expected to support the team if any of the situations arise for which they have a tool. Shamans have a tool for most situations.
This is another point I'd slightly change, making some talents considerably stronger or weaker in performing certain utility stuff. This can help shamans focus more on their actual on paper role like dps or healer and

real wf buffs.
In turn I'd give enhancement shamans an efficient crowd control ability (you can't expect the mail gear guy to rely on frost shock, earthbind totem and prayers when it's time to run against a bunch of enemies). This would add survavibility.
A mass fear, a mass stun, a sleep effect or just making the shaman much faster for 10 sec to run away (even indoors), I don't know. The point is to give them an oh shít button because their gear is not strong enough to warrior they way out of a really bad pull. Ancestral guardian talent is useful but not enough.

author: Blondboombox
subject: Shaman Class Identity
content_md:
I've been doing a good amount of reading about Shamans as well as playing them extensively, mostly Enhancement. They're an incredible support class with huge amounts of versatility and utility. I think fundamentally the thing that needs to be changed is how Shamans inherently lose personal buffs, dps, survivability at the cost of their support ability. Ex. Bloodlust not being cast on shaman in addition to party target, WF totem being useless to the shaman personally at the expense of not having Grace of Air or Grounding, and of course Thunderhead, storm strike applying a debuff which can be triggered by party members nature damage.

Things id love to see as fixes for this, (besides better scaling) provide additional personal buffs to the shaman. Thunder head should at least make it castable on yourself AND a party member, same with Lust, Stormstrike should be a personal buff instead of a debuff, Flametongue and WF totems could apply an increased personal buff to the shaman, Grace of Air and Strength of Earth could provide increased AGI and STR to the shaman.

Shamans identity as a support isn't one i want fundamentally changed, but instead be able to be singularly capable instead having to sacrifice so heavily to provide for party or raid scenarios.

author: Ryo3000
subject: Enhancement Talents Suggestion
content_md:
I was thinking a bit about the whole debate on suggestion about Enhancement buffs from dual wielding to outright buffs to Enhancement as a whole (which wouldn't be bad at all if that's the way it goes)

But there's a lot of room for improvement on Shaman's skill tree without necessarily just changing the class identity (like dual wielding)

First reworking "Improved Lightning Shield" to

"Improve Elemental Shield"
Increases the effects of your Lightning Shield, Water Shield and Earth Shield by 5/10/15%

 15% more mana from water shield and 15% more healing from earth shield help every shaman across the board

Then replace thunderhead, it's a fun idea but it doesn't really work.
You get all the aggro from the damage, can't use it on tank if they're alliance and it's a bit bugged because you can use it to override other shamans elemental shields, even if they're better than the lightning shield you're casting.

We keep the pre-req of level 3 "Improved Elemental Shield" but replace the effect with something that Shamans kinda need, mana regen

"Storm's Attunement"
While you have an elemental shield on, critical effects from spells and melee attacks restore 1% of your maximum mana.

And for Enhancement Capstone

"Aftershock"
Whenever you use a shock spell increases the attack speed of your next attack by 100%.

I really believe these changes would help the class without fundamentally changing it, the focus is still on crit effects and the class really want those heavy weapons for Aftershock, still useful for the team of course but they're more meaningful than just dropping totems.

What do yall think of the ideas, good? Bad? Too strong? Too weak?

Water shield  3 - 155 mana 3x80 240 (3x92 276)* mana

author: Mativh
subject: Spirit Plant Brews | A New Shaman Class System
content_md:
Shamans have various interesting class systems, like the Totems.
I propose an additional one, that could be used to deliver changes/fixes, as well as flesh out further the unique differences depending on the race of choice;

That system is **Spirit Plants**

An ability Shamans would be able to level as a class profession, akin to the Rogue Poisons, and it'd allow them to make mind-altering entheogenic brews from spiritual plants and mushrooms, like Shamans have been doing since forever in real life in all cultures.
In fact it has always been an integral part of Shamanism.

The plant/mushroom ingredients could be picked by Shamans in the world or by all herbalists.
 *(or sold at vendors, but profession-class interaction is good for immersion and economy, poison reagents should also be coming from herbalists/rogues picking them instead of an NPC vendor)*

There would be brews that'd be race-specific.

 **Orc Shamans**

Drinking a brew from spirit plants that facilitates the communion with the spirits of the elements. The Orc peers beyond the Elemental Plane, gleaning visions of an ancient past where manifestations of volatile energies once raged unimpeded across primordial Azeroth deepen the Shamans connection to the Spirits, reducing temporarily the mana cost of Elemental spells.
(making Elemental tree at long last considerable for levelling compared to Enha)

Enhancement Shamans concocting potions from spirit mushrooms, fueling these ferocious elemental-powered fighters into a blood-chilling frenzy, making Enhancement better dps/tank. It could be given also to other melee classes by fellow shamans, most fitting would of course be fury warriors.

 **Tauren Shamans**

Drinking a brew from an entheogenic cactus that could be found mainly in Barrens either by herbalists or only pickable by Tauren Shamans, allowing them to commune with their ancestors, inspired by
[spirit plants used by native north american shamans.](https://www.notesfromthefrontier.com/post/hallucinogens-native-american-spirituality)
They'd assume temporarily:
Ethereal Form
an ability of Spirit Walkers from Warcraft 3
![Image](https://i.ibb.co/0sn8TVQ/BTNEthereal-Form-On.png)
Turns the Tauren Shaman ethereal, makes him unable to attack, reduces physical damage taken but increases magical damage taken by x%.

Tauren Druids are, unlike Night Elven Druids, in contact with Shamanism and used to be Shamans before learning about Druidism from the Night Elves, they could have a racial ability allowing them to drink a brew made by fellow Restoration Shaman players from a [sacred vine](https://medium.com/@SandeepPrakash/dreams-are-nature-nature-is-eternal-jung-and-individuation-in-light-of-ayahuasca-shamanism-8dc22347fdc6), facilitating them to enter into the Emerald Dream. It'd explain why they could keep up with the much more experienced Night Elf Druids.

 **Troll Shamans**

That are Witch Doctors (there is always a cauldron near one) making brews that'd require also macabre non-plant ingredients, allowing them to deal (Shadow) Voodoo magic damage, apart from elemental.

Zuvembi brew is arguably a witch doctor's most insidious concoction. Driven by the cauldron master's strength of mind, Zuvembi brew takes the will of those who breathe its fumes. It makes them compliant and easily manipulated. It is low magic, relying upon ancient cantrips and recipes known only to witch doctors of a certain skill. The witch doctor can add drops of the Zuvembi brew to any potion. The brew creates a powerful suggestive state in the imbiber that he can trigger and control. After drinking a Zuvembi brew potion, the imbiber can be dominated by the witch doctor.

The arts of the witch doctors originated with the trolls, and they make up the vast majority of those who practice these arts. Some of these witch doctors have agreed to take on the occasional non-troll apprentice, usually from among the orcs.

The witch doctor is an alchemical and spiritual master, skilled at not only simply brewing potions and alchemical goods, but at awakening the spirits of the ingredients that go into his goods. A witch doctor at work can be unsettling, for he croons and chants to the herbs and animal parts that go into his brew, shaking a rattle to awaken them from their slumber, and sometimes even bursting into dance to appease them and make them favor him.

The witch doctor's seething cauldron contains a hallucinogenic mixture of herbs, poisons, crushed insects and other noxious materials. He may add drops of this Shaka brew to improve the efficiency of any potion or alchemical item he creates. The Shaka brew maximizes all variable, numeric effects of the witch doctor's potions or alchemical creations. Drinking a potion treated with the Shaka brew leaves the imbiber with a euphoric buzz. The Bambe brew is a secret recipe that extendes the effectiveness of magical potions. Drinking Bambe brew potions leaves the imbiber with a faint crawling sensation over their skin.

Troll Priests could be given a brew from fellow Troll Shamans that'd allow them to commune with the Loa and temporarily shapeshift like Troll Loa worshippers do.

Feel free to suggest more entheogenic shaman brews made from Spirit plants.
I'll later add more examples for potentially new Shaman races, like the Dwarves, Vrykul & Ogres.

subject: Re: Spirit Plant Brews | A New Shaman Class System
content_md:
I love the idea! Let shamans get high!

However, I think us cows are getting the short end of the stick. Trading the ability to attack for physical damage resistance is somewhat lackluster, because if you're receiving physical damage, it means you have aggro. If you have aggro, it means you're in melee, so being unable to attack is not ideal. The only thing you CAN do (I assume) is to cast spells, but those will get pushed back like crazy while you have aggro. So maybe we could add an additional effect to the Ethereal form:
"You have 70% to avoid pushback from physical attacks while casting spells."
Assuming a 5-10 sec duration, it should allow you get a heal or two off unless interrupted/stunned.

OR make it an escape tool by adding a movespeed increase, like the ability had in WC3.

author: Terras
subject: Shaman Shields Redesign
content_md:
So, there was a cool convo going on that died right as I posted in it, and I was hoping that I could get some feedback on what people think of a rework of the "Shields" used by Shamans.

BLUF
I would love the shaman to have abilities that tied into the concept of communing with elements while they fight. The longer they commune with an element the better the effects and to get the greatest benefit they have to learn to balance communing with the different options effectively like the warrior class has traditionally done with the stance dance.

#1. Give lighting shield (LS) a debuff based stacking effect. Let's say that each time a mob takes damage from LS they gain a stack of Static Charge (SC). Now let's have SC give something like the following effect: "For each stack of SC the effected unit has the aggro of lighting-based spells against it increased by X% and the damage by X%. For each stack of SC there is an X% chance to restore 1 charge of LS to the target if LS is active. Effect may stack up to X number of times." This would give a chance to have a slow build aggro and damage boost that is usable with a range of shaman abilities.

#2. Give Earth shield (ES) a buff based stacking effect. For this one we will go with the effect Stubborn Earth (SE). SE would be triggered as normal per ES but have the following effect instead: "For each stack of SE the shaman's armor is increased by X% and their spell resistance is increase by X. For each stack of SE, the shaman regenerates X% of max HP over X seconds. Effect may stack up to X number of times."

#3. Give Water Shield (WS) a buff based stacking effect. First, I would remove the charge effect from WS and make it more like an aura while keeping it exclusive against LS and ES. Next, I would give it the effect Ebb and Flow (EF) which would be as follows: "While WS is active the shaman gains 1 stack of EF every X seconds up to X number of times. For each stack of EF, the shaman receives X mana every X seconds. Each time the shaman casts a spell they lose all stacks of EF."

#4. Give the shaman a skill/talent at around lvl 50 that makes them immune to crit/crushing blows from mobs while they have a shield equipped in their off hand and any of their shield spells active.

I don't claim to be a shaman expert and I just want to see if i can add to the conversation without taking from anyone else.

author: Snigery
subject: Re: macro totems help!
content_md:
> **Vandy wrote: Fri Nov 03, 2023 5:05 pm**
> I'm looking for macros to put several totems in a row with one click:
>
>  example: /castsequence reset=3 Strength of Earth Totem, Mana Spring Totem
>
>  It doesn't work and I get the use /help message
>
>  Can you help me, do you know what's wrong or any addon? thank you

You can use the *RegisterCVar* function here to store a global variable within your game client, global meaning it can be used across macro calls. Register a *counter*.

You can make a separate macro and run this macro each time you start your game, or just type it into chat just as this.
Code: Select all

```
/run RegisterCVar( "c1", 1 )
```

If you want to see it working, you can use this in a macro file,
Code: Select all

```
/run local a = { "Totem A", "Totem B", "Totem C" } b = GetCVar( "c1" ) * 1 if b > 3 then b = 1 end SendChatMessage( "Counter: " .. b .. ", Totem: " .. a[ b ],'say') SetCVar( "c1", b + 1 )
```

Then just replace with the cast by name function.
Code: Select all

```
/run local a = { "Totem A", "Totem B", "Totem C" } b = GetCVar( "c1" ) * 1 if b > 3 then b = 1 end CastSpellByName( a[ b ] ) SetCVar( "c1", b + 1 )
```

Only problem is you have to press the button more than once which I see you wanted a single press. Oh well, but using this method you can do a lot of other cool stuff like swapping between gear sets instantly, assigning other skills to a single button to save action bar space, just toggle between them, and all other sorts of toggling actions. Make sure you don't spam the button faster than the GCD, or the counter will still increase and skip a totem.

From my experience of fights against other twinks being less geared, I can advise not to rely on your damage. Use crowd control as much as possible. Dispel enemy buffs, heal allies if needed. Avoid 1vs1, assist your strong teammates.

author: Queenoona
subject: Re: Shamans : New talent trees dropped
content_md:
Kevin Jordan also says that in hindsight he would have increased tanking capabilities to add a couple extra Tank classes into the game. (Shaman being one of them)
The important thing to note in this interview is that to the original team had the primary concern of making sure the Class can get in the raid. (Shaman as a whole) and then they would look at the specs as secondary.

This meant that due to time constraints itemization happened for the already good spec (Resto) but not as much for Enhancement/Elemental. They also didn't get the design attention that they needed for the same reason.

Hopefully if the Turtle Team goes this route it means they can also pick up where Kevin left off and try to amplify Shaman to a proper tanking position as well as DPS in their 2 other specs. Similar to how Feral Druid functions.

Enhancement offers a lot of support to its group, but so does Warrior. (Sunder Armor, Battle Shout, Demo Shout, Disarm, Thunderclap)

content_md:
Sorry no logs or vids.
Stats wise Shaman tanks do alright, they can reach decent levels of stamina, coupled with high dodge and a good shield just little wotse than bears just in stats.
Turtle wows coding is a bit more friendly towards grounding totem which helps with some specific boss fights, and the armor buffs in their talents helps some.
The durability problem is if your healer can't heal you, generally you are SOL. If you pull too much or a boss is dealing high burst damage there isn't a button to push that will help. Stacking dodge and stamina is the best shamans can do, but without any defensivea and the worst armor value of all the tanks your health bar can be spikey. That's the RNG, sometimes it's dodge, dodge, block, parry. And other times you get crit three times in a row.
There are obviously strategies for most things, but that requires planning and setup. And you don't always get the ideal setup, it can get messy and you're not going to be able to pull kite everything.
But generally, shaman tanks are so fun, especially in dungeons because doing a good pull feels so nice.
Set the appropriate totems and cast Lightning shield
Cast LB on the max range target, cast chain lightning on a closer target, and cast earth shock on another target if you procc'd clear casting. Then tab auto target till they die, and refresh lightning shield if the DPS is pumping.
There is also casting multiple rank 1 LB to proc clear casting before the mobs hit you.

author: Gdawg45
subject: Re: Shamans : New talent trees dropped
content_md:
What about making shaman be more helpful with group damage mitigation?  See explanation below:

Currently, Spirit Link works by displacing damage done to a target by sharing 15% of the damage taken by the target with party members next to the target.  Currently, this damage type is classified as spell damage.  Why not change that classification of damage from spell to physical.

What will this do?  It will allow the shaman, whether it be healer/melee/caster, to use different totems to increase the damage mitigation effects for the grouped members.
The shaman could use stoneskin totem to reduce the shared physical damage taken by the party members.  Using stoneskin instead of healing stream would allow the shaman to use the water totem for poison/disease dispels or fire resist totem.  If the group is more caster heavy or if the fight is longer and more mana is needed then mana spring can be used as an additional option.

Any thoughts?

author: Imonobor
subject: Let's talk about Stormstrike
content_md:
Ahh, Stormstrike, the Enhancement Shaman's only attack. And it turns out, it's totally not worth it. Here are the problems with it:

First off, the mana cost. At Rank 1, it costs 21% of base mana, which is extremely expensive for what it is. I've been so excited to pick it up, and since picking it up I've used it around 5 times, because it's so damn expensive. Maybe it's going to get better once I get Rank 2 (12% base mana). But something has to be done about its mana cost, it's not worth it to use it, since for the same mana you can cast a lightning bolt or shock and do way more damage (especially for 1-hander users like me).

Second, which is actually the bigger pain point for me, is its secondary effect:
"The next 2 sources of Nature damage dealt to the target are increased by 20%."
And they really mean ANY sources of nature damage. If you or ANYONE else in your party has any item that has "Adds 3 nature damage to attacks" (<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?spell=16615> , I have 2 of those by the way), or god forbid the tank is buffed with thorns, kiss those 2 debuff stacks goodbye before your GCD is done, for a total increase of 1 damage (if that, lol). Actually with 2 of the aforementioned items, the debuff doesn't even show up, because the attack caused by stormstrike consumes them. This makes Stormstrike really trash tier if you're relying on these effects to proc Clearcasting.

TLDR:
So here are my suggestions to fix the skill:
 1. Reduce the mana cost, especially for Rank 1. I propose 15% base mana for Rank 1 and 10% base mana for Rank 2.
 2. Make it so the nature damage debuff can ONLY be consumed by the shaman's own spells (Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning, Earth Shock or Lightning Shield).

The shaman consortium and the elements thank you for your time and consideration.   smiling_turtle

Having Stormstrike restore mana would be really nice and a welcome change, but we'd have to be careful not to make it too overpowered. Maybe instead it could reduce the mana cost of the next damage spell as a way to "regain" some of the mana lost for Stormstrike while incorporating it into the rotation better? Or cause the debuff to restore some of your mana when a stack is consumed?

Earth's Grasp - The Earthbind range is nice for kiting, but that's about it. Even so, rarely will you be tasked with kiting anything in a dungeon, and you don't want a shaman to do it.
Elemental Warding - Mabye in PvP it's great, but in PvE it's not. There are some fights where i'll take some dot damage, or some aoe damage, but not enough to justify three talents
Call of Flame - Not good. I guess for magma totem on some fights, but the damage output increase is so minimal.
Elemental Devastation - Useless, just, useless.

Eye of the Storm - Useless, in PvP mabye not, but even so I've never seen it taken.

That's six talents that are basically dead in PvE. At the very least they could combine Improved Fire Totems and Call of Flame, and Earths Grasp into one talent, and rework elemental devastation to where instead of melee attacks it's just "attacks".

author: Jstansberry
subject: Re: Leave any shaman buff that you want here
content_md:
For shaman tanking to be viable, they'd need

- A defensive cooldown

- A taunt

- AOE threat generation

- Better mana management

- itemization: shaman tank custom items are locked behind world boss drops that have very low drop chances and other very inaccessible sources
So they are lacking every tank tool other than single target threat generation.

Enhancement DPS needs

- Actual buttons to press: Shocks on a 6s CD and Stormstrike every 12s is not a rotation. Totem twisting is bad. Usually players utilizing unintended mechanics such as WFT buff "sticking" would be a good thing, but leaning into totem twisting would be a mistake. Reducing an entire spec to providing 4% more crit to warriors because it is the only benefit it has over the other two specs that actually fulfill an entire role on top of shitting out totems is not good game design.

- Better mana management: even without twisting an enhancement shaman will easily run out of mana in a 3 min+ fight.

- Better scaling: AP scales terribly on enhancement compared to other melee DPS specs while melee crit - their best scaling stat - is basically hardcapped at 38% due to outputting almost exclusively white hits. They scale even worse with SP, gaining ~0.072 DPS per point of spellpower if the enhancement shaman is casting shock spells every cooldown.

- Any real reason to take an enhancement over a ele or resto shaman. In other words, an actual identity and role: Bloodlust is all enhancement has over the other shaman talents trees and in it's current implementation enhancement is basically just a 5 min cooldown single target buff provider. Because the resto tree is also lackluster and provides very minimal benefits to a Chain Heal spamming resto shaman, many "resto" shamans just go deep into enhancement only so they can cast Bloodlust. Making enhancement the "support" spec is another huge mistake in my opinion. Enhancement was never the support spec, that is a concept people have convinced themselves of because totem twisting - an unintended mechanic - is more feasible for an enhancement shaman than it would be for an ele or resto shaman who are busy actually contributing to the raid. It provides a marginal benefit at the cost of the shaman's entire role being reduced to totem twisting due to the mana cost involved and is generally just a janky, uninteractive, and unrewarding chore to partake in. Making enhancement a competent melee DPS is the only logical route.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Leave any shaman buff that you want here
content_md:
Restoshamans end of tree powerspike is not big enough. Thanks to most classes having a much easier time with mana thanks to Arcane mages, Shadow Priests, access to tea with sugar, new powerful manareg items and other sources the Manaflood totem is something healshaman can easily sacrifice for bloodlust. That means restos can pick up bloodlust without much of a drawback, even competing with enhancers for the tiniest of niches the latter actually should have.

Maybe add an extra bounce for chainheal talent next to purification for 1-2 extra bounces. Just so a raidhealing shaman actually has an opportunity cost when going bloodlust. (this particular suggestion is probably a bit too string, but its more about the idea than the execution here)

Thunderhead is a conceptually very cool talent, but some things hold it back from the status it could have:
 1. It does not benefit from manacost reductions from Elemental Focus. Lightning shield end up costing more mana than earthshock per point of damage factoring that in. Even considering shocks abyssmal misschances.
 2. It causes threat for the shaman casting it. Making it relatively useless as a supporting tool
 3. It not being usable with Earth and Watershield. Making it strictly offensively useful.

Enhancer is already a weak spec baseline. But the skilltree adds insult to injury by placing reverberation, Elemental Focus Elemental Devastation, Nature's Guidance & Totemic focus so far away from one nother, that you can never grab all of them.
Move totemic focus to the 1. row of the Restro tree, allowing enhancer to get something useful from his first 5 points into the resto tree.
Swap elemental Devastation for Call of Flame or Earth's grab. Giving enhancers an alternative to the aggressively mediocore Concussion talent

Buff Elemental Devastation to have a mirrored component giving 3/6/9% spellHIT uppon landing a critical melee hit on your target. This would finally solve the hit problem enhancers have with their shocks in pve. In conjunction with Nature's Guidance shocks could relatively reliably hit raidbosses.

Give us some Weaponskill with two handed maces & Axes on the Weapon mastery talent. As a class that derrives the vast majority of its damage from white hits, shaman get ruined by glancing blows to an unfair amount. A built in way to combat that would be very helpful

And as an ardent defender of the totem twist playstile - give shamans a talent that restores manacost based on the remaining duration of a totem when it's destroyed or overplaced by another totem. (e.g. when you replace strength of the earth totem after 60 seconds, you get 50% of its manacost back). This allows enahncer to twist without it being a massive drain on his manapool for an admittably relatively mediocore benefit.
While at it, remove this placing 4 totems at once change. Totems should be part of shamans gameplay, not a macroed button you passively press at the beginning of combat and forget they exist.

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: Leave any shaman buff that you want here
content_md:
Hey! I'd list the things which (in my opinion) should be changed for the shaman builds without proposing solutions.

Ele:
 * Bad mana regen. Build is very spell intensive and there is no talent which either allows mana regen or gives you mana back somehow.
 * Shock radius doesn't match with lightning bolt/chain lightning radius after related talent is taken (storm reach). Can be clunky.
 * Too reliant on nature damage. Raids with high nat prot give ele a very bad time. Mages can respec to freeze at MC/BWL and fire at Naxx. Imagine locks and shadow priests if Turtle introduces a custom raid with over the top shadow rez on mobs.
 * Doesn't benefit from any warlock curse.
 * Fire totems are clunky. Searing totem pulls, magma and fire nova are melee range. Imagine your caster running at the tank, place an aoe totem, running back and starting to cast spells 4 sec in the fight.

Enh:
 * Game says it can tank, it can't really tank.
 * Damage is abysmal, melee gameplay is boring (shock, autoattack, stormstrike, autoattack, shock, bloodlust, autoattack etc).
 * No real CC. Build wears leather until lvl 40 and is kinda expected to 'just take it' as a warrior if things go badly.
 * Some core talents are really misplaced. Like the game forcing you to dig kinda deep into resto tree to get 3% melee hit chance or go a bit deep into ele for shock cooldown reduction.
 * Doesn't have talents to improve melee-range fire totems (if anyone, enh could make use of them).
 * Weapon enh spells last so short, using them is a chore.

Resto:
 * End of the talent tree is so weak you usually give up half of the tree just to get bloodlust.
 * Mana regen, just like ele.

Itemization:
Most shaman tier items give spirit, too. Spirit is almost useless for shamans, no talent combos with it and no shaman will afk <5 sec in a fight for mana. Shaman is a hybrid class, needing many kinds of stats. Please remove the one from the items shamans need the least and add something enh could use, like agi or strength (if strength is not already on the item). Inmagine warrior tier itemsn with intelligence instead of stamina for example (okay, here I exagerate a bit).

author: Batey9
subject: Re: Leave any shaman buff that you want here
content_md:
Not really a buff but I want dual wield just because I want it.  I don't care if it's a dps nerf.  Just don't attach some busted talent to it like they did on Live.   Make it's addition to Shaman completely inconsequential to people who want to use 2h.  You just buy it at your trainer like every other dual wield class.

Move Nature's Guidance from Resto to Enh.  Move it to second line Enh in the Improved Ghost Wolf position.  Paladins have it in their tank spec.  Why not Shamans?  Move Imp Ghost Wolf to the Ancestral Knowledge slot and change it to "Decreases cast time of Ghost Wolf by .2/.4/.6/.8/1 second".  Move Ancestral Knowledge to the current Nature's Guidance position and change it to "Increases Maximum mana pool by 3/6/10%" (calculated after items and buffs).  This may be an issue for Ele because this would force them to take points out of their Resto sub spec at lower gearing tiers.  But if that's really an issue, maybe we can just split this talent into 2 talents.  One for melee hit and one for spell hit and leave the spell hit half where it currently is and maybe combine Ancestral Knowledge with it?  5% mana pool is less shit when it comes bundled with spell hit.  Or, this issue could be completely averted if they actually add melle/spell hit to their tier sets with the coming set changes.

Maybe give Enh a talent that returns mana based on weapon speed from melee crits.  Not really sure where or how to add that, though.

Increase totem range to base 30 yards to be more in line with paladin auras.  10 yards is really bad and makes it so you basically have to follow the melee train around.  Which is really bad if you are resto or ele.  It's not really an issue in PvE.  But it is kind of a problem in PvP.  However, paladin auras will probably have to be buffed in some way to compensate because totems are just far better than paladin auras.  Alternatively, you can change totems to be casted on a targetted spot rather than at the feet of the shaman.  But that's a pretty big gameplay change and I don't even know if that's something you can do in the vanilla client.

As it stands now, shaman weapon buffs don't do anything for Ele or Resto.  That should probably change.  That's a core class mechanic that does nothing for 2/3 specs.  However, the buffs that it applies should be good enough that you can justify using them over Oils.  Something like:

Flametongue Weapon:  Deals fire damage based on speed of the weapon and increases spell power by X amount and X mp5.
Frostbrand Weapon: Deals frost damage based on speed of the weapon and increases heal power by X amount and X mp5. (Frost damage changed from CoH to give it more utility.  Can change between this and Flametongue based on the fight and the resistances of whatever you are attacking.  Molten Core, for example.  Also would be very handy on Viscidus where number of frost hits is what matters.)
Rockbiter Weapon: Increases melee attack power and threat from melee damage and totems.  Also, increases your spell crit chance by X%.
Windfury Weapon: 20% chance of gaining 2 extra attacks with increased attack power and increases your haste by 10%.

This gives the buffs a purpose for the caster specs as well as helps with their mana management.  Can swap around mid-fight based on what you need.  Maybe also take them off the GCD like they did for Totems?  But maybe that's too much.

author: Irhideine
subject: Are shamans obsolete?
content_md:
TLDR; there are no shamans.

So, recently I found an addon called CensusPlusTurtle. Let me make this clear, I'm not saying you should install it or anything. I want to tell you something.

As of this moment, the addon has collected data on 3578 characters using the /who functionality. It provides breakdowns on classes, races, and guilds of said characters, but only as part of graphs and not including any individual attributes of the characters it finds.

So there is something particularly concerning with the data I've obtained. There are only 14 shamans.

I've been standing in the middle of Orgrimmar, spamming target nearest friendly unit, without any updates to the amount of characters surveyed. This addon is cross-faction anyway.

I've noticed a lot of guilds recruiting resto shamans lately, so I guessed the shaman population was low. But I didn't realize it was this bad.

Now, it's possible this addon is wrong and not functioning properly. Still, I think this is something that should be investigated further. Is the lack of level 60 shamans really this extreme?

author: Irhideine
subject: Re: Are shamans obsolete?
content_md:
Just to clarify, I don't currently play a shaman but I wouldn't mind doing so; especially a restoration shaman. But at this point I have no choice but to believe this class is in an abnormal state. However, I do not agree that paladins would be the only reason, even if their buffs (double meaning intended) are part of it.

Typically (at least according to what I've experienced in MMOs) some people will always choose the less optimal classes for whatever game mode they prefer, be it soloing or PvP or raiding. Simply because those classes have their own strengths, and their own unique playstyles. For example, there will always be some people who prefer to play as moonkins rather than mages.

No, I think this is a case of lacking viability. That's when I think people really stop playing a class or a spec. After all, there will always be some people who choose their class not based on performance but based on their enjoyment of the class, or any number of other reasons.

What I suspect is, shamans will not be invited as DPS in PvE. They're not just  second rate; they're unwanted. As healers, their role is perhaps limited to bringing Windfury, eventually pushing healing shamans to spec enhancement. As for PvP, shamans aren't the only class affected by the paladin domination; they're pushing everyone else out as well. I'm unsure why shamans would be more affected by this than the other non-paladin classes.

Beside this, there would also have to be a lack of options for shamans as farmers, casuals, questers and so on. Or there would still be at least some shamans around.

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: Are shamans obsolete?
content_md:
Hey! Maining a shaman, can give my impressions.
Even if the tool you used is correct, you only see the logged in players at a given time I guess.
There are a few shamans but we are not extinct at all.
Gameplaywise... Leveling is hard. Ele is a drinking simulator mage who can be a backup healer in exchange. As a leveling enh you rush mobs like a warrior and pray that your leather (later mail) equipment is enough to survive. Frost shock and earthbind totem are not really useful oh shít buttons.
Resto feels kinda fine and viable but you have to accept that your healing is below what a priest can do and in exchange of a wf totem you are oom after healing two mob clears.
WF is by itself an interesting question. It is an extremely op totem rewarding kinda everyone except you (shamans rarely choose melee, see above).
Being a shaman has its own perks though. Immense utility. Fear, sleep, charm? Handled. Poison, disease? Handled. You need fire, frost or nature resistance? Handled. Wanna breath underwater? Handled. Shamans are great at solving problems but are also weak on their own.
What people tend to misunderstand is that shamans needn't be as strong as the others because the idea behind shamans is making everyone else stronger while contributing somewhat on their own.
Raiding is easy as a shaman, you can go to any guild but strictly as a resto.
People tend to regard shamans as utility units which have some key stuff, namely tremor, windfury, chainheal and bloodlust. As a utility unit people expect the one class from shaman which can give all of these utilitiy (bloodlust resto hybrid). Ele, full resto or full enh don't bring the same 'utility items' to the table. Maybe you can argue deep resto for better chain heals but serious raiding guilds have no ele or enh.
What I'd change is that each build gives a narrow but very good utility, so people would look for a bigger variety of shamans.
My idea is nerfing chain heal and wf totem. Resto gets a good chain heal, gets buffs to mana and life totem (maybe even 3* increase) and a new ultimate instead of manatide. Like healing rain (x min cd aoe heal which gives you 1-5 mana after each 100 health restored, making it up). Enh could get the real wf, bloodlust plus some survivability for leveling. Ele could have spell damage totem and added mana regen.

author: Klouther
subject: Shaman Tweaks while waiting for Class changes 2
content_md:
Well, the tittle of the post is quite self explanatory so I will get straight to the point; Shaman is not in a good spot and it shows in the class population and relegation as a totem dispenser in raids. So here are a list of changes I have seen mentioned in the discord, this forum and some I have thought myself:

 1º- Turn [Rockbitter Weapon] into a sort of stance just like the paladin equivalent seal was turned into [Righteous Fury] by the end of WoW's Beta. It's a long overdue change that's within TWoW philosophy of finishing what the original game couldn't at the time. Here's a suggestion for it;
[Rockbitter Warden
Fills your body with the strength of the Earth, increasing your attack power by (charlevel*10), the threat generated by your physical attacks and weapon imbues by 100% and the threat of your frost, fire and nature spells by 35%.]

This idea is to reinforce the current enhance tank playstyle without destroying [Rockbitter Weapon] identity and making it a knock-off [RIghteous Fury]. I'm not including redirecting threat from totems because that's more than likely going to be a talent in Class Changes 2.

 2º- Make weapon imbues self buffs with a 15min duration at the very least. The current iteration is simply cumbersome to use and it deprives enhancement of the option of using sharpening stones or benefiting from your own WFT or FTT(never seen that one used before). On that note, why there isn't a Frostbrand totem even if just for flavor/consistency?

 3º- Make the class quest for totems actually rewarding instead of a lenghty chore to be able to use half of your skill kit(looking at you, water totem questchain). The "mirror class" to shamans, paladins, only need to complete two class quest for base skills with the low level ones giving a nice tanking shield and a 2h weapon that last until the mid 30's levels. So my proposal is to make the actual totems hogging 4 bag spaces have an on use effect with a shared short CD(1min maybe?):

[Earth Totem: increases your armour value by X% and resistances by Y% for Z seconds.]
[Fire Totem: your attacks and spells deal an additional (charlevel/4 + X% SP * base attack/casting speed) fire damage to your target and all enemies within 5yard for the next Yseconds.]
[Water Totem: increases your HP5 and MP5 by (charlevel + X% spirit) for the next Yseconds.]
[Wind Totem: reduces your threat generation by 20% for the next 20s.]

These are just personal suggestions for the effects, the core idea is to make the item totems useful.

 4º- Buff [Stormstrike]. It's an incredible contender for the worst melee skill in the game: it's literally a glorified AA. Just give it a hefty AP and SP scaling so it actually hits like a lvl 30 talent with a long CD and mana cost should. Just to point out, the "mirror class" paladin [Holy Strike] is a baseline lvl 10 skill with +dmg and SP scaling as well as having the best dmg type in the game.

 5º- Merge [Nature's Guidance] from the resto tree into [Elemental Warding] from the ele tree(mostly to avoid talent clutter). Where [Nature's Guidance] is right now doesn't make any sense, it should be in the first row's of the ele tree so both dps/tank specs can easily grab it.

 6º- Either up Totems duration or reduce their mana cost across the board. They are the utility the class provides to a group yet it's objectively inferior to paladin blessings over a dungeon/raid clear: far higher mana cost for uptime, they are position dependant and their base range is shorter than paladin auras(which are permanent and free to boot).

 7º- Prune some of the skills to let way for others that might be actually used. Shamans currently have 22 different totems some of which have the same effects as some skills(Poison Cleansing Totem&Cure Poison, Disease Cleansing Totem&Cure Disease) or are straight up useless(Windwall Totem, Stoneskin Totem to some degree due to armour diminishing returns, Tranquil Air Totem also since it depends if you are in dps melee group or not and you have the mana to twist into WFT).

Poison Cleansing Totem&Disease Cleansing Totem could be easily merged into one and Mana Spring Totem&Healing Stream Totem are also good candidates.

 8º- This is just a personal nitpick since shamans are supposed to be fighters wielding the elements so... rework [Lightning Bolt] into [Elemental Bolt] and tie the type of damage it deals to your active weapon imbue;
 -nothing or wf-> nature damage
 -flametongue-> fire damage
 -frostbrand-> frost damage

As I said, personal nitpick but if it could be done, it would help the class fantasy and make ele/enhancement more versatile and also improve the synergy with other classes(why does locks [Curse of Elements] only affect frost and fire damage? Why hasn't it changed already to include nature dmg?).

Well, if you stuck around till the end, please rip these suggestions as much as you like and tell me why they are stupid/unnecessary/over the top or whatever. Correct me as much as you like and give everyone and the devs more ideas to think about to help shamans not be a totem dispenser any more   satisfied_turtle_head

author: Chappinhas3000
subject: SHAMAN FIXES
content_md:
Shamans and Paladins stand out from the other classes since they are thematically support classes, this is to say that they shine greater when in a party. However, given the recent changes to paladins and the subsequent power boost they receive it is apparent that once more shamans have been left outcasts and the player base shows that latent issues prevent the class from reaching it's true potential. I have made a list of changes and tweaks i believe could be implemented that may flesh out the meta and playability of the shaman class.
Before i engage in the crunch, i find it important to determine what exactly defines a support class and how best to understand the shaman's role. From where i see it, paladins and shamans have the uncanny ability to improve overall dps of a party and aid both in combat and healing, furthermore, the shaman class distinguishes itself for the use of magic in favour of physical damage. This factors lead to a class that must have some downtime within it's rotations so as to focus those moments on support, be it the application of totems, the occasional support heal or simply a moment of repositioning. Additionally, the shaman class has always flirted with tanking capabilities by shield and threat even tho it does not use plate, this as often been cause for contention and excitement among would-be tanks. The following propositions seek to adress these issues without crossing the shamanistic spirit.
Generally speaking, should shaman tank, damage mitigation should arrise from stoneskin totem like effect, additionally talents that may increase chance to be missed or less chance to be crited should be favoured, this is due to the armour factor forcing the shaman to control more thuroughly the incoming damage, the mana factor also takes a great toll on this playstyle and should be resolved thru the use of totems and elemental shields has it would have class RP.
On the enhancement factor, the greatest deal arises from the weapon enchantment commitment that prevents the shaman from using consumable and enchants to empower his melee attacks, additionally the mana issue remains, albeit to a smaller degree.
The elemental playstyle is dull and repetitive showing innovation only in a shield melee build not adequate for late game content, an over relliance on castable spells and limited toolset prevents the spec from reaching further.
restoration, despite it's great advantages and suficient healing lacks luster and can prove equally dull at times, point in case, the lack of interesting spells on the spec tree.

To solve these issues the following is proposed:

 - Base Spirit, and agility increase
 -Rockbitter weapon : the addition of damage mitigation ( akin to stoneskin totem) and possible healing spell power, to allow both resto and shaman tanks to use it in diferent forms, additionally it could incentivize the tank shaman to heal himself as means of accrueing aura threat.
 - Flametongue weapon : the addition of spell power to generally increase elementall damage numbers.
 - Frostbrand weapon: a flat increase in damage to counter it's relation with flametongue and the adition of mp5 buff.
 - Totems: a yard increase to 35yards, allowing for more interaction and less placing of totems
 - Shields: an increase in charges ( possibly by enhancement talents) and inner cooldown to prevent the fast deprecation of the same, this would make them more mana efficient.) additionally passive effects while the shield holds, mana regen for water, damage reduction for earth and crit for lightning ( possibly only accrued at lvl 60) giving them more versatility for team situations. Additionally water shield should come at lower levels to aid shamans with early mana issues.
 - Flame Shock: allow for the dot to crit
 - Lightning bolt: reduce the cast time by 0.5 sec, allowing for LB weaving in between attacks when using a very slow 2hand weapon
 - Off-hand Fist weapons: a niche and possibly pointless change that would add variety in playstyles and be thematically cool, these could either be enchanted by shaman weapons or force the shaman to seek shadow oil's or frost oils for his magical needs. As a counter to tradicional dual weilding, this offhand useage could ignore dual wield hit penalty and be counted as typical 1 hand 5%.
 - Bloodlust: make it so you always buff yourself and an ally when you cast it and reduce the cooldown to match it's duration allowing for perma use of the spell, reduce it's effect to compensate for the permanent presence of the spell, this would allow the shaman to aid an ally without compromising itself.
 - Enhancment tree should have a talent, maybe on dodge effect that allows for 15 % mana regen to continue while in combat, high enough in the tree that it could be picked by resto and ele.
 - WFT and FTT Should not count as weapon enchants and be considered buffs instead, aditionally they should stack with the shaman's own weapon provided it is not the same as the totems.
 - Allow for enchanting shaman weapons.
 - Slight increase in stonekin totem damage reduction
 - Threat transferal from magma totem

content_html:
Shamans and Paladins stand out from the other classes since they are thematically support classes, this is to say that they shine greater when in a party. However, given the recent changes to paladins and the subsequent power boost they receive it is apparent that once more shamans have been left outcasts and the player base shows that latent issues prevent the class from reaching it's true potential. I have made a list of changes and tweaks i believe could be implemented that may flesh out the meta and playability of the shaman class.
Before i engage in the crunch, i find it important to determine what exactly defines a support class and how best to understand the shaman's role. From where i see it, paladins and shamans have the uncanny ability to improve overall dps of a party and aid both in combat and healing, furthermore, the shaman class distinguishes itself for the use of magic in favour of physical damage. This factors lead to a class that must have some downtime within it's rotations so as to focus those moments on support, be it the application of totems, the occasional support heal or simply a moment of repositioning. Additionally, the shaman class has always flirted with tanking capabilities by shield and threat even tho it does not use plate, this as often been cause for contention and excitement among would-be tanks. The following propositions seek to adress these issues without crossing the shamanistic spirit.
Generally speaking, should shaman tank, damage mitigation should arrise from stoneskin totem like effect, additionally talents that may increase chance to be missed or less chance to be crited should be favoured, this is due to the armour factor forcing the shaman to control more thuroughly the incoming damage, the mana factor also takes a great toll on this playstyle and should be resolved thru the use of totems and elemental shields has it would have class RP.
On the enhancement factor, the greatest deal arises from the weapon enchantment commitment that prevents the shaman from using consumable and enchants to empower his melee attacks, additionally the mana issue remains, albeit to a smaller degree.
The elemental playstyle is dull and repetitive showing innovation only in a shield melee build not adequate for late game content, an over relliance on castable spells and limited toolset prevents the spec from reaching further.
restoration, despite it's great advantages and suficient healing lacks luster and can prove equally dull at times, point in case, the lack of interesting spells on the spec tree.

To solve these issues the following is proposed:

- Base Spirit, and agility increase
-Rockbitter weapon : the addition of damage mitigation ( akin to stoneskin totem) and possible healing spell power, to allow both resto and shaman tanks to use it in diferent forms, additionally it could incentivize the tank shaman to heal himself as means of accrueing aura threat.
- Flametongue weapon : the addition of spell power to generally increase elementall damage numbers.
- Frostbrand weapon: a flat increase in damage to counter it's relation with flametongue and the adition of mp5 buff.
- Totems: a yard increase to 35yards, allowing for more interaction and less placing of totems
- Shields: an increase in charges ( possibly by enhancement talents) and inner cooldown to prevent the fast deprecation of the same, this would make them more mana efficient.) additionally passive effects while the shield holds, mana regen for water, damage reduction for earth and crit for lightning ( possibly only accrued at lvl 60) giving them more versatility for team situations. Additionally water shield should come at lower levels to aid shamans with early mana issues.
- Flame Shock: allow for the dot to crit
- Lightning bolt: reduce the cast time by 0.5 sec, allowing for LB weaving in between attacks when using a very slow 2hand weapon
- Off-hand Fist weapons: a niche and possibly pointless change that would add variety in playstyles and be thematically cool, these could either be enchanted by shaman weapons or force the shaman to seek shadow oil's or frost oils for his magical needs. As a counter to tradicional dual weilding, this offhand useage could ignore dual wield hit penalty and be counted as typical 1 hand 5%.
- Bloodlust: make it so you always buff yourself and an ally when you cast it and reduce the cooldown to match it's duration allowing for perma use of the spell, reduce it's effect to compensate for the permanent presence of the spell, this would allow the shaman to aid an ally without compromising itself.
- Enhancment tree should have a talent, maybe on dodge effect that allows for 15 % mana regen to continue while in combat, high enough in the tree that it could be picked by resto and ele.
- WFT and FTT Should not count as weapon enchants and be considered buffs instead, aditionally they should stack with the shaman's own weapon provided it is not the same as the totems.
- Allow for enchanting shaman weapons.
- Slight increase in stonekin totem damage reduction
- Threat transferal from magma totem
- Increase in stoneclaw totem health and threat generation
- Decoupling of fire nova, allowing it to be cast at all times emanating from both the current fire totem and the shaman alike.
-Add a water nova effect, capable of being cast at all times emanating from both the current water totem and shaman alike ( possible resto talent), small heal and mana recovery and cleanse effect around 20 sec cooldown
-Add a sand blast effect, capable of being cast at all times emanating from both the earth totem and shaman alike, providing enemy armor reduction and chance to miss
-Add a wind nova effect, capable of being cast at all times emanating from both the wind totem and shaman alike, providing allies with a slight haste bonus and movement speed buff.
-Add a ele talent to incentivize shock weaving, something as simple as next diferent shock damage increase
-Add a special effect to enhanc shaman block based on current elemental shield, forked lightning( low damage high threat) for lightning, rejuvenation like effect for earth and mana regen for water.

I believe these changes could aid the class significantly and allow for new ways of making shamans, in conclusion, the damage mitigation is ensured by direct flat vaklue damage reduction, the dps increase by buff spell flexibilitiy and the mana issues i believe can be countered by less totem usage and some increase mana regen from water shield and dodging ( for would be tanks)

content_html:
Shamans and Paladins stand out from the other classes since they are thematically support classes, this is to say that they shine greater when in a party. However, given the recent changes to paladins and the subsequent power boost they receive it is apparent that once more shamans have been left outcasts and the player base shows that latent issues prevent the class from reaching it's true potential. I have made a list of changes and tweaks i believe could be implemented that may flesh out the meta and playability of the shaman class.
Before i engage in the crunch, i find it important to determine what exactly defines a support class and how best to understand the shaman's role. From where i see it, paladins and shamans have the uncanny ability to improve overall dps of a party and aid both in combat and healing, furthermore, the shaman class distinguishes itself for the use of magic in favour of physical damage. This factors lead to a class that must have some downtime within it's rotations so as to focus those moments on support, be it the application of totems, the occasional support heal or simply a moment of repositioning. Additionally, the shaman class has always flirted with tanking capabilities by shield and threat even tho it does not use plate, this as often been cause for contention and excitement among would-be tanks. The following propositions seek to adress these issues without crossing the shamanistic spirit.
Generally speaking, should shaman tank, damage mitigation should arrise from stoneskin totem like effect, additionally talents that may increase chance to be missed or less chance to be crited should be favoured, this is due to the armour factor forcing the shaman to control more thuroughly the incoming damage, the mana factor also takes a great toll on this playstyle and should be resolved thru the use of totems and elemental shields has it would have class RP.
On the enhancement factor, the greatest deal arises from the weapon enchantment commitment that prevents the shaman from using consumable and enchants to empower his melee attacks, additionally the mana issue remains, albeit to a smaller degree.
The elemental playstyle is dull and repetitive showing innovation only in a shield melee build not adequate for late game content, an over relliance on castable spells and limited toolset prevents the spec from reaching further.
restoration, despite it's great advantages and suficient healing lacks luster and can prove equally dull at times, point in case, the lack of interesting spells on the spec tree.

To solve these issues the following is proposed:

- Base Spirit, and agility increase
-Rockbitter weapon : the addition of damage mitigation ( akin to stoneskin totem) and possible healing spell power, to allow both resto and shaman tanks to use it in diferent forms, additionally it could incentivize the tank shaman to heal himself as means of accrueing aura threat.
- Flametongue weapon : the addition of spell power to generally increase elementall damage numbers.
- Frostbrand weapon: a flat increase in damage to counter it's relation with flametongue and the adition of mp5 buff.
- Totems: a yard increase to 35yards, allowing for more interaction and less placing of totems
- Shields: an increase in charges ( possibly by enhancement talents) and inner cooldown to prevent the fast deprecation of the same, this would make them more mana efficient.) additionally passive effects while the shield holds, mana regen for water, damage reduction for earth and crit for lightning ( possibly only accrued at lvl 60) giving them more versatility for team situations. Additionally water shield should come at lower levels to aid shamans with early mana issues.
- Flame Shock: allow for the dot to crit
- Lightning bolt: reduce the cast time by 0.5 sec, allowing for LB weaving in between attacks when using a very slow 2hand weapon
- Off-hand Fist weapons: a niche and possibly pointless change that would add variety in playstyles and be thematically cool, these could either be enchanted by shaman weapons or force the shaman to seek shadow oil's or frost oils for his magical needs. As a counter to tradicional dual weilding, this offhand useage could ignore dual wield hit penalty and be counted as typical 1 hand 5%.
- Bloodlust: make it so you always buff yourself and an ally when you cast it and reduce the cooldown to match it's duration allowing for perma use of the spell, reduce it's effect to compensate for the permanent presence of the spell, this would allow the shaman to aid an ally without compromising itself.
- Enhancment tree should have a talent, maybe on dodge effect that allows for 15 % mana regen to continue while in combat, high enough in the tree that it could be picked by resto and ele.
- WFT and FTT Should not count as weapon enchants and be considered buffs instead, aditionally they should stack with the shaman's own weapon provided it is not the same as the totems.
- Allow for enchanting shaman weapons.
- Slight increase in stonekin totem damage reduction
- Threat transferal from magma totem
- Increase in stoneclaw totem health and threat generation
- Decoupling of fire nova, allowing it to be cast at all times emanating from both the current fire totem and the shaman alike.
-Add a water nova effect, capable of being cast at all times emanating from both the current water totem and shaman alike ( possible resto talent), small heal and mana recovery and cleanse effect around 20 sec cooldown
-Add a sand blast effect, capable of being cast at all times emanating from both the earth totem and shaman alike, providing enemy armor reduction and chance to miss
-Add a wind nova effect, capable of being cast at all times emanating from both the wind totem and shaman alike, providing allies with a slight haste bonus and movement speed buff.
-Add a ele talent to incentivize shock weaving, something as simple as next diferent shock damage increase
-Add a special effect to enhanc shaman block based on current elemental shield, forked lightning( low damage high threat) for lightning, rejuvenation like effect for earth and mana regen for water.

I believe these changes could aid the class significantly and allow for new ways of making shamans, in conclusion, the damage mitigation is ensured by direct flat vaklue damage reduction, the dps increase by buff spell flexibilitiy and the mana issues i believe can be countered by less totem usage and some increase mana regen from water shield and dodging ( for would be tanks)

Shams are not buffers, they are a glorified windfury totem. Even Blizzard "solved" this by giving druids the windfury ability in SoM, making Shams virtually useless.

Sham is by far the worst class in Classic or Classic-alikes : non existent DPS, underwhelming/non-existent tanking, okay healing but I'd take a paladin ANY DAY over a sham.

The class is poorly designed on the get-go. The talent tree is garbage. The totems, while cool, are just a concept that is badly executed in practice: even with heavy talent investment, it has limited range, heavy mana cost, and underwhelming effect.

And worst issue of all: the class starves mana like crazy. Enhance is virtually unplayable because of this.

subject: Suggestion to make Shaman Enhancement gameplay more fun and "complex"
content_md: I would like to suggest to the developers to place an effect right after activating the Shaman's weapon enhancements, for example, when using windfury, you will have an increase in attack speed for 10 seconds, when using flametongue, your first auto attack will cause a fire damage in the area, things that encourage not to leave just a single effect always active that we only have to worry about renewing when it ends, it could be balanced by putting a low cooldown of 3 or 4 seconds, obviously the numbers are things that should be studied in depth, however this gameplay that encourages using various elements in the weapon in a fight would make the specialization very dynamic.

It seems Blizz intended Shamans to be "swapping" their Enchantments around often (like one second DPSing a heavy armory mob with Flametongue then quickly switching to Frostbrand to kite a dangerous mob)

Thats why they only last 5 mins.
Like Paladin buffs they were supposed to "swapped" around to fit the situation.

However no one uses them this way. You just stick with your 'favorite/ideal' one and have to refresh it (annoying) every few minutes.

author: Chappinhas3000
subject: Shaman Fixes v2
content_md:
In accordance to my last post, some changes i made

Shaman Weapons:

 - Rockbitter Weapon: Add attack power to weapon, increases threat from auto attacks, and reduces the damage taken by an amount.

 -Flametongue weapon: Add fire additional fire damage to attacks and grant the shaman additional spell power

 -Frostbrand weapon: Chance on hit to deal extra frost damage, increases MP5 and add frost and fire resistance to the shaman

 -Windfury Weapon: Increases attack speed by 5%, Chance on hit to deal 2 aditional attacks the damage from this attack counts as nature damage.

Shaman Shields:

 - Lightning Shield: summon three orbs that protect and empower the shaman dealing nature damage to attackers and increasing critical strike damage from attacks and abilities by 10%

 -Earth Shield : Summon three orbs that protect and empower the shaman healing the target on damage taken and reducing the damage taken by the target by an amount

 -Water Shield: summon three orbs that protect and emppower the shaman granting mana on damage taken and increasing mana regeneration by an amount

Shaman Totems:

 - Stoneskin Totem : reduces melee damage taken by an amount and reduces the chance to be critically hit.

 - Magma Totem : deals damage in an area around the totem, the threat is transfered to the caster

 - Healing Stream totem and Mana Spring totem ( combined) : heals an amount and grants mana every 2 seconds

 - Windwall totem: reduces ranged damage taken and increases the chance to be missed

 - Stoneskin Totem: Taunts enemys in an area around the totem, the totem takes reduced damage from melee attacks

Shaman Talents:

 -Enhancement:
 - Bloodlust: ROW 5: grants the caster and the target 5% melee attack speed and 5% melee damage for 15 seconds, 15 sec CD
 - Improved Bloodlust :ROW 6: Requires Bloodlust: Shaman Criticals Reduce the CD of Bloodlust by 1 sec
 - Weapon Mastery : ROW 6: 5 points: grants 1% weapon damage and 1% chance to hit with melee attacks
 - Primal Strike: ROW 7 : 1 point: Strike the target dealing Weapon damage and granting the shaman an effect based on current shaman weapon: Fire DOT for flametongue, Damage shield for Rockbitter, Freeze for Frostbrand, Threat reduction for Windfury
