author: Akos1896
subject: For new resto shamans who approach level 60
content_md:
Hey!

This article is for new resto shamans. I wanna list some tips for you which either helped me during the early phases of raids or I regretted not doing them earlier.
The goal is to make the initial raiding experience as a resto shaman smoother.

So you're either approaching level 60 or are a fresh level 60. Here are my tips.

BoP gears:
 * Spam BM for Totem of the calming river. It will give you a base mana regen boost which is a blessing at the early stages of raiding. Alternatively you can spam Scholo10 for totem of sustaining. Lesser healing wave is not our most used heal but this relic still helps a lot. If you farm it via a 10man raid, you make your life easier. Also, good for AD rep runs. All in all, BM relic is better for you.
 * Spam Kara5 for 5% mana regen items to make your mana management at early raids better. It's mostly for the initial raiding stage, I replaced these items rather soon but for the first 1-2 months of raiding, they are a huge help. Also, I kept them as a set for really long boss fights to have mana.
Notable items:
 -> Memento of the lost - Extremely good neck item but should later be replaced via Jindo's evil eye or amulet of the shifting sands. Lady Maye's pendant might be somewhat better but not worth the price. Will go in detail a bit later.
 -> Loop of the forgotten - Very good mana regen ring. I'd only consider getting rid of it when you have two high +healing purple rings.
 -> Remains of the lost - It's so rare that I don't recommend farming it just to have an advantage at early raids. Even if it's on AH, it is so expensive that that gold is better spent elsewhere. More about this later.
 -> Shroud of haunted torment - I think it is a preBIS cape for you unless you are willing to pay a lot for hide of the wIld.

BOE gears:
 0. Get to Hyjal. You will need the tea and if you're willing to farm, satyr farm opens up some really good options for you (unless you have another char which can farm gold at a very high rate somewhere).
 1. If you're willing to farm, get 150 bright dream shards for dreambreeze cowl. Top priority BoE.
 2. If you're okay with farming a bit more, get verdant dreamer's breastplate. Top priority BoE.
These two give you an initial boost of 10% normal mana regen while casting while also giving stats and +healing.

From this part I advise useful ones which can be ignored, though.
 3. Hide of the wild. Extremely good cape, until BWL you don't find a comparable item. It is lower on my list though because it doesn't help as much with mana management as the first two items and shroud of haunted torment is a very decent replacement in my opinion. Less healing, less stats, more mana regen, added casting speed.
 4. Corehound belt, corehound gloves. Huge items but if you buy all these you'll lose the initial fun of raiding because you'll receive half the upgrades you'd otherwise receive. Gloves have a comparable item in AQ20 (gloves of dark wisdom) belts are better for a longer time. If you wanna buy one, buy the belt, it's cheaper anyway.
 5. If you wanna overkill, you can go for a dawnstone hammer. But it is extremely expensive. You're probably better of by fishing for jindo's hexxer in ZG + having an offhand.
 6. Alchemist's stone: a trinket to consider for the early raids. Improving on your mana pots makes your mana management better. But keep in mind that you get Hakkar's heart relatively soon and the zandalarian hero charm is BIS for you for a long period of time. Same about sliver of hope from Kara10. You might spend a fortune for it just to replace it soon.
 7. Lady Maye's pendant - I'm against buying it. It's a nice one but spending a bunch of gold for a BoE which gets replaced in ZG or AQ20 is a bad decision. Kara5 neck is perfect for that part of the raid progression.
 8. Remains of the lost is for collectors and some weird arcane mages. If you somehow loot it during a Kara5 run, it's okay. But otherwise, don't spend thousands of gold for this 'upgrade' just to replace it with zandalarian hero charm and sliver of hope.

 1 and 2 makes sure that you're way better with mana and give you enough +healing to start spell downgrading. Everything else you get below 1 and 2 further helps with downgrades.
As a general rule I advise people using chain heal rank 2 with a bad gear. If +healing starts to look good, rank 1 can become the default if there is no oh shít situation.

I advise having at least +10% normal mana regen while casting gear on you until you are restricted with T2,5+T2. That plus oranges takes care of most of the mana problems.
Also, once you have the ZG rep for it, make sure that you always have some spirit of zanza. That +50 spirit makes wonders if you have the mana regen items.

Hey!

This article is for new resto shamans. I wanna list some tips for you which either helped me during the early phases of raids or I regretted not doing them earlier.
The goal is to make the initial raiding experience as a resto shaman smoother.

So you're either approaching level 60 or are a fresh level 60. Here are my tips.

BoP gears:
* Spam BM for Totem of the calming river. It will give you a base mana regen boost which is a blessing at the early stages of raiding. Alternatively you can spam Scholo10 for totem of sustaining. Lesser healing wave is not our most used heal but this relic still helps a lot. If you farm it via a 10man raid, you make your life easier. Also, good for AD rep runs. All in all, BM relic is better for you.
* Spam Kara5 for 5% mana regen items to make your mana management at early raids better. It's mostly for the initial raiding stage, I replaced these items rather soon but for the first 1-2 months of raiding, they are a huge help. Also, I kept them as a set for really long boss fights to have mana.
Notable items:
-> Memento of the lost - Extremely good neck item but should later be replaced via Jindo's evil eye or amulet of the shifting sands. Lady Maye's pendant might be somewhat better but not worth the price. Will go in detail a bit later.
-> Loop of the forgotten - Very good mana regen ring. I'd only consider getting rid of it when you have two high +healing purple rings.
-> Remains of the lost - It's so rare that I don't recommend farming it just to have an advantage at early raids. Even if it's on AH, it is so expensive that that gold is better spent elsewhere. More about this later.
-> Shroud of haunted torment - I think it is a preBIS cape for you unless you are willing to pay a lot for hide of the wIld.

BOE gears:
0. Get to Hyjal. You will need the tea and if you're willing to farm, satyr farm opens up some really good options for you (unless you have another char which can farm gold at a very high rate somewhere).
1. If you're willing to farm, get 150 bright dream shards for dreambreeze cowl. Top priority BoE.
2. If you're okay with farming a bit more, get verdant dreamer's breastplate. Top priority BoE.
These two give you an initial boost of 10% normal mana regen while casting while also giving stats and +healing.

From this part I advise useful ones which can be ignored, though.
3. Hide of the wild. Extremely good cape, until BWL you don't find a comparable item. It is lower on my list though because it doesn't help as much with mana management as the first two items and shroud of haunted torment is a very decent replacement in my opinion. Less healing, less stats, more mana regen, added casting speed.
4. Corehound belt, corehound gloves. Huge items but if you buy all these you'll lose the initial fun of raiding because you'll receive half the upgrades you'd otherwise receive. Gloves have a comparable item in AQ20 (gloves of dark wisdom) belts are better for a longer time. If you wanna buy one, buy the belt, it's cheaper anyway.
5. If you wanna overkill, you can go for a dawnstone hammer. But it is extremely expensive. You're probably better of by fishing for jindo's hexxer in ZG + having an offhand.
6. Alchemist's stone: a trinket to consider for the early raids. Improving on your mana pots makes your mana management better. But keep in mind that you get Hakkar's heart relatively soon and the zandalarian hero charm is BIS for you for a long period of time. Same about sliver of hope from Kara10. You might spend a fortune for it just to replace it soon.
7. Lady Maye's pendant - I'm against buying it. It's a nice one but spending a bunch of gold for a BoE which gets replaced in ZG or AQ20 is a bad decision. Kara5 neck is perfect for that part of the raid progression.
8. Remains of the lost is for collectors and some weird arcane mages. If you somehow loot it during a Kara5 run, it's okay. But otherwise, don't spend thousands of gold for this 'upgrade' just to replace it with zandalarian hero charm and sliver of hope.

1 and 2 makes sure that you're way better with mana and give you enough +healing to start spell downgrading. Everything else you get below 1 and 2 further helps with downgrades.
As a general rule I advise people using chain heal rank 2 with a bad gear. If +healing starts to look good, rank 1 can become the default if there is no oh shít situation.

I advise having at least +10% normal mana regen while casting gear on you until you are restricted with T2,5+T2. That plus oranges takes care of most of the mana problems.
Also, once you have the ZG rep for it, make sure that you always have some spirit of zanza. That +50 spirit makes wonders if you have the mana regen items.

If you want your spells to automatically downrank based on missing HP percentage of the mouseover target, you can use SmartHealer (<https://github.com/melbaa/SmartHealer>) - it works with the mouseover functions of pfUI, Clique and ClassicMouseover. I've only used pfUI of the three and it works well, although you might also need TheoryCraft for precise calculations.

author: Froghijab420
subject: Flavorful Enhance Suggestions
content_md:
I really enjoy the Shaman vs Paladin class identity in Vanilla wow, and how the classes are polar opposites of each other.

 **Shaman**
 -Horde Only
 -Most  offensive healer, with purges/grounding, windfury/earth, etc, bursty spells.
 -Mana-inefficent, most powerful AOE heal.

 **Paladin**
 -Alliance Only
 -Most  defensive healer, with plate armor/BOP/Bubble etc.
 -Mana-efficent, best single target heals.

With Paladins getting a better version of Stormstrike baseline, this kind've breaks the design due to retribution paladins being more defensive and offensively stronger than enhancement shamans.

Here are some small flavorful changes that will not make Shamans a ret copy cat, but by strengthening other aspects such as offensive mobility.

 **1. Ghost Wolf**
![Image](https://imgur.com/a/XMsLvz8)
Give us TBC version of Ghost wolf (2 second cast vs current 3 second cast).  With the "Improved Ghost Wolf" talent, Ghost wolf will be instant cast.

Move talent **"Improved Ghost Wolf"** down a row.
![Image](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=16287/improved-ghost-wolf)
Moving this down a row will prevent Ele/resto shamans from getting both "Nature's Swiftness" and instant ghost wolf if they decide to.

Other melees have great mobility (Warrior charge/intercept, Rogue sprint/stealth, Druids nuff said) and Shamans only have slows (no hard CC); Counter-able with dispel.
 *Optional Change
 -Make Ghost Wolf usable indoors.  It's Shamans only spell you can't use indoors, and flavor-wise I felt it more matching for the Druid to have the only spells you can't use indoors.

TURTLE SELL GHOST WOLF SKINS (SUCH AS GHOST RAPTORS, Kodo, etc.)  If Ghost Wolf is used all the time for mobility, more people would use it and more opportunity to sell skins for it.

 2. **Flurry Change**
![Image](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=12974/flurry)
I don't like how the Flurry talent is a straight copy from the warrior class.  I think it would be fun if another talent linking with Flurry or if it was

changed to ...**Elemental Flurry.**
Same effect, but would (or new talent) add a random small fire, frost, nature attach during flurry.  This would be flavorful (with Shamans using Windfury - outside of shocks, 0 elemental damage from their weapon), and would allow procs of Elemental clearcasting.  (or call it Storm Flurry, and make it add small nature dmg).

Elemental clear-casting procs won't be OP, due to top parsing Shamans already using mana consumes, would make pvp and general play less painful.

 3. **Change Bloodlust to a new melee oriented haste boost.**
Current Bloodlust is weak, unfun, and mostly used by restoration healing shamans.

Example:
 **"Stormrush", "Al'Akir's Essence", "Doomwinds"**
Windfury procs cause all party members to gain X increased attack speed for X seconds.
Numbers can be adjusted, but would give Enhance a raid-spot in melee dps groups.

author: Akos1896
subject: Do you think 8/32/11 can work?
content_md:
Hey!

Was theorycrafting with the talent tree. Wanted to create a melee+totem-twist focused enh build with added utility from bl.
Gave up many talents from ele for it. Do you think this can work for PVE?

![Image](https://i.postimg.cc/KjBQ1mNj/pic.png)

Wanted nature's guidance for hit reliability and went 3 talents deep into totemic focus to make twisting more manageable.
Kept every enh talent which gives an offensive melee support.
In ele I went for cheaper shocks and bigger fire totems. Gave up on shock CD reduction, clearcasting and elemental devastation. First two is ok for me, I wanna theorycraft a less shock-heavy build. Lack of elemental devastation kinda hurts but it is too deep in ele tree plus my test subject won't really have high enough spell crit% to make it reliable.

What I wanna accomplish with this build:
Either
Melee hit focused, utility DPS. Pull happens, you run in. WF, strength, mana and magma totems are down, magma gives a decent amount of damage by itself. WF and grace of air are twisted. Shocks come on CD but not big emphasis. Made them as cheap as possible, focus is on maintained totem twisting while hitting.
Or
The more support-oriented version. Barely a melee anymore. Same with nightfall. You put down the totems, twist, shock on CD and nature's guidance helps to proc that nightfall more consistently.

In short:
 * less bonus for shocks
 * cheaper totems for better twisting

Do you think it would work?

author: Bigsmerf
subject: Enh sham suggestions
content_md:
Don't worry, no wacky suggestions or primal strikes here, just some little tweaking ideas from someone with extremely limited knowledge. Down below is everything I've thought up or gathered from other posts. Mostly other people's ideas.

Nature's guidance (the hit talent I think) is not a healer talent. Put it early in enh or maybe ele, but preferably enh since that's the spec we're here to help.

Stormstrike doesn't work good right now. I'd probably lower the mana cost by a bit, and turn the effect into something that increases ALL nature damage instead of just 2 instances of damage for maybe half the time the CD lasts, so it's not up all the time but still offers a pretty consistent bump to dps for other shams and general nature effects/balance druids that use wrath.

Give a new rank of earth shock that doesn't do extra threat but is otherwise the same as regular earth shock. Would let you go ham on bosses in the beginning. Could remove the interrupt but that might add some bloat in forcing you to use two earth shocks on a class that already has tons of buttons to press.

Maybe do a similar thing with rockbiter weapon wherein you don't deal extra threat but the damage is the same.

Make Ancestral knowledge give 2% max mana per point and 10% when capped out. It's not a lot but it'll help with mana more than it normally would. Maybe swap it for Elemental Devastation in the ele tree too because that is NOT an ele talent in the slightest.

Make thunderhead change lightning shield to also discharge when you cast it on yourself, when you STRIKE an enemy, instead of being struck by them, you take up an orb charge and deal 50% of regular orb damage. This would give it use for a raiding sham that never gets hit and would bump up DPS by a good bit. BUT, you can only cast it on yourself every 30 seconds, so you're not spamming it and wasting mana but also making things busted, 'cause admittedly this might be a pretty drastic change.

Maybe change thundering strikes to also refund 2% mana per melee and/or earthshock crit, but make it so the effect only happens every... Ten seconds, I guess.

So then- what do we think? Am I butchering the entire game balance with this, or do we think it'll all work out pretty decent and bump enh up to become a bit more desirable to bring along/play as? I'm sure some of this isn't essential since shaman as a class already brings so much to the table for a group, but it's cool to speculate.

Make Ancestral knowledge give 2% max mana per point and 10% when capped out. It's not a lot but it'll help with mana more than it normally would. Maybe swap it for Elemental Devastation in the ele tree too because that is NOT an ele talent in the slightest.

Make thunderhead change lightning shield to also discharge when you cast it on yourself, when you STRIKE an enemy, instead of being struck by them, you take up an orb charge and deal 50% of regular orb damage. This would give it use for a raiding sham that never gets hit and would bump up DPS by a good bit. BUT, you can only cast it on yourself every 30 seconds, so you're not spamming it and wasting mana but also making things busted, 'cause admittedly this might be a pretty drastic change.

Maybe change thundering strikes to also refund 2% mana per melee and/or earthshock crit, but make it so the effect only happens every... Ten seconds, I guess.


So then- what do we think? Am I butchering the entire game balance with this, or do we think it'll all work out pretty decent and bump enh up to become a bit more desirable to bring along/play as? I'm sure some of this isn't essential since shaman as a class already brings so much to the table for a group, but it's cool to speculate.

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: Shaman's most urgent adjustment
content_md:
I think that adding to the enhancement combat rotation leads to a dilemma.
Every +melee hit you grant them is a potential WF proc which can loop into itself. Honestly, in PVE I wouldn't find it unfair since fury warriors usually have access to WF in raids and them spamming hamstring is not frowned upon. But in PVP it could be disgusting.

One workaround would be to somewhat nerf the WF effect but honestly, that would cause an uproar in the community (my idea would disallow WF procs to be procced from WF procs).
Adding new shock-like effects wouldn't help imo. Enh shamans can already shock every 5 sec and allowing a melee class to have a shock-like effect every 2-3 sec would be oppressive.
I see two design spaces as workarounds.
 1. Give them a melee haste talent, for example 10% haste for 5 tp. Sounds extreme but it would only have 2 effects: enh shamans would autohit every 2,7 sec not 3 sec with a 3 sec 2h weapon -> somewhat less downtime and tanks would be better with threat since they wanna spam rockbiter procs on targets.
 2. A raptor strike-like effect which makes your next auto-attack stronger. Would feel like doing something instead of spamming auto-attack on a slow weapon, would increase DPS and this ability would only enhance one strike, meaning that WF procs won't become disgustingly powerful.

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: [beta]Shaman's most urgent adjustment
content_md:
I will give a more detailed answer this time but first I need to rant a bit.
Honestly, I've nowhere else seen the toxicity level for classes that shamans and palas produce.
Most shaman players live by the narrative that they are 'oppressed' by the evil, pala-maining admins while palas frequently combine a weird superiority complex with arrogance and by being extremely butthurt towards every pala-related criticism.
I agree that shaman classes are still not totally coherent (specially enhancement) but you guys still remember the old days of a more expensive stormstrike on a 20 second CD, lack of bloodlust, lack of water and earth shields, lack of totemic recall, having to relearn 2H weapons every time you respecced, having parry (!) as a talent in the tree and having to waste a bunch of time for CDs every time you wanted to totem twist? Shamans are so ignored and oppressed here that they are the only class receiving (admittedly bad) custom class racials.

I agree that there are problems. Devs probably didn't have an experienced shaman player among them when the balance updates were made because some of these changes were weird/useless (like thunderhead) or they just didn't solve something obvious (hit/spell hit talent is still not in enhancement tree).
In the meanwhile palas got a decent help and became an absolutely valid class for each build (I won't go into details for PVP, they are definitely a problem there). Imo the difference is that while devs wanted the best both for pala and shaman, they only knew in case of pala what they were doing. But noone oppresses the shamans, just compare what they had in Vanilla and what they have here.
PS: Don't ban me, devs. Love y'all.
Rant off.

For more exact changes, I'd like to check what the current builds have or lack.

Ele ->
+ Good burst
+ General shaman utility
+ Very good at PVP
 - Mana is still an issue but consumes helped a lot
 - Threat. They can't use their threat reduction totem because team wants WF
 - Spell penetration. They keep spamming nature damage but have no way to handle high nat rez mobs

Change ideas:
 * Either give them a threat reduction talent or put tranquil air totem to fire element (after renaming it). This way ele threat problems are not so bad anymore.
 * Buff ancestral knowledge from 5% to 10% mana. This is arguably the weakest +mana/int talent in the game and the class which has it has to spam totems every minute, always interruptiong full spirit mana regen
 * Change back clearcasting -> 100% discount for 1 spell not 40% for 2. Helps timing chain lightning and can help reach full spirit mana regen
 * Give them a talent which reduces the target's chance to resist nature damage

Enh ->
+ Has some key utility
 - A weird patchwork of good/bad (totem) utilities, tanking talents and DPS talents, a totally incoherent tree
 - Not enough talent to make tanking viable, not enough talent to make melee DPS good
 - You rely on a slow 2H as a DPS and people can't really give melee talents to you because you could really go off at PVP with that amout of WF procs

Change ideas:
 * As said, ancestral knowledge going up to 10% mana
 * Giving them a new strike which only makes the next auto-attack stronger (no added WF proc)
 * Thunderhead being useful (f.ex. adding n% bonus for each shield).
 * Loved Atreidon's idea, giving ghost wolf the above-discussed effect
 * Moving elemental devastation and +hit talent to enhancement tree

Honestly, a raptor strike, better shields, more cleverly placed talents and slightly more mana could mostly solve enh problems.

For tanks:
I did some tanking with shaman but no raid tanking. My experiences are until up until Black Morass where I was seriously overgeared when I was messing around.

 * Linking fire totem damage to shaman as threat
 * Increasing fire totem threat
 * New earth shock level, giving taunt - much less damage but can't be resisted (spell can still miss - wanna avoid a taunt which can both miss and can also be resisted)
 * A defensive CD
 * Better stoneclaw totem

Resto ->
I like them mostly. They are really good.
+ Best raid heal
+ Usual utility
 - Mana during leveling
 - End-tree is so insignificant, people take bloodlust over like 20 healing talents

Change ideas:
 * Make totemic recall even better (more mana back when recalling). That + the 10% added mana should help.
 * Make the end of the tree more interesting. Honestly, noone gives a damn about mana tide in a server where mana problems are almost solved at raiding (spriests, arcane mages, tea, custom consumes like merlot, bunch of meditation items). Even the talent above that. Really? 5 point to make the most useless totem (healing) into a less useless but still useless totem? Scrap those 6 talent points and make something interesting. Riptide, spirit link, something original, whatever. Interesting but not broken it shall be.

+1 thing
Their change to reduce stormstrike CD from 20 sec to 12 sec shows that they cared and they also had a 'gameplan' but they lacked deep knowledge about shamans.
TWOW stormstrike CD is matching shock CDx2. I guess the base idea was that the enhancement shaman keeps up flame shock at every 2nd shock CD and will usually go for earth shock in the others. Meaning flameshock 1x every 12 seconds and earth shock (amplified by stormstrike) every other 12 seconds.
The problem is that 99% of the enhancement shamans who have stormstrike also have the elemental talent which reduces shock CD to 5 sec. It is so common that seeing an enhancement shaman with a 6 sec shock CD is very rare.
And here the whole thing becomes clunky, because the ability which was designed to flawlessly merge with your shock schedule gets off CD at very inappropriate times.
So adding to enhancement change ideas:
 * Stormstrike CD to 10 sec.

author: Akos1896
subject: The shaman tanking experience
content_md:
Hey!

First off, I'm not Shockwarden or a highly experienced shaman tank. I don't want to give such false vibes that the things I write about are words from an expert. I'm an average shaman who tried out tanking and giving my impressions about it.
 **The goal is to give some practical advices for those who also wanna give it a shot.**

This article is NOT for experienced shaman tanks who tanked raids. Those guys know this stuff better than I do.

For actual experts, I propose this (very good but refers to Vanilla, TWOW changes are not mentioned there):
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kKQnV-kpDhU&t=1347s>

 **Note: Some of the things I mentioned are factually incorrect.**
Correction1: Rockbiter gives TPS, a slower weapon gets more threat for the hit (but if hit is missed, that's a larger time window without threat).
Correction2: Rockbiter doesn't stack with WF totem buff. WF is not good for shaman tanks.

After testing out shaman tanking I have to say that it is possible but it requires a different approach than usual tanks. In short, you have to 'outsorce' more, usually to DPS. With proper gear and enchants (this is a must - if you decide to shaman tank, you start from a disadvantage, you have to be okay with farming good items and using enchants like the +2% threat glove one) you are able to reliably keep around 3 mobs. This means that at certain pulls you will need help.

 **In general:**
 * Always check your group composition and know which classes can provide which CC. Do you have hybernate, sap, sheep, fear etc in your arsenal? If the pull seems to be too big to properly handle, ask a party member to CC one of them. Keeping the number of targets at a manageable amount is key.
 * Consider asking a melee DPS to offtank one mob if the pull is too big (even after CC). A hunter pet, a druid, a warrior, a rogue, a pala or an enh shaman should be perfectly able to keep one elite mob focused. Usually the skull. This way by the time the DPS targets 'your mobs', you've built up a high threat on them.
 * Symbols are key, specifically for a shaman tank. Always have the below symbols keybinded: 1st target, 2nd target, CC target, offtank target, a symbol to mark patrol. When skull dies, changes marks accordingly, it is your responsibility as a tank.
 * You are very weak regarding AoE threat. Ask the casters not to AoE unless it is a big pack consisting of many mobs which die fast.
 1. If you are fighting 3 elite mobs and keeping threat properly, a caster doing AoE messes up everything. Mobs will probably go rampant, people will probably die. Never allow this.
 2. If there's a pack with a bunch of non-elite mobs for example, accept your fate - you won't be tanking those properly. Open with a chain lightning, run in and help the work of the caster - use earthgrab and fire nova/magma. Earthgrab makes sure that those mobs die by the time they'd reach the caster while the fire totems help killing them. If the pack consists of many weak minions, you don't tank, you help the kiting/AoE process.
 3. If there are some elites and many trash, focus on those elites. Tank those and help casters clear up the trash via earthbind and fire nova/magma.
 * You don't have a taunt but you have many ways to generate a lot of threat if you are well-geared/enchanted (it is a must). Discuss things with the party. Tell them, that if they pull aggro, they should run to you and stop damaging immediately. Their threat will drop. You take over the threat. As a shaman tank you will never get aggro back if someone pulls and then goes all in on the DPS-meter while the mob is running towards him. Make it clear that if aggro happens, DPS has to stop on the target.
 * Forget stoneskin totem 90% of the time. The prerequisite of the whole shaman tanking thing is to be geared enough to be able to take some hits. You need strength totem much more.
 * Both grace of air and windfury totem are a good choice. Grace of air gives you dodge and crit chance which helps with flurry and clearcasting. However, people underestimate windfury for shaman tanks. It helps melee threat, including you. The thing is that your primary job is to keep the healer alive. If you put down a windfury totem, melee DPS can aggro much more frequently but it is fine as they should be able to take some hits. If you use windfury, you risk losing threat to melee for added DPS and for making sure that casters and healers have a real hard time taking aggro.
 * In very situational cases you can use tranquil air totem. If you don't talent totem radius increase, your totems will have a 20 yard radius. If some casters are really problematic, you can put down a tranquil air in the back and run towards the target. If the caster is within totem range and casting range while you are out of totem range, you reduced caster threat by 20%. It costs your grace of air or windfury totem though.
 * Spamming fire nova and stoneclaw totem right after eachother generates some AoE threat. But it is expensive, has high CD and the generated threat is low. Use only if you really need that AoE threat.

One last thing regarding this part. Again, know your teammates and have a general knowledge about how other classes work. It helps if someone pulls aggro too frequently. If this person is using a specific ability, you might ask them to avoid using that. Have ShaguDPS installed so you see who does what when dealing damage, it helps analyizing why certain aggroes happen.
For the below: any of the below abilities can be fine during a run if they don't cause overaggro. It is only needed to intervene if the below things cause problems during the run.

Some examples:
 * A warlock using searing pain. It's a no-no. Also, warlocks usually have no way to reduce their threat. You might want to ask them to start with curse and corruption so you have time to establish threat before their big hitters come.
 * A shaman opening with a chain lightning is a no. Ask him to hold back a bit so you can establish threat. Also, a shaman using earth shock or having rockbiter weapon on can be a problem.
 * Shadow priest using vampiric embrace. Passive lifegain is good but it has a lot of threat. Advised to use it only at bosses.
 * Warrior spamming heroic strike. Honestly, just let it be, he should be able to tank the mob.
 * Hunter pets growling. Should never happen unless there's an emergency.
 * Pala having righteous fury on. Probably a mistake. Also, if you have threat problems, ask the pala to put salvation on the problematic person (check threatmeter to know who's problematic).
 * Mage or warlock spamming AoE if they see more than 1 mob. That will ruin your tanking (see earlier part).
 * Rogue for any reason using agitating poison.

 **Regarding your toolkit:**

You have earth shock for spell threat every 5 seconds - use at least 3 ranks. Rank 1 for interrupt, mid-rank for threat spike if you don't need to pump threat and max rank if you need as much threat as possible.
You have flame shock which helps you keeping threat on a mob for 12 seconds. Use it only if you don't think you need to 'taunt' within 5 seconds. You can use it on a secondary target to keep threat on it or on your main target to maximize threat. I think max rank alone is enough.
You have elemental shields. For lightning, use at least three ranks again. Max rank for big threat, first rank if you are really low on mana and an inbetween solution. Honestly I mostly advise lightning shield for leveling or when you need max threat. I don't really like it since it is a bit unreliable which target gets the threat.
Water shield is my usual go-to elemental shield when tanking. As long as something is punching you, you get a bunch of mana. Keep it on all the time if possible. Honestly, water shield helped that much that I frequently had close to full mana when the mages asked to stop for a drink. Just don't overuse your abilities and your mana is spared. No matter if you keep threat by 3% or 80%, if you consistently keep it, go cheap, slack some shocks etc and recharge mana for the next pull.
Earth shield is your go to shield for real big hitters, usually certain bosses. Use only if target hits REALLY big.
You also have stormstrike which is a very good tanking tool. Put it to a big button on PFUI so you always see how much time you have left until you can use it again. Whenever I pull, I stormstrike skull first to initiate threat. If you need to maximize threat on a target, just stormstrike, earthshock and...
And bloodlust. As a tank, this ability is for you. Use it when you immediately need a threat spike. 20% haste is really nice, it helps a lot.
And of course rockbiter.

That's your basic tanking tool.
However, consumables/engineering items and racials can further help. If you wanna shaman tank, you have to get engineering. As a D tier tank you have to take every option to make yourself more viable.
Just make sure that you have some target dummies and sappers at your disposal. Don't overuse them. Would zero down your wallet and you'd totally lose motivation to do this. Only use them if you find it extremely important that in this specific situation aggro has to be kept. Don't use it everytime you lose aggro or you go bankrupt. Unless you're mega-rich then do whatever you want.

For racials: each race has something going for it.
Orcs mostly have the weapon skill. If you find a good, fast axe (remember, rockbiter has a static added threat, you need a fast weapon - for a shaman tank a weapon with above 2 sec weapon speed just doesn't exist) that weapon skill can help a lot. Easier itemization etc. However class changes wil in theory change how weapon skill is working. It is possible that orc will be the only suboptimal choice for shaman tanking very soon.
Taurens have added health and war stomp (if only spirit link were castable on yourself...). Added health is always nice on a fragile tank and war stomp can help if you are overwhelmed with mobs.
My personal favourite though is the troll. Berserking. You basically receive a second bloodlust on a 3 minute CD. These two make sure that you can receive extra haste almost any time, so you can consistently rely on it whenever you need more threat.

This is the talent tree I was using:
![Image](https://i.postimg.cc/J0rsJJm8/Talent.png)

It has strengths and weaknesses:
+ Gives both good melee DPS and also a good damage coming from shocks
+ Has all the defensives I need
+ I consider stormstrike and bloodlust totally necessary tanking abilities

 - Mana problems have to be solved by clearcasting and water shield. Totems are expensive and have small radius.
 - Hit chance.

Hit chance is the really big one. I've never raided as a shaman tank and now I'd need a bunch of hit and spell hit to punch reliably. However, taking that talent in the restoration tree takes away too many crucial talents.
Right now I wait and see what class changes bring and if you can get hit+spell hit without sacrificing the core of what you are trying to do, I might try that out.

For items/stats:
Get some intellect but only until you feel comfortable tanking if you don't overspend your resources and water shield is recharging you all the time. Once it's manageable, ignore int.
Agility and stamina every day. Agility helps you dodge (you are quite good at dodging in general), gives some armor and gives melee crit which makes things cheaper via clearcasting and flurry helps with threat. But top prio has to be stamina, you are the fragilest tank after all.
Strength to some degree for bigger hits (to get good threat both from rockbiter and from the damage you deal) and bigger blocked amount. But don't forget you'll usually have a strength totem down, meaning that you'll magically get 88 strength anytime.

Melee crit. Very important.
Haste -> Almost as important. For you melee crit basically gives haste via flurry. But still, the faster you hit the targets, the more rockbiter 'stacks' you apply. As a shaman tank the name of the game is hitting them as fast as possible. Fast weapon, bloodlust, flurry, haste items: you keep aggro by distributing packages of threat super fast.
Dodge is also good, specially via enchants. Get the Kara enchant which gives 2 dodge to a head or leg item. With the 5 dodge from talents, the 2x2% kara enchant dodge and the cloak enchant dodge you'll start off with 10% base dodge. Since you are kinda fragile, the best thing you can do is to avoid hits totally. Unlike bears and warriors, you don't wanna be hit for getting rage.
Before I forget: thorium spikes onto the shield! You need that thorn-effect. Also, don't consider speed enchant on the boot, you need the stamina one. Threat enchant on gloves is a must. Other than that, what you deem the best for yourself. I use agility on my belt but I can easily see someone needing the int more. You really need the enchants to fight the handicap of tanking as a shaman, don't slack it off.

In my opinion:
stam>agi>melee crit>haste> dodge/parry>strength>int

I advise using a weapon swap macro and having at least two (enchanted) weapons. One for threat, one for survival (added armor, parry chance, whatever makes you die harder). If there's a big problem, switch to survival weapon.
Don't slack off consumes. Have health pots available, keybinded.

 **Lastly some tips how different classes can help you:**

 **Druid:** Generic buffs, thorns, innervate. If the guy is a DPS you can ask him anytime to bear-offtank a target. Also roots outdoors and hybernate.
 **Hunter:** Helps with problematic pulls, can handle his threat, pet can OT, hunter can kite, can give trueshot aura (sometimes). Also, freezing trap is a very good CC to take away one mob from the pull.
 **Mage:** Drink machine, intellect buff, sheep and freezes. Don't underestimate slows and freezes, even encourage the mage to use them if you face any trouble with keeping threat.
 **Rogue:** Sap, can offtank,, best stuns, can handle his threat. Interrupts.
 **Paladin:** Very good blessings, also the option to put salvation on an overeager DPS. Can stun a target and has extra utility against undeads. Ask actively for blessing of freedom if you get a lot of movement impairment in a dungeon.
 **Warlock:** Ask for imp buff and healthstone. King of fears, just make sure you cleared up enough space and pull back if fear is needed. Also banish. Never trust enslave demon.
 **Priest:** Shackle undead, priest buffs, fear. Also, if priest is holy, ask for the champion buff which gives attack and spell power. You need every bit of threat you can get. Also you don't use rage, you can be shielded. Ask for shields.
 **Shaman:** Discuss who does which totems, both grace of air and windfury can be huge. King of ranged interrupts.
 **Warrior:** Interrupts, shout, offtanking, fear. Give him a WF and in exchange ask him to harmstring melee targets so even if you guys lose aggro to a caster, mobs are slow and die by the time they get there.

content_html:
Hey!

First off, I'm not Shockwarden or a highly experienced shaman tank. I don't want to give such false vibes that the things I write about are words from an expert. I'm an average shaman who tried out tanking and giving my impressions about it.
The goal is to give some practical advices for those who also wanna give it a shot.

This article is NOT for experienced shaman tanks who tanked raids. Those guys know this stuff better than I do.

For actual experts, I propose this (very good but refers to Vanilla, TWOW changes are not mentioned there):
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kKQnV-kpDhU&t=1347s

Note: Some of the things I mentioned are factually incorrect.
Correction1: Rockbiter gives TPS, a slower weapon gets more threat for the hit (but if hit is missed, that's a larger time window without threat).
Correction2: Rockbiter doesn't stack with WF totem buff. WF is not good for shaman tanks.

After testing out shaman tanking I have to say that it is possible but it requires a different approach than usual tanks. In short, you have to 'outsorce' more, usually to DPS. With proper gear and enchants (this is a must - if you decide to shaman tank, you start from a disadvantage, you have to be okay with farming good items and using enchants like the +2% threat glove one) you are able to reliably keep around 3 mobs. This means that at certain pulls you will need help.

In general:
* Always check your group composition and know which classes can provide which CC. Do you have hybernate, sap, sheep, fear etc in your arsenal? If the pull seems to be too big to properly handle, ask a party member to CC one of them. Keeping the number of targets at a manageable amount is key.
* Consider asking a melee DPS to offtank one mob if the pull is too big (even after CC). A hunter pet, a druid, a warrior, a rogue, a pala or an enh shaman should be perfectly able to keep one elite mob focused. Usually the skull. This way by the time the DPS targets 'your mobs', you've built up a high threat on them.
* Symbols are key, specifically for a shaman tank. Always have the below symbols keybinded: 1st target, 2nd target, CC target, offtank target, a symbol to mark patrol. When skull dies, changes marks accordingly, it is your responsibility as a tank.
* You are very weak regarding AoE threat. Ask the casters not to AoE unless it is a big pack consisting of many mobs which die fast.
1. If you are fighting 3 elite mobs and keeping threat properly, a caster doing AoE messes up everything. Mobs will probably go rampant, people will probably die. Never allow this.
2. If there's a pack with a bunch of non-elite mobs for example, accept your fate - you won't be tanking those properly. Open with a chain lightning, run in and help the work of the caster - use earthgrab and fire nova/magma. Earthgrab makes sure that those mobs die by the time they'd reach the caster while the fire totems help killing them. If the pack consists of many weak minions, you don't tank, you help the kiting/AoE process.
3. If there are some elites and many trash, focus on those elites. Tank those and help casters clear up the trash via earthbind and fire nova/magma.
* You don't have a taunt but you have many ways to generate a lot of threat if you are well-geared/enchanted (it is a must). Discuss things with the party. Tell them, that if they pull aggro, they should run to you and stop damaging immediately. Their threat will drop. You take over the threat. As a shaman tank you will never get aggro back if someone pulls and then goes all in on the DPS-meter while the mob is running towards him. Make it clear that if aggro happens, DPS has to stop on the target.
* Forget stoneskin totem 90% of the time. The prerequisite of the whole shaman tanking thing is to be geared enough to be able to take some hits. You need strength totem much more.
* Both grace of air and windfury totem are a good choice. Grace of air gives you dodge and crit chance which helps with flurry and clearcasting. However, people underestimate windfury for shaman tanks. It helps melee threat, including you. The thing is that your primary job is to keep the healer alive. If you put down a windfury totem, melee DPS can aggro much more frequently but it is fine as they should be able to take some hits. If you use windfury, you risk losing threat to melee for added DPS and for making sure that casters and healers have a real hard time taking aggro.
* In very situational cases you can use tranquil air totem. If you don't talent totem radius increase, your totems will have a 20 yard radius. If some casters are really problematic, you can put down a tranquil air in the back and run towards the target. If the caster is within totem range and casting range while you are out of totem range, you reduced caster threat by 20%. It costs your grace of air or windfury totem though.
* Spamming fire nova and stoneclaw totem right after eachother generates some AoE threat. But it is expensive, has high CD and the generated threat is low. Use only if you really need that AoE threat.

One last thing regarding this part. Again, know your teammates and have a general knowledge about how other classes work. It helps if someone pulls aggro too frequently. If this person is using a specific ability, you might ask them to avoid using that. Have ShaguDPS installed so you see who does what when dealing damage, it helps analyizing why certain aggroes happen.
For the below: any of the below abilities can be fine during a run if they don't cause overaggro. It is only needed to intervene if the below things cause problems during the run.

Some examples:
* A warlock using searing pain. It's a no-no. Also, warlocks usually have no way to reduce their threat. You might want to ask them to start with curse and corruption so you have time to establish threat before their big hitters come.
* A shaman opening with a chain lightning is a no. Ask him to hold back a bit so you can establish threat. Also, a shaman using earth shock or having rockbiter weapon on can be a problem.
* Shadow priest using vampiric embrace. Passive lifegain is good but it has a lot of threat. Advised to use it only at bosses.
* Warrior spamming heroic strike. Honestly, just let it be, he should be able to tank the mob.
* Hunter pets growling. Should never happen unless there's an emergency.
* Pala having righteous fury on. Probably a mistake. Also, if you have threat problems, ask the pala to put salvation on the problematic person (check threatmeter to know who's problematic).
* Mage or warlock spamming AoE if they see more than 1 mob. That will ruin your tanking (see earlier part).
* Rogue for any reason using agitating poison.

Regarding your toolkit:

You have earth shock for spell threat every 5 seconds - use at least 3 ranks. Rank 1 for interrupt, mid-rank for threat spike if you don't need to pump threat and max rank if you need as much threat as possible.
You have flame shock which helps you keeping threat on a mob for 12 seconds. Use it only if you don't think you need to 'taunt' within 5 seconds. You can use it on a secondary target to keep threat on it or on your main target to maximize threat. I think max rank alone is enough.
You have elemental shields. For lightning, use at least three ranks again. Max rank for big threat, first rank if you are really low on mana and an inbetween solution. Honestly I mostly advise lightning shield for leveling or when you need max threat. I don't really like it since it is a bit unreliable which target gets the threat.
Water shield is my usual go-to elemental shield when tanking. As long as something is punching you, you get a bunch of mana. Keep it on all the time if possible. Honestly, water shield helped that much that I frequently had close to full mana when the mages asked to stop for a drink. Just don't overuse your abilities and your mana is spared. No matter if you keep threat by 3% or 80%, if you consistently keep it, go cheap, slack some shocks etc and recharge mana for the next pull.
Earth shield is your go to shield for real big hitters, usually certain bosses. Use only if target hits REALLY big.
You also have stormstrike which is a very good tanking tool. Put it to a big button on PFUI so you always see how much time you have left until you can use it again. Whenever I pull, I stormstrike skull first to initiate threat. If you need to maximize threat on a target, just stormstrike, earthshock and...
And bloodlust. As a tank, this ability is for you. Use it when you immediately need a threat spike. 20% haste is really nice, it helps a lot.
And of course rockbiter.

That's your basic tanking tool.
However, consumables/engineering items and racials can further help. If you wanna shaman tank, you have to get engineering. As a D tier tank you have to take every option to make yourself more viable.
Just make sure that you have some target dummies and sappers at your disposal. Don't overuse them. Would zero down your wallet and you'd totally lose motivation to do this. Only use them if you find it extremely important that in this specific situation aggro has to be kept. Don't use it everytime you lose aggro or you go bankrupt. Unless you're mega-rich then do whatever you want.

For racials: each race has something going for it.
Orcs mostly have the weapon skill. If you find a good, fast axe (remember, rockbiter has a static added threat, you need a fast weapon - for a shaman tank a weapon with above 2 sec weapon speed just doesn't exist) that weapon skill can help a lot. Easier itemization etc. However class changes wil in theory change how weapon skill is working. It is possible that orc will be the only suboptimal choice for shaman tanking very soon.
Taurens have added health and war stomp (if only spirit link were castable on yourself...). Added health is always nice on a fragile tank and war stomp can help if you are overwhelmed with mobs.
My personal favourite though is the troll. Berserking. You basically receive a second bloodlust on a 3 minute CD. These two make sure that you can receive extra haste almost any time, so you can consistently rely on it whenever you need more threat.

It has strengths and weaknesses:
+ Gives both good melee DPS and also a good damage coming from shocks
+ Has all the defensives I need
+ I consider stormstrike and bloodlust totally necessary tanking abilities

- Mana problems have to be solved by clearcasting and water shield. Totems are expensive and have small radius.

Hit chance is the really big one. I've never raided as a shaman tank and now I'd need a bunch of hit and spell hit to punch reliably. However, taking that talent in the restoration tree takes away too many crucial talents.

subject: [alpha]Improving utilization ratio of  Earth，Light, Water Shield
content_md:
There is no doubt that these three shield skills are extremely effective and practical. Because of this, you must always keep an eye on the BUFF column during combat to ensure that it can be replenished when it disappears. If you reuse it before it is exhausted, a lot of mana will be wasted. unfortunately, this spell is consumed and used very frequently, This causes you to either constantly stare at its consumption, or frequently waste a lot of mana, which makes it unbearable.

I think there needs to be a way to make them easier to use. My suggestion is to delay the mana cost of this spell until the time the skill takes effect, not when the skill is used.

content_md:
On quite the contrary, enhancement is famously in pve quite the bad spec. and even still, you see quite a few of em. That is a testiment that the gameplay of the class is desirable for players. It has a performance problem, not a boring gameplay.

You say you are not, but you are trying to change shamans gameplay with the suggested change.

There are alternative solutions you could propose that would achieve a similar performance improvement without also altering the gameplay. here are a few:
Reduce base manacost of Earth & / or Lightning shield.
Make earth & /or Lightning Shield consume elemental focus charges for reduced mana cost.

author: Manletow
subject: Thunderhead: A Beautiful Failure
content_md:
Thunderhead is a custom T-WoW Talent that:
"Allows Lightning Shield to be cast on one friendly target. Also reduces Lightning Shields cost by 20%"

Whoever created this should be hailed as a 200 IQ champion of Turtle WoW and the Shaman Class.   turtle_in_love_head
They understand precisely how Enhancement Shaman is meant to be played and how it should be designed.

Reasons why "Thunderhead" is S-Tier Game Design:
- 1) Instead of being some corny/broken new ability -- it simply takes an existing ability and allows it to be used in a fresh way. This is clever, conservative, and reduces ability-bloat.
 2) It gives the player an actually desirable reward for investing 3 Talent Points into the normally god-awful 'Improved Lightning Shield".
 3) It gives Shaman a "normal" Magic-type buff to apply. It's amusing game-play variation from the often tedious normality of being 'tied to totems' if you want to buff anyone. (The Water Walking/Breathing buffs dont count.)
 4) It doubles down on the class fantasy of "Enhancing Others" and being "A Supporter". **Based!**
 5) It addresses a very common complaint of 'not getting value from Shields unless personally getting hit'.
 6) It addresses a very common complaint of 'Lightning Shield costing too much'.
 7) It addresses a very common complaint of 'Having nothing to do while waiting for Stormstrike CD.' You will be refreshing this on the Main Tank often.
 8) It synergizes with your Stormstrike debuff (if you are afraid to use Earth Shock due to threat).
 9) It has unlimited range (very bizarre but bemusing to buff someone from 500 yards away. KEK)
... yet despite all this -- 'Thunderhead' has been a (nearly) complete failure. Why? Simple:
It got mega cucked by the newly added Water/Earth Shields.   crying_turtle
These fresh faced custom competitors are excellent and do NOT require a 4 Talent Point investment.

(also I will admit -- Shaman already have Mana issues so keeping Lightning Shield constantly refreshed was unrealistic)

However; it was at least not an 'Epic' Fail because it still saw some use from level 20-59 Shamans (mostly just for the 20% reduction)

Anyway this post is a loving tribute to this 'soon to be removed/replaced' ability/talent.
(Its getting swapped in favor of a new Melee attack that is basically Holy Strike Jr. -- Devs are caving to the endless whining for 'moar deepz' and making a Shield into an ability that you actively attack people with.)

Good night, sweet prince. You were too pure for this World (of Warcraft).   dead_turtle_head

author: Spacepony
subject: Deep resto
content_md:
This post is about ideas to adjust the restoration tree, especially the bottom of the tree.

Is it possible to improve the bottom of the tree while:
 1) not making resto shamans overpowered in PVE
 2) preserving the unique strengths and weaknesses of different classes
 3) making deep resto more desirable than deep enhance etc for shamans who want to heal

I find it hard to reconcile these 3 goals.  One idea is that deep resto has a lot of room for improvement in PvP and it would still stay mediocre.  I would like to see a talent like Nature’s Guardian that was introduced in TBC:

“Whenever a damaging attack is taken that reduces you below 30% health, you have a 50% chance to heal 10% of your total health and reduce your threat level on that target.  X second cooldown.”

Then at least a deep resto build would gain more survivability in PVP which seems like a fair trade off for eschewing the huge damage boost of deep elemental.

I could also see talents that support earth shield being a good avenue to pursue, as this seems like it would help Shaman healers in some content without buffing chain heal  output in raids.

Curious what others would suggest.

subject: [alpha] Talent StormReach should also act on purge
content_md:
purge is a powerful means of attack for a shaman, but what does a 30-yard range mean?

Means that shaman's lightning chain is meaningless when the enemy enters the shaman's 36 yard range, because when the enemy enters the 30 yard and passes through your purge spell, their health will be full.

So, StormReach(Increases the range of your Lightning Bolt and Chain Lightning spells by 3 yards) should also act on purge.

I think a lot of us are disappointed with overall changes to shamans and most classes. We wanted some changes, but a lot of these are out of nowhere and have blindsided us.

author: Voodoochile
subject: Re: I don't want 1.17.2
content_md:
I know I cant speak for everyone when I say this, but the appeal for shaman to me is the buffing and utility of the class. Some of my most fun in vanilla is totem twisting WF/Agi, or WF/Nature Res Totem and keeping Ancestral Healing up as often as I could with r1 healing waves in downtime and managing mana gear and items and Mana Tide to maintain the buffs.

But with these changes, to my understanding totem-twisting is dead, as resto any micro in regards to mana conservation and restoration has been handicapped for the lowest common denominator who REFUSE to use their totems on the class who's unique feature is exactly that and replaced instead with passive proc chances...

Is this retail? This SOUNDS like retail.

You guys talk about 'slow-cast high value AOE healing' as well while making a talent that makes it a 2 second cast and making it just worse for the other specs who are already NOT GEARING FOR HEALING. You guys are actually just devolving our hybrid class of choice into another specialist by nerfing the base kit and lower portions of the talent trees.

Why not lock the other trees until you get the capstone while we're at it? Ooo, how about lightning bolt regens your mana too, and maybe add a-a-a-a secondary resource that you build up and spend on different spells? Shamans are AOE healers right? Why not make it, idk, RAIN or something to heal in an AOE? Maybe make healing totem 2 charges? Give shamans an ability to cast while moving while we're at it.

After seeing how the team has responded to it, I believe you are correct in saying that it was an oversight for them.

But it doesn't make sense that it would be problematic when being a utility class is the CORE of shamans. Shamans are NOT Warriors, they are NOT Priests, and they are NOT Mages. Why shouldn't we be allowed to lean into the core identity of the class we choose?

It is truly disheartening that to even deliberately move the totem talents in the enh tree up to the FIFTH row from their original 2nd and 3rd row is a good design choice in their mind.

They are designing around players who pick shaman to completely REFUSE to use their unique utility in their base kit. They are designing shamans around people who want to be WARRIOR DPS, PRIEST HEALS, and MAGE DPS.

They are making you choose to be a specialist when you decided to be a hybrid class generalist in character select, and nerf the core mechanic that sits square on the shaman identity

Now, now, dont be so rash... I follow what you are saying, and I share some of your opion, to me Shaman's, Paladin's and Druid's always have been the Jack of all Trades, capable of doing a little of everything, and doing just fine if you try it hard enough.

But as such, those class should have been Masters of None, because if they can do everything at once, and been great too, then who would play the other class? I mean, they should NOT top the rankings on DPS, Healing, Tanking, just because they can do all at once.

Anyway, the changes on the Shaman tree dont seems bad to my at all, to be honest, they where need it to boost the support rol, but the localitation of some talents in the row is what it feel wrong:

Elemental:
Flame Guidance it should be a baseline skill if you ask me, is worthy to have as a Resto Shaman to help you party with a little DPS, because a good healer can and must put some DPS, not been a heal bot only. But fine if it should be on the talent tree, but not in the 5th row, 2th or 3th it should be the place. In the first place, it doesnt boost your DPS, is just QoL, so with is so deep?

Call of Flame can stay where it is, but I should move it to the 5th row, and give the talent the boost to the Crit Damage compounen of the Flame Totems, thing it was remove from the original Elemental Fury talent (with 3 talent points it would be 33/66/100% crit damage). I know the new Electrify Talent give +10% nature damage with full stacks, but the Fire Totems are something that help the Elemental Shamans on the move, who are a casting turret dps kind of spec.

Enhament:
Swaping place between Totemic Alignment and Enhancing Totems. In the first place, there are to many tanky talents on the first part of the Talent Tree, not even one in the deep part. Melee DPS have little choice to where put points after taking Ancestral Knowledge > Thundering Strike > Stable Shields > Lightning Strike. It just to straight forward.

And in second place, the Imp. Weapon Totem was so deep in the Talent Tree only for the AP bonus to the WF Totem, with the change to this totem, there is not need to put a talent with buff 4 totems so deep.

Restoration:
Fusing Tidal and Totemic Focus was the right choice. Im the kind of Shaman to go Resto for Totemic Mastery talent on all my builds. and wanting to try and been Tank Shaman here really hurt me to put points in a first talent row as it give me nothing at all.

Moving Tidal Mastery to the 2th row is not a choice I feel so right about it, but I understand it was the same kind of choice as Fusing the Focus Talents: to give Elemental Shamans wanting to go for Totemic Mastery a talent in the tier 2 it doesnt hurt them, so it not a problem.

There with just that, to me the Shaman talent tree are great. You have a lot of options going deep in a Spec, but you also can stay Jack of all Trades, Master of None and been usefull.

I think a lot of us are disappointed with overall changes to shamans and most classes. We wanted some changes, but a lot of these are out of nowhere and have blindsided us.

This really looks like moving towards the direction of the Vanilla+ server (confusing since it's not really a vanilla experience) and other servers that have changed core gameplay, where classes have largely been reimagined. I wouldn't be surprised if many of the changes were inspired from there; the servers collaborated in the past, so people working on them might have overlap.

The big thing is that if I'd wanted such core vanilla gameplay changed, there are many other servers I could have chosen. Now Turtle is closer to being one of those many other servers. As a result, there's little reason for me (and a lot of us that desire the vanilla experience) to stay here.
I'll stick around since I was pretty much out of things to do. But if it had these changes out when I was looking for a server I don't think I would have started playing. It was easy to suggest turtle to someone just looking to get into wow, now I don't think so.

subject: Re: I don't want 1.17.2
content_md:
Purification doesnt increase your healing output by 10% it increases the base healing of your spell before addheal is taken into consideration by 10%.
For a shaman in actual raid healergear, about half of his healing output comes from +addheal.
Meaning purification ends up being a +5% total healing output which admittably you loose.

In exchange for it, you gain healing way which does increase your total output by 6% per stack for chain heal. At one stack its already better than purification was for CH.

Unless you're in a long fight over an AV graveyard or AB point there's basically no way you're ever going to get that buff to 5 stacks in PvP early enough for it to matter. author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Spirit Link aka Joe Pesci Link
content_md:
So firstly, i left the class council months ago because i was dissatisfied with many changes - among which was the insistence to make totems be absolutely frictionless rather than combat definining abilities (aka enhancer the one that specializes in totems dropping them and then forgetting he is a supporter for the next 2 minutes)

So i do share some of your frustrations too.

Manaflood was axed back then because it didnt really fit. For starters, in most guilds you dont have the luxury of running your shamans in the healergroup. Melee supporting totems are a bit too good to justify a shaman in the healergroups.
Considering we also thought tea was here to stay and do so unnerfed, it made sense to give shaman something else instead.

The insane mana reg boosts he has from watershield certainly handsomely reward the shaman himself for the loss of manflood & manaspring nerf. While in most cases, you just dont benefit a group of 5 manausers to begin with.

Why spirit link was the choice talent, i frankly dont know

The reason why resto needed these changes is to ensure speccing into deep restio and spending at least 30 pts there offers you actually noticeably better healing than a 30/0/21 ele spec.

I would have personally kept ch at 2.5 and made the penultimate talent shave off 0.5 seconds to fit in with the numbers of literally every other spell. This is so there is an actual powerincrease in the tree, becauss god knows 10% base healing amount wasnt it

author: Azuredrak0
subject: Shaman Tanking - Opportunities to make it better
content_md:
Quick shout-out to the devs.  While there is a lot of dooming going around, I personally enjoy the proposed Enh changes, and there is a lot to be said about making the life of Enh DPS and possibility of Shaman Tanking (Warden) much more realistic.

I used to be a Shaman tank, but I achieved my goals for the class and moved on to another class having been satisfied with how far I could push it.  Interestingly my issue with continuing was not so much the durability of the tank, it wasn't even the notable lack of threat, it was the constant requirement of the group that I purposely nerf my tanking capabilities to boost the DPS of the group - i.e. I needed to always drop Windfury totem (and twist it if possible).  Windfury totem does not benefit the shaman in the slightest, it simply benefits the group.

So, here we go, a suggestion - is there a way to provide synergies that benefit the shaman when a totem that does not benefit the shaman is dropped?

Here's an example - when one of the team members triggers Windfury, the shaman gains either 3% block and/or 10 SP (stacks up to 5) for 5 seconds.  The benefit can be baked into Totemic Alignment talent and depend on whether the shaman is wearing a shield or not.  Something different that's along these lines can be done for Flametongue.

This can serve as an additional incentive for consistency of the totem placement.

Alternatively, Windfury Totem can simply stack with Windfury Weapon and both can be tuned to work together.

author: Froghijab420
subject: Ele Sham should get same treatment as other caster hybrids
content_md:
Other caster hybrids (Balance, Smite + Shadow priest) are getting lots of love in the new class changes patch.

Here are some small QOL suggestions/buffs from the 1.17.2 changes.

 1.
> Elemental Fury has been replaced by Electrify: Your Lightning Bolt and Chain Lightning spells charge you with electricity, increasing your Nature damage dealt by 2% and the critical strike damage bonus of your offensive spells by 20%. **Lasts 20 sec**. Stacks up to 5 times.

Please change the duration of this from **20 seconds** to something like **40 or 60** seconds.
As this current change stands, this will make you lose your spell damage buff that you use to have baseline, between every dungeon pack pull, or drink breaks.

 2.
> Move Lightning Mastery [0/5] up in the talent tree
>  Reduces the cast time of your Lightning Bolt and Chain Lightning by (.2, .4, .6, .8, 1.0)

This will allow players more choice is choosing what spec to level with, this talent being so far down is the only reason why elemental is only viable for leveling at 39ish+; with the enhance changes - even if this talent is moved up - it will still most likely be the much better leveling spec.

 3.
> Elemental Focus: Mana cost reduction Increased from 40% to 60%.

Elemental Focus reduces 2 spells by 60% after a crit, **change it to reduces 1 spell mana cost by 100%**.
On regular classic wow, Elemental Focus added chain lightning into single target rotation, it would be nice to still have it included in the rotation - even during mana conservation phases.  I miss using chain lightning while leveling, etc.

 4. Better pushback talent.

Some very very small changes that would make elemental much more enjoyable.

Other caster hybrids (Balance, Smite + Shadow priest) are getting lots of love in the new class changes patch.

Here are some small QOL suggestions/buffs from the 1.17.2 changes.

1.
Elemental Fury has been replaced by Electrify: Your Lightning Bolt and Chain Lightning spells charge you with electricity, increasing your Nature damage dealt by 2% and the critical strike damage bonus of your offensive spells by 20%. Lasts 20 sec. Stacks up to 5 times.
Please change the duration of this from 20 seconds to something like 40 or 60 seconds.
As this current change stands, this will make you lose your spell damage buff that you use to have baseline, between every dungeon pack pull, or drink breaks.

2.
Move Lightning Mastery [0/5] up in the talent tree
Reduces the cast time of your Lightning Bolt and Chain Lightning by (.2, .4, .6, .8, 1.0)
This will allow players more choice is choosing what spec to level with, this talent being so far down is the only reason why elemental is only viable for leveling at 39ish+; with the enhance changes - even if this talent is moved up - it will still most likely be the much better leveling spec.

3.
Elemental Focus: Mana cost reduction Increased from 40% to 60%.
Elemental Focus reduces 2 spells by 60% after a crit, change it to reduces 1 spell mana cost by 100%.
On regular classic wow, Elemental Focus added chain lightning into single target rotation, it would be nice to still have it included in the rotation - even during mana conservation phases. I miss using chain lightning while leveling, etc.

4. Better pushback talent.

Some very very small changes that would make elemental much more enjoyable.

author: Voodoochile
subject: In Regards to patch 1.17.2
content_md:
I've been very critical about the patch from the moment I started reading it, and I want to start by saying I didn't really bother to read all the changes to all the classes; only for the classes I play, being Shaman, Warrior, and Druid. I've been caught up in my emotions saying my piece in regards to how I believe the patch diminishes the Shaman's class identity and role in the game, and it has led some to believe that I simply hate change to #muhclassic. And I want to clarify my position:

I believe changes to Vanilla Shaman are necessary for the game to improve, and that pre-1.17.2 Shaman was only marginally better than Vanilla and still needed to be iterated on. But the changes proposed, which are now live, in particular affecting Resto talents and abilities and builds, serve in my opinion only to attempt to make each Shaman spec semi-viable at the cost of their class identity, namely around the changes to the Talent Trees, Totems, and Healing, ie: The outright removal of Mana Tide Totem, the nerfing of Mana Spring (and Enamored Water Spirit by extension), the increase in Talent Point costs to reach key Talents that were previously accessible to those cross-speccing, and the nerfing of Chain Heal cast time.

And, while I believe that the removal of existing abilities is taboo to a Vanilla+ experience, I do not believe this option can be wholly forgone if what replaces it preserves the identity of the class, while improving poor aspects of the class. But the removal of Mana Tide Totem to be replaced with personal mana regen serves only to diminish the Shaman's identity as a Support Class, or to be a bit more accurate, an Enabler, which I personally believe the curtailing of is antithetical to the idea of a Vanilla+ Shaman. This in tandem with baseline Chain Heal being nerfed for no good reason only to be BUFFED in the resto tree, and moving improved totems in the Enh Tree from 2nd & 3rd Tier Talents to **5TH TIER** re-enforce their move to prop up spec identity at the cost of class identity.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

I wish to provide a more constructive aspect of my thoughts on what I believe Shaman changes should look like that would preserve their unique class identity as a Hybrid Group-Support Class, and which changes I believe were good for the class.

Firstly, I love that Spirit Link is no longer Tauren exclusive as it is an amazingly synergistic ability with Chain Heal and Healing Totem that emphasizes a specialty of Shaman: AoE Healing, and more generally AoE buffing.

Secondly, I believe Bloodlust was also reworked in a very tasteful way that makes Enhance feel good for the Shaman playing it while still being beneficial to their party without being too strong AND not just preserving, but enhancing the Support Class identity.

Thirdly, I am a little disappointed tho in that the Elemental Tree didn't get anything meaningful aside from marginally better mana efficiency, while also nerfing Shaman's ability to burst and forcing them to build up damage. Many encounters in the end are already very melee-centric because their damage is front loaded with no wait time, leaving casters in the dust for encounters with short kill times, and this change actually only makes Shamans even worse in this aspect in PVE from a personal performance stand point, but ontop of that they simply don't do shit buff-wise in comparison to Enhance and Resto, and especially because the only caster-centric buff at their disposal is Mana Spring.

I would've liked to see something like the addition of Totem of Wrath or Wrath of Air Totem in the Tree, maybe make the Keystone Talent give additional effects to all the Totem Types so Fire gets a Totem of Wrath bonus, Wind gets Wraith of Air bonus, Water could maybe gets a Mana Tide effect if it REALLY needed to be removed from the Resto Tree, and idk for Earth Totem.

But another thing that urks me about the lack of Elemental changes is that Elemental just feels awful to level. You spend a majority of your time in melee playing a worse Enhance shaman that does no damage when you are oom, and the lower end of the talent tree offers nothing to make this experience any better. If NOTHING else got changed in the tree, I'd atleast ask to make Lightning Bolt a 2.5 second cast baseline and nerf Lightning Mastery Talent to give only .5 seconds off the cast for a net even cast time of 2 seconds with the talent so leveling feels a little less shit. Going back to my argument for the ability for Shaman to be a Hybrid, I believe making Lightning Bolt have a lower baseline cast speed would improve that.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Now for my unhinged ideations of a potential version of Shaman:

I need to admit upfront that, as I have stated earlier, I did not read the entire patch notes for the changes to most of the other classes. This being said, I have not read the Paladin changes, nor do I play Paladin. But I have read people complaining about Holy Paladins now being Melee Healers, and let me say that sounds fucking badass. In my mind, BOTH Paladins and Shamans should fill the same fantasy of a Group Support, but more over that they should be melee focused no matter the spec.

At this point, I've played nearly all versions of WoW excluding MoP and WoD. And although I did not end up liking WotLK, I LOVED Spell-hance Shaman in Wrath. I dislike DW for Shaman, but I believe the idea of a melee Shaman casting Chain Lightning and Chain Heals while popping buffing his group with Totems and Bloodlust is absolutely fucking peak GigaChad Who-Gives-A-Fuck-If-I'm-Not-On-Top-Of-The-Charts-I'm-Fucking-Thrall-Bitch.

And obviously we couldn't be that strong in Vanilla for obvious reasons, but in my mind being a melee-enhancer is peak shaman fiction. And with that in mind, I believe that it would be better served to have Spirit Link if not a baseline ability, then a 21 Cost Talent in Resto instead of 31 Cost so it can serve as Shaman Defensive CD for Tank Shaman, or for Ele-Shaman who opt out of Elemental Mastery. For Tank Shaman in Particular, I believe that simply leaving them as simply another viable tank is not serving to preserve their identity and have them stand out from the other tank options. With Spirit Link as a Defensive CD, Tank Shaman can in effect become support Tanks, who even if they are not the Main Tank in raid, they can provide their Main Tank extra survivability based on their own health pool that allows additionally Resto-Shaman to be more useful on Solo-Tank Pulls.

Alright, thats pretty much all that I had to say for now. Ultimately I just don't want to play SoD again or TBC or Wrath or Cata again. I want to play Vanilla+, and I want Twow to stay true to that and as of now I am very disappointed with the design they have chosen regardless of viability.
