content_html:
I've been very critical about the patch from the moment I started reading it, and I want to start by saying I didn't really bother to read all the changes to all the classes; only for the classes I play, being Shaman, Warrior, and Druid. I've been caught up in my emotions saying my piece in regards to how I believe the patch diminishes the Shaman's class identity and role in the game, and it has led some to believe that I simply hate change to #muhclassic. And I want to clarify my position:

I believe changes to Vanilla Shaman are necessary for the game to improve, and that pre-1.17.2 Shaman was only marginally better than Vanilla and still needed to be iterated on. But the changes proposed, which are now live, in particular affecting Resto talents and abilities and builds, serve in my opinion only to attempt to make each Shaman spec semi-viable at the cost of their class identity, namely around the changes to the Talent Trees, Totems, and Healing, ie: The outright removal of Mana Tide Totem, the nerfing of Mana Spring (and Enamored Water Spirit by extension), the increase in Talent Point costs to reach key Talents that were previously accessible to those cross-speccing, and the nerfing of Chain Heal cast time.

And, while I believe that the removal of existing abilities is taboo to a Vanilla+ experience, I do not believe this option can be wholly forgone if what replaces it preserves the identity of the class, while improving poor aspects of the class. But the removal of Mana Tide Totem to be replaced with personal mana regen serves only to diminish the Shaman's identity as a Support Class, or to be a bit more accurate, an Enabler, which I personally believe the curtailing of is antithetical to the idea of a Vanilla+ Shaman. This in tandem with baseline Chain Heal being nerfed for no good reason only to be BUFFED in the resto tree, and moving improved totems in the Enh Tree from 2nd & 3rd Tier Talents to 5TH TIER re-enforce their move to prop up spec identity at the cost of class identity.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

I wish to provide a more constructive aspect of my thoughts on what I believe Shaman changes should look like that would preserve their unique class identity as a Hybrid Group-Support Class, and which changes I believe were good for the class.

Firstly, I love that Spirit Link is no longer Tauren exclusive as it is an amazingly synergistic ability with Chain Heal and Healing Totem that emphasizes a specialty of Shaman: AoE Healing, and more generally AoE buffing.

Secondly, I believe Bloodlust was also reworked in a very tasteful way that makes Enhance feel good for the Shaman playing it while still being beneficial to their party without being too strong AND not just preserving, but enhancing the Support Class identity.

Thirdly, I am a little disappointed tho in that the Elemental Tree didn't get anything meaningful aside from marginally better mana efficiency, while also nerfing Shaman's ability to burst and forcing them to build up damage. Many encounters in the end are already very melee-centric because their damage is front loaded with no wait time, leaving casters in the dust for encounters with short kill times, and this change actually only makes Shamans even worse in this aspect in PVE from a personal performance stand point, but ontop of that they simply don't do shit buff-wise in comparison to Enhance and Resto, and especially because the only caster-centric buff at their disposal is Mana Spring.

I would've liked to see something like the addition of Totem of Wrath or Wrath of Air Totem in the Tree, maybe make the Keystone Talent give additional effects to all the Totem Types so Fire gets a Totem of Wrath bonus, Wind gets Wraith of Air bonus, Water could maybe gets a Mana Tide effect if it REALLY needed to be removed from the Resto Tree, and idk for Earth Totem.

But another thing that urks me about the lack of Elemental changes is that Elemental just feels awful to level. You spend a majority of your time in melee playing a worse Enhance shaman that does no damage when you are oom, and the lower end of the talent tree offers nothing to make this experience any better. If NOTHING else got changed in the tree, I'd atleast ask to make Lightning Bolt a 2.5 second cast baseline and nerf Lightning Mastery Talent to give only .5 seconds off the cast for a net even cast time of 2 seconds with the talent so leveling feels a little less shit. Going back to my argument for the ability for Shaman to be a Hybrid, I believe making Lightning Bolt have a lower baseline cast speed would improve that.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Now for my unhinged ideations of a potential version of Shaman:

I need to admit upfront that, as I have stated earlier, I did not read the entire patch notes for the changes to most of the other classes. This being said, I have not read the Paladin changes, nor do I play Paladin. But I have read people complaining about Holy Paladins now being Melee Healers, and let me say that sounds fucking badass. In my mind, BOTH Paladins and Shamans should fill the same fantasy of a Group Support, but more over that they should be melee focused no matter the spec.

At this point, I've played nearly all versions of WoW excluding MoP and WoD. And although I did not end up liking WotLK, I LOVED Spell-hance Shaman in Wrath. I dislike DW for Shaman, but I believe the idea of a melee Shaman casting Chain Lightning and Chain Heals while popping buffing his group with Totems and Bloodlust is absolutely fucking peak GigaChad Who-Gives-A-Fuck-If-I'm-Not-On-Top-Of-The-Charts-I'm-Fucking-Thrall-Bitch.

For Tank Shaman in Particular, I believe that simply leaving them as simply another viable tank is not serving to preserve their identity and have them stand out from the other tank options. With Spirit Link as a Defensive CD, Tank Shaman can in effect become support Tanks, who even if they are not the Main Tank in raid, they can provide their Main Tank extra survivability based on their own health pool that allows additionally Resto-Shaman to be more useful on Solo-Tank Pulls.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Alright, thats pretty much all that I had to say for now. Ultimately I just don't want to play SoD again or TBC or Wrath or Cata again. I want to play Vanilla+, and I want Twow to stay true to that and as of now I am very disappointed with the design they have chosen regardless of viability.

I am a Naxx and ES geared Shaman who's played here for over a year and was excited for Kara. I have spent plenty of money to support the project. But I simply have no desire to play my Shaman anymore due to the changes, and I find it hard to log in that I cannot play my favorite class across all of WoW.

author: Terras
subject: Re: In Regards to patch 1.17.2
content_md:
Greetings,

To start, while I have not always agreed with your opinion on all things shaman, I have always appreciated the fact that you take the time to post like this with a background and explanation of where you are coming from. Additionally, I too am in the "melee healee sure sounds niftee" camp and do play some paladin myself. I feel like you have some good points about the feel vs the utility of Restoration and Elemental and are touching on something I have been thinking about in regard to Enhancement, more specifically tanking Enhancement. I shall lay these out below.

As the base of all my thoughts on the shaman changes, I believe that a more basic form of spirit link should have been made baseline to the shaman (Note: I am not so far into the calculations of the game as to include numbers so I will place variables for all).
This would be in the form of a single target link between your target and another player based not on how close they are but on who has the highest armor and health other than the target within a set range. The base version would split X% of damage between the two per usual with the addition that each of the trees would have a modifying talent for the skill (Note: a possible change I would add for the spell to improve utility would be a chance to avoid spell knockback for a linked caster).
This basic version would allow any shaman to provide a minor form of assistance to a party member in trouble. Examples would include a tank during a high damage portion of a fight or a healer/DPS being assaulted by adds.

Class specific additions.

Restoration: (My secondary play style)
I will start with the Restoration variant of the spirit link. I would trade the Spirit Link talent with the talent 'Restorative Totems', it would add an additional target to Spirit Link with the effect that after the spirit link wears off each person effected would have a HoT placed on them that healed x% of the damage they received during the link which scales off of x% of the shaman's Sp/Hp.
I would modify the 'Restorative Totems' into a capstone talent called 'Totem of Restoration' Which would place down a totem that restored x% of the shaman's mana and health to all party/raid members within X distance.
While I am not sure the effect this would have in a raid situation it feels better thematically and restores an aspect of the mana tide totem that many shaman healers seem to miss.

Enhancement: (My primary play style)
The variant of Spirit Link I would add here would be folded into the talent 'Spirit Armor' at the second talent point. This variant would change the behavior to always link the shaman with another player but increase the resistances of both players by X times the shaman's level amount and their armor by X% of both the shaman and linked player's total armor.
I would modify the 'Stormstrike' talent to have a chance to proc 'Lightning Strike' (If available) that cannot crit for free, with slower weapons having a higher chance to proc the attack (Note: This may be too much, but I am very underwhelmed by cost/benefit of both 'Lightning Strike' and 'Stormstrike).
I would also modify 'Lightning Strike' to burn two charges of the current shield with a commensurate increase in effect if it lands a critical blow.
Finally, to improve their overall defenses I would increase their block scaling in relation to their defense skill and change the effect to the Stoneskin totem in the 'Enhancing Totems' talent so that it would redirect the extra critical hit damage to the totem destroying it instead of increasing the damage resistance (Note: I would keep the block amount increase).

As I play a shaman tank, I have perhaps over tuned these changes, but I feel the spirit link adds a needed defensive cooldown and the general increase in block along with the ability to mitigate a critical hit at the cost of the totem would go a long way in making a fun tanking play style. I also think that with the egregious increase in mana cost for the strike attacks melee damage dealers would feel better with more synergy there.

Elemental: (My least favorite play style and therefore probably completely off base, I'm guessing here)
This variant would get added into the 'Eye of the Storm' talent with it having the unique distinction of being the only variant with multiple tiers. At tier one the variant would flip the equation for the link making it link the shaman and the player with the highest mana total and mana regeneration and sharing X% of the mana used/man burned between the players but adding X% of the players combined mana regeneration as MP5 to both. At tier 2 both players would receive the focused casting proc chance and increase the % of the mana regeneration given. At tier 3 the mana cost of spirit link would drop by X% and further increase the mana regeneration bonus.
I would baseline the nature damage portion of the electricity mechanic to the lightning spell and then add "allow X% of mana regeneration to continue in combat for each stack of electricity" to the 'Electrify' talent to help with the mana starvation complaints I have heard.

As I do not regularly play Elemental I can understand if this portion is just ignored outright or if i have failed to think of the potential secondary effects these changes would have.

Thank you for reading I hope I didn't bore you.

content_html:
I
've been very critical about the patch from the moment I started reading it, and I want to start by saying I didn't really bother to read all the changes to all the classes; only for the classes I play, being Shaman, Warrior, and Druid. I've been caught up in my emotions saying my piece in regards to how I believe the patch diminishes the Shaman's class identity and role in the game, and it has led some to believe that I simply hate change to #muhclassic. And I want to clarify my position:

I believe changes to Vanilla Shaman are necessary for the game to improve, and that pre-1.17.2 Shaman was only marginally better than Vanilla and still needed to be iterated on. But the changes proposed, which are now live, in particular affecting Resto talents and abilities and builds, serve in my opinion only to attempt to make each Shaman spec semi-viable at the cost of their class identity, namely around the changes to the Talent Trees, Totems, and Healing, ie: The outright removal of Mana Tide Totem, the nerfing of Mana Spring (and Enamored Water Spirit by extension), the increase in Talent Point costs to reach key Talents that were previously accessible to those cross-speccing, and the nerfing of Chain Heal cast time.

And, while I believe that the removal of existing abilities is taboo to a Vanilla+ experience, I do not believe this option can be wholly forgone if what replaces it preserves the identity of the class, while improving poor aspects of the class. But the removal of Mana Tide Totem to be replaced with personal mana regen serves only to diminish the Shaman's identity as a Support Class, or to be a bit more accurate, an Enabler, which I personally believe the curtailing of is antithetical to the idea of a Vanilla+ Shaman. This in tandem with baseline Chain Heal being nerfed for no good reason only to be BUFFED in the resto tree, and moving improved totems in the Enh Tree from 2nd & 3rd Tier Talents to 5TH TIER re-enforce their move to prop up spec identity at the cost of class identity.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

I wish to provide a more constructive aspect of my thoughts on what I believe Shaman changes should look like that would preserve their unique class identity as a Hybrid Group-Support Class, and which changes I believe were good for the class.

Firstly, I love that Spirit Link is no longer Tauren exclusive as it is an amazingly synergistic ability with Chain Heal and Healing Totem that emphasizes a specialty of Shaman: AoE Healing, and more generally AoE buffing.

Secondly, I believe Bloodlust was also reworked in a very tasteful way that makes Enhance feel good for the Shaman playing it while still being beneficial to their party without being too strong AND not just preserving, but enhancing the Support Class identity.

Thirdly, I am a little disappointed tho in that the Elemental Tree didn't get anything meaningful aside from marginally better mana efficiency, while also nerfing Shaman's ability to burst and forcing them to build up damage. Many encounters in the end are already very melee-centric because their damage is front loaded with no wait time, leaving casters in the dust for encounters with short kill times, and this change actually only makes Shamans even worse in this aspect in PVE from a personal performance stand point, but ontop of that they simply don't do shit buff-wise in comparison to Enhance and Resto, and especially because the only caster-centric buff at their disposal is Mana Spring.

I would've liked to see something like the addition of Totem of Wrath or Wrath of Air Totem in the Tree, maybe make the Keystone Talent give additional effects to all the Totem Types so Fire gets a Totem of Wrath bonus, Wind gets Wraith of Air bonus, Water could maybe gets a Mana Tide effect if it REALLY needed to be removed from the Resto Tree, and idk for Earth Totem.

But another thing that urks me about the lack of Elemental changes is that Elemental just feels awful to level. You spend a majority of your time in melee playing a worse Enhance shaman that does no damage when you are oom, and the lower end of the talent tree offers nothing to make this experience any better. If NOTHING else got changed in the tree, I'd atleast ask to make Lightning Bolt a 2.5 second cast baseline and nerf Lightning Mastery Talent to give only .5 seconds off the cast for a net even cast time of 2 seconds with the talent so leveling feels a little less shit. Going back to my argument for the ability for Shaman to be a Hybrid, I believe making Lightning Bolt have a lower baseline cast speed would improve that.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Now for my unhinged ideations of a potential version of Shaman:

I need to admit upfront that, as I have stated earlier, I did not read the entire patch notes for the changes to most of the other classes. This being said, I have not read the Paladin changes, nor do I play Paladin. But I have read people complaining about Holy Paladins now being Melee Healers, and let me say that sounds fucking badass. In my mind, BOTH Paladins and Shamans should fill the same fantasy of a Group Support, but more over that they should be melee focused no matter the spec.

At this point, I've played nearly all versions of WoW excluding MoP and WoD. And although I did not end up liking WotLK, I LOVED Spell-hance Shaman in Wrath. I dislike DW for Shaman, but I believe the idea of a melee Shaman casting Chain Lightning and Chain Heals while popping buffing his group with Totems and Bloodlust is absolutely fucking peak GigaChad Who-Gives-A-Fuck-If-I'm-Not-On-Top-Of-The-Charts-I'm-Fucking-Thrall-Bitch.

And obviously we couldn't be that strong in Vanilla for obvious reasons, but in my mind being a melee-enhancer is peak shaman fiction. And with that in mind, I believe that it would be better served to have Spirit Link if not a baseline ability, then a 21 Cost Talent in Resto instead of 31 Cost so it can serve as Shaman Defensive CD for Tank Shaman, or for Ele-Shaman who opt out of Elemental Mastery. For Tank Shaman in Particular, I believe that simply leaving them as simply another viable tank is not serving to preserve their identity and have them stand out from the other tank options. With Spirit Link as a Defensive CD, Tank Shaman can in effect become support Tanks, who even if they are not the Main Tank in raid, they can provide their Main Tank extra survivability based on their own health pool that allows additionally Resto-Shaman to be more useful on Solo-Tank Pulls.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Alright, thats pretty much all that I had to say for now. Ultimately I just don't want to play SoD again or TBC or Wrath or Cata again. I want to play Vanilla+, and I want Twow to stay true to that and as of now I am very disappointed with the design they have chosen regardless of viability.

I am a Naxx and ES geared Shaman who's played here for over a year and was excited for Kara. I have spent plenty of money to support the project. But I simply have no desire to play my Shaman anymore due to the changes, and I find it hard to log in that I cannot play my favorite class across all of WoW.

Shamans are doing something on CD and at lvl 30+ dungeons they are in the top dps, on par with hunters and mages. On BG, this is generally a 50% one-shot for cloth. What kind of mess is this? Who even came up with the idea that a support class, with a wonderful arsenal of spells, should be one of the top dps?
And I see the following picture. A mob casts fear, or an AoE version of shadowbolt on the whole team - the shaman doesn't care - he is a top dps. author: Ryken
subject: Electrify requiring 5 stacks is too much - for PvP
content_md:
Five stacks of Electrify in order to obtain 100% crit bonus to offensive spells, which was previously a passive, is too much of a nerf for Elemental PvP. Fights are too short and CC-heavy to make this regularly achievable.

Elemental Mastery giving 2 stacks isn't enough to bring us back on par to what we had as default, and is only available every few fights and is attached to a clear 'quick, CC me!' animation. The 10% extra bonus damage at 5 stacks also isn't that useful the stacks can't be maintained in the first palce.

For PvE, change seems fine (better for longer fights like bosses, though annoying for trash/shorter fights).

But for PvP, I've been playing regularly since the patch dropped and the frustration is immense.

Players are actively trying to CC you, and since shocks don't add to electrify (yet they also suffer the crit penalty from the changed talent), in active combat you are dead before 5 stacks can be reached.

The only success of getting 5 stacks is if you are able to free-cast while the enemy is focusing on your teammates, and the enemy in that case is dumb and would die even if there was no crit bonus anyway.

The other likely chance is building up 5 stacks using rank 1 on a nearby enemy pet, then hoping your 20sec doesn't drop off before you get into combat (it often does). This creates a very frustrating mini-game, without the fun, to constantly monitor and manage your stacks.

I agree with concept behind trying to reduce burst non-interactive PvP (I guess that is over to arcane mages now), but please consider a slight adjustment such as making it a maxium of 3 stacks of electrify with 33% bonus each is much more viable and still addresses the burst concerns.

As it currently stands, Ele is extremely frustrating to play in PvP and I'm close to retiring the spec alltogether, which was the main reason I leveled this class to begin with.

Correct me if I'm wrong, but 3 stacks of Electrify is not enough to get to the pre cc2 power level - let's say your LB hits for 1000, so with 6% nature damage bonus and 60% crit bonus your LB will crit for 1908, while pre cc2 it would've critted for 2000. However, you did not account for the fact that:
a) it is very rarely that you are allowed to freecast 4 LB/CLs in a row in PvP, unless your opponents are braindead;
b) nature damage buff from electrify does not affect non-nature sources of damage, such as Frost and Flame Shock as well as Fire Totems, making them less substantial for ele burst than before, forcing you to use Earth Shock;
c) old Elemental Fury granted 100% crit bonus to any spell AND totem damage, while after cc2 we need to spend 4 extra points to make totems crit for the same amount that pre-cc2 totems did, and Fire Nova totem was always a great spell in ele shamans toolkit, especially against melees.

I'm also struggling to see how Lightning Strike is a strong counter to melees. With the old go-to 30/0/21 ele pvp build you get much higher utility and survivability by getting 70% chance to avoid healing spell pushback and NS, especially when you use it against melees to insta-heal.
After cc2 talents changed and moved in such way that 30/0/21 became much gimped compared to pre-cc2.

Take a look at pre-cc2 30/0/21: [https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... 1000000000](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/calculator/custom?t2=je6rvnk1qX&t1=bqPySyG3I6&t0=AxVijEWJ5G&t=0500033010502300210000500000-0000000000000000000000000000-0050032005000050001000000000)
Old talent distribution allowed you to get all crucial talents from both ele and resto trees - clearcasting, +10% crit chance on LB/CL, +15% damage to fire totems, pushback immunity on crit, almost instant Fire Nova totem, 36yrd range, 100% crit damage on all spells and fire totems, 1sec faster LB/CL, 3% spell hit, 70% chance to avoid pushback on heals and NS as a great utility CD

Take a look at post-cc2 30/0/21: [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... AIAAAAA%3D](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=FADYIoTARAAoAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAEoDoCIAAAIAAAAA%3D)
With new talent changes and different distribution, we lose: +15% damage to fire totems, 100% crit damage bonus to fire totems and most importantly the 100% critical damage bonus on spells, which now we have to stack at least 4 times to get to pre-cc2 power level and that only lasts for 20 seconds until you need to stack all over again.

The best solution here would be to revert changes to ele tree, or to redesign it with a better talent budget in mind and some changes to Electrify (reduce number of stacks to 3, increase their duration, make it lose 1 stack after that duration instead of all the stacks), that will give ele shamans an option to replicate trusty ol' 30/0/21 in addition to whatever is the new most viable ele pvp build.

author: Akos1896
subject: 2 Tank 2 Shaman
content_md:
Hey!

This is an almost-guide. I wanna share my experience with yall with the hope that
 1. It helps warden tanks.
 2. It motivates someone to try out shaman tanking.

I don't wanna act like a know-it-all. Changes happened not a long time ago, we don't have established guides and in-depth knowledge about these topics.
At any point, I might be wrong.

So, about 2 Tank 2 Shaman

![Image](https://i.postimg.cc/nrL0m3Zs/tank.png)

 **The scope:**
Shaman tanks are designed to be 100% viable tanks during leveling. They can be used at raids, too but they are less optimal there. The lack of a defensive CD becomes a pain point.

 **Strengths:**
 * Very good initial threat.
 * Very good AoE threat during leveling (lack of good totem scaling makes it worse later).
 * High dodge, many times you won't even get hit.
 * High utility via totems.

 **Weaknesses:**
 * Mana user, can get oom mid-fight.
 * Lack of defensive CD.
 * Squishier than the other tanks.
 * Aoe threat? Yes. Aoe taunt? No.
 * Mobility. No inherent speed buff, no charge options.

 **Other interesting points:**
 * Usually relies on totems which make WF totem and strength totem harder to use. Melee DPS might hate shaman tanks.
 * They are the closest thing to be an 'against spell damage-tech tank' with some gimmicks (elemental warding talent, T2,5 set bonus). But all in all they are not anti-spell damage-specced, they just have some limited tools for it.

 **Their toolkit**

 **For pulls**

Lightning bolt and chain lightning are great for pulls. Chain lightning can worth it even for 1 target. Don't forget that r1 lightning bolt can be cast faster than the max rank one. If you have the time, you can cast some r1 bolts to try proccing clearcasting until the mob gets to you.
Also, if you have relics, make some good relic swap macros. Totem of crackling thunder loves lightning bolts while totem of the storm loves both bolts and chain lightnings.
If you wanna min-max, keep in mind that weapons and shield can be swapped while being in combat. You can macro a pull with a SP weapon set and immediately swap back to the normal set if you wanna do that.

This will get you a great initial threat and hopefully a clearcasting buff, maybe also a haste proc from lightning bolt.
Your next step is to maximize threat on the mobs who run to you:
 1. Time a fire nova totem well! Make it explode the second the mobs arrive. Huge threat spike. Follow it up with a magma totem for maintained threat.
 2. If you go full on threat, support this with a stoneclaw totem. Your logic should be something like this:
 -> Do I expect fear? -> Tremor
Nah. -> Do I need more threat? -> Stoneclaw.
Nah. -> Am I not confident in my defenses? -> Stoneskin
All g. -> Strength (Helps you and all of the melee.)

In practice it usually means strength totem unless fears happen or DPS does really high numbers.

Don't forget: as a warden shaman you can range-pull really well but you're 'charging' is awkward. You just randomly jog up to the monsters.

 **During fight**

Use **shocks** on CD but only if elemental devastation is procced (it usually should be). You can still use shocks without the buff but if the mob is a higher level one, I'd wait for the proc. You need that spell hit buff.
Use earth shock (max level) for threat, around rank 5 for Tesco budget threat and r1 if you wanna only interrupt and mana is really low.
In practice after these changes I suggest using max rank almost always.

 **When not to use shocks?**: If your threat-lead is enough, **preserve mana**. Parties hate having a 2 min break after each pull. The art of shaman and pala tanking is finding the necessary minimum of abilities to keep threat while saving the rest of the mana for the future. It's a long process. When practicing, just spam shocks on CD initially and when you learn to have reliable threat always assess if you can allow yourself to save mana at any given moment. That is the moment when downgrading or skipping shocks can start to become inportant.
Frost shock is the weird replacement for earth shocks for high nat rez mobs.
Flame shock gives a 'long term threat' on a target. Personally I don't find this so important since we have AoE threat now.
Don't forget, shocks like totem of rage, macro them to a good old relic swap.

Earth shocks also benefit from...

 **...the new, 8 sec CD stormstrike.**
As I said, shocks like elemental devastation buff. They are specially happy if they get the stormstrike buff, too. Use stormstrike on CD unless you can afford to save mana and use it strategically keeping the option of a bigger earth shock in mind.

 **Lightning strike** has a 10 sec CD. It's super good. And elemental shield-dependent.
I usually go for water shield to be better with mana. But for shield selection you should ask these questions:
Are my defensives high enough? -> If no, use earth shield and LS with it. After all, worst tank is a dead tank.
Is threat okay? -> If no, go for lightning shield.
Am I confident in survival and threat? -> Go for water shield. Help with mana means less downtime in a dungeon run.

 **Taunt** is of course there as an emergency button.
I've seen an error people do sometimes. When you pull and the first mob comes, you don't need to taunt it as a first action, unless it is targeting another party member. Just greet them folks with a stormstrike for initial threat (aided by your totem threat).

 **Bloodlust:**
You can use it as a threat spike and as a utility button. You really struggle keeping threat on a boss? Raise your haste. You want a target to die asap? Bloodlust and your crits grant haste to party members.

The big pain point here is the lack of defensives. I can't advise you to go to AQ40 f.ex. as a warden shaman. You def can but it's really hard both for you and for the healers.

PS: I personally like to make a startattack macro after the strikes, just in case.

 **The totems**

There are 4 elements. Each one can help you a lot. My priorities are as follows.

 **Air**
Is there any instant spell I need to avoid (think of Hakkar or the Kara Crypt mobs)? -> Grounding
Things go normally? -> Grace of air.
Is melee DPS throwing a tantrum? -> WF totem (but only then).

WF totem is actively hurting you. While it gives nothing to you since you use **rockbiter** (never question this, USE ROCKBITER), it raises melee DPS threat with the extra attacks. So you give up much needed crit and dodge so that DPS can take over threat easier. I only use it if melee is REALLY nagging.

 **Earth**
As written above.
In a sequence I suggest using stoneclaw for initial threat then swapping to stoneskin or to strength.

 **Fire**
You don't benefit from flametongue. Same problem as WF totem but people don't have the reflex to expect it fortunately.
So.
When pulling back -> Fire nova, followed by magma.
Normally -> Magma.
For single-target, if there are no nearby sheeps etc -> Searing.

 **Water**
Healing stream totem is still bad. If you really have a hobby of dying, try it out but water totem logic for me goes like this:
Any poison/disease? -> Related cleansing totem.
If not -> Do I want fire rez? -> Fire rez totem.
If not -> Mana totem.

So
 **You pull back:**
Fire nova is ticking, stoneclaw totem is helping to get threat. Mobs arrive, fire nova explodes, you switch to magma and put down grace of air and (usually) mana totem. After some stoneclaw ticks you can switch to strentgh unless health is a problem in which case it is stoneskin.

 **You run in:**
Stormstrike for inital threat and magma+stoneclaw (+grace of air+mana). After some seconds switch to stoneskin or to strength.

 **You fight one big baddie:**
Grace of air, stoneskin/strength, mana and searing totem.

 **The main logic of shaman tanking is this:**
You have several tools to get more threat, get defenses or to get mana. But at many times you can only choose one. You have to observe yourself (how is your health bar moving, how much mana you have, what does threat addon say) to decide which utility you need at the moment. This is the main logic which should determine what shield you use or f.ex. you use stoneclaw, stoneskin or strength totem.

 **PS:** Since I shaman tanked before the changes, I have some old reflexes, f.ex. having some oils of immolation at me at all times. I suggest the same, specially during early practice. It helps you out if you did something wrong. Think of items like oils and target dummies as get out of jail cards while you're practicing the build.

 **For races:**
All are viable but if you're a minmaxer, not all are equal.
Orcs have some threat spike with blood fury and have some weapon skill advantage but they are probably the worst option. At least their shaman racial is cool for tanking, too.

I think trolls are the mid options. Health regen is better now but still not a serious racial. Their main selling point is berserking which got nerfed but it's still awesome. Hex is mostly useless for a tank.

Taurens give +life for a mail-wearing tank. New racial also seems good (but never seen it in practice). I think they are the strongest choice if someone really cares about these minimal differences.

PS: If I can send a message to devs, we are 1 step away from making warden a valid tank at high raids. **Please give them a defensive CD.** Please.

___________

I almost forgot: an old trick you can do as a shaman tank, if casters have really high threat is leaving a tranquil air totem behind. You don't have improved totem radius so if you position well and you're okay with giving up an air totem slot, you can give 20% threat reduction to the casters. It's a very niche thing though.
content_html:
Hey!

This is an almost-guide. I wanna share my experience with yall with the hope that
1. It helps warden tanks.
2. It motivates someone to try out shaman tanking.

I don't wanna act like a know-it-all. Changes happened not a long time ago, we don't have established guides and in-depth knowledge about these topics.
At any point, I might be wrong.

So, about 2 Tank 2 Shaman



The scope:
Shaman tanks are designed to be 100% viable tanks during leveling. They can be used at raids, too but they are less optimal there. The lack of a defensive CD becomes a pain point.

Strengths:
* Very good initial threat.
* Very good AoE threat during leveling (lack of good totem scaling makes it worse later).
* High dodge, many times you won't even get hit.
* High utility via totems.

Weaknesses:
* Mana user, can get oom mid-fight.
* Lack of defensive CD.
* Squishier than the other tanks.
* Aoe threat? Yes. Aoe taunt? No.
* Mobility. No inherent speed buff, no charge options.

Other interesting points:
* Usually relies on totems which make WF totem and strength totem harder to use. Melee DPS might hate shaman tanks.
* They are the closest thing to be an 'against spell damage-tech tank' with some gimmicks (elemental warding talent, T2,5 set bonus). But all in all they are not anti-spell damage-specced, they just have some limited tools for it.

Their toolkit

For pulls

Lightning bolt and chain lightning are great for pulls. Chain lightning can worth it even for 1 target. Don't forget that r1 lightning bolt can be cast faster than the max rank one. If you have the time, you can cast some r1 bolts to try proccing clearcasting until the mob gets to you.
Also, if you have relics, make some good relic swap macros. Totem of crackling thunder loves lightning bolts while totem of the storm loves both bolts and chain lightnings.
If you wanna min-max, keep in mind that weapons and shield can be swapped while being in combat. You can macro a pull with a SP weapon set and immediately swap back to the normal set if you wanna do that.

This will get you a great initial threat and hopefully a clearcasting buff, maybe also a haste proc from lightning bolt.
Your next step is to maximize threat on the mobs who run to you:
1. Time a fire nova totem well! Make it explode the second the mobs arrive. Huge threat spike. Follow it up with a magma totem for maintained threat.
2. If you go full on threat, support this with a stoneclaw totem. Your logic should be something like this:
-> Do I expect fear? -> Tremor
Nah. -> Do I need more threat? -> Stoneclaw.
Nah. -> Am I not confident in my defenses? -> Stoneskin
All g. -> Strength (Helps you and all of the melee.)

In practice it usually means strength totem unless fears happen or DPS does really high numbers.

Don't forget: as a warden shaman you can range-pull really well but you're 'charging' is awkward. You just randomly jog up to the monsters.

During fight

Use shocks on CD but only if elemental devastation is procced (it usually should be). You can still use shocks without the buff but if the mob is a higher level one, I'd wait for the proc. You need that spell hit buff.
Use earth shock (max level) for threat, around rank 5 for Tesco budget threat and r1 if you wanna only interrupt and mana is really low.
In practice after these changes I suggest using max rank almost always.

When not to use shocks?: If your threat-lead is enough, preserve mana. Parties hate having a 2 min break after each pull. The art of shaman and pala tanking is finding the necessary minimum of abilities to keep threat while saving the rest of the mana for the future. It's a long process. When practicing, just spam shocks on CD initially and when you learn to have reliable threat always assess if you can allow yourself to save mana at any given moment. That is the moment when downgrading or skipping shocks can start to become inportant.
Frost shock is the weird replacement for earth shocks for high nat rez mobs.
Flame shock gives a 'long term threat' on a target. Personally I don't find this so important since we have AoE threat now.
Don't forget, shocks like totem of rage, macro them to a good old relic swap.

Earth shocks also benefit from...

...the new, 8 sec CD stormstrike.
As I said, shocks like elemental devastation buff. They are specially happy if they get the stormstrike buff, too. Use stormstrike on CD unless you can afford to save mana and use it strategically keeping the option of a bigger earth shock in mind.

Lightning strike has a 10 sec CD. It's super good. And elemental shield-dependent.
I usually go for water shield to be better with mana. But for shield selection you should ask these questions:
Are my defensives high enough? -> If no, use earth shield and LS with it. After all, worst tank is a dead tank.
Is threat okay? -> If no, go for lightning shield.
Am I confident in survival and threat? -> Go for water shield. Help with mana means less downtime in a dungeon run.

Taunt is of course there as an emergency button.
I've seen an error people do sometimes. When you pull and the first mob comes, you don't need to taunt it as a first action, unless it is targeting another party member. Just greet them folks with a stormstrike for initial threat (aided by your totem threat).

Bloodlust:
You can use it as a threat spike and as a utility button. You really struggle keeping threat on a boss? Raise your haste. You want a target to die asap? Bloodlust and your crits grant haste to party members.

The big pain point here is the lack of defensives. I can't advise you to go to AQ40 f.ex. as a warden shaman. You def can but it's really hard both for you and for the healers.

PS: I personally like to make a startattack macro after the strikes, just in case.

The totems

There are 4 elements. Each one can help you a lot. My priorities are as follows.

Air
Is there any instant spell I need to avoid (think of Hakkar or the Kara Crypt mobs)? -> Grounding
Things go normally? -> Grace of air.
Is melee DPS throwing a tantrum? -> WF totem (but only then).

WF totem is actively hurting you. While it gives nothing to you since you use rockbiter (never question this, USE ROCKBITER), it raises melee DPS threat with the extra attacks. So you give up much needed crit and dodge so that DPS can take over threat easier. I only use it if melee is REALLY nagging.

Earth
As written above.
In a sequence I suggest using stoneclaw for initial threat then swapping to stoneskin or to strength.

Fire
You don't benefit from flametongue. Same problem as WF totem but people don't have the reflex to expect it fortunately.
So.
When pulling back -> Fire nova, followed by magma.
Normally -> Magma.
For single-target, if there are no nearby sheeps etc -> Searing.

Water
Healing stream totem is still bad. If you really have a hobby of dying, try it out but water totem logic for me goes like this:
Any poison/disease? -> Related cleansing totem.
If not -> Do I want fire rez? -> Fire rez totem.
If not -> Mana totem.

It helps you out if you did something wrong. Think of items like oils and target dummies as get out of jail cards while you're practicing the build.

WF and flametongue totems now DO stack with your weapon enchant, they act as normal aura buffs now. So using them benefits the melee and yourself as well, even if they have poisons/sharpening stones and whatnot.

Here are some things from my shamatanking experience:
 -Hand of edward the odd is amazing MH, since you get instant healing wave and chain lightning procs.
 -Blade of eternal darkness (+a few elemental damage on melee attack pieces and flametongue totem) is great for mana upkeep. Keep on swap when your mana is low.
 -Black grasp of the destroyer, while not a tank item, is great for threat and a bit of mana regen (especially with fast weapons and WF totem).
 -Don't be afraid to plop down an earthbind totem and frost shock/kite the mobs if things go south - if your healer is dead or oom.
 -Tea is your best friend.

author: Fornow
subject: Re: 2 Tank 2 Shaman
content_md:
If there's melees in the dungeon group i would almost always prioritize windfury totem (interject spellbind totem where necessary), it's just that good and you don't gain that much from the bonus agility.

Another great weapon at 58+ is the epic dagger Alcors Sunrazor. Picked up mine for 70ish gold from the auction house which is a very fair price.

Before the talent changes I would actually go into the resto tree so grab the extended totem range. More range = better uptime and less replants in between groups. Mana management is indeed key. But also a very fun skill to master with a high skill ceiling. While your inexperienced you'll often be drinking while the group is waiting on you.

Shaman tanks humiliates caster packs btw. Scholomance is a joy to visit when your main rotation interrupts spells every 5-6 seconds. Downranking earth shock is worth it too. You should have Rank 1 earth keybound separately just for cheap interrupts.

Oh and remember to have any priests preshield you whenever as you don't suffer the rage gain penalty.

What's not nice for tank shamans are nature immune (or resistant) mobs which hamper use of earth shock. Best strat is to simply warn your group ahead of time, come up with an adhoc tactic for difficult packs (depending on group composition).

author: amanagor
subject: elemental tragedy
content_md:
Elemental shaman was in a bad state before the patch, and is now in an even worse state. In pve, it is a bottom of the barrel dps spec,  provides no utility over other shaman specs, and so is not taken in end tier raids. This issue is likely going to be aggravated for Karazan.
The spec still has clear mana issues, as the changes to elemental focus and water shield do not compensate for the nerfs to tea, and do not  allow elemental to use any other spell than lightning bolt in their rotation without ooming quickly.
On top of that, even without ooming, the spec under performs compared to other dps specs.
Shaman is also the second least played class in the game for dps in naxx. (behind only priest)
Somehow turtle devs think this is acceptable, as they state they are happy with  how elemental performs, as they use this statement to justify how little the spec was touched in 17.2 (other than destroying it in pvp).
On the subject of pvp, Elemental is now objectively garbage, as it needs multiple casts to start providing useful damage due to the new electrify talent. The only scenario where elemental is viable in pvp, is in a group fight where the opposing team is incompetent, and completely ignores the elemental, letting it hard cast for 10 seconds
Against competent players, the elemental just gets focused before it has time to build up stacks, and doesn't have the utility, or mobility to survive.
In a 1V1 scenario, don't even think of building up stacks of the buff, elemental is literally a free kill at this point.
Currently There is no aspect of the game where elemental performs well. The spec is roughly equal in strength to its classic version, in regards to pve, and significantly worse for pvp.
The question i'm asking the devs, is if they are planning on making the spec viable, or if people that want to play elemental should just give up and go play somewhere else?

author: Weskil
subject: Re: elemental tragedy
content_md:
I've always mainly played elemental in PvP. The class identity to me was mostly about burst damage, with some extra party support in longer fights where the burst doesn't matter as much. In solo fights using ghost wolf to position and get a surprise burst on your target, or in group fights trying to spike down the healers fast. The tradeoffs being that mana is a constant issue, you're somewhat of a glass cannon, and if a mage gets a counterspell off then you're almost entirely out of action for the fight.

Balance druid has always had better mobility with travel form being instant cast and the ability to get out of snares. They're also less threatened by mages due to having two damage schools, and moonkin gives them better survivability overall. Now balance also does more burst damage than elemental which leaves my favorite class kind of lacking an identity?

I stand by my previous suggestion, return elemental fury as it was and change electrify to stack something more meaningful to the PvE longer-form fights that it seems intended for, like maybe allowing mana regen while casting. I don't raid so someone more experienced could suggest something better. The idea is that you choose to spend your points in burst damage or sustained damage, and it'd be costly point-wise to do both.

author: Ladhihs
subject: Re: elemental tragedy
content_md:
The fundamental issue is that the developers don't play the game.

When the shaman discord was discussing the talent before it was released and how it will kill elemental pvp, Haaxor:
didn't understand why shamans "can't just get 5 casts off" to get the full buff
didn't understand why shocks are important to elemental burst
insisted shamans use the new Elemental Mastery to make Electrify less painful

Not only is it bad game design to be pigeonholed into a talent to get around another talent that only exists to nerf your potential, it goes against vanilla's design. It's intentional that shamans have a choice between EM and NS; do you want a guaranteed crit or be more versatile? Turtle is trying to remove that choice as a roundabout way of further nerfing shaman.

Shaman was designed as the Horde's offensive answer to the Alliance's defensive bulwark that is paladin. As paladin had the best cooldowns and utility but no damage, shaman was given damage but no cooldowns, mobility, or utility. Its sustain was also poor. By nerfing shaman's niche the class is effectively dead and faction balance is now heavily skewed towards Alliance.

It is obvious that they are approaching class design in a class by class basis. They have no vision of how the classes are meant to interact with each other. This is why EF got turned into Electrify, while Ruin/Arcane Potency didn't get changed. It's why Enhancement's Flurry got nerfed and Warrior's didn't. No other class has to "ramp up" their damage and they retained their kit. Hell, most of them have only gotten better with this patch.

As of CC2 shaman is now objectively the worst class and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone.

author: Weskil
subject: Re: elemental tragedy
content_md:
> **Ladhihs wrote: Wed Nov 20, 2024 3:36 am**
> *post*

To extend an olive branch a bit and make this more constructive, from an elemental PvP perspective. I want to expand on this a little and explain my feelings on the matter while turning down the anger a bit (however justified).

> **Ladhihs wrote: Wed Nov 20, 2024 3:36 am**
> didn't understand why shamans "can't just get 5 casts off" to get the full buff

I think there are really two problems here. The first issue is that PvP fights are *fast*. The only time you'd ever get five hard casts off in a one-on-one encounter at all is if you're fighting an especially tanky opponent. Especially for a glass cannon build like elemental shaman, five hardcasts is just not ever going to happen in any PvP fight except for an extended fight over an AV graveyard. This is really different from PvE, especially raiding, where fights last longer and that five hardcast on-ramp is much less of an issue. The average player has 4k-5k hp, if you're dealing ~750 damage per lightning bolt and doing nothing else, your target is almost guaranteed to be dead before getting 5 hardcasts off.

The second issue I have with it is that it doesn't quite fit the class identity of elemental shaman. The spell is LIGHTNING bolt, lightning strikes fast, zapping an unlucky area with a blast of sudden energy that's gone in a blink. In the original classic design lightning bolt and chain lightning hit at the same time for burst damage, giving the playstyle that sort of lightning-fast explosive feeling. That's why the "shock" spells are instant cast.

> **Ladhihs wrote: Wed Nov 20, 2024 3:36 am**
> didn't understand why shocks are important to elemental burst

I am admittedly less clear on this one. I've always used shocks either to confirm a kill if the initial burst doesn't do it, or more for their utility.

> **Ladhihs wrote: Wed Nov 20, 2024 3:36 am**
> insisted shamans use the new Elemental Mastery to make Electrify less painful

You talked about it a bit in your post but I think it's worth emphasizing. There's a real choice to be made between Elemental Mastery or Nature's Swiftness. On one hand Nature's Swiftness is an exceptionally versatile skill, you can instant-cast a lightning bolt to add more damage to a burst, or use it on a heal to save a party member in a tight spot. Compare to Elemental Mastery which is all damage, it lets you control exactly when you will get a burst so you can time it for effectiveness, or use it as a type of ambush. There have been, and continue to be, constant arguments over which one is better in PvP. It's a really compelling, difficult choice in the normal vanilla talent tree that doesn't really exist anymore in CC2.

If you're going with Elemental Mastery the guaranteed crit is **the most important time** to have your crit damage bonus at 100%. This isn't currently possible unless you've already done three hardcasts, which not only restricts your ability to time a burst but also makes it effectively impossible to ambush someone at full power. For someone doing a long PvE fight using EM to keep mana costs down and score some extra free damage it's not an issue but this change makes the ability barely worth using in a PvP scenario.

author: Zeena
subject: Elemental Devastation Talent Change
content_md:
Hello fellow adventurers,

I've been reflecting on the recent change to the Elemental Devastation talent and I’m struggling to understand the reasoning behind it.

Previously, this talent granted +9% melee crit chance after a successful spell crit. This made perfect sense within the Elemental talent tree, as it synergized beautifully with the ultimate talent that provides 100% spell crit chance. The intent seemed clear: encourage a hybrid playstyle where shamans alternate between ranged spells and melee attacks, embodying the hybrid nature of the class.

Now, Elemental Devastation provides 3% base spell and melee hit, plus 9% spell hit after a melee crit. This feels like the complete opposite of its original design. Instead of promoting the hybrid playstyle, it now pushes us towards stacking hit, which we already achieve through base talents and gear.

Questions:

What’s the rationale behind doubling down on spell hit?
Wouldn’t crit-related bonus align better with the name Elemental Devastation? If it were about hit, it would have been called Elemental Precision.

Wouldn’t a more balanced approach be 3% base hit (spell and melee) plus 9% melee crit after a spell crit? This would maintain synergy between ranged and melee damage, allowing shamans to adapt fluidly in combat—a hallmark of the hybrid class fantasy.

I’d love to hear from the community on this. Am I missing something? Does anyone else feel this change undermines the hybrid shaman playstyle?

author: Voodoochile
subject: Re: Elemental Devastation Talent Change
content_md:
It really feels like the dev team doesn't understand what makes the class feel good. Like on paper making your spells miss less seems like a good trade, but the talent is explicitly designed with enhance in mind because it only procs on melee crits. But at the same time they made enhance even more melee-centric and getting an extra shock hit every 9-10 casts doesn't feel good. Not to mention it is just a dead talent now for ele since the point was to have increase your melee dps with synergy with your spell-crit focused scalings. From this design point, Ele's only lost out in the talent reshuffle as now they have the 3% spell hit but no elemental devastation ON TOP OF the nerf to their crit burst.

I firmly believe this patch was extremely detrimental to the Shaman class as a whole, but for the already semi-viable Elemental shaman in particular. And it only emphasizes why the timing of fresh classic servers feels so onpoint

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Elemental Devastation Talent Change
content_md:
The old elemental devastation was incredibly weak. If you play a hybrid playstile, hit, spellhit & spellcrit are consistently the most hard things to gear for.

By making elemental devastation provide spellhit on a physical crit, it allows for much more effective gearing for shamans who wanna do both, hitting in melee and dealing damage with spells.

While it looses part of its flavor, the talent was so bad it was never actually skilled by any shaman that knows what they are doing. Now its at least useful

Personally i would have prefered instead of having 3% spellhit be baked in to keep the old effect and add the new proc effect (so melee crits give spellhit and spellcrits give melee crit)

content_html:
Hello fellow adventurers,

I've been reflecting on the recent change to the Elemental Devastation talent and I’m struggling to understand the reasoning behind it.

Previously, this talent granted +9% melee crit chance after a successful spell crit. This made perfect sense within the Elemental talent tree, as it synergized beautifully with the ultimate talent that provides 100% spell crit chance. The intent seemed clear: encourage a hybrid playstyle where shamans alternate between ranged spells and melee attacks, embodying the hybrid nature of the class.

Now, Elemental Devastation provides 3% base spell and melee hit, plus 9% spell hit after a melee crit. This feels like the complete opposite of its original design. Instead of promoting the hybrid playstyle, it now pushes us towards stacking hit, which we already achieve through base talents and gear.

Questions:

What’s the rationale behind doubling down on spell hit?
Wouldn’t crit-related bonus align better with the name Elemental Devastation? If it were about hit, it would have been called Elemental Precision.

Wouldn’t a more balanced approach be 3% base hit (spell and melee) plus 9% melee crit after a spell crit? This would maintain synergy between ranged and melee damage, allowing shamans to adapt fluidly in combat—a hallmark of the hybrid class fantasy.

I’d love to hear from the community on this. Am I missing something? Does anyone else feel this change undermines the hybrid shaman playstyle?
I agree with you. It should provide +% crit instead. Getting a temporary +% hit buff is just weird meta all around.

And you are right that elemental devastation evokes the idea of critical damage.

subject: Re: Elemental Devastation Talent Change

The old elemental devastation was very good for tank shaman's mana efficiency especially in conjunction with flurry (increased attack speed after crit) and elemental focus (mana reduction of shocks after crit). As a tank you ideally used a fast weapon so you had crazy good proc rate on elemental devastation. If you played it right almost every earth shock got the mana cost reduction.

Now we have lightning strike to trigger an empowered water shield charge plus the new stable shields talent which ups the number of charges to a whooping 9. That also frees up a lot of global cool towns. Don't know whether mana efficiency is better now but from my limited play time today I would say: yes.

Note that during Bloodlust you still get up to the old attack speed you had with pre-nerf flurry.

Edit: shamans now essentially gain 5 talent points because they no longer have to "waist" 5 points on the first row of restoration to get to the 3% hit chance talent. Seems like a net positive.

author: Manletow
subject: CC2 has been great for Shaman! ^.^
content_md:
Preface: Don't really know/care about Raiding tbh

But from a PVP perspective -- CC2 has been **great** for Shaman!
Well done!

Elemental was somewhat overpowered...
And also boring to play (spam Lightning Bolts).
This was successfully addressed via various new hybrid spec / gameplay options.

Enhancement simply hit for rather lame, weak-sauce damage (if you played my favorite: Tank/Resto combo)

or it was a gamblers meme spec of Windfury 2hander (terribly unreliable)

or it was just 'Elemental Lite -- where you aim for huge Shock crits to win'

This was all successfully addressed.
You are now properly a 'scrappy jack of all trades brawler with spells'.

Deep Resto is now viable (at least in AV) as you can be a proper Chain Heal master.
And you save key targets with 'Spirit Link'. Probably great in Blood Ring.
Mana Tide Totem was GOD AWFUL and unplayable in PVP.

P.S. I often mocked "Lightning Strike" as "Holy Strike Jr.'
This was unwarranted.

First of all, Lightning Strike doesnt hit nearly as hard (wise)
Second of all, you have to spend Talent Points to get it (wise)
Thirdly, theres actually counter-play options for enemies (they can dispel the Shield buff -- neutering the attack)
Fourthly, it feels fun to use. Sounds and looks cool. Shaman vibes are strong.
Fifthly, the longer lasting Shield buffs/orbs are a great quality of life change.

Thunderhead, i loved thee but this new shit is actually incredibly well designed. I'm impressed.

P.P.S Purge is still overpowered however and should be nerfed.

author: Manletow
subject: Re: Is ele shaman done in pvp ?
content_md:
How do you play your ele shaman ?

For fun/solo memeing:
Use Flame Shock more often (30 yard range)
engage via melee attacks more often (lightning strike easy to get)
Use Rank 1 LB to get Electrified easily (less than .5 sec cast time)

For actually winning Battlegrounds:
Play as a conservative supporter:
 1. Spam Spam Spam Purge.
 2. Provide key targets emergency heals (you crit quite often. these crit heals also activate Clearcasting btw)
 3. Interrupt Spell casts
 4. Provide Totems (such as Grounding)
 5. Use Chain Lightning on groups (especially weakened groups)

Note: Ele Shaman was nerfed as this was considered "Fair"
Due to Paladin also being nerfed so it would revert back to being what it was meant to be (a Supporter)

The problem is that Paladins (and Shamans) all want to be "1 man armies".
So they salty AF

I appreciate you and other users who have said similar regarding shaman being the horde's offensive counterweight to the alliance's defense via paladin, and I've echoed this point in my posts as well. I hope we can keep driving it home because it is critical to the balance of vanilla.

 **In a sense, all of vanilla's class design philosophy hinged on the delicate dance between shamans and paladins, which were each unique to their respective factions.** They each had their strengths and weaknesses, and had meme specs to them, but for all intensive purposes these classes were equal. And because of that, vanilla wow, even with its imperfections, actually had designed a really great class ecosystem.

 **Turtle has disrupted this delicate ecosystem. First with its favortism towards paladin and neglect of shaman over the years, and now via CC2 which has overhauled many other classes and their identities as well.**

To your point on shamans being tanks, I don't quite agree. There was a skeleton within the vanilla shaman tree that suggested some tanking via shield talents etc. think it is okay for shamans to have some tank capacity, however I think they should be the weakest of the viable tanks. I'd like to write a post about this at some point if someone else doesn't get to it first.

 **Basically I think the order of viable tanks should be: Warrior > Druid > Paladin > Shaman, where shaman is clearly the worst physical tank but actually excels as a magic tank, which allows for unique scenarios and class fantasy.**

With all that said, I hope we can all continue to drive the point at the turtle devs that shamans and paladins must become more equal. Faction balance and the fate of the server depends on this.

imo it was a cool decision to give more power to enhance dps but that should only be a lvling thing and not viable for raiding. This makes us closer to druids than palys witch is wrong imo(2dps specs one tank and one heal).

The only true dps spec (ele) should be at the same power lvl like ret. Shaman is a Caster class after all.
Why paladin should have 3 viable specs and shaman only 2? Shaman is an offensive counterweight that horde has to defensive paladins of alliance, therefore shaman has more offensive options (enhancement, elemental) and paladin has more defensive options (holy, protection). Shaman tank is a travesty, was never intended to be one and is one of many mistakes twow developers did in 1.17.2 that nobody asked for
I appreciate you and other users who have said similar regarding shaman being the horde's offensive counterweight to the alliance's defense via paladin, and I've echoed this point in my posts as well. I hope we can keep driving it home because it is critical to the balance of vanilla.

In a sense, all of vanilla's class design philosophy hinged on the delicate dance between shamans and paladins, which were each unique to their respective factions. They each had their strengths and weaknesses, and had meme specs to them, but for all intensive purposes these classes were equal. And because of that, vanilla wow, even with its imperfections, actually had designed a really great class ecosystem.

Turtle has disrupted this delicate ecosystem. First with its favortism towards paladin and neglect of shaman over the years, and now via CC2 which has overhauled many other classes and their identities as well.

To your point on shamans being tanks, I don't quite agree. There was a skeleton within the vanilla shaman tree that suggested some tanking via shield talents etc. think it is okay for shamans to have some tank capacity, however I think they should be the weakest of the viable tanks. I'd like to write a post about this at some point if someone else doesn't get to it first.

Basically I think the order of viable tanks should be: Warrior > Druid > Paladin > Shaman, where shaman is clearly the worst physical tank but actually excels as a magic tank, which allows for unique scenarios and class fantasy.

With all that said, I hope we can all continue to drive the point at the turtle devs that shamans and paladins must become more equal. Faction balance and the fate of the server depends on this.

author: Neechy
subject: Remove Electrify
content_md:
Dear Turtle Wow Team,

I write this on behalf of the shaman community as you have likely seen (I hope) the majority disappointment with CC2 changes to shaman elemental spec in particular. And it is primarily due to replacing the iconic Elemental Fury talent with the highly flawed Electrify talent. While the community is of course happy with a number of aspects of this update, this was not one of them.

To quote @Ladhihs who captured the issue perfectly on a separate thread:

> **Ladhihs wrote: Wed Nov 20, 2024 3:36 am**
> The fundamental issue is that the developers don't play the game.
>
>  When the shaman discord was discussing [Electrify] before it was released and how it will kill elemental pvp, Haaxor:
>  didn't understand why shamans "can't just get 5 casts off" to get the full buff
>  didn't understand why shocks are important to elemental burst
>  insisted shamans use the new Elemental Mastery to make Electrify less painful
>
>  Not only is it bad game design to be pigeonholed into a talent to get around another talent that only exists to nerf your potential, it goes against vanilla's design. It's intentional that shamans have a choice between EM and NS; do you want a guaranteed crit or be more versatile? Turtle is trying to remove that choice as a roundabout way of further nerfing shaman.
>
>  **Shaman was designed as the Horde's offensive answer to the Alliance's defensive bulwark that is paladin. As paladin had the best cooldowns and utility but no damage, shaman was given damage but no cooldowns, mobility, or utility. Its sustain was also poor. By nerfing shaman's niche the class is effectively dead and faction balance is now heavily skewed towards Alliance.**
>
>  It is obvious that they are approaching class design in a class by class basis. They have no vision of how the classes are meant to interact with each other. This is why EF got turned into Electrify, while Ruin/Arcane Potency didn't get changed. It's why Enhancement's Flurry got nerfed and Warrior's didn't. No other class has to "ramp up" their damage and they retained their kit. Hell, most of them have only gotten better with this patch.
>
>  As of CC2 shaman is now objectively the worst class and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone.

With all that said, we do understand that the rationale for Electrify was to reduce shaman burst (because apparently no other classes have crazy burst in PvP right?). So if there is no budging on that then here is...

My suggestion:
Updated talent (1 point): Elemental Fury
"Casting your Shock spells invigorates you with Elemental Fury, increasing the critical strike damage bonus of your Fire, Frost, and Nature spells by 100%. Lasts 30 seconds"

 **What does this suggestion address?**
 - It is still a nerf from the original Elemental Fury talent because it requires having to "attune" yourself by casting a Shock first, slowing down the burst that you would normally have from opening with a guaranteed lightning bolt crit.
 - Does not affect totem crit damage as the OG Ele Fury talent, only spells the shaman casts. As such, TWoW's Flame Guidance talent is still viable and encouraged.
 - Still has a duration (although increased from 20 s -> 30 s), meaning the Shock charge up will be a regular part of rotation between fights
 - Does not have the +10% nature damage that came with 5 stacks of Electrify, because increasing damage that wasn't part of the original vanilla specs is leading to power creep, an issue that a lot of players are rightly concerned about.

content_html:
Dear Turtle Wow Team,

I write this on behalf of the shaman community as you have likely seen (I hope) the majority disappointment with CC2 changes to shaman elemental spec in particular. And it is primarily due to replacing the iconic Elemental Fury talent with the highly flawed Electrify talent. While the community is of course happy with a number of aspects of this update, this was not one of them.

To quote @Ladhihs who captured the issue perfectly on a separate thread:
The fundamental issue is that the developers don't play the game.

When the shaman discord was discussing [Electrify] before it was released and how it will kill elemental pvp, Haaxor:
didn't understand why shamans "can't just get 5 casts off" to get the full buff
didn't understand why shocks are important to elemental burst
insisted shamans use the new Elemental Mastery to make Electrify less painful

Not only is it bad game design to be pigeonholed into a talent to get around another talent that only exists to nerf your potential, it goes against vanilla's design. It's intentional that shamans have a choice between EM and NS; do you want a guaranteed crit or be more versatile? Turtle is trying to remove that choice as a roundabout way of further nerfing shaman.

Shaman was designed as the Horde's offensive answer to the Alliance's defensive bulwark that is paladin. As paladin had the best cooldowns and utility but no damage, shaman was given damage but no cooldowns, mobility, or utility. Its sustain was also poor. By nerfing shaman's niche the class is effectively dead and faction balance is now heavily skewed towards Alliance.

It is obvious that they are approaching class design in a class by class basis. They have no vision of how the classes are meant to interact with each other. This is why EF got turned into Electrify, while Ruin/Arcane Potency didn't get changed. It's why Enhancement's Flurry got nerfed and Warrior's didn't. No other class has to "ramp up" their damage and they retained their kit. Hell, most of them have only gotten better with this patch.

As of CC2 shaman is now objectively the worst class and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone.
With all that said, we do understand that the rationale for Electrify was to reduce shaman burst (because apparently no other classes have crazy burst in PvP right?). So if there is no budging on that then here is...

My suggestion:
Updated talent (1 point): Elemental Fury
"Casting your Shock spells invigorates you with Elemental Fury, increasing the critical strike damage bonus of your Fire, Frost, and Nature spells by 100%. Lasts 30 seconds"

What does this suggestion address?
- It is still a nerf from the original Elemental Fury talent because it requires having to "attune" yourself by casting a Shock first, slowing down the burst that you would normally have from opening with a guaranteed lightning bolt crit.
- Does not affect totem crit damage as the OG Ele Fury talent, only spells the shaman casts. As such, TWoW's Flame Guidance talent is still viable and encouraged.
- Still has a duration (although increased from 20 s -> 30 s), meaning the Shock charge up will be a regular part of rotation between fights
- Does not have the +10% nature damage that came with 5 stacks of Electrify, because increasing damage that wasn't part of the original vanilla specs is leading to power creep, an issue that a lot of players are rightly concerned about.

In conclusion, if the dev team is unwilling to bring back Elemental Fury as before (e.g. due to the ele spec in context of other class changes) then there has to be an overhaul of the Electrify talent that can respect the shaman spec identity and ensure its viability in both PvP and PvE.

I provided one possible solution and the rationale, I am happy to hear thoughts on this. And more than that, I think the shaman community would like to hear from the dev team to know that our feedback is being seriously considered and addressed.

Bumping this post. Electrify remains a terribly designed talent and needs an overlook or revert as soon as possible. You have shattered the spec for pvp, particularly in the chaotic CC2-meta, and the design strongly suggests that it was built on theorizing with little pvp testing.

author: Neechy
subject: Re: Remove Electrify
content_md:
I want to thank everyone who has engaged in these discussions in the past few weeks, and helped provide the necessary constructive criticism that CC2 warrants.

While I don't know if this thread influenced devs at all, I do know that our collective feedback is helping to push the needle. So please keep making your voices heard.

Dec 20 update resulted in the following change for Electrify...
> **Jamey wrote: Fri Dec 20, 2024 2:58 am**
> **Electrify:** Maximum stacks reduced from 5 to 2. Each stack grants 50% critical strike damage bonus and 5% increased Nature damage. Effect duration reduced from 20 to 15 seconds.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Balancing the value of Electrify's stacks will ensure the class can still enjoy a ramping power level over the course of a fight without over-reliance on Elemental Mastery as a cooldown or the use of unintuitive tactics to perform at an appropriate level.*
> ---

For added context, here are a couple replies to regarding the ???'th set of CC2 revisions:
> **Bjorn88 wrote: Fri Dec 20, 2024 8:12 pm**
> "Electrify: Maximum stacks reduced from 5 to 2. Each stack grants 50% critical strike damage bonus and 5% increased Nature damage. Effect duration reduced from 20 to 15 seconds."
>
>  Thank you, this is a step in the right direction to restoring the elemental spec.
>
>  To the many players that continue to be dissatisfied: Be active on forums, continue to make detailed, constructive posts.  The above changes to electrify were preceded by lengthy posts explaining why and how the talent change was a mistake.

> **Neechy wrote: Fri Dec 20, 2024 8:20 am**
> Is it just me or is anyone else annoyed by the bizarre and messy feel to some of the design changes, including point intervals? Vanilla had such a simple clean feel to class design and it feels like every round of class changes just tangles us more and more in some incoherent mess.
>
>  E.g.
> > **Jamey wrote: Fri Dec 20, 2024 2:58 am**
> > **Flurry (Shaman):** Attack speed bonus increased from 7/9/11/13/15% to 8/11/14/17/20%.
> >
> >  **Master of Arms:** Mace armor penetration reduced from 2/4/6/8/10 to 1.2/2.4/3.6/4.8/6 per level, meaning its reduced from 600 to 360 at Level 60.
>
>  This kind of stuff just looks odd on the tooltip. It confirms my fears that rather than reverting some of the more problematic talent/ability changes with CC2 all they are doing is adjusting numbers. It seems they aren't considering that the new talents and new/removed abilities might be the issues. Once again, it's starting to feel like a [CC2 sunk cost fallacy](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=111804).
>
>  As another example of this, they keep shaman Electrify but just reduce the number of stacks rather than removing/reverting the ability entirely. While I'm glad the stacks are at least reduced, it's like they don't even consider there are other design options than needing to stack. Once again, why do shamans have a stacking mechanic for their 100% crit bonus but destro locks and balance druids get theirs permanently?

So is the update to Electrify a positive?
Sure.
Yet it remains a net negative, because it maintains an awkward stacking mechanism that doesn't need to exist in the first place. Requiring 2 stacks still makes for annoying gameplay. And yet, it is innocuous enough that it feels like an admission by the devs that stacks were never needed.

As with many CC2 changes it has added unnecessary complexities to gameplay based on inadequate understanding of class dynamics within the overall class ecosystem. All changes seem to be applied in isolation, which overlooks the due consideration for class interaction that OG blizzard had.

Devs hear "shaman burst too OP" and just nerf the burst via a clunky stacking mechanic. Yet they do not provide explanations for why balance druids and destro warlocks maintain their own static 100% crit bonus damage talents.

Unlike CC1, TWoW's approach with CC2 has been radical overhauls of time-tested class design that has forced players to deal with clunky, unpolished changes on the live server.

The team stated that it would be making small changes based on player feedback, however these appear to be predominantly number tweaks. The issue with number tweaks is they don't address the fact that the real issue may *actually* be the new talents/ability changes themselves. I don't see how turtle is going to math its way out of the damage caused by CC2.

There have been talks on the forum/discord asking for the possibility of rolling back changes and allowing testing on a separate test server. I support this suggestion because this would have been a better approach for turtle to take in the first place. The way CC2 was released has simply led to a neverending set of revisions that has disrupted the playerbase, dev resources, and the rollout of new content including the long-delayed Kara40 raid.

Anyways that's my rant. Let's keep advocating for what we feel is best for the long-term health of the server. Thanks everyone.

author: Neechy
subject: Re: Remove Electrify
content_md:
> **amanagor wrote: Tue Dec 24, 2024 4:02 pm**
> The main reason ele appears so strong, is that it only ever has to fight alliance.

And this is the issue with changes like Electrify, let's be honest. It was applied because of PvP complaints.

They nerfed shaman burst while simultaneously buffing paladins out the ass because horde tends to attract more PvP-skilled players than alliance. As a result, they are punishing some players and appeasing others to "balance PvP" when it more often than not just boils down to skill issues..

And once again, shaman burst was nerfed without understanding why the burst exists in the context of other class interactions.

> **amanagor wrote: Tue Dec 24, 2024 9:49 am**
> While its an an annoying mecanique to get used to, its certainly a massive buff overall in pve and pvp.  Not needing to worry about threat on the first cast allows you to precast and go hard from start, and then you get 10%more damage. And in pvp, especially with 8 part t3 making shocks give electrify + extra damage on shocks, its trivial to get up and you can get big burst with 1 cast without any buildup that is even higher than pre cc2. Lightning bolt em chainlightning or lightning bolt em shock are both very strong comboes that dont require buildup. Ele burst is back and stronger than before imo.

Thing is, ele didn't really need buffs beyond mana efficiency imo. Same goes for other classes, because it introduces power creep and trivializes PvE. I'm sure many would be fine with losing the 10% extra nature damage if it meant a return the simple, static 100% crit bonus of elemental fury, in line with balance druids and destro locks.

Requiring specific gear to make Electrify less shitty is bad design. How many players are realistically able or want to grind for T3 8 piece? And let's say you get it.. now you are pigeonholed into wearing those 8 pieces just to maintain the benefit.

Armor effects and set bonuses should not determine the viability of an ability if that ability is essential to the entire spec, as Electrify is for shamans.

In conclusion, we will keep pushing for a return to Elemental Fury.
