Second use is at LOS pulling. If you put it down, the casters and you can unleash magical hell unto the approaching mobs so they get much weaker by the time they arrive. Just make sure that you regain threat on them asap. Best is if they focus fire 1 guy so even if he survives getting to you, you can just taunt it away.

Tremor totem
Utility when you expect fear, sleep or charm. Not much else to say.

Water totems

Mana spring totem
Has two uses. Use it every time when someone is drinking, and use it if you plan to stay in your immediate surrounding for more than 20 seconds (costs you 100 mana, gives the party 10 mana every 2 seconds). If you get good at expecting when you stay longer at one place and use it regularly, it helps a lot with mana management. Best case scenario is +200 mana for you, +300 mana for the party members after each full mana spring totem.

Healing stream totem
Very weak but a member of your 'defensive toolkit'. If you need to do everything to survive, use it with grace of air totem, stoneskin totem and earth shield.

Poison/disease cleansing totem
Use it when reoccuring, aoe poisons or diseases happen, f.ex. the belchers at Strat UD.
For 1 poison, manual removal via Decursive addon is better.

Fire resistance totem
Same logic as all resistance totems. Specilly good in Black Rock Mountain.

Fire totems

Fire nova totem
If you made a big LOS pul, it is good to start with a fire nova totem. It is counting down, then explodes when the mobs arrive if you're doing it right and gives you a ton of initial threat. It can be followed up by magma totem.
So its use is to maximize aoe threat output, usually for LOS pulls when maximizing threat is important.

Magma totem
Your expensive aoe threat option. Has no CD, it's spammable but it's super expensive. Use it when you'd use stoneclaw totem if a) stoneclaw totem is on CD, b) stoneclaw totem is not enough to keep threat. Use it sparingly, it is the biggest mana burner.
You can also downgrade it to save some mana but even lower versions are expensive.
Can also be used against a single target (usually boss) to maximize threat but only do it if you absolutely have to. Eats your mana like nothing else.

Searing totem
A cheaper solution to raise threat against 1-2 targets. I'd only consider using it against really overeager DPS since you should be able to handle 1-2 targets without totems usually.
Never used it if a target is sheeped, shackled or if there is a nearby pack or patrol.

Flametongue totem
The windfury situation again but at least melee is less aware of this and it is expected much more rarely. If asked, just say no. Less beneficial for melee than WF, you get nothing, you spend mana and you get locked out from useful fire totems which you might need.
Only use it for the melee emergency scenario when you give your melees each toolkit just to kill mobs asap.

Frost resistance totem
Same as the other resistance totems.

_____________

So, as a warden shaman, unlike any other kind of shaman, your thinking is not 'what totems are the best here'. Instead you go by 'what totems are absolutely needed'?

You are under emergency and are about to die?
grace of air, stoneskin, healing stream

You are under emergency but melee can save the day going Rambo?
WF, strength of earth, flametongue.

You are almost dead and started kiting the melee boss?
Earthbind, optinally searing totem and healing stream totem.

Etc. The situation determines the need of the totems and you usually go for the least amount necessary.
WF is the exception if melee really wants it.

____________

6. Elemental shields

Your default elemental shield is mana shield from level 26, when you learn it.
It helps restoring mana, enabling the 'smooth and fast' gameplay idea.

The other shields have uses, too, though.
Lightning shield is to maximize threat, if you really need to race for it (or to maximize damage).
Earth shield is to maximize survivability (alongside its best friends, grace of air totem, stoneskin totem and healing stream totem).

Usually you wear water shield but your threatmeter (lightning shield) and your health bar (earth shield) can convince you to swap if needed.

___________

7. Shocks

Earth shock has an innate 1,5x threat modifier (further affected by rockbiter weapon) and it's the only nature damage shock we have thus only this shock gets buffed by stormstrike. It is our default one.
I usually have max rank, rank 4-5 and rank 1 on my action bars. Rank 4-5 to save mana while still being effective, rank 1 if you only want to interrupt a casting and threat is good.

Frost shock usually comes into the picture either when the mobs have high nature resistance (some parts of Maraudon for example) or if you switched to kiting. Otherwise doesn't worth it. If you use frost shock for kiting, using a rank 1 is perfect, it saves mana (unless damage is important, too).

Flame shock does the most damage if the dot can fully expire on the target but has no threat modifiers. Can be used on your target to maximize damage if threat is in control otherwise, or you can use it on a non-skull enemy to 'give some passive threat' to you. It can be good if not everyone is following skull and you want some extra insurance against overaggro on that target. Flame shock is also excellent against targets which occassionally reset aggro, ensuring that even if it happens, you quickly (and automatically) reestablish some threat on the target. The same can be applied to each of our periodic damage-dealers, like magma totem or searing totem, too (as long as searing stays on target).

___________

8. Relics

If you wanna min-max, once you have several relics, macro them to spells. Shock tied to totem of rage, lightning bolt tied to totem of crackling thunder etc. Can cheat you some extra threat.
Heard about problems about relic swapping and GCD but never experienced it.

__________

9. Weapons

If you played a warden shaman before the class changes, you went for the fastest weapons.
The old mantra was:
1. While rockbiter's TPS scales with weapon speed, missing a hit with a slow weapon is way worse then missing a quick hit every now and then.
2. You have no aoe threat, you gotta stab around quick to establish threat on each target.

Now, with the threat from the totems and a safety taunt, this can be forgotten. Usually go for a slower one-hander!
Both SS and LS damage scale based on your weapon's damage, meaning that a slower weapon greatly increases your DPS and threat output.

The counter-argument people sometimes have is that any form of enhancement shaman is very crit-reliant, you need many procs to be consistent. But is it true?
Elemental devastation gives the spell hit bonus for 15 seconds (!) after a melee crit.
Clearcasting activates from spell crit and melee crit, too and stays active until you perform 2 damaging spells.
Flurry indeed needs a melee crit but its effect lasts for your 3 next swings, which is a decent time with a slower weapon.
Bloodlust gives a minimal haste buff to the party for 5 sec if you perform a melee crit.

There will be some situations when you lack a buff with the slower weapon which you'd otherwise have with a fast dagger.
But
* You can proc these reliably enough anyway, specially once geared a bit towards crit.
* The extra threat from SS and LS makes it worth it.
* Current flurry is a disgrace.

Other things to note:
* As an orc, of course prioritize axes.
* You can do the old shaman trick of using a spellpower weapon -> pulling -> switching to the normal weapon set but our threat is much more reliable now, there is less need for these tricks.
* You can keep a two-hander in your bag and occasionally switch to 'no shield tanking'. It generates much more threat (SS and LS still scale with weapon power) but do it only to catch up at bosses when taunt is on CD with a big number / the target cannot be taunted or when healer likes to live dangerously. You wear mail after all.
_________

10. The party and you

Honestly, I'm not that familiar with the new builds after CC2, so I might miss some things but wanna give some generic tips.
Let's say that one of the DPS is mage. Ask for water, vendor drink is expensive. Intellect is cool, helps with mana management. And sheep. When to ask for sheep? If the pack is big enough that pulling the whole thing can be risky (+ preferably no known patrol goes there to discover the sheep).
Arcane mage can give you +healing received but but + spell damage taken buff in places where you fight only melee.

Priest works the same way as mage's poly regarding shackle undead. Stam and spirit are super cool. If you're a priest's champion, ask for the + damage and spell damage one if the priest has no problems keeping you alive. Remember, fear ward is base now, if you got feared, raise an eyebrow towards the priest (sure, you have tremor but it's less reliable). Shadow resistance in places like Gilneas, of course.

Palas. Ask for wisdom unless threat is a problem and you don't want to confront DPS. If you're okay with confronting them, ask for wisdom and ask for salvation on the problematic DPS. If you get trapped in a net for example and the inability to move screws you, ask for freedom. Palas underuse freedom in my experience. Ask for devotion aura, specially pre-level 33. A good paladin friend during the early game is a blessing to your run, pun intended. A judgment of wisdom on a boss is a beautiful thing.

Druids. The usual. Druid buff is very cool. Expect to be the brez target if it is needed. Innervate optimally goes to healer, specially if you're confident with mana management and wanna make sure that you give everyone a fast run. I promise you, nothing makes them as happy as a speedrun in a place where they expected a 1-2 hour grind.

Warrior. If you plan to use LOS pulls, discuss with the DPS warrior first. They have that urge to charge at skull at the second your spell hits the target. Many of my ranged pulls became a very weird running all over the place when I hid behind a wall and waited for the mobs to come just to realize that warrior kept all of them far away with a charge. This can be discussed. Utility like shouts are very good (including the damage reduction one if you really need to survive) and sunder armor is situationally super good if they are willing to do it. Just like disarm. After ret palas, the second most vehement protesters if WF totem is not placed.

Rogue. Subtlety definitely does something and I have no idea how that works. Sub can also offer sap without pulling every mob to himself and die or force a vanish right after. Combat rogues are your usual DPS machines. Despite having a strike lowering their threat, combat rogues are the harder ones to keep threat away from.

Warlock. If needed, ask them to keep the imp out. Specially pre-level 33 when survival is a mess. They also have a threat-stone now but honestly, no idea how that works. Fear is super good when LOS-pulling and the area is cleared. But only then. Same goes to the priests' aoe fear of course.

Hunters. They have a tendency to want to dictate the tempo and to select a random mob which they decide to OT with their pet. Latter thing is totally okay, just let them enjoy the game on their terms. But if the hunter keeps pulling when healer has like 10% mana, ask them to stop. Cheetah when running around empty places and well-placed traps are super cool. Extremely high threat though, despite having abilities to reduce it.

Shamans. Honestly, shaman threat is kinda high and enh usually wants to drink after every 1-2 pulls, it's a bit annoying. What's important: if there are other shamans in the party, always discuss who uses what totem. Since you wanna AVOID using totems unless needed, try to ask them to please use this and that (they are perfect for WF totem).

Also:
Don't forget that you can manage poison and disease but you cannot demagic or decurse. Know in advance what to expect in an instance and if it has a very nasty magic or curse, try to gather a team accordingly. Poison and disease you can handle, a bad curse or magic, without a proper team can make whole runs a pain (think about SFK's ghost fest if noone can decurse or SM GY"s healing reduction decurse).

_____________________

11. Which race to choose?

The main rule is, as cliché as it sounds, is to follow your heart. If you hate playing as a tauren or a troll, you won't enjoy leveling up an 'optimized' tank shaman, so why not go for an orc?
But if you want to clear endgame with your char as a tank, things get more complicated. I usually dislike 'meta-slaves' like guys who couldn't imagine fury warriors not being a human or an orc before the class changes.
But warden shamans, unless patches make them more competitive, are objectively the worst tanks in the game. If you want to earn a place in a not 100% casual guild as a tank with a disadvantaged build, you'll need every possible advantage, including racials.

So that out of the way, how do the different races fare?

Orcs are probably the worst choice. You get some weapon skills, which can indeed be useful. When Kara40 comes out, we'll see what weapons get added to the game. This, plus an ancient war text and some weapon skills from here and there and you have the advantage of greatly reduced glancing blows when using an axe. Even if we don't min-max, if you use an axe as an orc, your glancing blows tend to have a smaller damage penalty.
Warden shaman's can be played as more spell-oriented and more melee-oriented ones (how much you rely on shock and spellpower vs. raw DPS with rockbiter modifier). The latter build can work out for an orc pretty well since all those damage points which are not lost when glancing help generating threat.
Hardiness is nice but it mostly helps in PVP.
Blood fury is a valid DPS and threat increase but the healing debuff is something you want to avoid as a tank.
All in all, you can play an orc warden shaman as a more melee-oriented tank (to benefit the most from the less glancing blow) which has the option to go for a high risk-decent reward threat increase via blood fury.
Orcs also have access to feral spirits, which is a fairly overpriced, slight DPS increase on CD. Currently discussing internally if feral spirit threat gets redirected to you or not.

Trolls are your more offensive option out of the remaining races. Unlike orcs, trolls don't punish you with a healing debuff when pressing the 'more threat' racial (berserking is still good). Honestly, if I disregard the party buff-effect, berserking almost feels like a second bloodlust on a 3 min CD. You also deal more damage to beasts but it is way too situational.
Your health regeneration became better but don't overvalue it!
The closest data I have found for the shaman's spirit-based health regeneration is this:
https://wowwiki-archive.fandom.com/wiki ... generation

As a reminder, regeneration, as it stands:
'Regeneration now increases health regeneration by 20% instead of 10% and allows 25% of total health regeneration to continue in combat instead of 10%.'
viewtopic.php?p=102974#p102972

In other words:
1.2*(Spirit * 0.11 + 7)/4 -> If I am correct.

Warden shamans are not famous from their over-the-top spirit. Let's say that your spirit is 200, after buffs!

1.2*(200*0.11 + 7)/4 = 1.2*29/4 = 8.7 HP every 2 seconds with the racial during combat if my math was correct.

I reserve the right to be wrong at maths though.
(If you want to abuse the regeneration racial, create a warrior tank with high spirit and extra meditation for health! The warrior's spirit conversion formula is much more interesting.)

What I wanted to say -> The trolls have one really relevant racial which is extremely good and can give you threat spikes 'on-demand'. Since you mostly cast instant spells during fight, berserking is mostly a melee ability for you.

Taurens are the more defensive iteration of warden shamans. 10 nature resistance is nice but we are talking right now because of three reasons:
* Endurance gives you 5% more HP (after buffs).
* War stomp gives you an aoe stun.
* Totemic slam reduces the target's haste.

Each of these abilities help you to survive. And as a warden shaman you wear mail and have no defensive CD.
The usual thinking regarding tanks is that you have to have just enough survivability and once it is reached, get as much threat as possible. Taurens can be slightly more threat-oriented with their gearing or they can just be a 'safer version of the most fragile tank in the game'.
Also, tauren shamans can 'buy themselves a free lesser healing wave' with war stomp.

In short
Less recommended: orc ( melee-warden build)
More recommended: troll (threat spikes via berserking), tauren (better defensives, allows more offensive gearing)
_____________________

I hope this will help some new warden shamans.
One last thing.
When leveling a tank, I usually avoid red dungeons but go to orange ones without any problem.
As a shaman tank, I avoid red dungeons and I usually reconsider if it's okay for me going into an orange one.

Main takeaway: be frugal, avoid totems and just auto-attack, unless you are forced to do actions. Saves mana, enables smooth runs.

12. PS:
I almost forgot. Even if you tank many mobs, position yourself in a way that:
1. Each of them is facing you. Parry, block and dodge won't work if the mob is hitting you from the back.
2. ...in a way that you turn the mobs around so the DPS instantly sees their backs and can start DPSing right away. Important for melee, since mobs, just like us, can't parry, block or dodge when attacked from behind.

Tanking talents won't help "lack of tanks" LFT problem for a long term.
Right now, queue times might be lower, but it can be just because people want to try new build.
What is really matter is "will enhs be able to tank without specific tanking talents".
Your basic toolkit matters more than talents, because during leveling, very few people will invest to specific talents.
Thats why I think that tanking talents were aimed to raid tanking.

I assume, main problem of enhs in role of tanks was lack of mana-sustain. It was greatly improved by mana-shield and Lightning Strike. You also get "defensive stance" in form of Rockbiter. So I think that this goal was successfully achieved. Baseline taunt also helped very much.

 20 defense in talents won't really help you to build raid-viable tank. Warriors and paladins deal with criticals and crushing by pushing them out of attack table by high block chance.
Capping defense is "TBC" way of gearing.

Lack of emergency CD is true. But I am afraid, such feature could cause "overpowered in PvP" problem. Regardless of whether it is true or not. Imo, shamans deserve good defensive toolkit because paladins got good offensive abilities.

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: What exactly does a shaman tank lack?
content_md:
I try to phrase what I think very cautiously, I have no intention to be hurtful to anyone.
In my opinion, half of a tree was sacrificed (maybe rather 30%) to make a viable tanking option for dungeoning, without real later support (talent-wise or gear-wise), except for that random T2,5 set.
I see Xudo's point but I stand by my belief that LFT was in a gruesome state with the waiting times and allowing another class to tank properly made the waiting times somewhat more bearable (tbh I have no statistical data).
BUT
It was done by sacrificing the completeness of enh DPS (they are an interesting build now built around being oom) - the talents for tanking could be replaced by new talents, enabling upkeeping your rotation for a whole bossfight for example.
But no, enh DPS didn't get enough talents to work consistently.
I mean, even abominations like ancestral knowledge prove this. The devs were like 'this DPS build doesn't work, let's just give them the most OP stat buff talent, maybe it will balance things out'. (It buffs 10% each stat after modifiers despite what it says.). Despite this, balance was not achieved.

The other way to go around it would have been the 'feral method', sneaking in more modifiers behind rockbiter, maybe a shaman ability which requires rockbiter etc. And then having enough talent slots to include things like a def CD. This option would have been about making both builds good.

But neither happened.
I still love tank shaman, don't get me wrong.
But mana management, despite shields and LS is only good if you are not forced to keep up your rotation for a longer time. Even using mana shields and giving up TPS, mana is a problem. Maximizing TPS with lightning shield makes mana go down to 0 really fast.

How I see this:
To appeal a minority of players and to make LFT less of a pain, TWOW decided to host two builds mostly under enhancement tree (and some ele).
This was not an expectation by the gaming community, people expected a good enh.
Even tank shaman fans (most of them at least) weren't expecting this, they have accepted prior that their build is a meme and went on using oil of immolation etc to cheeze things into a semi-workable category. Then, the expectation of the shaman tanks were so low that it was just a challenge. Those guys, if asked for changes before CC2 mostly mentioned things like 'please add a next level of earth shock that taunts'.
But TWOW gave so much boost to the tank archetype that their are not jokes/challenge materials anymore.
They moved from the joke category to the inferior category where they represent the functional but worse tanking option. Tanking as a shaman is no longer an incredible challenge. You do it, it's totally manageable and the end result is just a worse pala, bear or warrior 99% of the time.

So people were expecting 1 thing from enh tree: good enh.
LFT needed a way to reduce waiting time.
TWOW gave enh two roles:
'oom enh' and 'where defensive?' tank.
Which would have been fine if enh and tank were fun and good.
Not meta-breaking, but moving up from meme category to the inferior category just makes all the challenge and fun disappear and you're left with a boring option producing annoying numbers.
Maybe people wanting to spam SM wait 5 mins shorter in average.
I know, shaman is a utility powerhouse etc but TWOW itself showed via the paladins that you can be a utility powerhouse, a fun class to play and a totally viable option. Not hating on paladins here, good paladin players are usually amongst my fav people on the server, just behind those happy dwarven hunters.

Now challenge tanking is rogue, hunter, warlock and even priest.
Shaman is just a boring option which does the job but everyone secretly wishes you were a bear, a warrior or a pala. Unless you drop WF then lose threat to the melee all the time.
But all good, LFT waiting times are a bit shorter, right?

I'm happy that shaman tanks exist, however I didn't expect it to happen. But if you decided to make this move, go all the way long. Make both DPS and tank both fun and viable.

Thank you.

>  Fine then make it give X armor for each charge if you dont like my idea.

That is NOT how the classic attacktable works.
You start filling from 0%
Add all the effects beneficial to the defender (dodge parry block, miss, glance)
And then fill all the remaining slots with effects beneficial to the attacker (Crit & Crush).
The rest you fill up with white hits.

Considering boss mobs have ~6% crit and a 15% chance to crush.
Unless you reach over 79% combined dodge parry block & miss, block chance will NEVER prevent any crush/crit from occuring nor reduce their damage

Max armor is much more linearly useful, so that is more easily implementable

In my Shaman rework proposal I bring up again the concept of making Spirit Link into an ability available to Enh shamans as a form of single target dmg mitigation in a way that is unique and fits the theme of Shaman as a Utility-centric class. author: Toxo
subject: Re: What exactly does a shaman tank lack?
content_md:
I've played shaman tank through early raids near the end of last year, only to move afterwards to Enhancement Dps. The spec worked ok up to mid Bwl bosses given my items and it probably can work further, as people pushed into tanking bosses in Aq40 and even Naxx, but it requires a lot of dedication and meticulous itemization just to be decent and those items are T2.5, which would make us kind of overgeared in earlier raids and require us to go with higher raiding guilds into Aq40, so we can overgear ourselves for earlier raids within our own guilds. That's basically been my experience from my time trying to make the spec work and how its item progression seems to go here on Twow, which is why I just stuck to Enhance dps instead.

I think Shaman has as far as single target the foundation of a solid tank spec, the way that AoE threat was handled is really interesting and I dig it, but there are some drawbacks that could be improved and make it possible to be strong tanks alongside the other 3.

In short, the itemization is pretty poor, the AoE threat while a neat idea, ends up being a weaker consecration that is more mana hungry and requires 2 totem types to uphold, and we don't have even one single Defensive cd.

I think all these problems could be fixed with a few quick solutions, add Defense stat to T2 Enhancement pieces the same way Druids got this on their T2 Feral pieces (we both share 4 specs in one class and we both have a tree split for Tank or Melee Dps), tweak the % number of threat transferred to the user from Totemic Alignment to make it work at least as well as Consecration and even if a Defensive cd would take some time, we could theorycraft over that and find out something Shaman flavored that puts them at close to even footing with other tanks.

Other than that though, just those 2 earlier suggestions for quick fixes could help the struggle that Shaman tanks face by a lot.

Another Totem it could be of use to addres the issues is the Healing Stream Totem.. I, for one, have little to none interest to using it just because Mana Stream Totem is better option in the long run, but, if Healig Stream Totem could give Defense (lets say 2 x Rank, a total of 10 to Rank 5 lv60, the same as Warrior and Paladin have with their talents), it would addres the Crusing Blow problem a little, and it would give me another choice for my Water Totem slot.
Again I'm gonna reference my rework proposal (link in my signature below) putting the idea of making WF the Enhance tree's Keystone and making it an additional effect to the Agility Totem so that enhance dps and tank can get the benefit of Agility without gimping their group and there will be more synergy with Druids and Hunters in the tank group.

Also maybe the Twow team can increase the Strength scaling of block value for Shamans either baseline or from talents and make Stoneskin a more resto-centric utility.

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: Shaman Leveling tips
content_md:
Totally viable. In TWOW you can find a raidspot wit basically any build unless you really meme one.
On the other hand, shamans are the biggest on-demand class there is because of how their buff works.
You ideally want 1WF totem for each melee group, maybe 1 agi totem for a hunter group and very maybe 1 tranquil air totem for a caster group.
Mostly WF totem carries, though.
End result is guilds taking any kind of shaman just for the buff (but secretly hoping for a resto).
From raid pov while all shaman builds are wanted because of the buff, the builds are from different tiers:
 * Resto is close to being broken. Huge mana pool, spammable, quick chain heal. Imagine old T2,5 resto shaman stealing prot pala's mana management. Raids love them, they are a bit too OP probably.
 * Enh is much worse as a DPS than resto is as a healer but the have their own niche. They are designed as mostly single-target focused, burts DPS, meaning that in shorter windows they can output disgusting damage. Very good for farmed contents, not really effective for progression.
 * Ele is okay. You really want a thunderfury tank. You're probably forced to use WF totem and you are kinda boring imo but they work.

You can easily find raid spots with any of these, except for high-end speedrun guilds where (usually) resto has a high prio and (maybe) enh has some for the farm speed. Ele is less successful there if I know well.

Only exception is tank shaman.
As a tank shaman you can't expect raid spots. First you need a chill and friendly guild. With them, you can raid as a tank shammie but it's rather a favor from the bros, not an on-demand spec. On paper they have their own niche (spell damage resistance) but in practice they are objectively the weakest tank at raiding level.

For resto, best is probably 0 8 43 (getting the extra shield to combo with improved water shield talent).
Unsure aout the others atm.

I level as enhancement, and after the last content patch it is a lot of fun.

With the first 11 points,  get the elemental focus talent from the elemental tree. Focus on agility gear to improve crit chance. When you clear cast, cast your shock.

content_md:
Hi, unfortunately you are making a good observation. The "electrify" talent is a significant nerf to ele pvp, particularly when the latest patch also increased the burstiness of other classes, even creating new ones such as the disc priest.

Electrify effectively means you start every combat at 50-66% of your power level. If you are in endgame/tier3 gear you can still manage, however as relatively fresh you will likely struggle to get there at all. I am confident this aspect was not part of the twow devs' calculation when they designed this sad talent.

As you've noticed, Electrify has been one of the most criticized talents since the announcement of CC2. It has already been quasi-buffed once - initially you needed 5 stacks instead of 2 to gain the 100% boost. But there seems to be a lot of pride in CC2 so I doubt we will ever see the needed reversal back to Elemental Fury.

content_md:
Ele is in an interesting spot. You still got a bunch of utility + for a caster, you can get disgusting amount of armor.
BUT
Class changes made many other builds more bursty while ele became less bursty. It's still kinda bursty but they are nerfed in this department.

Earlier you had the 100% crit damage upon crit as a passive.
Now your landing (!) bolts and chain ligtnings build up up to a stack of 2 (shocks don't), each one adding 50%. At the bright side you get some passive damage increase with the stacks (up to 10%).
But this means les burstiness. You running around, seeing a guy and starting to attack means no instant giga-crits.
But you still have totem support, heals, big armor, 5-6 sec CD interrupt, slow and purge.

author: jmwg
subject: I don't understand the nerf to Shaman's Flurry
content_md:
Since the introduction of dual-wielding for Shamans in *Wrath of the Lich King*, the Flurry talent was nerfed. However,
"In Turtle WoW, the Shaman's Flurry has been nerfed to 20%."
, especially when Warriors still retain a 30% Flurry effect. Granting Shamans dual-wielding to address the current overabundance of hit rating would be a fantastic improvement.
This reflects a specific balance change on the *Turtle WoW* private server, where the Flurry ability's attack speed bonus was reduced to 20%, contrasting with its historical values (e.g., 25-30% in official versions) or other
Wrath of the Lich King (2008–2010): Dual-Wield Era Overhaul**
 - **Mechanic Rework**: Renamed **Flurry** . Triggered by crits, granting **5/10/15/20/25%** attack speed with a **stacking mechanic** (up to 3 stacks).
 - **Dual-Wield Synergy**: Frequent crits from dual-wielding improved stack stability, boosting burst potential.
 - **Talent Tree Position**: Remained a core Enhancement talent (5 points to max).
To the dev team: If you see this message, please respond. I heard that after adding the Dragonhead Buff to Shamans during testing, they became overpowered.

content_md:
Mining and blacksmithing is far from "optimal" for tank sham. You'd likely want engineering more than anything, since up until 40 you can't even use the mail gear you get from blacksmithing.

If your concern is viability, the playstyle has been "viable" since CC1 (CC2 was the most recent big class balance overhaul) in the sense that it's usable for almost every raid. Now, it's much smoother to do content with.

I can't exactly help with rotation all that well and what I share will be very simplistic fundamentals you can likely figure out yourself, but- here they are anyways.

Always keep rockbiter on.

Use your highest rank of earth shock as a "pseudo taunt" for snap threat or initial threat rather than your constant on CD main threat generator. It can burn through mana like no tomorrow if you're not careful and leave less flexibility with using other tools like totems. Your second highest rank should be your steady threat generator, with rank one being used solely for interrupts if you wanna be super optimized.

For multiple targets, use fire nova totem and tab target smacking to keep threat. I'm not sure if magma totem is better since I haven't gotten that on my sham but experiment between the two if you can't learn which is better. I would imagine they both have their purposes. I imagine you'll want stoneskin over strength of earth for mitigation despite how much your melee DPS might want it.

At lower levels, like in RFC (and possibly WC-ish?) you can safely heal yourself mid fight with rank 1 healing wave so long as the number of enemies is low and since it comes out so quick while giving a decently substantial amount for the level and also technically being "aoe threat" since you generate threat through healing. Maybe you can squeeze in a rank 2 with slower attacking enemies but that's probably stretching it. Also, ALWAYS remember tremor totem, especially in WC since the druids sleep you a lot. After that, though, I can't help. It's up to you to discover things for yourself or keep asking around.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Elemental Shaman with Lightning Strike for pvp
content_md:
Stable shields is an awful talent for pvp.
You increase the the charges of lightning shield from 3 to 9 but you slow the time you can expend charges substantially. While with regular lightning shield, you get 100% of your spellpower against your target in 10.5 seconds at best, with stable shields that time is extended to 13.5seconds and only after 18 seconds in combat do you gain any value off of the talent.

How often do you have a pvp fight that lasts more than 18 seconds without you having an oportunity to recast shield?

Stable shield is a nerf to your shield and you should only ever skill it if you grab it for lightning strike.

And lightning strike want you to wear slow weapons. Hand of edward has a chance to give you a decent lightning bolt afterwards, while any "Good" weapon just ensures the lightningstrike itself at least hits hard.

author: Franktank
subject: Theorycrafting: The Electrify Enhancement Shaman
content_md:
Hey Shamfam,

Been wanting to submit a post on here for a while to discuss some theorycrafting around an Ele/Enh hybrid. I've been messing around over the past month, and here's the build so far (still WIP). Apologies if this is a repost, but I haven't found anything like it yet, and I am not active on the Discord. All negative/positive feedback is greatly appreciated.

The core of this build is a basic Enhancement Shaman while capitalizing on the Electrify talent to further increase crit damage and reduce mana consumption with the constant uptime of Elemental Focus from crits. With the changes the devs have made, it feels like they’re opening up a lane for Shaman to be a viable melee caster. It’s kind of weird, but there is some synergy there.

 **Talents**
[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... AAAAAAAAA=](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=FgAYNQAABAAAAAFAFYIIFALIAoAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=)

 * 1st tier
 5/5 Convection: Shaman is mana-hungry
 5/5 Concussion: higher damage with CL and LB to build stacks for Electrify
 5/5 Ancestral Knowledge: flat increase to stats

 * 2nd tier
 3/3 Elemental Devastation: +3% hit for raids and +9% spell hit for shocks/lightning
 5/5 Thundering Strikes: higher crit chance = more EF procs/DPS
 3/3 Stable Shield: easier mana sustain with Water Shield OR higher DPS with Lightning Shield. Without Water Shield, mana can be a problem, but since storm and lightning strike work with clear-casting its a bit better.

 * 3rd tier
 1/1 Elemental Focus: This build crits almost constantly, so this is a mandatory talent for mana sustain
 5/5 Reverberation: Shocks are spammed on CD
 1/5 Call of Thunder: burner point for the next tier, though you could swap points from Concussion for higher Lightning crit%—totally up to you.
 1/3 Calming Winds for lower threat OR 1/3 Ancestral Guardian as a filler point. I'd go for less threat when raiding
 1/1 Lightning Strike: more hits for crits + it benefits from weapon/Nature/SP scaling + procs Lightning or Water Shield.

 * 4th tier
 5/5 Flurry: higher attack speed for more crits, procs, and DPS.

 * 5th tier
 1/1 **Electrify**: Like many of you, I scoffed when I first saw this new talent, but at 2 stacks you get +100% crit damage to offensive-spells (Shocks, Frostbrand procs, Lightning spells). Especially fun when Hand of Edward the Odd procs a lot and the RNG gods are in your favor. +10% nature is nice too for earth shocks and lightning spells
 1/2 Enhanced Totems: small stat increase for Air/Earth totems
 3/3 Elemental Weapons: this makes Frostbrand proc A LOT. You could still use WF for extra attacks or against Frost-resistant mobs, but Frostbrand feels more consistent overall right now.
 1/1 Stormstrike: another attack for more procs + 20% increased Nature damage is welcome

 * 6th tier
 5/5 Weapon Mastery: more damage.

Now, you could sacrifice Electrify for Bloodlust for higher group DPS, but that would make this build feel pointless—at that stage, pure Enhancement would be better.

 **Stats**
Currently prioritizing Attack Power > AGI > Spell Power > Hit/Crit% since these all affect our main damage sources:
Auto attacks (AP/Agi)
Shocks (AP/SP)
Frostbrand procs (SP)
Nature spells (SP)

Still testing, but AP seems king after the Shaman rework.

 **Gear**
Running a mix of T1/T2/epics at the moment.
Hand of Edward the Odd was made for this build—fast attacks = more Frostbrand procs + instant CLs. I have mine ench with SP since it'll increase many sources of damage, but crusader is fine too. An off-Hand that provides more SP is nice. With the threat this thing rolls out you could slap on a shield and go OT/bruiser playstyle.
Two-Handers still provide amazing damage. Nightfall works pretty well too since that 10% increase will affect your shocks and frost-brand procs. So many different set-ups here. Cast Rank 1 LB's to keep electrify up.
Haven't experimented with t3 sets yet but hopefully there are some tier set synergies that work with this playstyle.

 **Rotation**
 1. Chain Lightning or Lightning Bolt opener for Electrify stacks. In fast fights, I usually just do one CL and move on. You can also cast 2 Rank 1 LBs to build 2 stacks in 3 seconds as its only 1.5s cast time
 2. Frost Shock for guaranteed Frostbrand crits (or Earth Shock if running WF). Since shocks scale with AP now, it should hit like a truck when it crits.
 3. Spam auto attacks, Lightning Strike, Stormstrike.
 4. If using Hand of Edward the Odd, spam CL when it procs, especially with Electrify & Stormstrike up. Without Hand of Ed, use CL/LB as you see fit between Shock/Strike cooldowns to keep Electrify up.
 5. Keep spamming Shocks/Strikes/CL as they come off cooldown.

 **Cons so far**
 - CL/LB cast time feels awkward mid-fight—if you time it well, it's fine, but still a hassle.
 - Frostbrand is useless against Frost-resistant mobs.

Anywho, I’d love to hear all of your guys’ thoughts and input.
content_html:
Hey Shamfam,

Been wanting to submit a post on here for a while to discuss some theorycrafting around an Ele/Enh hybrid. I've been messing around over the past month, and here's the build so far (still WIP). Apologies if this is a repost, but I haven't found anything like it yet, and I am not active on the Discord. All negative/positive feedback is greatly appreciated.

The core of this build is a basic Enhancement Shaman while capitalizing on the Electrify talent to further increase crit damage and reduce mana consumption with the constant uptime of Elemental Focus from crits. With the changes the devs have made, it feels like they’re opening up a lane for Shaman to be a viable melee caster. It’s kind of weird, but there is some synergy there.

Talents
https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... AAAAAAAAA=

* 1st tier
5/5 Convection: Shaman is mana-hungry
5/5 Concussion: higher damage with CL and LB to build stacks for Electrify
5/5 Ancestral Knowledge: flat increase to stats

* 2nd tier
3/3 Elemental Devastation: +3% hit for raids and +9% spell hit for shocks/lightning
5/5 Thundering Strikes: higher crit chance = more EF procs/DPS
3/3 Stable Shield: easier mana sustain with Water Shield OR higher DPS with Lightning Shield. Without Water Shield, mana can be a problem, but since storm and lightning strike work with clear-casting its a bit better.

* 3rd tier
1/1 Elemental Focus: This build crits almost constantly, so this is a mandatory talent for mana sustain
5/5 Reverberation: Shocks are spammed on CD
1/5 Call of Thunder: burner point for the next tier, though you could swap points from Concussion for higher Lightning crit%—totally up to you.
1/3 Calming Winds for lower threat OR 1/3 Ancestral Guardian as a filler point. I'd go for less threat when raiding
1/1 Lightning Strike: more hits for crits + it benefits from weapon/Nature/SP scaling + procs Lightning or Water Shield.

* 4th tier
5/5 Flurry: higher attack speed for more crits, procs, and DPS.

* 5th tier
1/1 Electrify: Like many of you, I scoffed when I first saw this new talent, but at 2 stacks you get +100% crit damage to offensive-spells (Shocks, Frostbrand procs, Lightning spells). Especially fun when Hand of Edward the Odd procs a lot and the RNG gods are in your favor. +10% nature is nice too for earth shocks and lightning spells
1/2 Enhanced Totems: small stat increase for Air/Earth totems
3/3 Elemental Weapons: this makes Frostbrand proc A LOT. You could still use WF for extra attacks or against Frost-resistant mobs, but Frostbrand feels more consistent overall right now.
1/1 Stormstrike: another attack for more procs + 20% increased Nature damage is welcome

* 6th tier
5/5 Weapon Mastery: more damage.

Now, you could sacrifice Electrify for Bloodlust for higher group DPS, but that would make this build feel pointless—at that stage, pure Enhancement would be better.

Stats
Currently prioritizing Attack Power > AGI > Spell Power > Hit/Crit% since these all affect our main damage sources:
Auto attacks (AP/Agi)
Shocks (AP/SP)
Frostbrand procs (SP)
Nature spells (SP)

Still testing, but AP seems king after the Shaman rework.

Gear
Running a mix of T1/T2/epics at the moment.
Hand of Edward the Odd was made for this build—fast attacks = more Frostbrand procs + instant CLs. I have mine ench with SP since it'll increase many sources of damage, but crusader is fine too. An off-Hand that provides more SP is nice. With the threat this thing rolls out you could slap on a shield and go OT/bruiser playstyle.
Two-Handers still provide amazing damage. Nightfall works pretty well too since that 10% increase will affect your shocks and frost-brand procs. So many different set-ups here. Cast Rank 1 LB's to keep electrify up.
Haven't experimented with t3 sets yet but hopefully there are some tier set synergies that work with this playstyle.

Rotation
1. Chain Lightning or Lightning Bolt opener for Electrify stacks. In fast fights, I usually just do one CL and move on. You can also cast 2 Rank 1 LBs to build 2 stacks in 3 seconds as its only 1.5s cast time
2. Frost Shock for guaranteed Frostbrand crits (or Earth Shock if running WF). Since shocks scale with AP now, it should hit like a truck when it crits.
3. Spam auto attacks, Lightning Strike, Stormstrike.
4. If using Hand of Edward the Odd, spam CL when it procs, especially with Electrify & Stormstrike up. Without Hand of Ed, use CL/LB as you see fit between Shock/Strike cooldowns to keep Electrify up.
5. Keep spamming Shocks/Strikes/CL as they come off cooldown.

Cons so far
- CL/LB cast time feels awkward mid-fight—if you time it well, it's fine, but still a hassle.
- Frostbrand is useless against Frost-resistant mobs.
- Very RNG-dependent—some fights, you top the meters, others, you don’t. Classic Shaman experience.
- Threat Magnet - beg for salv

Anywho, I’d love to hear all of your guys’ thoughts and input.

author: Taralej90
subject: Comprehensive DPS test of different weapon imbues
content_md:
Test done with pre-raid BiS gear + some epics, using Nightfall as a signature Enh weapon. 308 weapon skill from orc racial + book quest, 31.22% crit, 758 AP (from Ony buff). Only auto-attacks.

 **10 min vs 60lvl dummy:**

 - **Rockbiter** - 178 DPS
 - **Windfury** - 220 DPS
 - **Flametongue** - 178 DPS
 - **Frostbrand** - 178 DPS
 - **Frostbrand + WF totem** - 230 DPS

 **10 min vs Boss dummy:**

 - **Rockbiter** - not tested due to threat issues making it non-viable
 - **Windfury** - 167 DPS
 - **Flametongue** - 138 DPS
 - **Frostbrand** - 151 DPS
 - **Frostbrand + WF totem** - 167 DPS

 **Disclaimer:**

 - FT and FB use spell crit and only crit for 50% dmg
 - FT and FB crits can proc Clearcasting but not Flurry
 - FT and FB are both affected by Nightfall debuff
 - FT can be partially resisted (for 25%, 50% or 75% of the dmg)
 - FB cannot be partially resisted but can be fully resisted
 - FB is the only weapon imbue that interacts with WF totem
 - FT and FB do not scale (Rockbiter also doesn't scale)
 - Effect of Elemental Weapons on FB is unusable because bosses are immune to the effect of Frost Shock
 - Effect of Elemental Weapons on WF diminishes significantly as you gain more weapon skill.
 - WF attacks can be glancing blows. I'm taking 308 (racial + book) as the baseline. Obviously, with more weapon skill (AQ40 gloves) the DPS of WF will go up.
 - Autoattack and WF crits cannot be glancing blows.
 - WF attacks can proc Flurry but do not consume Flurry stacks
 - WF itself does not scale (like Rockbiter), but the 2 extra attacks scale with the rest of your gear
 - During a WF proc, you have a small window of about 1 sec where you gain the increased 323 AP from the WF proc. Any attacks (or last-rank shocks) done during that 1 sec window will benefit from that 323 AP.

Interaction between weapon imbues and "strikes" (Stormstrike and Lightning Strike):

 - FT and FB both proc from strikes. They only proc once from LS. Rockbiter is a flat AP increase, so it affects both strikes significantly, as well as the elemental shield proc of LS (which scales with AP). WF can proc off strikes, but doing so resets the AA timer. Because of this and because of the way WF works (last point in Disclaimer), it is best to delay your strikes for just after your AA.

 **Conclusions:**

 **Windfury** comes out on top in almost every situation. It also scales with the rest of your gear, unlike all other weapon imbues. However, it is also the most severely affected by glancing blows, making the orc racial(+3), skill book(+5) and specific items(+6/7/8) extremely important. Frostbrand being unable to be partially resisted makes it better than Flametongue, but Flametongue is buffed by 45% by T1. Even with that buff and adding Searing Totem into the mix (from Elemental Weapons increasing Fire spell + totem dmg by 30%), Flametongue would be barely equal to Windfury, and only in raids where enemies aren't resistant to Fire dmg. By the time you have full T1, Windfury would just be way too far ahead for Flametongue to catch up. The fact that bosses (and many raid mobs) cannot be affected by Frost Shock debuff means Frostbrand cannot show its true potential in most cases.

As you gain more gear, more crit and more weapon skill, Windfury completely overshadows the other three weapon imbues, mainly due to the fact that they don't scale and only crit for 50% dmg. Should these two things be changed, then Enh Shaman may see usage of FT and FB beyond memes, PvP and leveling.

Rockbiter remains the best weapon imbue for **leveling** due to its consistency and raw output. The 10% dmg reduction from Elemental Weapons is also always active and requires no management or mana spent. Windfury remains the best end-game weapon imbue.

author: Akos1896
subject: Rating totems
content_md:
Hey!

I wanted to create a totem tier list with some added notes next to each ranking.
Tiers are:
 * Nerf or rework is needed
 * Strong
 * Mid
 * Weak
 * Buff or rework is a must
 * Not applicable

Let's go in an ascending order!

 **Not applicable Tier:**
 * Sentry Totem - This totem has some PVP niche but for a class who already has far sight, it's a weird addition. Has no PVE use but has a weird niche for creating group selfies.

 **Buff or rework is a must Tier:**
 * Windwall Totem - Lowering ranged attack damage on the same element where WF exists? The only case where this would in theory be used is a custom instance where we have to fight off an army of archers somehow. Only limiting its effect to ranged damage makes it useless.

 * Healing Stream Totem - It is a very weird totem, arguably giving shamans a precedent for HoT usage. But for what it does, it barely ever worths it, even if it is upgraded via 5 talent points. Its scaling is way off, putting it down is usually just wasting mana.

 **Weak Tier:**

 * Nature Resistence Totem - On paper all resistence totems are equally strong but their element is an important thing to look at. You barely ever use nature resistence totem even at high nature damage places because of windfury. The only time I remember using it is in AQ40 before CC2 where the frost oil prevented WF from going off at Viscidious and at Huhuran, via totem twisting. But twisting is no more.

 * Stoneskin Totem - Not a bad idea for a totem but the design is badly executed. Even as a tank I barely ever use it. The problem with it is the lack of scaling. You are usually way better off by giving strength to the party and kill things faster.

 * Searing Totem - The effect itself would put it in the Mid tier but it is extremely unreliable unless you spend talent points to ensure it doesn't pewpew down sheeps and patrols (?). Because of this I lowered its rank by one.

 **Mid Tier:**
 * Earthbind Totem - It has a decent utility for kiting and during PVP against a melee but most opponents can destroy it from afar or can charge to it - and it has an internal CD so it isn't spammable. Also, shaman is not the best kiter in the world.

 * Tranquil Air Totem - The effect itself is strong but very limiting. It never really sees play when you play alone or go to dungeons. It is very strong in raids in a caster group but barely any shaman goes to a caster group at raids. It has its potential for late game but windfury ensures the shaman's placement in a melee group.

 * Flametongue Totem - The current iteration is weird and personally I don't like it, but I have to admit, it is a straight buff to the melee 'for free' and the shaman is usually in the melee team.

 * Frost Resistence Totem - Better then the nature one because you don't have to sacrifice WF to use it. But its use is kinda limited, would benefit from more frost magic-using enemies.

 * Mana Spring Totem - Not bad, if the party stays in one place for a longer time. Its mana recharge is below blessing of wisdom but is still respectable. The problem is its initial cost. If your team moves fast and you spam mana spring, chances are, you just burn up your mana to give some small mana ticks to party members. Even after 5 talent points of investment.

 * Fire Nova Totem - It definitely has its uses but its higher skill ceiling (you gotta make sure that the enemy gets in the range way before it goes off) and its CD limits it from a higher tier.

 * Magma Totem - Does okay damage despite not having the best SP coefficient in the world and is a staple for shaman dungeon tanking. Has no CD. But it's extremely expensive, limiting its usefulness.

 * Stoneclaw Totem - Besides dungeon tanking, also has some limited use but it mostly gets its point as a dungeon-tanking tool. Arguably the best of the bunch but that's all it's really useful at. The fire aoe totems also help during PVP or as a DPS. Stoneclaw's non-tank utility, while exists, is extremely limited.

 **Strong Tier:**

 * I think this is our best resistence totem. Uses water element which we can 'sacrifice' quite easily and there are many instances where the enemy casts fire spells. From BRD up to BWL, super useful (but not broken at all).

 * Grace of Air Totem - The favourite of all kinds of enhancement shamans but never used by enhancement shamans. This agility buff is extremely strong (above leader of the pack with Kara10 relic!) but the totem happens to be in the same element as windfury.

 * Strength of Earth Totem - Its buff is very useful for melee and is almost always used. While being very strong, it is not broken, if we compare it to other buffs (for example, blessing of might).

 * Disease Cleansing Totem - Super limited use but when its needed, it's awfully effective. Turns out that having its effect work even during etb ('enters the battlefield') comboes well with the fact that it doesn't have any CDs, allowing it to be spammed. Usually useless but if diseases happen, this totem alone negates the whole thing for the entire party.

 * Poison Cleansing Totem - Same as the disease one but poisons happen more often in my opinion. An absolute beast in ES.

 * Tremor Totem - Its use is very limited but when it is needed, it steals the show. Tremor makes encounters involving fear (charm, sleep) way more trivial. I kept it in strong only because of its limited use and because it is a bit unreliable (uses area-based pulses every 4 second to dispell, if not used with experience, can go wrong).

 * Grounding Totem - I agree with the GCD nerf, this totem was (and is) a PVP menace. Giving a class which can interrupt every 5-6 seconds a totem which nopes a targeted spell every 15-12 seconds is extremely strong. It has some PVE uses and has a good skill sceiling to know when to use it. Its internal CD and GCD usage limits it from being higher up on the list. But to be honest, it would never reach windfury anyway.

 **Nerf or rework is needed Tier:**

 * Windfury Totem - One totem (without GCD) giving your 4 melee party members 20% chance for a free hit every time they hit is 1) beyond broken 2) scales with the equipment of the party members really well. WF is so strong, it warps common sense. Level 56 shamans are invited for entry-level  raid pugs (I'm not sure if the game still allows this) just to spam this one totem. Summoning this totem suddenly 'almost creates' a melee character out of nothign if we add together the DPS increase it causes. Tranquil air totem never and agility totem barely sees play because of this bad boy. This totem ensures that all shaman goes to the melee party.

author: Voodoochile
subject: Re: Rating totems
content_md:
Also I would like to point out that Healing Stream Totem is literally the most mana efficient heal in Shaman's kit by a massive margin and is, matter of fact, impactful. It just doesn't FEEL impactful. It's a low profile form of sustain in the same vein as Stoneskin Totem is a low profile dmg mitigation. Especially together, these totems provide a sizeable amount of survivability in dungeons essentially allowing leather and mail wearers tank on its own, and even applicable survivability in raids.

The flat number reduction, which is made even stronger with the Enhancing Totems talent, ranges between 1%-4% mitigation from melee dmg in raids, and has higher value than armor upgrades in some cases because of DR on armor dmg mitigation, and obviously has highest value on aoe pulls where many auto attacks are coming in.

Again, the issue is that what it does is passive and quickly erased by healing in comparison to dmg numbers which are constantly popping in your face, and that these buffs typically only help a single individual who has threat as opposed to everyone who does melee dmg, or everyone who uses mana.

author: estebanmgn
subject: SHAMAN RACES: ORC AND TROLL
content_md:
Hi! my first post! ☺

First:

I don't know if you've seen the abysmal difference between the orc shaman and the troll shaman.

The orc wins in absolute everything, both elemental and tank enhancement or dps enhancement.

The active racial of the orc plus its expertise is ahead by far, I think they should touch either the troll (improving their racial) or the orc (nerfing him a touch).

All the tests I performed, the difference between orc and troll (significantly increasing the troll's racial values) won the orc.
I would put 20% passive speed. (rage becomes that)

I tried that and in long-lasting scenarios where you manage to stay alive (longer than 22 seconds) the troll can win. Otherwise, I see everything considerably in favor of the orc.

Current Status: The Orc is clearly superior in almost all scenarios.  scared_turtle_head

Superior in short fights by Blood Fury
Best Against Controlled Classes by Hardiness
The troll's regeneration is insufficient to compensate

With my proposal of 20% passive attack speed for the troll:  smiling_turtle_head

The troll would slightly outperform the orc in sustained DPS
I would have more Windfury proc opportunities
Lower stun resistance would still be a disadvantage

 ***And user of this forum said on another post "Comprehensive DPS test of different weapon imbues":***

"
> **Conclusions**:
>
>  Windfury comes out on top in almost every situation. It also scales with the rest of your gear, unlike all other weapon imbues. However, it is also the most severely affected by glancing blows, making the orc racial(+3), skill book(+5) and specific items(+6/7/8) extremely important. The fact that bosses (and many raid mobs) cannot be affected by Frost Shock debuff means Frostbrand cannot show its true potential in most cases.

"

Then, the orc is always ahead. I think trolls would need an upgrade that can help in late combat..

author: Avalok
subject: Clearcasting Talent Affectation
content_md:
**Clearcasting talent of Shamans now apply to abilities, and not just spells. This means that melee abilities that do damage are now affected by the Clearcasting buff, such as Storm Strike and Lightning Strike.**

I do not admire this new implementation, simply because the melee abilities mentioned to be affected by Clearcasting have no practical or reasonable benefit. the melee damaging abilities of Shamans have little requirement for mana as opposed to any damaging spells they have. This is especially sensible as an Enhancement Shaman, for one of their main damage and threat generating outputs come from Shock spells, which are of high mana requirement. If the damaging melee abilities were to expend a charge of Clearcasting, it would really be a waste if they weren't instead be expended on shock spells.

I would like to suggest now that The Clearcasting buff of Shamans be reverted back to its older version of just affecting spells instead, and to not affect melee abilities as well.

On that note, I would like to say that I am happy with an adjustment they made on Shaman Clearcasting regarding the percentage of mana reduction it has. It has now been increased to 60% as opposed to the earlier amount of only 40%. This change makes it feel more delightful to play as an Enhancement Shaman.

content_md:
It is useful if you crit reliably enough (an enh should focus on high crit).
The reason behid it is shock CD.
Clearcasting gives 60% mana cut for the next 2 spells.
If you're not a Hand of Edward the Odd enjoyer, from melee range those spells are shocks (or the melee abilities we talk about now).
Shock has 5 or 6 sec CD, depending on talent picks, optimally 5.
If clearcasting ignores SS and LS and it becomes a shock discount talent, then it takes you 2 shocks' time to have a full benefit from a crit. Optimally shamans crit much more often, specially with SS and LS being extra hits, not even counting the extra from WF.
With regular crits you can have cheaper SS, LS and the same cheaper shocks you want at the same time.

Yes, I understand where you're getting at, and I do notice and am aware of that mechanic.

In fact, I know how to apply it to my gameplay well. There is a talent that increases the proc chance of Frostbrand by 25% of its base proc chance, with the base proc chance being "15 multiplied by weapon speed". Also, units affected by Frost Shock causes Frostbrand procs to critically hit 100% of the time, thus, when critically hitting with Frostbrand causes Clearcasting to activate on the player. This is why I made this post. I thought that it would be more efficient if only my Frost Shock were to expend a stack of Clearcasting. I'm now starting to see that it isn't really much of an issue as I play the game more. So, I guess I can say that my suggestion to revert Clearcasting to an older version can be dismissed.

Another thing that comes to mind is that I set the talents on my Shaman to have Tanking capabilities as well. This tells me that I can't always rely on the advantage of Frost Shock and Frostbrand combo, for it seems to be more DPS oriented since it lacks a greater generation of threat when compared to using the Rockbiter and Earth Shock combo. This means that being a Shaman Tank isn't as mana conserving as it is. I wish there would be a compromise to that, along with FLametounge and Flame Shock combo, in terms of mana conservation like it has with the Frostbrand and Frost Shock combo without relying as much on crit chance accumulated from gear.

Greetings,

Not long ago we asked for your thoughts on potential PvP changes in this thread. First off we'd like to thank everyone who has taken the time to write constructive feedback and input.

Drawing on your suggestions and our own internal discussions, we're ready to share what's coming next. PvP updates will arrive in two stages across Patch 1.18.0 and Patch 1.18.1.

Patch 1.18.0
Beginning with Patch 1.18.0, every player who enters a Battleground or Arena will automatically receive a universal buff/debuff that:
  • Reduces incoming Physical Damage by x%.
  • Reduces incoming Magical Damage by x%.
  • Reduces incoming Healing by x%.
  • Reduces incoming Shields by x%.
Please note that all above percentages only have placeholder values. The actual values will be made public and definitive once we get closer to Patch release.

Patch 1.18.0 will also:
  • Add a New Arena Map.
  • Add the return of 2v2 Arenas.
  • Add Rated Arena Teams.
  • Introduce a stacking debuff to anyone holding the flag for an extended period of time in Warsong Gulch.
  • Players who are standing in spots that we deem safespots (as described by our rules) will now receive a Damage over Time debuff that will last as long as they are in such a position. These positions will be continuously updated by the team.

Patch 1.18.1
The follow-up patch focuses on broadening PvP's appeal:
  • Rework Rewards & Gear Progression so that PvP will be a truly viable gearing path.
  • Partially rework the current Honor System to reduce the brutal race against the clock at high PvP ranks.
  • Several new Open-World PvP Events.
  • A Brand-New Battleground.

Why a universal debuff instead of PvP-specific stats?

When looking at what could be done to extend PvP battles & combat and reduce some of the volatile burst that exists now we've opted to go for a more general debuff rather than having PvP specific gear that does the same through set bonuses or adding on more of a resilience-like stat.

Our main reason for this is that once we start reworking the gear progression for PvP we want to make sure we can stat this new gear somewhat similarly to the current PvE tiers with a few more minor benefits to PvP. This avoids forcibly splitting up 2 communities based on the gameplay they prefer.

We feel that if a player who has geared mainly through PvP progression wants to dabble in PvE raiding they should be able to with the gear achieved in PvP without starting back at zero with stats that are mainly useless, and vice versa for PvE -> PvP.


Once we get closer to release this information will be updated with the latest changes.

See you in Azeroth!

author: Noce
subject: melee + fast casting
content_md:
i really liked the enha shaman in wotlk. with all those maelstrom stacks and instant casts. it just fits thematically. hand-to-hand combat and quick lightning casting.

which leads me to the idea of ​​​​somehow doing it here. of course without copy-paste and a lot of changes. I know that there is a possibility for that right now but somehow a lot is lost on both sides, on ele and enha to achieve that. and still i does not fulfill the class fantasy.

for it to be useful, without LM talent it is simply not possible to be enha and cast. and LM is too deep. that's why I'm making a suggestion: to swap places of FLURRY and EW. and to also add a casting speed to flurry. e.g. 3/6/9/12/15%. to somehow be in par with LM talent from ele tree.

and also, somehow it makes more sense to switch places of FLURRY and EW talents in enha. EW is more beneficial to all trees during lvling than FLURRY is.

i'm really interested in your thoughts on this idea.

author: ForumGentleman
subject: Re: How's shaman now in PVP?
content_md:
Shaman PVP is in a weird state honestly.

Enh: actually pretty good AND fun with the new abilities.
Great damage, more abilities to click. You still get kited to death and you struggle to reset a fight

Ele: not that great and honestly just a downgrade from vanilla. There is barely any new talent for PVP. That fire totem talent sucks and has no use in PVP.
You are less bursty since the nerf. And if you are really serious about PVP, you should still grab nature swiftness anyways
Overall, a big disappointment for me.

Heal: Kinda strong but not that fun imo. Again, they failed to implement any meaningfull AND fun PVP oriented talent.
The spec is still good cuz of earthshield and reduced GCD on totems but the talent tree is really uninspired and clearlydesigned for pve only..

Imo; both heal and ele need 1 or 2 pvp oriented talents and a good spammable ability that synergizes with other spells.

author: FrankFankledank
subject: Re: How's shaman now in PVP?
content_md:
Disc Priests are in fact the highest range class now.

Track Humanoids doesn't give half the edge it used to with PvP mods that scour combat logs to detect players within your radius.

Concussive as a snare is a complete nonfactor, barely noticeable, its primary use is praying to the slot machines that maybe it'll get the improved stun off this time (it doesn't, it refuses to stun unless the enemy is already at 10% life and being dogpiled by 3 others).

Flare is a joke unless you're clairvoyant and dropping it directly onto an invisible player. You can easily still get opened on if you try to squat in it.

Frost Trap only shares cooldown with one of your most important damaging skills, but yes if you ignore it and the automatic serpent sting talents you too can regularly drop one of the most blatantly telegraphed "hey press frost reflector now" tells in the game. Also got severely nerfed with the trinket change.

If Mail is 'big armor' then Warriors should have no problems since they have, y'know, bigger armor. Yes, you can play like that one dwarf, go full stamina stacker + world buffs for 10K HP, give your pet your character name for maximum sweat-tactics, have a healer up your rectum all day long and avoid any objective you don't substantially outnumber already to preserve your 150gold in consumes and youtube combo video clips, it won't actually contribute to winning much but you can at least pretend your class is viable.

Warriors have: Platemail, Demo Shout, Thunder Clap, Piercing Howl, Hamstring, Improved Hamstring, Intimidating Shout, Defensive Stance, Disarm, Shield Block, Blood Craze, Bloodthirst, Charge, Intercept, Intervene... oh, and Shield Wall.

content_md: In some ways the addon is more concise as it displays detailed info for everyone in your radius instead of just a bunch of nebulous names on dots that you have to guess or manually target to see what exactly they are. Warrior has also disarm (yes it doesnt work if tagert has chain, but only ppl focused on pvp use it)

author: Markka
subject: Re: Elmental Weapon : Frostband idea
content_md:
In addition to many mobs being downright immune to the Frost Shock effect, which completely gimps the damage of Frostbrand, it is also anti-synergistic with certain classes and specs which makes it worse in group play.

Melee hunters that spam Wing Clip, or frost mages that inflict a slow effect either block Frost Shock from being applied, or even downright override the effect which completely cripples your damage. I have already had to ask people to not use their slowing abilities just so I can do damage. It's a really bad oversight.

If the current implementation of Elemental Weapons is intended to stay, Frost Shock has to be functional on enemies that aren't immune to frost, even if it doesn't slow them. Frost Shock also must not get blocked or knocked off by a similar or stronger effect. Alternatively, it would have to be reworked a bit like some of the earlier suggestions.

Also, it is strange that Frostbrand does not override Flametongue Totem and Windfury Totem effects without there being any mention of that in the tooltip(s). I appreciate that I can actually make use of 50% of my totems, but why do the other weapon imbues not get the same treatment?

author: Azuredrak0
subject: Real issue with Shaman Tanking
content_md:
Hi everyone,

TLDR - real issue is raid expectations and more specifically expectation to Windfury Totem...  for more details, read on -

I've played a shaman tank for a while.  I know many shaman tanks and myself have tanked content all the way through Naxx, and have surprised plenty of people with capabilities expanded and adapted for shamen to be able to do that.

While there are plenty of challenges to choosing to tank on a Shaman (lack of cooldowns, complexity of rotation, mana upkeep, ect.), the biggest elephant in the room I wanted to address though is perception and expectation from the shaman.  And to be even more specific, the problem with Windfury totem.

Raid expectation from a shaman is to be a raid strength augment, and any shaman that will be permitted to tank will still be expected to drop the most coveted totem of all, you guessed it, the Windfury Totem.   This augments the melee DPS of the group by quite a bit.

Here's the problem with this - dropping Windfury provides no benefit to the shaman and in fact robs him 4% crit and dodge provided by the Agi (Grace of Air) totem.  This causes a funny conundrum for shaman tank who boosts DPS of his group, which robs him of more mitigation and threat.

Proposal for future enhancement shaman ... enhancements
- let's make a symbiotic relationship that benefits the shaman for dropping Windfury totem - When party members proc Windfury, shaman gains 5% block for 10 secs, stacking 5 times - now there's a good benefit that could be tied to Spirit Armor talent

- let's not forget our Enhancement brothers - When party members proc windfury, shaman gains 50AP, stacking 5 times for 10 secs - this benefit may be tied to Calming Winds talent

- Alternatively both effects can be combined into Enhancing Totems talent and the benefit provided can be tied to wearing a shield or not

author: Toxo
subject: Re: Real issue with Shaman Tanking
content_md:
I don't know that this alone would solve the whole issue of Shaman Tanks if we're talking raids, having only 1 half set with defense stats, lack luster stamina on items, no def cds, no idol buffs etc. As far as I've seen the issues need something like this, plus a couple of other tweaks in other places, that would address the multitude of issues this spec has.

That said though, I do like this idea as an addition to what Enhance Shamans are missing, it also plays nicely into the Shaman fantasy while solving one of Shaman's biggest issues, WF totem serving as a support to allies and allies' procs looping back into supporting you.

As for talents that can add this effect, I think the first 2 ideas work better, because Spirit Armor is strictly a Tank specific talent, one that Enhance Dps can't benefit from as it requires wearing a shield to get its bonus armor and it improves blocking, likewise, Calming Winds reduces threat, which is something you obviously do not want as a Tank.

The 3rd idea I don't think would be as elegant and present a fair share of problems, as Enhancing Totems is more of a neutral talent between the Dps and Tank sides of Enhance, but it would also turn it into another mandatory talent for the Tank side..
This side I think is already burdened enough with needing every talent from the Dps side to have threat and this will add more load to it, example, Dps side only needs Calming Winds as a mandatory talent if you have high gear, Enhancing Totems is optional (maybe a hot take there, but the bonuses are pretty small and half of it basically doesn't exist, since we never get to use Grace of Air), in contrast to that Tank side's Ancestral Guardian and Spirit Armor are Absolutely Mandatory to have tank equivalent armor and decent mitigation, with a 3rd talent of Totemic Alignment being optional for some AoE threat, which, nobody really needs this, not as it is right now. This is why I think placing it to Calming Winds and Spirit Armor makes more sense for each spec.

What they'd look like:
Dps talents: [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... AAAAAAAAA=](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=DoAYNAAAAAAAAAFAFYYIFATIAoBAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=)
Tank talents: [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... AAAAAAAAA=](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=FADYLAAAAAAAAAFAFYALFQTIAoBAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=)

Lastly, one potential problem I see with this are instances where Dps can't be near the shaman tank. I think this is where Grace of Air comes to play, but is the totem by itself enough? Is the idea here that WF totem reinforces our missing Dodge from Grace of Air, or WF becomes a conduit for Block chance, while Grace of Air remains as it is, the go to for Dodge?

author: karuu
subject: Shaman Chain Lightning & Swing Timer Change
content_md:
Quick repost when I first submitted in suggestions.

Got some inspiriation after seeing that the devs added a SP coeffiecent (5%) to Lightning Strike, and I propose two very small changes:

1. **Revert the cast time of Chain Lightning to 2.5 seconds to fit in-between swings smoother.**
2. **Allow the swing timer to continue while casting Chain Lightning.**

Promotes build diversity (spellhance), adds to skill expression (timing, positioning, resources), and is thematic to the shaman fantasy (chain lightning=cool).

Chain Lightning is self-regulating, in that it has a CD (6 sec) and a high mana cost (lame). Could even make it a talent, though wording would be a disaster.

Not sure if this should be extended to Lightning Bolt as well, you'd have to crunch the numbers.
