content_md:
I wrote this out as my personal levelling plan after compiling a lot of different tips from discussions in the #shaman channel on the Turtle WoW Discord. Since I noticed a lot of people asking for one, I'll share this in case it helps anyone save time by not having to research the same stuff. I'll be editing this if I come across any more relevant info, and I'd be grateful for any corrections or additions that anyone is willing to make.

Big thanks to the following contributors who provided most of the knowledge compiled here: Squid, Zhafu, Rinzu, Peter Hammer, DemonBoyJr, Monolith, Akos, Not Normal, poto, Haaxor1689, Zaaparou and more (sorry if I forgot any).

 **Race**
All 3 races are pretty much equally well-performing here, so go with the one you find the most fun or aesthetically pleasing. That said,
 - Troll is the best min-max race for PvE (quasi-Bloodlust haste racial for PvE, and hex is decent for PvP)
 - Tauren is the best for PvP and the most tanky for leveling (+5% hp, nature resist) - Warstomp is the best PvP racial + Plainsrunning is the biggest QoL racial in the game (saves us 2 talents on imp Ghost Wolf as well)
 - Orc is still a decent choice for Enhance PvE (axe skill helps + Blood Fury)

 **Gear & Stat Prios**
 - Stats for tanking while leveling: +stam > +agi > +str > +int (when tanking at 60, +str becomes 2nd most important and +agi third)
 - For healing: +int = +hp
 - For DPS: +str = +agi > +stam > +int (+str & +agi roughly on par, at 60 +str is more valuable than +agi)
 - Stat prios thread: [viewtopic.php?t=21159](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=21159)
 - For calculating AP: shamans get 0 AP per agi, 2 AP from str and 1% dodge and 1% crit per 20 agi
 - A shield with high armor is a always a top prio, eg. Compendium of the Fallen quest reward -> SM Cath shield -> Gilneas shield / Mara goblin shield / SWV shield. When in doubt between two, choose the higher armor one (it scales with tanking talents that boost armor on shields by 30%, and all items by 15%). You can run an EHP calc just checking your % damage reduction on A shield vs B shield listed on your character sheet: EHP = HP/(1-%DR), then see which one gives you the most EHP. As a quick shortcut, in most cases, 10 armor is roughly equal to 1 stamina

 **Talents & Rotation**
With this build, you can fill any role in dungeons: tank, DPS or heal. We'll be picking tanking talents, but even if you solely want to DPS, this is arguably still the best build because you do practically the same DPS (the difference is really negligible) + have the benefit of being more tanky. That is, unless you're levelling in a group and don't have to care about mitigation. If you want to skip the tank talents, you could swap out Shield Spec. for Ancestral Knowledge. For healing, all you'll need is some +int gear and you're good to go for dungeons.

To level 33
 - 24p in enh: 5/5 Shield Spec > 2/2 Totemic Alignment > 3/3 Stable Shields > 3/3 Ancestral Guardian (before LS for mitigation) > Lightning Strike (take before AG if threat is a problem) > 1/5 Thundering Strikes > 2/2 Spirit Armor > 4/5 Thundering Strikes > 3/3 Elemental Weapons (first if feeling squishy) > Stormstrike (first if want more threat): [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... oUYALAQDI-](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=-AoUYALAQDI-)
 - Rotation: Rockbiter + Lightning Shield, using Lightning Strike -> Storm Strike -> Earth Shock -> Lightning Strike. You spend your mana at the beginning, then melee the mob down because you want to start the mana regen ASAP. Using totems isn't recommended, though Searing is probably fine if you're sticking in the same location long enough to get value
 - Weapon: until Lightning Strike, a high dps dagger is just as good as a slow 2H; after Lightning Strike, a slow 2H is best
 - From around level 25, focus on getting a good shield with high armor. At level 28, you can get the Compendium of the Fallen quest from Sage Truthseeker in Thunder Bluff (34.7, 47.8) and do SM: Library for the shield quest reward
 - At level 33, get the Jewelcrafting +stam trinkets

Level 34-44
 - 11p in ele: 5/5 Convection > 2/5 Concussion (since few mobs do elemental dmg) OR 2/3 Elemental Warding (for mitigation in Maraudon) > 3/3 Elemental Devastation > Elemental Focus (Clearcasting!): [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... oUYALAQDI-](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=FQAYI-AoUYALAQDI-) OR [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... oUYALAQDI-](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=FACYI-AoUYALAQDI-)
 - Between level 35-41, try to get the Totem of Tides from the orc boss in Stormwrought - it's phenomenal for tanking dungeons + farming Lashers
 - As a Tauren, at level 40, get Plainsrunning: head to the 2nd village you visit in Mulgore when you make a Tauren. The mount trainer there provides you a quest that leads to STV

Level 44-50
 - 6p in enh: 5/5 Thundering Strikes > 5/5 Element's Grace (raises threat w/o necessarily spending mana): [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... YALAQDIAo-](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=FQAYI-AoVYALAQDIAo-) OR [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... YALAQDIAo-](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=FACYI-AoVYALAQDIAo-)
 - Rotation: after getting Elemental Focus at level 44, Frostbrand + Water Shield, using Frost Shock -> Stormstrike -> Lightning Strike
 - Optional: between 44-48, farm Earth Elementals in Badlands + occasional Uldaman runs to get the Goblin brainwashing machine for dual speccing (if the spot isn't camped too much, it might be possible to get the Goblin brainwashing machine for dual speccing, though this might be an unrealistic goal)
 - Around level 50, it's pretty easy and worth it to get this axe: <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=51892>
 - For the level 50 Spirit Totem quest, the trick here is that the Vultures have a higher chance of dropping the Spider Eye and the Black Claw than the spiders and the bears themselves

Level 51-60
 - Respec to 5/5 Ancestral Knowledge: [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... YALAQDIAo-](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=FQAYI-FAVYALAQDIAo-) OR [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... YALAQDIAo-](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=FACYI-FAVYALAQDIAo-)
 - 6p in enh: Bloodlust; 3p in ele: 3/3 Reverberation (take this before Flurry for more QoL in managing threat + more frequent spell interrupt); 5p in enh: 5/5 Flurry; 1p in ele: 3/5 Concussion: [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... ALFQDIAoB-](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=FYAYL-FAVYALFQDIAoB-) OR 3/3 Elemental Warding over 3/5 Concussion (Warding = a bit more tanky, but elemental damage is limited; Concussion = more threat): [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... ALFQDIAoB-](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=FADYL-FAVYALFQDIAoB-) OR for cheaper totems: [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... BQDIAoB-Ao](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=FACYL-FAVYALBQDIAoB-Ao)
 - From level 52+, when you get r5 Fire Nova, you can farm Lashers in Dire Maul East. See the guide on this below, but note that between levels 52-54, you might have better success just doing the first three groups as the aggro of the wandering mobs is kind of crazy
 - Spam HFQ and BRD to 55-57 (get pre-raid BiS), then switch to Scholo/Strat; 55+ dungeons are often run and rerun for stuff (remember to befriend healers)
 - Get WS: [viewtopic.php?t=16790](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=16790) / <https://turtle-wow.fandom.com/wiki/Weapon_Skill>

OR, if you're wanting to go resto at 60:

Level 51-60
 - Respec or dual spec to resto here in order to farm pre-raid BiS early. Rush Imp Water Shield with Stable Shields first, so like this: [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... FoDoYIEYQC](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=-FAAY-FoDoYIEYQC)
 - After that, finish every talent in resto except imp Reincartion, Healing Focus and Spirit Link: [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... oaIFYQKFAB](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=-FAAY-FoDoaIFYQKFAB)
 - Similarly as the enhancement pre-BiS farm, spam HFQ and BRD to 55-57 (get pre-raid BiS), then switch to Scholo/Strat; 55+ dungeons are often run and rerun for stuff (remember to befriend tanks)

 **Lasher Farming**
Here's a video on it by Zaaparou:
[embed: https://www.youtube.com/embed/o90HvELvCpA]
Make sure to have a 2nd account with a level 1 -> invite it to the group, make it party lead; once you've finished a run, log out on your shaman, switch over to the 2nd account and reset the dungeon (click on the torch and it'll port you to DM: West entrance). Rotate Nova > Magma > Nova on each pack, heal up & drink between packs; during the pack, you'll have to swap to Earth Shield for 100% pushback protection + do 1-2 Healing Waves on yourself, then switch back to Water Shield. Basically, you do 1 pack at a time. Have Water Shield on, aggro the pack, drop Stoneskin, agility, Healing Stream. When the pack gets close, drop Fire Nova. Then use Magma. Usually, you'll dip to around 50% health at this time, so you can use Earth Shield + cast 1-2 Healing Waves. Switch back to Water Shield, Fire Nova when it's off cooldown, drop Magma again. Usually, the pack will be dead at this time, but sometimes a 3rd Fire Nova totem is needed. You should finish each lasher pack at like 60% health and 40% mana. Talent-wise, you'll need this specific spec with all the talents that increase totem damage (Elemental Weapons in enhance - Flametongue - for +30% damage increase to fire totems) and the ones that transfer totem threat to you (otherwise the Lashers will kill your totems), as well as 12 points in resto for pushback protection: [https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... AQDI-FoAAC](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c/1.18.0/shaman?points=FAAQ-AoUYALAQDI-FoAAC). Also make sure to have Totem of Tides from the new Stormwrought dungeon - it deals aoe frost damage every time you are hit while having water shield active. Gear-wise, bring +int/mp5 and +stam gear (e.g. the shield from ST - Eranikus; Princess Dagger - the blue one with +int/mp5; or just some green "of stamina" mace). A good potential farming trinket: Blood-etched Fetish (from RFD - Death Prophet Rakameg, 25% drop rate). After raids are out, stack some vampirism - around 10% (Drillborer Disk and the Rag Flame Trinket and totem). Having herbalism helps the gold you earn because you can potentially get Black Lotus from picking the Dream Foil in there.

 **Tanking Rotation**
 - Goal: to save mana, never generate more threat than needed to maintain aggro - your primary job is to keep aggro, not deal damage. Try to match your healer's mana use rate to keep the pulls rolling as much as you can. It’s much safer to make sure you have the resources (mana) to save a pull that goes south than to spend everything trying to shorten the encounter. So whenever possible, skip using the rotation below and just do auto-attacks + taunt. Or downrank your shocks when you don't need to go all out. Especially avoid the AoE fire totems if possible. Rather than using Earth Shock on cooldown and being caught out with a mob running towards the healer, make sure you can react to any situation that might come up
 - Imbue Rockbiter on a 1H and use a shield
 - Mark your targets; the party should be focusing on your kill order to not split your threat thin. Put a skull and cross mark and only tag other mobs so the healer doesn't get aggro and keep threat on skull (if someone goes for cross before skull is dead, they can tank it)
 - Always ask for Judgment of Wisdom on the skull if there's a pala in the party to help with mana
 - Totems: with >=2 DPS in the party, placing down a Windfury Totem is justified. Especially if they are higher level or well-geared. Just tell them if they rip threat, they tank that mob as a deal. With a pala, Blessing of Salvation (-30% threat generation) can also be placed on the melee DPS in exchange for Windfury. Use Mana Spring only if you're going to stand close to it for >20s
 - You can use Lightning Shield for the pull for added threat, switch to Water Shield halfway through and switch back to Lightning Shield whenever Clearcasting procs. If you have Totem of Tides, you can start with Water Shield already during leveling, but Lightning Shield with Lightning Strike is still the best for ST threat
 - Pull with rank 1 Lightning Bolt (big range, basically 0 mana) + Chain Lightning (to establish max initial threat). For real max threat, optionally add a Molten Blast after as it has a short cast time which you can fit in the time the mobs run to you
 - Running in, you'll want to Stormstrike on target 1, tab switch to Earth Shock target 2, and Lightning Strike target 3. If a target resists nature damage, use Frost Shock instead of Earth Shock
 - Tab switch between targets giving each of them an Earth Shock and melee auto attack. When in doubt, place a Stoneclaw Totem (though the threat per mana is great and allows you to passively regen and chain pull). Drop an Earthbind after Stoneclaw expires, if needed
 - Use rank 1 Earth Shock to interrupt spells
 - AoE threat for >3 mobs: Stoneclaw Totem, or fire totems - Fire Nova and Magma. If targets resist fire damage, Stoneclaw is your only AoE threat
 - Oh shit: if a pull was bigger than anticipated or to quickly get aggro off healers: Fire Nova - huge snap threat, but mana intensive
 - Mini oh shit: save your taunt to force a mob to attack you when it's attacking your healers
 - When a mob gets loose or runs towards a sheeped target, use max rank Lightning Bolt for high threat or Earth Shock for big snap threat
 - Healing yourself is a last resort; it's almost always better to pop Earth Shield, a Healing Potion or a Healthstone if you have one. If things get dicey, make sure to use those; never start casting while taking hits
 - After a pack is almost dead, move to a new one and Earth Shock one of those mobs to bring in that next pack
 - To kite melee mobs & nuke them with casters before they arrive, use Chain Lightning to pull and Earthbind Totem to snare them. Optionally Frost Shock to help kite. Earthbind also works as an "oh shit" button to help a healer catch up
 - For Caverns of Time: Black Morass, bring a Druid, Warlock or Hunter to help CC the mobs during those 3/4 Dragon pack pulls leading to the first boss (this dungeon eats every tank; it's not a shaman-specific thing to struggle here). Having a pala friend is huge for devotion aura. When the last boss enrages, find a way to kite it. Aim for approx 6k armor and 4k hp unbuffed before tanking it. It's also recommended to get 4* the best armor kits and initially a fortitude and armor potion + health potion. Some cool items which can help you reach the needed mitigation: Hateforge trinket, even the lvl 33 stamina JC trinket, Hateforge tank neck, shield with the biggest armor you find (preferably 1900+), Helm of Narv (if you wanna buy a BoE), Kara Crypt tank ring, Naglering
 -> With the new "Spell AoE tank" build ([https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... YALBQDIAY-](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?points=FQDYLAADAC-FAVYALBQDIAY-)), if you really want to cook some threat on a ST, you can rotate in Fire Nova -> Magma totems and Stoneclaw, like you're doing AoE threat. But it's very expensive to do that so you won't usually maintain that (or need to)

 **Enh DPS Rotation**
 - In dungeons while leveling, use a 2H with Flametongue or WF (*anything but* Rockbiter - at 60 WF) as imbue + Lightning Shield, using Lightning Strike -> Storm Strike, maybe Earth/Flame Shock on bosses -> Lightning Strike
 - After Ele Focus/Weapons, use a 2H with Frostbrand + Water Shield, using Frost Shock -> Stormstrike -> Lightning Strike/Shield
 - Totems: Strength of Earth, Flametongue, Windfury (once you have it) and Mana Spring.
 - Imbues: Frostbrand for some dungeons or soloing. Windfury is preferred for raiding and what you use when you’ve got a real weapon that you wanna do real numbers with.
 - At 60 as you get more crit / focus procs, but be ready to chug mana pots and tea on CD to max damage to sustain Lightning shield longer otherwise you swap to Water shield when you're low on mana. Your mana consumption will also go down in raids, especially if you have ferals around. Blessing of Kings, Mark of the Wild, elixirs like Mongoose and Dreamshard, etc.
 - Rotation at 60: use Windfury imbue + Lightning Shield; swap to Water Shield when low on mana. Keep up Lightning Shield. Don’t use Flame Shock on targets that won’t live more than 9-15 seconds. The point at which a Flame Shock becomes more worth than Earth Shock depends on your gear and level, so test on a dummy. At max level it’s always at least 3 ticks (9 seconds). For the rotation, put down totems first -> cast Flame Shock (or Earth Shock if immune) early when running in -> Stormstrike -> Lightning Strike -> Earth Shock (or Flame Shock to reapply debuff), repeat. TL;DR: FS/ES -> SS -> LS, repeat.

 **Healing Rotation**
 - No imbue
 - Put down totems that are most beneficial for your group, but only if needed to conserve mana (they have a 30y radius now, so sometimes you won't need to put them down again for a new pack): Strength of Earth, Flametongue, Windfury (once you have it) and Mana Spring (except when you need frost resistance and/or tremor/grounding). Situationally, use poison/disease cleansing, Fire Resistance or even Healing Stream totems
 - To keep your tank up in dungeons, use the latest rank of Healing Wave and Lesser Healing Wave, and -2 downranked Healing Wave, eg. r5 HW and LHW + r3 HW. It's also recommended to use r1 Healing Wave sometimes just to trigger Healing Way procs and fish for +armor on tanks
 - Chain Heal occasionally if there's lots of cleave dmg on the party
 - Once you're raiding, all you really need is Chain Heal rank 1 besides dropping totems within range of your group. Besides that, you can throw out Spirit Link on tanks during enrage phases, eg. use on Maexxna before web wrap

 **Totem Use While Solo**
 - They're not often worth dropping since you’ll be killing faster than the mana is worth to drop them (the mana cast is balanced around your whole party benefiting)
 - That said, Earthbind weaving with a Swing timer is worth doing if you care about reducing the damage you take fighting mobs 1v1
 - After getting Clearcasting, you can use Searing Totem + Stoneskin occasionally, mainly when it‘s possible to chain pull multiple mobs to the same spot
 - To maximize your fire totems' damage when you have Elemental Weapons, you could use the Flametongue imbue - but generally Frostbrand is still superior while leveling

 **Earthbind Weaving/Kiting**
 - Earthbind Totem > Searing Totem > Flame Shock
 - Melee, side strafe through them (don't expose your back) to get out of their range while your auto attack is resetting
 - As your swing timer is resetting, position to re-enter the mobs' hitbox and swing again
 - Re-apply Flame Shock / Lightning shield if efficient

 **Profs**
 - Skinning & LW while leveling since nodes are highly contested on Ambershire atm. And LW allows you to make Stormshroud armor around level 50 (especially the shoulders and hands, they're pre-BiS for enhance), and Devilsaur hands/legs around level 53/55 respectively
 - Alternatively, could take Mining & Blacksmithing as enhance; the Hateforge set is pretty nice around level 50; then after Kara10 comes out, you can get the Towerforge set -> you can also just buy these sets or pieces (chest and legs especially) from AH
 - To be more economical, you could skip LW/BS and go straight for herbalism & alchemy from the start
 - At ~53 when you start farming lashers, after making Stormshroud, drop LW for herbalism to beef up your gold farming by getting Dream Foil with a chance at Black Lotus
 - At 60, herbalism & alchemy for general use and late-game gold (Black Lotus hunting is fun)
 - Consider dropping alchemy for engineering - dropping Sappers/Dynamite will help your raid clear faster + if you plan to PvP there’s a lot of utility, even outside of stun grenades

 **Spells to Buy**
 - You can skip all but 1st rank of Resurrection
 - Can technically skip Flametongue imbue
 - Totems: you likely won't use the nature/frost/fire resistance totems during leveling enough to justify getting those. If you want, you can probably skip all totems besides the Poison/Disease cleansing totems, though for tanking you might want the strength/agi/WF totems. Water totems are optional (pretty weak while leveling but can be nice)
 - If you don't plan to tank or play ele, skip the ranged damage spells (but never shocks)
 - Everything else you need no matter the spec

 **Pre-BiS**
 - **Enh DPS:** check out this post in the #shaman channel: [https://discord.com/channels/4666224558 ... 0462362656](https://discord.com/channels/466622455805378571/810850759658831903/1415067340462362656) Aim for 8% hit for melee. You'll get 3% from talents, and another 1% from Weapon Skill book (250g + quest for permanent 5 weapon skill: [viewtopic.php?t=16790](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=16790) & <https://turtle-wow.fandom.com/wiki/Weapon_Skill>). So usually, you'll only need to get 4% more from gear/weapon skill. At level 58+ pick up a quest from Shaman trainer in Org, turn in some gems and then kill a mob in Scholomance for Skyfury Helm: <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?quest=7667> (otherwise the Mail helm from Strat, Eyepatch from BRD, or Eyepatch from UBRS are also good options). Take a look at Blacksmithing for the Hateforge Armor set for pre-BiS (<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=615>) and once Kara10 drops the Towerforge Battlegear (<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=630>). Also, check out this video for a general idea:
[embed: https://www.youtube.com/embed/SgkuSNu-AMQ]
Later on, follow this explanation for any build trying to get crush/crit immune (= reaching 440 defense) <https://wowwiki-archive.fandom.com/wiki/Attack_table>. More suggested items: pre-BiS mace: <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=83440>, Breastplate options: <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?quest=5166>; <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60008>; <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=14611>; <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13090>, shoulders: BM +2% hit one or the Kara 5 one. Arcanite reaper or Bonecrusher are best options for pre-BiS, but could also try Treant's Bane if you are a masochist: <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18538>. If you are a double masochist, become exalted in Alterac Valley -Unstoppable Force is great: <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=19323>. Eventually, the rule of thumb is to get 30-35% crit, then start stacking AP and +haste (the more haste you get the better)
 - **Tanking:** focus on +stam and armor gear, ignoring defense beyond 15 (with the caveat that you'll still want defense, agility or direct dodge stats when it doesn't compromise stamina or armor to grab it). Generally speaking, just try to get the best threat/defense piece you can for each armor slot because sometimes you need to max your defense out, but sometimes you need a lot of threat, so it’s just dependent on the fight. Shields: SWV shield or the one from Kara5 are acceptable as pre-BiS. The one from BM can probably also be used (less stamina though)
 - **Resto:** Get as much +healing and +int as you can. Just do all the high level dungeons a few times and you should be good, eg. get the legs from DM West, decent options from BRD are the gloves from either Emperor or Moira/Mantle of Lost Hope/Soot Encrusted Footwear/Guiding Stave of Wisdom/Second Wind, Rivendare's Robe from Stratholme UD, Royal Seal of Eldre'Thalas from Dire Maul. As for crafted items, the crafted cloak, and maybe even the crafted chest are great options if you can afford it. Black Morass has the BiS totem until Naxx, and some caster stuff, as well as Kara Crypts. I wouldn't recommend it since it's easy to get similarly strong items in MC/BWL/AQ40, but you could look out for high healing power lvl 54+ green gear on the AH such as Created Cape (you won't need to replace it until the cape from AQ40's final boss), the chest piece and maybe Corehound Belt (optional because costly) - some of those pieces are better than even MC T1 (for example the legs), but it comes at the cost of stam & int (on a badly geared resto shammy, int is pretty important; around a 4k mana pool is recommended - or if your guild clears raids fast enough, you can just drink more pots/tea and oranges between pulls). Enchants to get for resto besides the typically recommended ones outside of T-WoW are enchanted armor kits that give +9 spell power. 2% haste to shoulder enchant, and then 1% haste vs +12 spellpower to helm/legs; ring/neck enchants (+12 healing) from JC. Belt buckle for +10 intellect. Other ideas: the helm and trinket from AD faction, Mindfang from AB exalted, offhand from AV exalted, the shield from BM exalted, totem from BM drop, decent ring from BM faction if Urok LBRS ring evades you, UBRS trinket with AD trinket will be BiS. Strat chest vs BM faction chest could go either way. For weapon, the weaker +healing enchant. Tbh for pre-BiS, it's probably not worth it to enchant gear you're going to replace soon - especially the nitpicky ones like +100hp on chest and such (instead, you can spend the gold on more mana pots and teas). +12 on neck and rings when you have decent ones are worth since it's pretty cheap, then gloves/wrist/weapon if you have good ones
 - **Ele:** check the pinned in #shaman for a doc with ele pre-BiS. Basically need 15% hit on spells, as much int and crit as possible and spd, hit > crit > spd > int. If you have some gold there are two pairs of crafted cloth gloves that are really good, one with crit and one with haste. T1 belt/wrist from AH. The blue crafted Bloodvine set but don’t spend to much gold on stuff you can replace from Kara10. 2% crit quest reward trinket and DM trinket. It won’t be hard to get Onyxia group fairly fast, then you can get the Horde head and a good ring. UBRS has two trinkets and a great cloth head. Gloves of Unwinding Mystery
 - You could look at a Classic BiS list and use Atlasloot to check the new dungeons like Kara Crypts (eg. Crown of Shattering, and pre-BiS mace: Boneshatter Maul), Black Morass (eg. a very good mp5 totem), Hateforge Quarry (the Corrosive Core trinket is good if you lack +hit) and Stormwind Vaults (eg. Whip of Encouragement, haste is better if you're hit capped), and see if anything is an upgrade

 **Stat Prios at 60**

 **Enhancement DPS:**
 - 1 phys Hit % = ~29.09 AP / ~53.67 SP (up to cap of 8% - 4% from gear + Weapon Skill, 3% from talents, 1% from Weapon Skill book for 250g + quest)
 - 1 phys Crit % = ~20.69AP / ~38.16 SP (up to cap of 54%)
 - 1 WS = ~16.66 AP / ~30.73 SP (important for Orcs and Axes) -> Get WS: [viewtopic.php?t=16790](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=16790) / <https://turtle-wow.fandom.com/wiki/Weapon_Skill>
 - 1 Haste % = ~10.64 / ~19.62 SP
 - 1 STR  = 2.3 AP / 4.24 SP
 - 1 AGI = ~1.13 AP / ~2.08 SP
 - 1 AP = 1 AP / ~1.84 SP
 - 1 STAM
 - 1 INT = ~0.05 AP / ~0.10 SP
 - 1 Spell Hit = ~9.13 AP / ~16.83 SP
 - 1 Spell Crit = ~2.70 AP / ~4.98 SP
 - 1 Spell Power = ~0.54  AP / 1.0 SP
 - 1 Armor Penetration = ~0.34 AP / ~0.63 SP
 - 1 Spell Penetration = ~3.12 AP / ~5.75 SP

 **Consumables**

 **Enhancement DPS:**
For starting raids, stick to the following. This shouldn’t leave your wallet too drained. If you drop anything, drop the Arcane Elixir, then maybe ROIDS if you can't farm gold/the mats for it, but it is pretty good:
 - Mongoose elixir (never leave home without the 'goose)
 - ROIDS
 - Juju Power
 - Dreamshard Elixir
 - Greater Arcane Elixir (Nature Power is cheaper but unavailable until Emerald Sanctum)
 - Nordanaar Herbal Tea

If you want to go for a more comprehensive list, it should look something like this:

(1hr+ Consumes)
 - Concoction of the Emerald Mongoose
 - Concoction of the Arcane Giant
 - Concoction of the Dreamwater
 - Elixir of Greater Nature Power
 - Elixir of Greater Firepower
 - ROIDS
 - Flask of the Titans/Supreme Power
 - Spirit/Swiftness of Zanza
 - Mageblood Potion
 - Elixir of Superior Defense

(Food + Alcohol)
 - Danonzo's Tel'Abim Medley
 - Rumsey Rum Black Label/Medivh's Merlot

(Miscellaneous)
 - Juju Flurry
 - Nordanaar Herbal Tea
 - Major Mana Potion
 - Goblin Sapper Charge
 - Potion of Quickness

 **Resto:**

 - Dreamshard Elixir
 - Mageblood Potion when it becomes available
 - Spirit of Zanza when it becomes available
 - Brilliant Mana/Wizard Oil (Wizard for stronger heals) -> use normal Wizard Oil until Brilliant becomes available
 - Major Mana Potion
 - Nordanaar Herbal Tea
 - Greater Fire Protection

 **Macros**
 - [https://github.com/Meridaw/Vanilla-Macr ... ter/Shaman](https://github.com/Meridaw/Vanilla-Macros/tree/master/Shaman)
 - [viewtopic.php?t=20390&sid=e49005ee5c14e ... 13b1a3c66f](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=20390)
 - Place all totems:
#showtooltip Flametongue Totem
/cast Flametongue Totem
/cast Strength of Earth Totem
/cast Mana Spring Totem
/cast Windfury Totem
/cast Water Shield
 - With Call of Elements addon: new slot under keybinds + /coe for set up

 **Weapon Imbues & Shields**
 - Rockbiter + Lightning Shield until level 41/42
 - Then Frostbrand becomes better with Elemental Focus + Elemental Weapons talents
 - At 60 you’re gonna use Windfury imbue, but you’re still gonna drop Windfury Totem (and Flametongue Totem) for your party even if you don’t benefit from it

 **Weapons**
 - Until you get the Lightning Strike talent, a high-DPS dagger is just as good as a slow 2H
 - After getting Lightning Strike, try to have as slow of a 2H as possible
 - In general, enhance prefers slow weapons with high top-end dmg, counting for both 1H and 2H
content_html:
I wrote this out as my personal levelling plan after compiling a lot of different tips from discussions in the #shaman channel on the Turtle WoW Discord. Since I noticed a lot of people asking for one, I'll share this in case it helps anyone save time by not having to research the same stuff. I'll be editing this if I come across any more relevant info, and I'd be grateful for any corrections or additions that anyone is willing to make.

Big thanks to the following contributors who provided most of the knowledge compiled here: Squid, Zhafu, Rinzu, Peter Hammer, DemonBoyJr, Monolith, Akos, Not Normal, poto, Haaxor1689, Zaaparou and more (sorry if I forgot any).

Race
All 3 races are pretty much equally well-performing here, so go with the one you find the most fun or aesthetically pleasing. That said,
- Troll is the best min-max race for PvE (quasi-Bloodlust haste racial for PvE, and hex is decent for PvP)
- Tauren is the best for PvP and the most tanky for leveling (+5% hp, nature resist) - Warstomp is the best PvP racial + Plainsrunning is the biggest QoL racial in the game (saves us 2 talents on imp Ghost Wolf as well)
- Orc is still a decent choice for Enhance PvE (axe skill helps + Blood Fury)

Gear & Stat Prios
- Stats for tanking while leveling: +stam > +agi > +str > +int (when tanking at 60, +str becomes 2nd most important and +agi third)
- For healing: +int = +hp
- For DPS: +str = +agi > +stam > +int (+str & +agi roughly on par, at 60 +str is more valuable than +agi)
- Stat prios thread: viewtopic.php?t=21159
- For calculating AP: shamans get 0 AP per agi, 2 AP from str and 1% dodge and 1% crit per 20 agi
- A shield with high armor is a always a top prio, eg. Compendium of the Fallen quest reward -> SM Cath shield -> Gilneas shield / Mara goblin shield / SWV shield. When in doubt between two, choose the higher armor one (it scales with tanking talents that boost armor on shields by 30%, and all items by 15%). You can run an EHP calc just checking your % damage reduction on A shield vs B shield listed on your character sheet: EHP = HP/(1-%DR), then see which one gives you the most EHP. As a quick shortcut, in most cases, 10 armor is roughly equal to 1 stamina

Talents & Rotation
With this build, you can fill any role in dungeons: tank, DPS or heal. We'll be picking tanking talents, but even if you solely want to DPS, this is arguably still the best build because you do practically the same DPS (the difference is really negligible) + have the benefit of being more tanky. That is, unless you're levelling in a group and don't have to care about mitigation. If you want to skip the tank talents, you could swap out Shield Spec. for Ancestral Knowledge. For healing, all you'll need is some +int gear and you're good to go for dungeons.

To level 33
- 24p in enh: 5/5 Shield Spec > 2/2 Totemic Alignment > 3/3 Stable Shields > 3/3 Ancestral Guardian (before LS for mitigation) > Lightning Strike (take before AG if threat is a problem) > 1/5 Thundering Strikes > 2/2 Spirit Armor > 4/5 Thundering Strikes > 3/3 Elemental Weapons (first if feeling squishy) > Stormstrike (first if want more threat): https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... oUYALAQDI-
- Rotation: Rockbiter + Lightning Shield, using Lightning Strike -> Storm Strike -> Earth Shock -> Lightning Strike. You spend your mana at the beginning, then melee the mob down because you want to start the mana regen ASAP. Using totems isn't recommended, though Searing is probably fine if you're sticking in the same location long enough to get value
- Weapon: until Lightning Strike, a high dps dagger is just as good as a slow 2H; after Lightning Strike, a slow 2H is best
- From around level 25, focus on getting a good shield with high armor. At level 28, you can get the Compendium of the Fallen quest from Sage Truthseeker in Thunder Bluff (34.7, 47.8) and do SM: Library for the shield quest reward
- At level 33, get the Jewelcrafting +stam trinkets

Level 34-44
- 11p in ele: 5/5 Convection > 2/5 Concussion (since few mobs do elemental dmg) OR 2/3 Elemental Warding (for mitigation in Maraudon) > 3/3 Elemental Devastation > Elemental Focus (Clearcasting!): https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... oUYALAQDI- OR https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... oUYALAQDI-
- Between level 35-41, try to get the Totem of Tides from the orc boss in Stormwrought - it's phenomenal for tanking dungeons + farming Lashers
- As a Tauren, at level 40, get Plainsrunning: head to the 2nd village you visit in Mulgore when you make a Tauren. The mount trainer there provides you a quest that leads to STV

Level 44-50
- 6p in enh: 5/5 Thundering Strikes > 5/5 Element's Grace (raises threat w/o necessarily spending mana): https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... YALAQDIAo- OR https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... YALAQDIAo-
- Rotation: after getting Elemental Focus at level 44, Frostbrand + Water Shield, using Frost Shock -> Stormstrike -> Lightning Strike
- Optional: between 44-48, farm Earth Elementals in Badlands + occasional Uldaman runs to get the Goblin brainwashing machine for dual speccing (if the spot isn't camped too much, it might be possible to get the Goblin brainwashing machine for dual speccing, though this might be an unrealistic goal)
- Around level 50, it's pretty easy and worth it to get this axe: https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=51892
- For the level 50 Spirit Totem quest, the trick here is that the Vultures have a higher chance of dropping the Spider Eye and the Black Claw than the spiders and the bears themselves

Level 51-60
- Respec to 5/5 Ancestral Knowledge: https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... YALAQDIAo- OR https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... YALAQDIAo-
- 6p in enh: Bloodlust; 3p in ele: 3/3 Reverberation (take this before Flurry for more QoL in managing threat + more frequent spell interrupt); 5p in enh: 5/5 Flurry; 1p in ele: 3/5 Concussion: https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... ALFQDIAoB- OR 3/3 Elemental Warding over 3/5 Concussion (Warding = a bit more tanky, but elemental damage is limited; Concussion = more threat): https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... ALFQDIAoB- OR for cheaper totems: https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... BQDIAoB-Ao
- From level 52+, when you get r5 Fire Nova, you can farm Lashers in Dire Maul East. See the guide on this below, but note that between levels 52-54, you might have better success just doing the first three groups as the aggro of the wandering mobs is kind of crazy
- Spam HFQ and BRD to 55-57 (get pre-raid BiS), then switch to Scholo/Strat; 55+ dungeons are often run and rerun for stuff (remember to befriend healers)
- Get WS: viewtopic.php?t=16790 / https://turtle-wow.fandom.com/wiki/Weapon_Skill

OR, if you're wanting to go resto at 60:

Level 51-60
- Respec or dual spec to resto here in order to farm pre-raid BiS early. Rush Imp Water Shield with Stable Shields first, so like this: https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... FoDoYIEYQC
- After that, finish every talent in resto except imp Reincartion, Healing Focus and Spirit Link: https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... oaIFYQKFAB
- Similarly as the enhancement pre-BiS farm, spam HFQ and BRD to 55-57 (get pre-raid BiS), then switch to Scholo/Strat; 55+ dungeons are often run and rerun for stuff (remember to befriend tanks)

Lasher Farming
Here's a video on it by Zaaparou: Make sure to have a 2nd account with a level 1 -> invite it to the group, make it party lead; once you've finished a run, log out on your shaman, switch over to the 2nd account and reset the dungeon (click on the torch and it'll port you to DM: West entrance). Rotate Nova > Magma > Nova on each pack, heal up & drink between packs; during the pack, you'll have to swap to Earth Shield for 100% pushback protection + do 1-2 Healing Waves on yourself, then switch back to Water Shield. Basically, you do 1 pack at a time. Have Water Shield on, aggro the pack, drop Stoneskin, agility, Healing Stream. When the pack gets close, drop Fire Nova. Then use Magma. Usually, you'll dip to around 50% health at this time, so you can use Earth Shield + cast 1-2 Healing Waves. Switch back to Water Shield, Fire Nova when it's off cooldown, drop Magma again. Usually, the pack will be dead at this time, but sometimes a 3rd Fire Nova totem is needed. You should finish each lasher pack at like 60% health and 40% mana. Talent-wise, you'll need this specific spec with all the talents that increase totem damage (Elemental Weapons in enhance - Flametongue - for +30% damage increase to fire totems) and the ones that transfer totem threat to you (otherwise the Lashers will kill your totems), as well as 12 points in resto for pushback protection: https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... AQDI-FoAAC. Also make sure to have Totem of Tides from the new Stormwrought dungeon - it deals aoe frost damage every time you are hit while having water shield active. Gear-wise, bring +int/mp5 and +stam gear (e.g. the shield from ST - Eranikus; Princess Dagger - the blue one with +int/mp5; or just some green "of stamina" mace). A good potential farming trinket: Blood-etched Fetish (from RFD - Death Prophet Rakameg, 25% drop rate). After raids are out, stack some vampirism - around 10% (Drillborer Disk and the Rag Flame Trinket and totem). Having herbalism helps the gold you earn because you can potentially get Black Lotus from picking the Dream Foil in there.

Tanking Rotation
- Goal: to save mana, never generate more threat than needed to maintain aggro - your primary job is to keep aggro, not deal damage. Try to match your healer's mana use rate to keep the pulls rolling as much as you can. It’s much safer to make sure you have the resources (mana) to save a pull that goes south than to spend everything trying to shorten the encounter. So whenever possible, skip using the rotation below and just do auto-attacks + taunt. Or downrank your shocks when you don't need to go all out. Especially avoid the AoE fire totems if possible. Rather than using Earth Shock on cooldown and being caught out with a mob running towards the healer, make sure you can react to any situation that might come up
- Imbue Rockbiter on a 1H and use a shield
- Mark your targets; the party should be focusing on your kill order to not split your threat thin. Put a skull and cross mark and only tag other mobs so the healer doesn't get aggro and keep threat on skull (if someone goes for cross before skull is dead, they can tank it)
- Always ask for Judgment of Wisdom on the skull if there's a pala in the party to help with mana
- Totems: with >=2 DPS in the party, placing down a Windfury Totem is justified. Especially if they are higher level or well-geared. Just tell them if they rip threat, they tank that mob as a deal. With a pala, Blessing of Salvation (-30% threat generation) can also be placed on the melee DPS in exchange for Windfury. Use Mana Spring only if you're going to stand close to it for >20s
- You can use Lightning Shield for the pull for added threat, switch to Water Shield halfway through and switch back to Lightning Shield whenever Clearcasting procs. If you have Totem of Tides, you can start with Water Shield already during leveling, but Lightning Shield with Lightning Strike is still the best for ST threat
- Pull with rank 1 Lightning Bolt (big range, basically 0 mana) + Chain Lightning (to establish max initial threat). For real max threat, optionally add a Molten Blast after as it has a short cast time which you can fit in the time the mobs run to you
- Running in, you'll want to Stormstrike on target 1, tab switch to Earth Shock target 2, and Lightning Strike target 3. If a target resists nature damage, use Frost Shock instead of Earth Shock
- Tab switch between targets giving each of them an Earth Shock and melee auto attack. When in doubt, place a Stoneclaw Totem (though the threat per mana is great and allows you to passively regen and chain pull). Drop an Earthbind after Stoneclaw expires, if needed
- Use rank 1 Earth Shock to interrupt spells
- AoE threat for >3 mobs: Stoneclaw Totem, or fire totems - Fire Nova and Magma. If targets resist fire damage, Stoneclaw is your only AoE threat
- Oh shit: if a pull was bigger than anticipated or to quickly get aggro off healers: Fire Nova - huge snap threat, but mana intensive
- Mini oh shit: save your taunt to force a mob to attack you when it's attacking your healers
- When a mob gets loose or runs towards a sheeped target, use max rank Lightning Bolt for high threat or Earth Shock for big snap threat
- Healing yourself is a last resort; it's almost always better to pop Earth Shield, a Healing Potion or a Healthstone if you have one. If things get dicey, make sure to use those; never start casting while taking hits
- After a pack is almost dead, move to a new one and Earth Shock one of those mobs to bring in that next pack
- To kite melee mobs & nuke them with casters before they arrive, use Chain Lightning to pull and Earthbind Totem to snare them. Optionally Frost Shock to help kite. Earthbind also works as an "oh shit" button to help a healer catch up
- For Caverns of Time: Black Morass, bring a Druid, Warlock or Hunter to help CC the mobs during those 3/4 Dragon pack pulls leading to the first boss (this dungeon eats every tank; it's not a shaman-specific thing to struggle here). Having a pala friend is huge for devotion aura. When the last boss enrages, find a way to kite it. Aim for approx 6k armor and 4k hp unbuffed before tanking it. It's also recommended to get 4* the best armor kits and initially a fortitude and armor potion + health potion. Some cool items which can help you reach the needed mitigation: Hateforge trinket, even the lvl 33 stamina JC trinket, Hateforge tank neck, shield with the biggest armor you find (preferably 1900+), Helm of Narv (if you wanna buy a BoE), Kara Crypt tank ring, Naglering
-> With the new "Spell AoE tank" build (https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/shaman?p ... YALBQDIAY-), if you really want to cook some threat on a ST, you can rotate in Fire Nova -> Magma totems and Stoneclaw, like you're doing AoE threat. But it's very expensive to do that so you won't usually maintain that (or need to)

Enh DPS Rotation
- In dungeons while leveling, use a 2H with Flametongue or WF (*anything but* Rockbiter - at 60 WF) as imbue + Lightning Shield, using Lightning Strike -> Storm Strike, maybe Earth/Flame Shock on bosses -> Lightning Strike
- After Ele Focus/Weapons, use a 2H with Frostbrand + Water Shield, using Frost Shock -> Stormstrike -> Lightning Strike/Shield
- Totems: Strength of Earth, Flametongue, Windfury (once you have it) and Mana Spring.
- Imbues: Frostbrand for some dungeons or soloing. Windfury is preferred for raiding and what you use when you’ve got a real weapon that you wanna do real numbers with.
- At 60 as you get more crit / focus procs, but be ready to chug mana pots and tea on CD to max damage to sustain Lightning shield longer otherwise you swap to Water shield when you're low on mana. Your mana consumption will also go down in raids, especially if you have ferals around. Blessing of Kings, Mark of the Wild, elixirs like Mongoose and Dreamshard, etc.
- Rotation at 60: use Windfury imbue + Lightning Shield; swap to Water Shield when low on mana. Keep up Lightning Shield. Don’t use Flame Shock on targets that won’t live more than 9-15 seconds. The point at which a Flame Shock becomes more worth than Earth Shock depends on your gear and level, so test on a dummy. At max level it’s always at least 3 ticks (9 seconds). For the rotation, put down totems first -> cast Flame Shock (or Earth Shock if immune) early when running in -> Stormstrike -> Lightning Strike -> Earth Shock (or Flame Shock to reapply debuff), repeat. TL;DR: FS/ES -> SS -> LS, repeat.

Healing Rotation
- No imbue
- Put down totems that are most beneficial for your group, but only if needed to conserve mana (they have a 30y radius now, so sometimes you won't need to put them down again for a new pack): Strength of Earth, Flametongue, Windfury (once you have it) and Mana Spring (except when you need frost resistance and/or tremor/grounding). Situationally, use poison/disease cleansing, Fire Resistance or even Healing Stream totems
- To keep your tank up in dungeons, use the latest rank of Healing Wave and Lesser Healing Wave, and -2 downranked Healing Wave, eg. r5 HW and LHW + r3 HW. It's also recommended to use r1 Healing Wave sometimes just to trigger Healing Way procs and fish for +armor on tanks
- Chain Heal occasionally if there's lots of cleave dmg on the party
- Once you're raiding, all you really need is Chain Heal rank 1 besides dropping totems within range of your group. Besides that, you can throw out Spirit Link on tanks during enrage phases, eg. use on Maexxna before web wrap

Totem Use While Solo
- They're not often worth dropping since you’ll be killing faster than the mana is worth to drop them (the mana cast is balanced around your whole party benefiting)
- That said, Earthbind weaving with a Swing timer is worth doing if you care about reducing the damage you take fighting mobs 1v1
- After getting Clearcasting, you can use Searing Totem + Stoneskin occasionally, mainly when it‘s possible to chain pull multiple mobs to the same spot
- To maximize your fire totems' damage when you have Elemental Weapons, you could use the Flametongue imbue - but generally Frostbrand is still superior while leveling

Earthbind Weaving/Kiting
- Earthbind Totem > Searing Totem > Flame Shock
- Melee, side strafe through them (don't expose your back) to get out of their range while your auto attack is resetting
- As your swing timer is resetting, position to re-enter the mobs' hitbox and swing again
- Re-apply Flame Shock / Lightning shield if efficient

Profs
- Skinning & LW while leveling since nodes are highly contested on Ambershire atm. And LW allows you to make Stormshroud armor around level 50 (especially the shoulders and hands, they're pre-BiS for enhance), and Devilsaur hands/legs around level 53/55 respectively
- Alternatively, could take Mining & Blacksmithing as enhance; the Hateforge set is pretty nice around level 50; then after Kara10 comes out, you can get the Towerforge set -> you can also just buy these sets or pieces (chest and legs especially) from AH
- To be more economical, you could skip LW/BS and go straight for herbalism & alchemy from the start
- At ~53 when you start farming lashers, after making Stormshroud, drop LW for herbalism to beef up your gold farming by getting Dream Foil with a chance at Black Lotus
- At 60, herbalism & alchemy for general use and late-game gold (Black Lotus hunting is fun)
- Consider dropping alchemy for engineering - dropping Sappers/Dynamite will help your raid clear faster + if you plan to PvP there’s a lot of utility, even outside of stun grenades

Spells to Buy
- You can skip all but 1st rank of Resurrection
- Can technically skip Flametongue imbue
- Totems: you likely won't use the nature/frost/fire resistance totems during leveling enough to justify getting those. If you want, you can probably skip all totems besides the Poison/Disease cleansing totems, though for tanking you might want the strength/agi/WF totems. Water totems are optional (pretty weak while leveling but can be nice)
- If you don't plan to tank or play ele, skip the ranged damage spells (but never shocks)
- Everything else you need no matter the spec

Pre-BiS
- Enh DPS: check out this post in the #shaman channel: https://discord.com/channels/4666224558 ... 0462362656 Aim for 8% hit for melee. You'll get 3% from talents, and another 1% from Weapon Skill book (250g + quest for permanent 5 weapon skill: viewtopic.php?t=16790 & https://turtle-wow.fandom.com/wiki/Weapon_Skill). So usually, you'll only need to get 4% more from gear/weapon skill. At level 58+ pick up a quest from Shaman trainer in Org, turn in some gems and then kill a mob in Scholomance for Skyfury Helm: https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?quest=7667 (otherwise the Mail helm from Strat, Eyepatch from BRD, or Eyepatch from UBRS are also good options). Take a look at Blacksmithing for the Hateforge Armor set for pre-BiS (https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=615) and once Kara10 drops the Towerforge Battlegear (https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=630). Also, check out this video for a general idea: Later on, follow this explanation for any build trying to get crush/crit immune (= reaching 440 defense) https://wowwiki-archive.fandom.com/wiki/Attack_table. More suggested items: pre-BiS mace: https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=83440, Breastplate options: https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?quest=5166; https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60008; https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=14611; https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13090, shoulders: BM +2% hit one or the Kara 5 one. Arcanite reaper or Bonecrusher are best options for pre-BiS, but could also try Treant's Bane if you are a masochist: https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18538. If you are a double masochist, become exalted in Alterac Valley -Unstoppable Force is great: https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=19323. Eventually, the rule of thumb is to get 30-35% crit, then start stacking AP and +haste (the more haste you get the better)
- Tanking: focus on +stam and armor gear, ignoring defense beyond 15 (with the caveat that you'll still want defense, agility or direct dodge stats when it doesn't compromise stamina or armor to grab it). Generally speaking, just try to get the best threat/defense piece you can for each armor slot because sometimes you need to max your defense out, but sometimes you need a lot of threat, so it’s just dependent on the fight. Shields: SWV shield or the one from Kara5 are acceptable as pre-BiS. The one from BM can probably also be used (less stamina though)
- Resto: Get as much +healing and +int as you can. Just do all the high level dungeons a few times and you should be good, eg. get the legs from DM West, decent options from BRD are the gloves from either Emperor or Moira/Mantle of Lost Hope/Soot Encrusted Footwear/Guiding Stave of Wisdom/Second Wind, Rivendare's Robe from Stratholme UD, Royal Seal of Eldre'Thalas from Dire Maul. As for crafted items, the crafted cloak, and maybe even the crafted chest are great options if you can afford it. Black Morass has the BiS totem until Naxx, and some caster stuff, as well as Kara Crypts. I wouldn't recommend it since it's easy to get similarly strong items in MC/BWL/AQ40, but you could look out for high healing power lvl 54+ green gear on the AH such as Created Cape (you won't need to replace it until the cape from AQ40's final boss), the chest piece and maybe Corehound Belt (optional because costly) - some of those pieces are better than even MC T1 (for example the legs), but it comes at the cost of stam & int (on a badly geared resto shammy, int is pretty important; around a 4k mana pool is recommended - or if your guild clears raids fast enough, you can just drink more pots/tea and oranges between pulls). Enchants to get for resto besides the typically recommended ones outside of T-WoW are enchanted armor kits that give +9 spell power. 2% haste to shoulder enchant, and then 1% haste vs +12 spellpower to helm/legs; ring/neck enchants (+12 healing) from JC. Belt buckle for +10 intellect. Other ideas: the helm and trinket from AD faction, Mindfang from AB exalted, offhand from AV exalted, the shield from BM exalted, totem from BM drop, decent ring from BM faction if Urok LBRS ring evades you, UBRS trinket with AD trinket will be BiS. Strat chest vs BM faction chest could go either way. For weapon, the weaker +healing enchant. Tbh for pre-BiS, it's probably not worth it to enchant gear you're going to replace soon - especially the nitpicky ones like +100hp on chest and such (instead, you can spend the gold on more mana pots and teas). +12 on neck and rings when you have decent ones are worth since it's pretty cheap, then gloves/wrist/weapon if you have good ones
- Ele: check the pinned in #shaman for a doc with ele pre-BiS. Basically need 15% hit on spells, as much int and crit as possible and spd, hit > crit > spd > int. If you have some gold there are two pairs of crafted cloth gloves that are really good, one with crit and one with haste. T1 belt/wrist from AH. The blue crafted Bloodvine set but don’t spend to much gold on stuff you can replace from Kara10. 2% crit quest reward trinket and DM trinket. It won’t be hard to get Onyxia group fairly fast, then you can get the Horde head and a good ring. UBRS has two trinkets and a great cloth head. Gloves of Unwinding Mystery
- You could look at a Classic BiS list and use Atlasloot to check the new dungeons like Kara Crypts (eg. Crown of Shattering, and pre-BiS mace: Boneshatter Maul), Black Morass (eg. a very good mp5 totem), Hateforge Quarry (the Corrosive Core trinket is good if you lack +hit) and Stormwind Vaults (eg. Whip of Encouragement, haste is better if you're hit capped), and see if anything is an upgrade

Stat Prios at 60

Enhancement DPS:
- 1 phys Hit % = ~29.09 AP / ~53.67 SP (up to cap of 8% - 4% from gear + Weapon Skill, 3% from talents, 1% from Weapon Skill book for 250g + quest)
- 1 phys Crit % = ~20.69AP / ~38.16 SP (up to cap of 54%)
- 1 WS = ~16.66 AP / ~30.73 SP (important for Orcs and Axes) -> Get WS: viewtopic.php?t=16790 / https://turtle-wow.fandom.com/wiki/Weapon_Skill
- 1 Haste % = ~10.64 / ~19.62 SP
- 1 STR = 2.3 AP / 4.24 SP
- 1 AGI = ~1.13 AP / ~2.08 SP
- 1 AP = 1 AP / ~1.84 SP
- 1 STAM
- 1 INT = ~0.05 AP / ~0.10 SP
- 1 Spell Hit = ~9.13 AP / ~16.83 SP
- 1 Spell Crit = ~2.70 AP / ~4.98 SP
- 1 Spell Power = ~0.54 AP / 1.0 SP
- 1 Armor Penetration = ~0.34 AP / ~0.63 SP
- 1 Spell Penetration = ~3.12 AP / ~5.75 SP

Consumables

Enhancement DPS:
For starting raids, stick to the following. This shouldn’t leave your wallet too drained. If you drop anything, drop the Arcane Elixir, then maybe ROIDS if you can't farm gold/the mats for it, but it is pretty good:
- Mongoose elixir (never leave home without the 'goose)
- ROIDS
- Juju Power
- Dreamshard Elixir
- Greater Arcane Elixir (Nature Power is cheaper but unavailable until Emerald Sanctum)
- Nordanaar Herbal Tea

If you want to go for a more comprehensive list, it should look something like this:

(1hr+ Consumes)
- Concoction of the Emerald Mongoose
- Concoction of the Arcane Giant
- Concoction of the Dreamwater
- Elixir of Greater Nature Power
- Elixir of Greater Firepower
- ROIDS
- Flask of the Titans/Supreme Power
- Spirit/Swiftness of Zanza
- Mageblood Potion
- Elixir of Superior Defense

(Food + Alcohol)
- Danonzo's Tel'Abim Medley
- Rumsey Rum Black Label/Medivh's Merlot

(Miscellaneous)
- Juju Flurry
- Nordanaar Herbal Tea
- Major Mana Potion
- Goblin Sapper Charge
- Potion of Quickness

Resto:

- Dreamshard Elixir
- Mageblood Potion when it becomes available
- Spirit of Zanza when it becomes available
- Brilliant Mana/Wizard Oil (Wizard for stronger heals) -> use normal Wizard Oil until Brilliant becomes available
- Major Mana Potion
- Nordanaar Herbal Tea
- Greater Fire Protection

Macros
- https://github.com/Meridaw/Vanilla-Macr ... ter/Shaman
- viewtopic.php?t=20390&sid=e49005ee5c14e ... 13b1a3c66f
- Place all totems:
#showtooltip Flametongue Totem
/cast Flametongue Totem
/cast Strength of Earth Totem
/cast Mana Spring Totem
/cast Windfury Totem
/cast Water Shield
- With Call of Elements addon: new slot under keybinds + /coe for set up

Weapon Imbues & Shields
- Rockbiter + Lightning Shield until level 41/42
- Then Frostbrand becomes better with Elemental Focus + Elemental Weapons talents
- At 60 you’re gonna use Windfury imbue, but you’re still gonna drop Windfury Totem (and Flametongue Totem) for your party even if you don’t benefit from it

Weapons
- Until you get the Lightning Strike talent, a high-DPS dagger is just as good as a slow 2H
- After getting Lightning Strike, try to have as slow of a 2H as possible
- In general, enhance prefers slow weapons with high top-end dmg, counting for both 1H and 2H

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: Basic "TL;DR" Shaman Leveling Guide
content_md:
I'd add some personal takes here, focusing on tanking.
If you min-max, the orc is probably the least optimal choice, but the weapon skill bonus can still help with melee damage.
Tauren is more of a defensive choice which helps. Early game and at raid levels shamans are rather squishy, a pseudo-def CD racial and the added HP helps.
Trolls are the more offensive option, mostly because of berserking. It works as an almost bloodlust on a smaller CD, allowing you to generate threat spikes on demand.
Since a tank's abilities are mostly instant cast ones, the spike mostly manifests in increased auto-attack speed.

For talents.
Shield spec is probably better for early game when the shaman is very squishy.
I always change it to ancestral knowledge when stats become considerable enough.
Shammies have no ability to insta-raise block chance and do not really have block benefits like mana regen (pala) or rage regen (warrior).
I heard that crit immunity is possible at highest raid-gear but I haven't seen a crit immune shammie yet.
If crit immunity is possible and shield spec block chance is needed for that, it becomes justified super late-game but only then.

After that, totemic alignment and stable shields, followed up by ancestral guardian and LS. I personally advise guardian before LS because early game threat is absurdly high but mitigation is low. Guardian helps more.
One point in thundering strikes to open up a new row.
Spirit armor with huge prio. Both mitigation and threat. From around this time really focus on having a good shield.
Thundering strikes up to 4/5 and opening a new row.
Elemental weapons full for the 10% damage reduction. Around this time, alongside with the JC stamina trinkets, mitigation starts to be okay.
Then SS.

After this it becomes a bit flexible.
Best option is probably rushing clearcasting but I usually prefer thundering strikes 5/5 and 1 point in flurry since the first point gives a sizeable haste bonus.

Then, for leveling, convection > concussion. You won't always have a judgment of wisdom on the targets and you still don't have clearcasting.
Then either ele deva 3/3 or elemental warding 2/3. Both are fine, one is a bit defensive, other one makes your hits more consistent.
Then clearcasting asap.
After that either reverberation or element's grace. I'd say element's grace, it raises threat without necessarily spending mana.
Then bloodlust.
Fill the rest as you want. Elemental warding? Bigger shocks?
For raiding switch from cheaper shocks to bigger shocks. You'll get all the buffs and threat ceiling is more important.
Enhancing totems are also a valid choice. Or full flurry.

You can also give up bloodlust, some points in element's grace, too and rush elemental fury under elemental tree.
It gives you added shock damage 10% and makes the shock crits 100% bigger (also damaging totems but they matter less).
It is good if you can crit kinda consistently via shocks, depends on spell crit numbers.

For leveling, getting an early tidal focus is also an option. Not good late game but 25% cheaper totems make wonders to the mana bar while leveling.

_____________

Pulling

Rank 1 lightning bolt is warrior arrow. Big range, costs basically 0 mana.
Chain lightning is for max initial threat.
Max rank lightning bolt is for a high threat on a special target. Let's say mage sheeps a mob and you want to make sure poly stays.
Earth shock for run ins. Specially if you fought a pack, they mostly died, you move to a newer one and shocking one of them to call the next pack. I really like it for pala-like tanking.
Also run-in: starting with SS sets up higher nat damage/threat on the setup shock and LS as an option but lower base threat. Depends on how fast DPS would rip threat on the first mob.

You can also have a shooting range setup with many casters.
Earthbind down, chain lightning pull, melee (!) mobs come and you just nuke them before they arrive. Less effective, more flashy.

_______

Stats
For tanking stam is always prio (just like armor).
For leveling, agi is second for dodge and crit but str becomes 2nd most important lategame. Shocks and strikes will scale from AP at max rank and it's just threat.
Int's placement depends on how experienced you are. At the start int can almost be as important as stam because people waste mana all the time and a mid fight oom is bad.
As people learn what to use when or even downrank here and there, int falls behind agi/str.

__________

Gear:
Whatever you get, but shield with big armor is always a top prio, spec after spirit shield talent and those +stam trinkets are a must at level 33.
For shields, some ideas:
Compendium of the fallen q reward -> SM Cath shield -> Gilneas shield / Mara goblin shield / ... / SWV shield

__________

Threat

The main concept is to never generate too much threat. That just wastes mana.
Up to 3 mobs, you are fine without threat totems.
If in doubt, you can place a stoneclaw but it might be overdoing it.
You can dash out SS on target 1, shock on target 2 and LS on target 3.
For 3 target packs chain lightning is a cool range pull because initial threat is also established on each target.

Always ask for judgment of wisdom on skull if there's a pala in the party.
Skip using your rotation and do auto-attack+taunt as much as possible to save mana.

If a target resists nature damage, use frost shock.
If targets resist fire damage, your aoe threat is stoneclaw only.

Optionally use a lower rank but still strong earth shock to save mana when you don't need to go all out as much.
You can use lightning shield at pull for added threat and switch to water shield later.

Some classes will rip aggro anyway. Ironically ele and enh DPS are a mess. I just let em die whenever they don't focus threat meter.

Earthbind and frost shock can indeed turn a bad situation into a kite fest.
Regrettably tranquil air totem affects everyone so useless for you. With lower range I sometimes placed it a bit far away for casters and run in, outside its range.
If it had a clause not affecting you if you have rockbiter on, we'd have a salvation.

Windfury. It is a huge DPS boost and is mostly justified, specially if at least 2 DPS are melee.
It will however force you to spend way more mana to keep threat while never having a proc.
A friendly pala helps a lot, if you have it: jow solves the mana problems and in extreme cases, salvation can be put on melee in exchange for WF.
If the melee is higher level than I am or really geared, I usually give WF but telling them that if they rip threat they tank that mob as a deal.

Grace of air is a bit overrated for leveling I think but really good for raiding. You are usually better off by not spending mana on it, unless you need to go full defensive (earth shield + grace of air + stoneskin + maybe even life totem).

Grounding needs to be used strategically.
Well-timed fire nova for an los pull is a huge snap threat.

author: Duids
subject: Elemental Pre-raid & BiS by Phase
content_md:
Greetings, turtles,

With the release of Ambershire and the recent class changes, I see renewed interest in a list of Elemental Shaman BiS gear you can acquire before Molten Core and Onyxia are released.

author: pagu
subject: Feedback on elemental shaman in pve
content_md:
Want to share my thoughts and suggestions about current state of elemental shaman in pve
My experience is raiding as enhancement shaman up to nax and ele shaman (nature spec) up to aq40. Didnt try fire ele but there were shamans that spec in my raid so i made some conclusions

So, ele shaman has 2 ways to play now:
Nature spec classic ele - has low single target dps and good aoe/cleave. has 4 actively used situational spells, shocks, totems. pretty complicated rotation. need to track clearcasting procs not to be oom instantly. and even with perfect clearcasting management ooms fast. need to track fire shock duration to effectively cast molten blast. need weapon oil.
Fire spec ele (with elemental weapons) - has good 1 target dps. (escepically if can afford t3) and average aoe. has 1 spell, shocks, totems. dont need to track fire shock duration. dont need to track clearcasting. no rotation, just spam 1 button. hard to oom because no expensive mana cost spells. dont need oil. disadvantage - alot of fire immune bosses in mc/bwl+ony, so it cant be used as the only spec to play in raids. also may have threat issue but idk

For me nature ele feels clunky. Complicated rotation that easily breaks, is procs and cd based, sensitive for resists. Most of rotation is long casts. Mana. Pushbacks.
 1) mana.
enhancement and resto shaman have mechanics to better utilise water shield. why ele has only clearcasting?
clearcasting needs crits to work. if you give it even -100% cost to spells, its very unreliable. i have with very good gear (33%+ lightning bolt crit chance) and sometimes i have very long streaks with no crits at all. in a very bad situation i had almost 0 crits on onyxia and was oom in the middle of 2nd phase, eating big mana potion. do we have any another classes with such mana troubles?
and what makes situation even worse - 99% of time ele shaman is in party with melees or tanks to give wf. so no moonkin aura and shadow priest mana regen.
leveling as ele shaman means drink half of you life
 2) eye of the storm.
the worst antipushback for pve and even so it is nerfed in 1.18. that is brain cancer...
there are alot of packs and bosses where all raid gets damage. and shaman casts constantly pushed back. as ele shaman rotation is mostly of long casts that is so annoying, its just may halve dps.
 3) improved molten blast.
bad desing. i understand devs want to make molten blast good as spammable ability for nature immune targets and at the same time good for rare use on other targets.
but if you want to use it effectively, you need to constantly track fire shock duration. even with addons there is no good istrument to do that. and if your molten blast resisted, rotation is broken - you need to watch it and recast fire shock.
my suggestion for improved molten blast: molten blast has +100% crit chance but when it crits, you get debuff for 10/6 seconds that disables this bonus. if you already has this debuff and get another molten blast crit, dont refresh debuff duration.
that will make rotation more stable and predictable, dont break by resists, debuff is easy to track, helps to get more clearcasting especially for low geared shamans.
for those who cry about 100% crit chance is op - molten blast base damage is pretty low
 4) earthquake.
bad desing. it helps to get more dps in aoe situations but has alot of problems.
devs want it to be good for 1 targen and aoe, but for 1 target it is worse than ligntning bolt. it is 2.5 sec cast and has no crit bonus from talents. the only advantage it does 3 hits so more chances to get clearcasting. but if 1st hit is resisted, there are no 2nd and 3rd hits.
for aoe its useful on fat packs. but there are alot of aoe encounters with fast dying mobs. 2.5 cast is already too much, half of pack is dead when cast is finished. but if your target dies before cast finished, its canceled, so you just stay and do nothing. what a joke... even fire totems are more comfortable to use.
my opinion it needs to be revorked. if you want it to be castable aoe, make it area cast like dynamite. if you want in to be 1 target, make it instant.
but honestly i would change it to some passive effect. may be proc on chain lightning.
or give us elemental overload instead of this, for example. i know arcane mages have it now but so what?
or something like if you cast doesnt crit you get +10% spell crit. stacks until you get spell crit. ele shaman is extremely crit dependent spec. no crits - dps suck and you are oom
or may be shamanistic rage cd with strong mana regen and defensive buffs
 5) elemental mastery.
look at elemental mastery, then at bloodlust, then back at elemental mastery and laugh. need to be improved, duration extended, may be add spell crit or haste and buff party when shaman land a crit.
 6) searing totem.
please make it not attack controlled targets or targets out of combat
with extended range so much risk it pull extra pack, so i use it very rare, only on bosses or in safe situalions
 7) weapon enchants.
not sure may be i want too much... but it will be great to get spell power/healing shaman weapon imbue
 8) need some buff for caster party.
shaman is utility class but all it have for caster party is ridiculous mana spring totem or tremor in some cases
make wf totem to have elemental overload effect for party? for direct damage spells and/or heals. hm... looks very interesting but may be too strong. wf totem is very strong for melee party so why not to give equal for caster party
or make air totem that buffs spell hit/crit

All above is just my thoughts, i dont expect all of that will be implemented but may be devs notice that and make some changes for smoother ele playstyle

topic_title: Feedback on elemental shaman in pve

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: Feedback on elemental shaman in pve
content_md:
I think that the WF part cannot be helped.
Strictly speaking, WF totem was already nerfed but further nerfing it or locking it behind only certain builds would affect all melees in the game.
The problem with WF is that:
 1. it is so overpowered it determines how shamans are placed
 2. it doesn't benefit shamans (weapon imbues have prio, PVE casters and healers won't melee)
 3. it affects half of the playerbase so any nerf would mean an uproar from rogues, hunters, palas, warriors etc

In my opinion we have to accept that shaman at Vanilla is by design a melee support class which on top of that base can perform all four roles to a degree.

On paper you could put eles to a caster group, tranquil air totem has some form of stacking with salvation and you have water totems, too. But those benefits are not comparable to WF+ strength + FT.
The only positive thing I can state is that if a raid has too many shamans, eles usually have a priority to be put in a caster group. It is rare though.

Regarding the other points.
I think fire ele is an abomination. Molten blast should be a backup spell for high nat rez enemies, not an entire playstyle. Just something to press when mob says nope lol to lightning bolts.

For mana, improved water shield talent helps for passive regen but regen is weak.
Resto has a good regen with access to both improved shields and improved water shield but enh and ele struggles there.
There should be a way for those two to be more consistent at mana.
My suggestion would be making mana spring totem mana regen equal to max rank blessing of wisdom and make the totem cheaper since it has to be spammed (which is not only expensive kinda but it keeps interrupting full spirit mana regen).
Maybe just add a new AQ20 book for it.

Regarding weapon enchants, I am against it.
Weapon imbues are a speciality of enhancement shamans and all have a melee effect at Vanilla.
I think turning them to a generic, build-dependent buff would be against this identity.

Searing Totem: I agree that it should by default target the same mob as you do. Asking for a talent point for that is stupid.

 8) need some buff for caster party.
I am against this because of what had already been said.
Shaman by default is a melee support class. Weakening WF would cause an uproar. Giving shaman an equally potent caster buff would be too OP.

 5) elemental mastery.
No real opinion but please note that mastery, unlike bloodlust is not a capstone talent.

Earthquake.
I have a unique problem with that. In my opinion it should be an ice-based spell.
Hear me out.
Shaman weapon imbues can deal fire or frost damage.
Shaman shocks can deal nature, fire or frost damage.
Shaman casted abilities can give fire or nature damage (2 kinds).
Shaman totems each give fire damage.
The most underrepresented spell type is frost. If I wanna imagine elemental shaman as a master of elements, I want it to have certain amount of symmetry between those elements.
Adding another nature damage into the mix just makes the scales of damage types more imbalanced.
Let earthquake be avalanche or hail.

 2) eye of the storm.
Here I wanna defend the devs. Ele can use earth shield for 30% negation. Sure, some other casters have more but not each of them.
This 30% ensures that resto can go 100% for healing via talents.
But adding more to ele would badly hurt PVP in my opinion, since ele is a caster (at PVP) with a shield, a shitload of armor and slows. Allowing this bulky caster to self heal without interruption (for example) would be too much.

author: Chanchoberto420
subject: Shaman suggestion regarding mana efficiency
content_md:
I wanted to suggest a couple of things regarding mana efficiency. Im currently leveling an Enchancement Shaman. I specced for Elemental Focus talent, which I think is vital for mana efficiency.

First I think it would be good if Lightning and Earth Shield would benefit from Clearcasting. Elemental Focus improves our mana efficiency greatly but refreshing Lightning Shield is expensive. It would then become a choice for the player if they want to expend a proc of Clearcasting by casting the shield.

Second, I feel that the mana restored by Lightning Strike while using Water Shield to be very low. The only time I see a considerable mana increase is when using Rockbiter imbue and casting Lightning Strike with a Clearcasting proc. It would be nice if the mana restored by default covered the mana cost of Lightning Strike on top of the mana recovered by the orb. Maybe at endgame it scales better, but while leveling it seems like we only get a free strike that does like 50% weapon damage.

What does everyone think about this?

Dungeons are all kind of maraphone, where you need to think - do I really need to push all my buttons now, if I go OOM next and lose time on drinking?

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: Shaman suggestion regarding mana efficiency
content_md:
'Tank shaman is the least role with mana issues, since Mana Shield pops on incoming hits'

I have to disagree there.
The 'shaman mana engine' is improved water shield talent + stable shield talents.
Only resto can reach both, which gives them a lot of passive mana regen:
 9mp5 + 18% full mana regen while casting if all 9 orbs are active.
Plus healers downgrade spells all the time.
Resto is actually in a pretty good place with mana.

Enh DPS and Enh Tank are super JoW-dependent.
LS with water shield on is kinda bad even if it is scaling. Passive water shield orb procs are a nice supplementary but can't carry mana regen.
Played both pala tank and shaman tank. While both use mana, shaman tank mana management is infinitely worse. It has many reasons:
 * BoW is superior to mana totem. Mana totem kinda has to be spammed, not cheap, and it is below max rank BoW in mana regen if I remember right.
 * Water Shield LS is not comparable to JoW.
 * Water Shield passive is somewhat comparable to block mana regen pala talent.
 * Shammie tanks spams usually max rank abilities for rotation. Palas have to spam less abilities for the rotation (consec is area-based DoT, holy shield and holy strike is not comparable to constant SS, ES, LS spam + totem upkeep).

It is not an anti-pala post, just showing how a build with bigger mana spendings have worse mana maintenance, causing problems unless JoW is maintained by someone.

Enh DPS is in an even worse spot because optimally their rotation requires lightning shield and LS through that, saying no to mana regen.

Ele can in theory get either improver water shield or stable shields but not both.
Improved water shield alone is not a good mana regen talent, because it really scales with the number of shield orbs you have. If it is kept at 3, it won't help that much.
Also, the talent combination would be less effective with melees (orbs more likely to be consumed and on avreage enh has less spirit from gear). But still, it alongside mana totem, and LS would do the trick.

Enh DPS is a bit peculiar, but they had the option to switch between resource management mode (water shield) and DPS mode (lightning shield) so I think it's fair.
It would also allow enh tank to go for other shields more often, allowing DPS spiked (LS) or a more defensive setup (ES).
_________

I'm arguing for making improved water shield more accessible, because (unless we retweak a bunch of other stuffs), the shaman mana engine come from the combination of that talent and stable shields. If it is affordable for each serious build, this problem gets resolved.

subject: Re: Shaman suggestion regarding mana efficiency
content_md:
I never intended for mana to be infinite, but there should be mechanics to make it "self sustainable" in a way.

My reasoning regarding Enh DPS is that when we got Lightning Shield on we do high damage with Lightning Strike but we consume more mana, so its very reasonable that when using Water Shield we reduce our damage output to recharge our mana in return.

So we should be bouncing between LS and WS to keep up both our mana and dps. The problem I see is that Lightning Strike doesnt replenish enough mana, so I end up the whole dungeon using Water Shield so I dont have to sit down to drink after every encounter.
