author: Xudo
subject: Re: Shaman suggestion regarding mana efficiency
content_md:
I seen several shamans in dungeons. They were like "I have tons of buttons, so I should press them all". As a result, they did super high burst, but had to drink after each pull.

My first point is: if you want better mana sustain, you can just spend less mana.

My second point is: There might be a talent which reduce manacost of abilities during long fights. Like "after each block, you get buff for 10 sec, which reduces mana cost of abilities by 4%, stacks up to 20%.". Block is because it happens often in PvE tanking and rarely in PvP fights.

There is one major difference of shamans/paladin tanks compared to druid/warrior.
Shamans and paladin have max available resources at the start of the fight while rage-based tanks "charge up" during the fight. Lightning/crusader strike available right off the start also contribute to burst meta of the server.
This chargeable buff will encourage pressing buttons as later as possible, because initially they will be costly. In the same time, in long fight, you eventually should get positive mana income from your abilities.

Boss Pull
For shaman to tank he has to use:

 2. Lightning strike
 3. Earth shock MAX RANK
 4. Totem for Agi
 5. Totem for str/stoneskin/tremor

These are mandatory single target, and with these you can sustain yourself for long.

AOE:
All of the above PLUS mandatory these-
 6. Fire nove totem for instant (after pop) aoe aggro
 7. Magma totem for sustain AoE aggor
 8. Stoneclaw if people are out AOEing your aggro

Aoe pulls are THE MAJORITY of pulls in dungeon, and totems are expensive so even with totemic recall you just have to drink after ~2-3 pulls.

Shaman tank has sh-t tier progression, only set bonus is T2.5, the amount of good plate defense items >>>> mail.
Leather tank items are geared towards druids, and mana sustain is better for paladins.

author: Chanchoberto420
subject: Elemental Weapons and WF
content_md:
The Elemental Weapons talent is one of the most interesting reworks done to the Enhancement talent tree. It sets out to give each weapon imbue bonus features to accomodate for different playstyles and make each one more relevant within the Shamans toolkit.

Nevertheless, the bonus given to Windfury weapon is quite lacking compared to other imbues. Given that they were recent changes to the bonus, with equally lukewarm effects, it seems that the developers are not sure how to provide bonus to an echant that is already very powerful and the main choice for endgame Enhancement DPS.

What do you guys think could be an appropiate bonus for WF?

I got a couple of ideas:

 1) In line with the current bonus, gaining extra attacks increases movement speed AND chance to dodge attacks. This goes well with the wind theme and provides a defensive aspect thats useful for leveling, similar to what RB does with damage reduction.

 2) Extra attacks that crit damage up to 2 nearby enemies. This would give some additional AoE dps which the spec lacks. I also like the whirlwind cleave as part of the wind theme.

 3) If Im allowed to dream: Extra attacks that land have a chance to reduce the casting time for Lighting Bolt and Chain Lightning by 25%, stacking up to 4 times. I love Maelstrom Weapon from later expansions, and would allow Enh Shaman to add those spells to their rotation. Having instant CL would add AoE dps capabilities as well. I would leave the healing spells out as it would be too op in pvp I think.

I would love to hear your ideas about this.

author: Avalok
subject: 'Frost Shock' Should Affect 'Raid Bosses'
content_md:
The Shaman's Frost Shock debuff should affect Raid Bosses,
but with little to no movement speed reduction effect on them for balancing reasons.

This way, the shaman's "Frostbrand" imbue can always critically hit Raid Bosses more often if she has the
"Elemental Weapons" talent with her. The said talent allows Frostbrand imbue to always critically hit so long as the taget is under the Frost Shock debuff. This makes the Frost Shock + Frostbrand combo for Enhancement Shamans more viable in raids, specifically against Raid Bosses.

This also makes it more 'mana conservative' for Enhancement Shamans when fighting against Raid Bosses, due to the critical hits of the Frostbrand imbue activating their "Elemental Focus" talent, which gives the Shaman two (2) stacks of clearcasting buffs that reduce their spells and abilities' mana costs by 60%.

subject: Re: 'Frost Shock' Should Affect 'Raid Bosses'
content_md:
Honestly, shaman imbues by themselves are not a different playstile. Wether you end up using flametongue or frostburn doest change pretty much anything about your raid rotation (appart from having to keep a literally useless debuff active)

In raids, even if it is guaranteed to crit, frostburn sucks because its scaling is abyssmal and almost no matter what you do, it is subpar.
While i can see the use on dungeombosses, i would argure they die quick enough for manasaving concerns not to win out over the misunderstanding that having a slow apply but not actually slowing may cause.

The frostburn buff from the imbue talent does exactly what is is supposed to. Give shaman a good spellbased imbue during levelling. And it can get replaced by flametongue at highergear levels and raidsize.

Not every ability needs equal outcome for raid encounters. Having different imbues shine in different situations rewards mastering your class and picking the right tool for the job.
Of course, windfury is the king of weaponenchants currently, but for levelling content frostburn is already arguably a fantastic choice for shamans wanting to be more active and kite in between swings.

author: Cacuba123
subject: Shaman:Tank Idea
content_md:
Hi, long term tank. I have been tanking since vanilla, over 20 years. With 5 years on twow and involved in CC2 extensively. Yes, I take some personal blame for how some thing act/play…and love how some of it is.
I personally did not touch shaman as it had been 16years since I played a shaman. Now I'm getting the chance to try again and do i love it! Tanking on a shaman is so rewarding, but it definitely is lacking in areas.
So my current idea for talent changes is to create a new talent at the enhancement 25-30 point range
 3/3 stable shields-1/1 lightning strike then straight to requiring 25pts in enhancement for…
Elemental Shields: while wearing a shield Increases the CD for refreshing shield by 3/6/9 seconds but gain the following effects:
Water shield: Gain 1/2/3% dodge per shield charge
Lightning shield: Gain 1/2/3% increased nature damage per shield charge
Earthshield: Increases armor by 1/2/3% per shield charge

Do i know the ramifications…no… but its deep enough in the tree that itll make it less of a problem in pvp for ele/enhance pvp spec and more of a benefit to tanks.
 9 charges is the max, ofc and you lose 1 charge per hit taken and 1 charge per lightning strike which means youll be between 3-4 charges before you can recast.
Water shields maximum of 27% dodge is enough for shamans to be able to hit avoidance cap…even if we do lose it for a few seconds
Lightning shield makes it perfect for pulls with bonus damage on pulls woth earth shock/lightning bolt/chain lightning/Lighning strike
And earth shield is good for trash where you just want the bonus phy miti which should at most (ukara level) net 3000armor making shaman close to druid miti

Biggest ramifications would be pvp tanky builds, but they would lose out on 100% bonus crit dmg to spells and 10% bonus to all dpell damage. And gain these benefits with a shield.

subject: Re: Shaman:Tank Idea
content_md:
You are not forced to use lightning strike. In fact, with your talent suggestion it might be better NOT to use it, so the shield charges dont expire faster.

Because contrary to paladin you dont loose charges on your success state, you loose them on failsate. But even at maximum depletion rate (1 Globe every 4.5 seconds from being hit, + one on CD with LS, you will at worst be down 4 globes by the time you can refresh water shield.

Considering you come with over 20% innate parry and dodge chance before gear (block not included(5% parry and dodge innate, 4.4% dodge from grace and 6% from ancestral guardian)) without this talent, you will easily have over 50% chance to completely avoid auto attacks. meaning your likely only gonna drop a single charge during the full 9 seconds without using lightning strike, this is basically passive 24+% dodge chance.

Speaking of the gear
T2.5 would be ~5% dodge from agi + 1.5 dodge from defense & 1.5 parry from defense, Elementium Threaded cloak is 2% dodge and another 1% from the enchant. as well as 2% dodge on head and leg enchant each and another ~1% dodge from agility on gloves. ~2% dodge of qiraji belt and heck why not throw in 2 vigilance charms for another 4%

WIth that little setup tossed together, no neck, rings weapon or consumables /other classes buffs considered, you end up with 70% combined parry and dodge.

That is absolute overkill. Now if we make the globes translate to extra BLOCK chance or some other crit mitigation stat that doesn't just make you immune to physical damage, we certainly have something that can be workable , but a tank that under realistic raidbuff scenario has a 80+% chance to completely avoid physical damage is not gonna be healthy for the game.

author: Sylbrosa
subject: Nerf Shaman PVP
content_md:
I’m a min-maxer — always have been. I enjoy analyzing data and doing the math to squeeze out every bit of effectiveness in online games. That’s my hobby.

Lately I’ve been digging into Shaman PvP balance, and I think I’ve found the core of the problem: the Ancestral Guardian talent.

Originally, Shaman was designed as a glass cannon: very high burst damage, but a bit more on the fragile than other meele classes. If a Shaman got focused, they were supposed to go down quickly. That was the trade-off for having such explosive damage and strong offensive cooldowns.

But that trade-off no longer really exists.

With current tuning, Shamans still have the damage of a glass cannon — they can delete people in a couple of globals — and with only three talent points, they can massively increase their survivability.

Ancestral Guardian is a third-row talent with only three ranks and reads:

> “Increases your armor value from items by [5/10/15]% and your chance to dodge by an additional [2/4/6]%.”

This talent was clearly meant to make tank-style Shaman builds more viable, which is fine in theory. The problem is how much power is packed into such a small investment.

For comparison, Warriors and Rogues usually need to spend around five talent points to gain 5% dodge or parry. Meanwhile, a Shaman spends only three points to gain 6% dodge plus 15% increased armor from items.

In raw defensive value, that’s roughly equivalent to 8–10 talent points worth of stats, condensed into just three points.

So now we have a class that keeps its glass-cannon level damage, but for the cost of three talent points gains near tank-level resilience. That breaks the original class identity and removes the risk that was supposed to balance their burst.

The problem isn’t that Shamans have defensive options — it’s that Ancestral Guardian is massively overtuned for its tier and cost, especially in PvP where dodge and armor scale extremely well with gear.

In short: the design goal makes sense, but the numbers don’t.

Enhancement shaman is even more bursty, but they don't have armor nor dodge nor DR, so they are arguably a lot easier to kill even if they occasionally one shot people. Ret paladin versus enhancement shaman is 50/50 matchup whereas tank elemental shaman versus ret is 100/0 matchup.

Even post nerf to rockbiter, 10k armour on a caster is nuts, devs should push that talent deeper into the tree 100%. Using Kruul Axe against those shamans I've been hit harder by their elemental shield than what my attack did to them, I'm literally killing myself playing aganst that spec while he does 4k to me in one GCD.

ranged class can be on par with melee in two ways:

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: No changes for resto shamans in 1.18.1
content_md:
Dont underestimate the nerf to healpaladin. Shamans best capability has always been keeping groups of clumped players (often melees) alive. Their output at that has always been good and remains decent. But the abundance of healpaladin who splash their holy strike healing exclusively on melees makes it hard for shamans to unfold their maximim potential. Especially since their heal tends to leave targets at 95% hp, so they eat a bounce of cl. Since the holy paladins get nerfed quite a bit (especially when it comes to the t3.5 where they went truely insane), you are indirectly more attractive as a resto shaman.

Additionally, spirit link is an insanely useful defensive cooldown that trivializes enrages, tank stuns or tricky pulls greatly.

As for the t1 set. That has already been nerfed over a year back. It had been shadow unnerfed. (Prolly some teammember got 8/8 and needed to feel good, or someone merged without looking). This nerf is necessary or your gear progression for 8gearslots ends in molten core!

And lastly on the topic of resto being an absolute snoozefest - unfortunately true

content_md:
Hello, to answer your question, no, the Air Totem isn't useless. While the Wind Fury Totem is a significant DPS buff useful for melee classes, it's not for all classes:

 - Hunter (already mentioned),
 - Combat Rogue (who has a talent that increases their energy generation based on their agility),
 - Tank Shaman (to increase their critical strike chance and dodge ability),
 - Tank Druid (for the same reasons).

If you're raiding and have these classes, you can make a group with :
 - 1 Tank Shaman,
 - 1 Tank Druid,
 - 1 Combat Rogue,
 - 2 Hunters, with at least one Marksman for the Trueshoot Aura.

You can also make the same group with an Enhancement Shaman, which will allow them to benefit from additional buffs, since the Wind Fury Totem doesn't provide them with any.

I hope that answers your question :)

author: Elesion
subject: Re: Is the Grace of Air totem useless?
content_md:
> **Mimiwarmini wrote: Thu Feb 12, 2026 12:56 am**
> While the Wind Fury Totem is a significant DPS buff useful for melee classes, it's not for all classes:
>
>  - Tank Druid (to increase their critical strike chance and dodge ability).

> **Travoltino wrote: Thu Feb 12, 2026 8:49 am**
> Druids and Hunters are better with AGI.
>  Tanks are better with AGI.

As a bear tank I would strongly disagree. I maintain that the biggest buff to bears with CC2 was the Shaman class change giving us access to Windfury.

A bear's main threat engine is Maul, which is a queued skill replacing your next auto-attack. So a bear played properly will *never* white hit. You *always* want to have Maul queued.
But baseline (without talents) you don't generate any rage from yellow hits, only from white hits.

That meant that before CC2 bears were largely rage-capped. Dodge was seen as a very detrimental stat, because you relied on getting hit for your rage generation. Some bears even deliberately wore less mitigation to take more damage and generate more rage (which is rather counter-intuitive for a tank imo).

WF in bear form fixed all of that in an instant. You keep Maul queued 100% of the time and WF will still provide white hits inbetween, ensuring you have ample rage to spend even if you dodge a couple of times in a row. Having ample rage to spend means you can use Savage Bite and Swipe on CD. Using those instant cast abilities on cooldown, provides more triggers for WF, which means more threat and more rage. It's a beautiful snowball where you get to press buttons on cooldown without having to sabotage your avoidance and mitigation.

Grace of Air is not bad for bears (and probably superior for some fights). But WF fixing rage starvation and trivializing the rage economy is much *much* stronger 9/10 times in my opinion.

author: Travoltino
subject: T1 Resto shaman in 1.18.1
content_md:
Hello, I wrote a post like this on DC but I wanted to try making a topic as well.

T1 8/8 set for resto shaman is undoubtedly strong.
But I havent seen a single reason why it should be removed like this.

Common arguments I read:
 1. Its from MC - and?
So are +7 to Two Hand axes gloves which are BIS.
Accuria with +2% hit is also BIS for dual wielders.
Sigil trinket - absolute uncontested BIS for AOE dmg for mages.
Thunderfury - I have seen 1.5 thunderfury being made, before I got my full T1 set :)

 2. T1 sets are supposed to suck:
yes i read this.. moving on

 3. T1 resto shaman is so good its Kara 40 level:
Objectively no, but it IS a strong set BECAUSE it INTERACTS with shaman talents.
T2 T2.5 T3 - every resto shaman would replace those set bonuses with just more 'green text' stats.
They offer nothing, to a point of almost insulting worthlesness :D T2,5 was "fine ish" when spirit link had 1/3 of its cooldown but even then meh.
T2 is "fine" as it just gives almost green text bonuses
T3 ... as ele and enha are good, Heal is bad.
 2 set Cheaper totems - pointless you put totems before fight and orange.
More mana from mana totem - cool you get a FOUR SET T3 bonus of what pala gets from wisdom rank+1 book.
 6 set .. isnt bad but the proc rate RNG makes its a "nice to have sometimes"
 8 set is good
=
So the problem isnt T1 set is too good, its that others offer nothing.

And after 1.18.1 priests are getting VERY deserved buffs.
So what reason is there to **INVALIDATE** months of dedication for a niche set for Shaman?
 **A set which until its 8/8 its objectively worse than random slapped gear with high HP, Int, mana regen.?**
Its a comfy set to play where its healing spread range is pretty much melee range.
It required a full pump of haste to work, as the healing srpead doesnt happen if the primary target is full hp.
It takes 2.25 sec cast spell with no heal over time component, and which has some 0.8X coeficient and makes it useful.

And if it was just nerfed to 15% spread or it only spread to +1 instead of +2, or you "fixed" (aka bugged) its interaction with healing way mana return on target 2/3 .. then fine I can live with that.
But what we are getting is **PEAK** classic design of "here is a worthless set bonus lol"
